News.title: Blundering Burnham will bend over backwards for Brussels – even if Britain pays the price
News.content:
EU puppet







Next

SO, Prime Minister… deal or no deal?

Andy Burnham claimed a “win-win” EU reset, which will actually cost billions and do nothing to ease the cost of living, was there “in black and white”.



But the Brussels bankers insist the already one-sided agreement is dependent on him also capitulating to demands for us to subsidise EU students coming to UK universities, which could cost us more than £500million.

He inevitably will — to the detriment of our own debt-laden students — because, for people-pleaser Burnham, standing up for Britain’s interests comes a poor second to getting a pat on the head from the Eurocrats.



But now we learn the dodgy agreement may also include plans for Digital ID, despite the PM ditching that idea months ago in virtually the only cost-cutting decision of his reign so far.

Just like the Tories’ Rwanda scheme to tackle illegal immigration, which Labour ditched, it may now be discussed because his EU “friends” support it.

The PM must come clean on the full “reset” details because his dealings in Brussels look about as transparent as the Government’s questionable discussions with Manchester City’s Abu Dhabi owners.

And people are only learning the truth about THOSE because of The Sun’s revelations.

Six former Prime Ministers have now expressed either unease or outright dismay over Burnham’s Brexit betrayal.

He won’t listen.



Unless Brussels thinks differently, of course, and then he’ll change his mind soon enough.

Fear we go…

REOPENING the toxic Brexit debate sadly means more deluded Remainers pretending that leaving the EU has been the root cause of all Britain’s ills.

It is as much a lie now as it was during the 2016 referendum, when Project Fear’s doom-mongers predicted economic catastrophe if we left the bloc.

In fact, Britain has recently out-performed Europe and, with the growing AI revolution and Brexit freedoms, it can go further, faster.

A glance at the sluggish economies and social unrest on the Continent dispels any idea that the EU is a utopia.



As Tory leader Kemi Badenoch says, it is an important market but it cannot be our only market.

We need to aim higher and forge stronger links with modern superpowers, not lock ourselves into the trading shackles of the past.

Too many Remainers would rather talk down our country than accept they were wrong about Britain outside the EU.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Politicians need to take off their “gloom-tinted glasses”, to quote CBI boss Rain Newton-Smith.

Then they could unleash the power of our world-beating innovators, thrusting industrialists and aspirational workers currently held back by Labour’s high-tax, low-growth, big-welfare culture.

News.title: Man lured to remote villa in Spain before being tied up and beaten in 15-hour ordeal – as two arrested over ‘kidnapping’
News.content:
'KIDNAP' HORROR Man lured to remote villa in Spain before being tied up and beaten in 15-hour ordeal – as two arrested over ‘kidnapping’







Next

A MAN has been rescued after he was allegedly lured to a remote villa, tied up, beaten and threatened with death in a horror 15-hour ordeal.

A woman he considered a friend tricked him into visiting the isolated property near Montserrat, Spain, before he was ambushed, police said.



When he arrived, the woman and two other male captors allegedly restrained him with ropes and wielded a large machete in his face.

The victim, 54, was then forced inside where he was subjected to hours of physical assaults and denied sleep, according to the Civil Guard.



His accused kidnappers also continued to threaten his life with a range of bladed weapons and batons, seen arranged on a bed in evidence pictures.

They forced the man to record several videos addressed to his family in which he claimed to be doing well.



The hope was that they would stop his relatives from becoming concerned and launching a search for him.

The man was able to briefly make contact with his family asking for help and providing clues as to his location.

After the Civil Guard were contacted, officers were able to find the villa and free the man, who had sustained injuries of varying severity.

Police said that the victim was tricked into picking up the woman he considered a friend near Montserrat in order to drive her home.



When he pulled up to the meeting point, he noticed that the woman was with a man whom he barely knew.

The pair asked him to drive them to the villa, where a third man was lying in wait.

As they arrived, the victim then knew he had been set up.

Two of the alleged perpetrators were arrested at the scene during the rescue mission.

Cops seized several large bladed weapons, along with other items believed to have been used during the kidnapping.



Those arrested – a 41-year-old woman and 54-year-old man – are accused of unlawful detention.

The kidnapping was reportedly linked to a prior conflict between the people involved.

Investigators are still trying to establish a motive behind the kidnapping and whether there were other individuals involved.

News.title: Henry Novak killler Vickrum Digwa befriends black cab rapist John Worboys in jail as monsters play cards & table tennis
News.content:
Next

HENRY Nowak’s killer Vickrum Digwa has befriended black cab rapist John Worboys on a specialist prison unit.

They play table tennis, Scrabble and cards in the Westgate Unit at HMP Frankland, Durham.



The wing is usually for lags with personality disorders — but Digwa, 23, is there mostly to shield him from harm as its inmates are kept apart from other prisoners at the high security Category A jail.

A source said: “Digwa is extremely happy that he has secured a place on the unit.



“Bizarrely, he is getting along really well with Worboys and they chat a lot and watch TV together sometimes.

“But people are pretty disgusted by their friendship and it is the talk of the jail.”

Serial rapist Worboys, 69, is serving life for attacks on 16 women.

Sources say he was moved to the unit as part of a “pathway” to a move from prison to a secure hospital such as Broadmoor.

Digwa is serving a 25-year minimum for murdering Henry, 18, in Southampton last year then falsely claiming to be a victim of racial abuse.

We told how he had previously refused to go on to the prison wing at HMP Frankland where Soham killer was fatally attacked in February.



A Ministry of Justice spokesperson said: “Our thoughts remain with Henry Nowak’s family and friends.

“It’s right his killer received life and remains behind bars for this terrible crime.”

News.title: Saddam Hussein’s jet with private lounge & space for 330 passengers up for sale for £680,000 after 35 years in desert
News.content:
'FLYING PALACE' Saddam Hussein’s jet with private lounge & space for 330 passengers up for sale for £680,000 after 35 years in desert







Next

SADDAM Hussein’s plush private jet has gone on sale for just £680,000 after collecting dust in the desert for 35 years.

The “flying palace” reportedly ferried the ruthless dictator to diplomatic meetings around the world – boasting a VIP lounge and state suite.



It is one of two Boeing 747s that has been left to face the elements on the tarmac of a Tunisian desert airport for more than three decades.

They were rushed out of Iraq in 1991 for safekeeping just weeks before the Second Gulf War erupted.



Now, state-owned Iraqi Airways is flogging both aircraft at a bargain price that costs less than a brand-new Bugatti supercar.

The crown jewel of the pair is a rare Boeing 747SP, registered as YI-ALM and named Al-Qadissiya, which was kitted out as a luxury VIP plane for Hussein’s regime in 1982.



Inside, the flying fortress boasts a private stateroom, a conference room, and a plush lounge fitted with sleeper seats.

It is the 44th of only 45 of the 747SP models ever built.

While Baghdad hasn’t officially confirmed the tyrant flew on it, pictures from a 1986 trip to Moscow show Hussein posing in front of the jet.

The aircraft was also spotted in London during 1983 government talks with Hussein.



Its companion, a larger Boeing 747-200 registered as YI-AGP and also built in 1982, worked as a commercial passenger and cargo plane with 45 first-class and 285 economy seats.

The two jumbos touched down at Tozeur-Nefta International Airport in southwestern Tunisia on January 1, 1991, but never went home.

Upon arrival, both planes were slapped with a coat of white paint to hide their distinctive Iraqi green markings.



Over the past three decades, the harsh desert elements have stripped back the white coating, leaving the original green livery peeking through underneath.

Iraq initially sent mechanics to maintain the VIP jet every six months, but international sanctions, Kuwaiti disputes, and eye-watering airport fees left both planes stranded.

By 2020, the prolonged stay had racked up around £4 million in parking charges alone.

Iraqi Airways is now offering the jets through a direct sale for $900,000 (£680,000) each, or $1.8 million (£1.36m) for the pair.

But the jets are being sold strictly “as is” with no technical guarantees, and Tunisia has already branded them unairworthy.



Bidders must stump up a 20 per cent security deposit of $180,000 (£137,500) per plane, with the remaining balance due within five days of an offer being accepted.

Buyers will also have to fork out for transport, customs clearance, taxes, and any future parking bills – potentially costing a small fortune.

A committee at the Iraqi embassy in Tunis will review bids between December 21 and January 5, with the sale expected to wrap up by January 7, 2027.

Previous attempts to offload the planes have failed, including a 2023 listing that priced them at just $494,000 (£377,400) each.

Iraqi Airways will consider scrapping the historic jets if no buyer is found this time.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Hussein ruled Iraq with an iron fist from 1979 until he was toppled by the US-led invasion in 2003.

The tyrant was eventually captured in an underground hideout and executed on December 30, 2006.

News.title: Small boat migrant who raped woman sexually harassed another victim at station just 4 days after being let out on bail
News.content:
Next

A RAPE victim has told of her heartbreak after learning her attacker sexually harassed another woman while bailed during her battle to see him prosecuted.

Failed asylum seeker Moustafa Elbohy attacked the first woman after she headed home from a night out.



But the Crown Prosecution Service dropped the case after telling her she had “complied” during the ordeal.

The woman was given ten days to appeal under a victims’ Right to Review scheme — and after two months heard that the CPS had finally authorised charges.



Small-boat migrant Elbohy was later given bail. And four days on he approached his second victim.

Last night the rape victim, a high-flying city worker, told The Sun: “This man is a danger to women.



“My worst fears have been realised. Why was he still out there?”

She added: “I am so upset to hear about the second conviction. I had felt permanently on edge and so, so anxious. It wasn’t just for me, it was for all women, because I had experienced his anger and violence.

“I was just so worried that he was a threat to not just me, but to other women and girls. It’s so upsetting to hear that my worst fears have been realised.

“Why, once the charges had been reinstated for my case, why at that point was bail still granted?



“Why was he still out there in the community?”

Egyptian-born Elbohy, 32, was jailed last Monday for nine years. He had arrived in Britain in the summer of last year.

That September, he was removed from taxpayer-funded accommodation when his asylum claim, made on the basis he said he was gay, was rejected.



Eight days later, on September 20, he dragged his 49-year-old victim from a street near Embankment station in central London and into his tent in a homeless camp under Hungerford Bridge.

She had stopped to chat to him and his friends because she lived near “a lovely Middle Eastern community” and enjoyed listening to them speak Arabic.

But Elbohy used Google Translate to tell the worker: “I want to f*** you” before forcing himself on her twice.

The Sun exclusively revealed he had been charged with rape and he appeared in court on October 30.

A month later, the CPS discontinued the case, having questioned why the victim did not have “internal injuries”.



In a letter, a prosecutor said they were “not satisfied” that there was enough evidence to be sure of a conviction.

They added: “I recognise passive compliance, a common trauma response where a person may freeze and not resist, is a well-recognised coping mechanism in traumatic situations. I make no criticism of your response.”

The decision meant Elbohy, in prison on remand, was released back into the community.

He was moved to an Ibis hotel in Warwickshire, which was being used as supported accommodation.

He gloated about his lifestyle on social media, posting snaps of himself in front of local landmarks.



In February prosecutors U-turned and authorised the rape charge, which Elbohy denied.

He appeared in court on May 7 and was bailed. But on May 11 he was nicked again at Leamington Spa train station.

Sources said British Transport Police officers at the Warwickshire station were alerted when he made sexually charged comments to a woman on the platform.

He then attacked a man who attempted to intervene.

Three weeks after the attack, in June, he appeared before Westminster magistrates’ court for the re-authorised rape charge and he was remanded back into custody.



In August, Elbohy faced Coventry magistrates over the Leamington Spa incidents.

He admitted one count of threatening behaviour and one count of battery and was fined £200, but was told he did not have to pay compensation because of his “limited means”.

At his rape trial at Southwark crown court, jurors were told Elbohy’s DNA was found on his victim when she reported the attack within hours of it happening.

The court heard she was “fearful for her life” as she was forced to the ground.



Prosecutor Richard Milne said: “She knew she was going to be raped and she just wanted to get it over and done with as quickly as possible.”

Elbohy, whose address was given as the DoubleTree by Hilton Reading in Wokingham, Berks, claimed that his victim consented to sex.

Recalling when she was originally told the case would be dropped, his victim told The Sun: “It was still very soon after the rapes had happened and I was still extremely mentally fragile and vulnerable.

“My initial reaction was one of devastation and being so upset by the decision, and I felt that my account hadn’t been taken seriously.



“It was a very, very low and hard few days. I really had to find some kind of inner strength to try and make it right.

“What he did to me was illegal and so wrong, so I was doing it not just for myself, but for other women and girls. He is a danger to women, and the alternative world in which he is still free does not bear thinking about.”

She went on: “It’s really frustrating and upsetting that I had to advocate for myself and go through that Right to Review process to get them to look at it. Not all victims would be able to do this, and nobody should have to fight to get their case into court. I absolutely knew that I was telling the truth. I absolutely knew what he’d done to me was illegal and was a crime and he forced himself upon me.

“But I had to really, really advocate for that.”

Sources said Elbohy would be deported to his native Egypt at the end of his sentence.



Asked if she agreed, the woman said: “I don’t know the details of why he is seeking asylum.

“If his asylum application has been rejected not once, but twice, then it has been carefully considered and the Home Office has their reasons why they have rejected it.

“The focus should never have been on his immigration status or how he arrived in the UK, but on the crimes he has committed.

“My concern is that he is a dangerous individual. This second crime corroborates that. He’s a danger to women and girls, and he needs removing from the streets.”





A CPS spokeswoman said: “We recognise the impact our decision to initially discontinue the case had on the victim and have apologised for the distress that caused.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“After further evidence was received and the case reviewed again, the charges were reinstated.

“Once we became aware of the full extent of Elbohy’s offending, prosecutors successfully argued for bail to be removed. Elbohy is now serving a substantial prison sentence for his crimes.”

News.title: Thomas Markle ‘sent Christmas presents to young children in Far East for years’ before child sex abuse image charges
News.content:
Next

THOMAS Markle Snr sent Christmas gifts to families with small children in the Philippines, Cambodia and Vietnam for years, his son has revealed.

The estranged father of the Duchess of Sussex made regular trips abroad and his apparently generous gesture did not raise suspicions.



But the 82-year-old’s motives have been brought into question after he was charged in the US and in the Philippines over alleged child sex abuse stashes.

Thomas Markle Jnr, 60, said: “I remember in the 1990s seeing this big bag of packages and I could see some of the addresses.



“I go, ‘What’s this about?’ He just said they were gifts for some friends he’d made out there. I knew he made trips to Asia in the mid-80s

“But it went on for years afterwards. Up until about 10, 15 years ago, he’d send gifts every Christmas.”



Thomas Jnr, who was his father’s carer for four years, added: “When we were talking about moving to the Philippines, I’d even joke, ‘Well gee Dad, how many relatives am I going to find in the Philippines that I don’t know about?’

“At some point I was like, ‘Why are you sending packages and gifts and toys back to these really good friends of yours from 30 years ago?’

“It was always a bit of a mystery, a loose end in my mind. But with everything that has happened over the past few months things start to look a lot different.”

Thomas Jnr also said his father would regularly give toys to an Asian family with young kids in his former home city, Los Angeles.



He said: “Two years in a row we delivered two big trash bags with toys. We’d drive up from Mexico to Hollywood. He would give them money also.

“I just thought my dad was being a nice guy — there was no reason to question any of it.”

Markle Jnr handed to police boxes of vile material he allegedly found in his father’s home in the Philippines.



And he pointed out that Barbie dolls were among his dad’s belongings in a lock-up near his former Mexican home in Rosarito.

It was also found to contain alleged evidence of child sex abuse material.

Markle Snr denies all claims against him.

News.title: Asylum seeker, 20, arrested on suspicion of flashing near controversial migrant camp
News.content:
Next

AN asylum seeker housed at a controversial migrant camp has been arrested on suspicion of flashing.

The Iranian male, 20, was detained on Tuesday after cops received an alert on the behaviour near Crowborough Training Camp in East Sussex.



He has been released on bail as the investigation continues.

Sussex Police confirmed the man had been arrested and appealed for more information amid their ongoing investigation.



The Home Office confirmed it is supporting the police probe but said it would be inappropriate to comment further.

It comes after The Sun revealed that small boat migrant Aref Sadeghi had been arrested at the notorious camp in June after it was discovered he is wanted for an alleged rape in Germany.

A recent ITV undercover investigation found the Iranian rape suspect, 36, was free to enjoy unrestricted access to the surrounding area because staff did not know about the allegations.

He is set to be extradited to Germany.

Another migrant housed at the site, in his 20s, was arrested in July on suspicion of possessing indecent images of children and remains on bail.

The opening of the asylum site in January led to huge demonstrations over fears up to 540 men would be free to come and go from the former military base.



Community interest group Crowborough Shield is also planning legal action against the Home Office for the way it moved in the migrants.

News.title: My 2-year legal fight to protect my teen daughter after biological male pupil was allowed in her school changing room
News.content:
Next

ANY parent of a teenage girl would loathe the thought of a biological male seeing their daughter undress.

And that was exactly the case for one father who discovered his daughter’s school had a policy of allowing boys who ­identify as female into the girls’ changing rooms and toilets.



Dad John, who is in his 40s, describes himself as a Labour-voting liberal, and mindful of those values when it came to raising his children.

When choosing a school for his daughter Sophie, he had been pleased to note that every form room at ­Dorothy Stringer School in Brighton displayed posters advertising “a gay children’s club” held at lunchtime.

He said: “At the time I looked at it and thought, ‘That’s great. They’re accepting of everybody. This seems the school for my daughter’.”



Last year, the Supreme Court ruled that the word “sex” in the Equality Act 2010 means biological sex rather than gender identity.

Before that ruling, many institutions — including schools, the NHS, government departments and large charities — had not been operating in line with the law, but rather with what critics called “Stonewall Law” — named after the hardline campaigning sex equality charity.

Under that interpretation, biological men and boys who identified as females were allowed to enter female-only spaces.

In January 2024, when the way that schools were dealing with gender- questioning children was in the news, John asked Sophie if she had ever seen a boy in her changing room.

She told him there had been a ­biological teenage boy, allowed by the school to identify as a girl, in the female toilets.



John recalled: “When she said yes, I was stunned.”

Sophie, then almost 14, had been at the school for more than two years and was going through puberty.

John said: “I wrote a very polite, ­formal email to the school, asking them whether this was true and what their policies were about allowing biological males into female spaces and vice versa.”



The school’s reply said such matters were decided on a “case-by-case” basis.

Dissatisfied, John decided to challenge further, and said: “This was about protecting my precious daughter.”

He asked how often male pupils had been allowed into the girls’ changing rooms.

The school refused to provide figures, citing confidentiality, repeated its “case-by-case” position and pointed to Brighton & Hove City Council’s Trans Inclusion Schools Toolkit, which backs social transition at schools without parental consent.

John believes the Toolkit played a major part in what happened at Dorothy Stringer School.



He said: “It encourages schools to allow mixed-sex use of toilets, changing rooms and sleeping accommodation on school trips.

“Making those decisions without telling the girls and families affected is a safeguarding failure. The council should withdraw it.”

John was also aware of the controversy surrounding the methods used at the Tavistock Gender Identity Development Service in London.

Referrals to the service, for under-18s, had risen sharply in recent years, and teenagers — mostly girls, and many of them autistic — were being affirmed as transgender merely at their own say-so.

The Tavistock centre was closed in 2024, shortly before publication of the Cass Review of Gender Identity Services for Children and Young People.



By the time of last year’s Supreme Court ruling, John had already made a formal safeguarding complaint against Dorothy Stringer School, which his daughter still attends.

But his requests for written ­assurances and a formal policy change have been resisted at every stage.

By law, every complaint like John’s in England must have a Local Authority Designated Officer, or LADO, appointed by the council to oversee how such concerns are handled.



But John says his LADO refused to give him any information about the safeguarding and risk assessment. He said: “It’s a conspiracy at local level. All the agencies that are supposed to exist to help, ignore you.”

He went to his ward councillors, who he said did initially enter into email conversation with him, but soon stopped replying.

He complained to his MP, Sian Berry, but said she was totally captured by the ideology, “as are most Greens, devoted to this nonsense”.

Last December, the school claimed that John’s complaints were “vexatious”, or without merit, and declared it would stop responding to them.

In January this year, the Department for Education declined to intervene, though its review of the case partially upheld John’s complaint.



By March, a judicial review had been launched. Citing the 2025 Supreme Court ruling, lawyers acting for John and his daughter argued that the school’s case-by-case policy was itself a safeguarding issue, as well as one of dignity and privacy for female students.

John said he encountered resistance at “every single step of the way” — but then, in September, the school did finally change its published policies.

All changing room signs were ­modified, and male and female toilets are now strictly segregated, with ­single-use unisex facilities available for gender-questioning children.



When the school announced its new policies, John and Sophie dropped their legal case, but he insisted his job “isn’t done yet”. He is convinced that the new rules for the changing rooms and toilets resulted from the pressure from his legal challenge.

Yet the school has never conceded that this had anything to do with it, nor that anything they have done has been illegal or against guidance.

John said: “I can’t believe the people who made these decisions are still in post, that the governors have not asked for an investigation, that some level of responsibility won’t be taken.

“And it seems that if I don’t hold their feet further to the fire, nothing will happen.

“I have restarted my complaint. I want to know who was responsible for this decision and how it was waved through by the governing body.”

In 2023, another parent, Janice, made a formal complaint against the same school after discovering that her daughter — autistic and suffering major trauma — had been allowed to present as a boy in classes.



Branded transphobic during the complaints process, Janice also learned that her daughter had been using a breast binder while under 16, which can cause breathing problems and bruised ribs.

In this case, the governors found no case to answer. Janice says that ­teachers “get away with converting children and putting them on a path to medicalisation”.

In her view, it took both the 2025 Supreme Court ruling and parental pressure before teachers were willing to take the safeguarding of vulnerable children seriously.

Sophie is now 16 and in her final year. John said: “It must have been tough for her.

She can’t tell friends she is behind this case because she’s afraid of being cancelled and of what people might say about her. But she is very proud of what she has achieved.



“The school explicitly teaches children to not question this ideology.

“They expressly teach them to say that trans women are women, and you shouldn’t question trans women in female spaces, and reading between the lines, you shouldn’t trust your own senses.”

John is grateful to parenting website Mumsnet and said: “It gave me an enormous amount of support and advice when I thought the whole thing was pointless.”

He believes there would be a much bigger uproar if more parents knew what was going on in so-called ­progressive, inclusive schools. He said: “We trust schools to look after our children and we assume that safeguarding and risk assessments are being carried out properly.

“But you pick up the lid and look underneath, and you go, ‘Oh no’.”



Susan Chynoweth of For Women Scotland — the campaign group that took the pivotal “sex” definition case to the Supreme Court last year — said: “We continue to see local authorities and public bodies drag their heels or, in some cases, outright flout the law.

“Not only are they playing with taxpayers’ money, in many cases they are playing with the lives of women and girls.”

Both Brighton Council and Dorothy Stringer School were approached for comment.

News.title: Tim Lovejoy update after Sunday Brunch absence sparks worries for ex-Soccer AM host
News.content:
Tim Lovejoy update after Sunday Brunch absence sparks worries for ex-Soccer AM host

Former Soccer AM host Tim Lovejoy hasn't appeared on Sunday Brunch for three weeks, sparking concern among viewers.

View 2 Images Tim Lovejoy has now missed three weeks of Sunday Brunch. (Image: Channel 4)

Channel 4 has provided an update on former football presenter Tim Lovejoy following his absence from Sunday Brunch. The television presenter, who hosted Soccer AM for 11 years, from 1996 to 2007, hasn’t appeared on the morning entertainment show for three consecutive weeks, sparking concern among viewers on social media.

‌



With Lovejoy said to be taking a ‘break’, Denise van Outen joined Simon Rimmer on the latest episode without any explanation. A spokesperson for Sunday Brunch has since told the Mirror: “Tim is taking a break from the show and that we look forward to welcoming him back soon.”

The 58-year-old hasn’t presented the show since November 1, which has raised eyebrows on X. One user wrote: “Sounds nuts but always felt a connection to Tim Lovejoy as born a day apart.

“The fact no one is saying why he is not on @SundayBrunchC4 is worrying. Hope he is OK.”

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Another wrote: “No Tim Lovejoy on #SundayBrunch again. [sad emoji] I hope he's alright.”

A third user even speculated that Lovejoy could be jetting off to Australia to go on ‘I'm a Celebrity... Get Me Out of Here’. They posted: “Going in the jungle!"

Lovejoy made a name for himself on Sky Sports, presenting Soccer AM alongside Helen Chamberlain. Together, they faced a must-watch show for football fans across the country ahead of the weekend’s action.

View 2 Images Lovejoy made a name for himself on the popular Soccer AM football show (Image: SKY SPORTS)

Speaking to talkSPORT back in September 2024, Lovejoy reflected on his time on the programme, which aired its last episode in May 2023.

He recalled: “It was the perfect storm, it was the 90s, it was Brit Pop and Oasis. Football was exploding and we were in the right place and the right time, it was just so much fun to do, I absolutely loved it.”

Although Lovejoy and Chamberlain had a blast on Soccer AM, he regrets his role in the ‘Soccerettes’ segment of the show, which usually featured a young woman wearing a football shirt, walking down a catwalk and being interviewed.

It was dropped in 2015, eight years before the show itself was cancelled. He said: “Don’t bring that up.

“I cringe about that. But it was a different time and we were told to push the boundaries.

“We were just doing different stuff and people had a laugh and a joke with it.”

News.title: Mum charges family £25 each for Christmas dinner - and even bought a card reader
News.content:
Mum charges family £25 each for Christmas dinner - and even bought a card reader

Whitney Ainscough, 33, expects to earn £130 by charging her own family £25 each for their Christmas dinner - despite the feast only costing her £40 to make

View 4 Images The mum has taken frugality to a new extreme (Image: Whitney Ainscough / SWNS)

A mum is charging her own family £25 each for their Christmas dinner - and has even bought a card reader to make sure nobody can dodge the bill.

‌



‌



Whitney Ainscough, 33, charged adults £20 each last year, with children paying £10, but has increased both prices by £5 ahead of this year's festive feast.

‌



The social media influencer, from Rotherham, expects to collect £130 in total, despite estimating that the meal will cost her just £40 to prepare - leaving her with a £90 profit.

‌



Whitney first began charging relatives for her cooking after she stopped working her job as a pharmacy advisor and was on Universal Credit, leaving her unable to afford to cook for her family as often as she would have liked.

To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

View 4 Images Whitney Ainscough tucks into her roast dinner (Image: Whitney Ainscough / SWNS)

‌



This Christmas, she plans to use two chickens instead of turkey, as "no one can tell the difference". The meal will be served with vegetables such as carrots and sprouts, which she will buy when they are being sold off cheap.

Whitney says her family see the price as "fair" and have no problem paying.

‌



"I definitely make money on Christmas Day; I'm not going to lie to you," she said. "It's a nice Christmas tip for me, doing all the cooking and preparing.

"My sister always says she never has cash, so last year I bought a card machine, so no one can get out of paying. If you go to a restaurant, it's going to cost you £50 a head, and cooking is very stressful, whilst everyone else gets to chill out, so why shouldn't I charge?"

‌



View 4 Images Whitney said the feast will cost around £40 in total (Image: Whitney Ainscough / SWNS)

Whitney often cooks Sunday lunch for her family, with younger members doing the washing up afterwards to "earn their chip ins". She said: "It is an amazing Sunday lunch. It's worth every penny; that’s why they come back.

‌



"Normally it’s roast potatoes, mashed potatoes, pigs in blankets, chicken or beef, pork crackling, Yorkshire puddings, air-fried sprouts, honey-glazed carrots and parsnips, peas and broccoli."

This year's feast will be served to nine people, costing around £40 in total. It marks the third year Whitney has charged for Christmas, having hosted in 2023 and 2025.

‌



View 4 Images The mum expects to make a £90 profit (Image: Whitney Ainscough / SWNS)

"It's just everyone chipping in – I'm cooking and everyone prefers my cooking," she said. "Everyone sees it as a win-win."

‌



Although Whitney doesn't charge her own children, 14, nine and three, they are made to wash up and do other chores around the house.

Having shared her plans to charge for Christmas dinner on social media, commentators online have had "mixed" reactions.

Article continues below

She said: "A lot of people are like, 'I wouldn't charge for my family', or, 'we take it in turns', but everyone likes my cooking; that's why I do it."

News.title: Vladimir Putin's £150million warship Merkury 'blown apart near Benghazi' after Ukraine sea drone attack
News.content:
Vladimir Putin's £150million warship Merkury 'blown apart near Benghazi' after Ukraine sea drone attack

A warship believed to be Russia's £150million corvette Merkury was reportedly destroyed off the coast of Libya in yet another blow to Vladimir Putin

Russian warship reportedly struck near Benghazi

A Russian warship thought to be worth £150million has been rocked by a huge explosion at a Libyan port, with dramatic footage capturing a fireball tearing through the vessel.

‌



‌



The blast ripped through the ship while it was anchored at the port of Benghazi, in what is being investigated as a possible drone attack. The vessel is believed to be Russia's £150m corvette Merkury, although the circumstances surrounding the explosion remain unclear.

‌



Two Libyan military officials said an initial investigation suggested the warship had been targeted by Ukrainian sea drones launched from a base operated by Kyiv's forces in western Libya.

‌



At least four drones were intercepted and destroyed, while two others struck the vessel, severely damaging it and sparking a fire at the naval facility, the officials said.

View 5 Images Witnesses reported hearing three huge blasts at the port of Benghazi

To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

‌



They were affiliated with the Libyan National Army, which controls eastern and southern Libya, and spoke anonymously as they were not authorised to brief reporters.

Footage circulating online shows massive flames engulfing the ship followed by clouds of smoke rising high above the Mediterranean port.

‌



The 344ft warship had reportedly been stationed in Benghazi for several days before the incident, according to Naval News. It was said to be escorting a convoy of Russian cargo vessels used to transport military supplies.

View 5 Images A satellite image shows a thick plume of smoke billowing from the vessel (Image: Satellite image Â©2026 Vantor vi)

‌



Satellite images showed thick plumes of smoke billowing from the vessel as it sat docked at the port on Sunday. It later appeared partially submerged.

The Merkury is a Project 20380 Steregushchiy-class corvette assigned to Russia's Black Sea Fleet although it has reportedly been operating from Northern Fleet bases. It was commissioned in 2023 and has a crew of around 90 sailors.

‌



The explosion happened about 1,300 miles from the frontline in Ukraine.

Libya's eastern-based government said an initial investigation had pointed to an explosion aboard a Russian vessel at Benghazi naval base. Officials said the ship had called at the port to refuel and take on supplies when travelling back.

‌



View 5 Images The ship docked at the Benghazi port before the strike (Image: Satellite image ©2026 Vantor/AFP via Getty Images)

A joint investigation with Russia has been launched to establish the circumstances of the attack and who was behind it, the government said.

‌



Witnesses described hearing three enormous blasts near the harbour before flames and debris were seen flying through the air, according to local outlet Ean Libya.

There were also reports of aircraft overhead and apparent anti-aircraft fire around the time of the incident.

‌



Tawfiq al-Shamekh, a spokesman for eastern Libya's emergency authorities, said firefighters had managed to bring the blaze under control. Investigators were continuing to examine what caused the explosion, he added.

Italian news agency Agenzia Nova reported that either a Russian military vessel or its cargo could have been the target of an aerial attack.

‌



View 5 Images A view of the capsized ship after it was hit (Image: Satellite image ©2026 Vantor/AFP via Getty Images)

Local media also reported a separate sea drone strike on a Maltese-flagged commercial vessel of Benghazi on Sunday evening. Libyan forces reportedly destroyed at least 12 other sea drones near the city.

‌



The incident comes amid growing pressure on Russian shipping, after another vessel linked to Putin's military was struck by drones in the Gulf of Finland.

The sanctioned cargo ship Sparta II was hit by two drones on Saturday and was still ablaze in Finnish waters the next morning.

‌



The strike coincided with a huge Ukrainian drone attack on Russia's Leningrad region, which borders NATO members Finland and Estonia.

View 5 Images The ship had reportedly been stationed in Benghazi for several days

‌



However, Kyiv has not claimed responsibility for the attack on the cargo ship and there is no evidence linking Ukrainian forces to the incident.

Last year, Kyiv said it had attacked a Russian shadow fleet tanker off the Libyan coast, around 1,250 miles from Ukrainian territory.

Article continues below

More recently, Libyan officials said Ukrainian forces operating from bases in western Libya struck another Russian tanker near Maltese waters in March in a suspected sea drone attack.

It also comes just days after Ukrainian strikes caused serious damage to Russia's strategically important Crimean Bridge, a major transport link between the Russian mainland and the occupied peninsula.

News.title: Tragic cause of Mariella's 'controlling' behaviour in I'm A Celeb jungle as pals speak out
News.content:
Tragic cause of Mariella's 'controlling' behaviour in I'm A Celeb jungle as pals speak out

EXCLUSIVE: Friends have defended Mariella Frostrup's conduct in the I'm A Celeb kitchen, and suggested a reason for why she is so 'controlling' around the campfire

View 5 Images Mariella has come under fire but friends are fighting back (Image: ITV)

Mariella Frostrup's "controlling" nature when it comes to cooking may stem from her chaotic childhood in which food was scarce, friends claim.

‌



‌



The 64-year-old's behaviour as camp chef has come under the spotlight after bust-ups with both Joanna Page and AJ Odudu. The latter was reduced to tears.

‌



But friends have launched a defence of the broadcaster suggesting it could stem from her impoverished upbringing in which her family often went hungry. It comes as Mariella was embroiled in more rows on the ITV show tonight after accusing AJ of being "aggressive" which the Big Brother star found "triggering." But Mariella's friend said: "People are being very quick to judge Mariella, but there's a reason she likes to be in control, particularly when it comes to food.

‌



To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

View 5 Images Mariella experienced difficult hardship as a child (Image: Tim Merry/Staff Photographer)

"She grew up in a household where there wasn't always enough to eat and where things could be incredibly chaotic. She's never forgotten that. When you've experienced that sort of insecurity as a child, it's hardly surprising that you want to make sure everyone is fed and things are done properly. That doesn't mean she always gets it right but there's a lot more to Mariella than people are seeing on television."

‌



Mariella has previously revealed how she watched her mother break down because there was only dried spaghetti and golden syrup in the cupboard.

Mariella, who was eight at the time, said: "So we sat down at the table and treated it as a proper dinner. Psychologically, I think that was important, because when things are really bad there isn’t room to make a fuss." But she added: "When you've tasted poverty like that, you don't forget it."

‌



View 5 Images Mariella, Joanne and AJ have all come to blows (Image: ITV/Shutterstock)

In 2016, she also told how she was left to fend for herself after moving in with her alcoholic father aged 13 after her parents' divorce. She said: "He and I were living alone in a rented house in Dublin, and I was trying to go to school, and the house was just a tip, the kitchen was a disaster.

‌



"He was very depressed, he had slightly lost the will to live." She added: "I was horribly bossy, and I am to this day. Controlling. I don't know how much of it was already in me."

Her friends' defence comes as her behaviour around the campfire continues to cause friction among the celebrities. Mariella became irritated when AJ, 38, offered suggestions about preparing dinner, later complaining in the Bush Telegraph: "I would never go into someone's kitchen and start telling them what to do when they were making me dinner. There's a reason there aren't very many chef duos."

‌



View 5 Images Joanna Page was left distraught after clashing with Mariella (Image: ITV)

The pair were subsequently appointed joint camp chefs by Wayne Rooney, despite their disagreements. But tensions escalated after AJ used the remaining rice while preparing breakfast and lunch, leaving none for the evening meal.

‌



AJ later became tearful, saying: "I was trying to, I don’t know, make friends… and I’m feeling resistance, which doesn't feel nice." Gavin & Stacey actress Joanna Page had previously become frustrated with Mariella's instructions around the campfire. "Oh my God… this is doing my head in. I cannot listen to Mariella's voice any more," she complained, before storming off.

Mariella previously revealed her children had warned her against getting drawn into arguments with her fellow campmates, urging her to let things go. The broadcaster, who shares daughter Molly, 22, and son Dan, 21, with human rights lawyer husband Jason McCue, told the Mirror: "I know that that was the thing that my kids were most fearful of.

‌



View 5 Images AJ's celeb fans are furious about her treatment in the jungle (Image: Photo by ITV/Shutterstock)

"They were like, 'Mum, just let it go. Whatever it is, just let it go.' OK, I'll try. That's not my special skill. I don't like arguing. I think that disagreeing agreeably, you know, is a really important life skill." She also admitted she wanted to 'come out with my credibility intact'.

‌



Last night ITV insiders refused to be drawn on whether they carried out any welfare checks on AJ Odudu after her tears in camp. One source said only that all the campmates were monitored 24/7 by producers.

But AJ's celebs fans are furious at her treatment in camp. Presenter Melvin Odoom, who was in the jungle two years ago, said on social media: "AJ is a person who loves cooking for people and was just trying to help.

Article continues below

"It's such a shame Mariella found it so hard to cook in pairs. Last night she pretty much said they are cooking for survival (which can feel like the case in there) but it’s also about working as a team."

News.title: Psychologist's five-minute technique 'makes you fall asleep faster'
News.content:
Psychologist's five-minute technique 'makes you fall asleep faster'

Roughly one in three people in the UK struggle with sleep or insomnia

Doctors explains 'worst ever' sleeping position that causes illness

Struggling to sleep? A psychologist has shared a simple five-minute technique that she says could help you fall asleep faster.

‌



‌



Dr Ritz Birah, consultant counselling psychologist at Panda London, has explained how a quick bedtime brain dump can help park worries, clear your mind and take the pressure out of falling asleep. Dr Ritz Birah (Ritika Suk Birah) is an HCPC-registered Consultant Counselling Psychologist who serves on the Sleep Expert Panel at Panda London, advising on sleep habits, brain health, and wellbeing.

‌



She says that when people are struggling to sleep, the instinct is often to try harder. But she says that psychologically, that effort can sometimes become part of the problem. To help struggling Brits, Dr Ritz Birah has shared four techniques to take some of the pressure out of sleep, with one taking just five minutes.

‌



1. The 5-minute “park it” technique

Dr Ritz Birah says that one of the most counterintuitive things you can do at bedtime is give yourself permission not to solve anything. She says our brains often use the first quiet moment of the day to surface everything we have not yet processed: tomorrow's tasks, something somebody said, the conversation we need to have, or the thing we are worried we might forget.

Sleep expert shares top tips on how to set up bedroom to get the best night's sleep

She explained: "Try a five-minute bedtime brain dump. Keep a notebook beside the bed and use a simple ‘park it’ technique. Write down the tasks or worries on your mind, then note one next step for tomorrow. You are telling the brain: I have captured this, I know what I am going to do about it, and I do not need to keep rehearsing it tonight.

‌



"Sometimes the best way to quieten a busy brain is not to tell it to stop thinking, but to reassure it that nothing important is being forgotten."

2. Try to stay awake

Dr Ritz explains: "This might seem like the last thing you should do when you’re struggling to sleep, but rather than forcing yourself to fall asleep, deliberately allow yourself to stay awake instead. This is the principle behind a psychological technique known as paradoxical intention."

‌



She added: "When we start thinking, ‘I have to sleep now’, sleep can begin to feel like a task we have to perform. That pressure creates frustration and alertness, which are exactly the opposite of what we need."

Instead, allow yourself to lie quietly without trying to make sleep happen, she recommends. Don’t check the clock or calculate how much sleep you have left.

‌



"If sleepiness arrives, let it," she said. "The aim isn’t to stay awake all night, it is to remove some of the performance anxiety around falling asleep."

Ensure our latest headlines always appear at the top of your Google Search by making us a Preferred Source. Click here to activate or add us as a Preferred Source in your Google search settings.

‌



View Image About 1 in 3 people in the UK experience trouble getting to sleep or staying asleep

3. Give your brain something random to think about

If your mind becomes busy at bedtime, cognitive shuffle offers an alternative to trying to empty it completely. The technique involves moving your attention between unrelated, neutral objects or images, such as picturing a book, then a banana, then a bicycle.

‌



She said: "Trying to force the mind to go blank can become another form of effort. Instead, cognitive shuffling gives the brain just enough to focus on without creating a storyline, problem to solve or emotionally loaded train of thought. I particularly like this technique for people whose minds immediately jump into planning mode when their head hits the pillow."

4. Get out of bed when you can't sleep

When you’re struggling to sleep, getting out of a warm bed can feel completely counterproductive, but lying there becoming increasingly frustrated can teach the brain that bed is somewhere we stay awake and worry, Dr Ritz Birah said.

Article continues below

"This is why stimulus control is used within CBT for insomnia," she said. "If you have been awake for a while and feel yourself becoming frustrated or increasingly alert, get up and do something quiet in low light, such as reading a few pages of a book or listening to something calming.

"Then return to bed when you notice yourself becoming sleepy again. You are helping to rebuild the association between getting into bed and actually sleeping."

News.title: NHS doctor says 'unexplained' symptom could be prostate cancer sign as UK cases rise
News.content:
NHS doctor says 'unexplained' symptom could be prostate cancer sign as UK cases rise

Dr Jeff Foster, an NHS GP Partner and men's health specialist, has outlined the key warning signs all men should be aware of

View 3 Images Back pain can be a later sign (Image: Halfpoint Images via Getty Images)

New figures from Macmillan Cancer Support reveal that prostate cancer cases are climbing across the UK, with more than 68,000 men receiving a diagnosis each year — equivalent to one every eight minutes. UK Google searches for 'signs of prostate cancer' have rocketed by 235% in the past month alone, suggesting a surge in public awareness around spotting the warning signs and understanding prostate health.

‌



‌



A recent survey by Voy found that two in five men (40%) admit to having previously put off visiting a doctor about a health concern. In support of Men's Health Awareness Month throughout November, Dr Jeff Foster, NHS GP Partner and director of men's health and testosterone replacement therapy (TRT) specialist at Voy, has highlighted the crucial warning signs every man should know, while cautioning that the disease is frequently completely symptomless in its earliest stages.

‌



Vibrating mattress fights Alzheimer's, engineered cells crush brain tumours, stroke treatment breakthrough, and chewing gum beats cancer - all this and more in our science newsletter

‌



Three warning signs of prostate cancer men need to be aware of

While prostate cancer typically shows no symptoms in its earliest stages, Dr Foster pinpointed the key signs and changes men should never dismiss.

View 3 Images A doctor has given advice (stock picture) (Image: Lacheev via Getty Images)

New-onset urinary changes

Noticeable changes that have developed recently rather than gradually over decades, such as:

‌



Needing to urinate more frequently, especially during the night

A weak, slow, or interrupted stream

Difficulty starting or stopping urination

Straining, or feeling as though the bladder hasn’t completely emptied

Blood in the urine or semen

While less common, this requires prompt investigation by a GP.

‌



Ensure our latest headlines always appear at the top of your Google Search by making us a Preferred Source. Click here to activate or add us as a Preferred Source in your Google search settings.

Signs of more advanced disease

Persistent, unexplained bone or deep pain in the lower back, hips, or pelvis; unintended weight loss or unexplained, ongoing fatigue.

‌



Dr Foster said: "The difficult truth about prostate cancer is that in its early stages, it very often presents no symptoms at all. That is what makes it so dangerous and why awareness matters so much.

"Because the prostate sits just below the bladder and surrounds the urethra, urinary function is usually where men first notice that something has changed. But by the time symptoms become noticeable enough to prompt a GP visit, the disease may already have been developing for some time.

‌



"The important thing to remember is that these symptoms are not unique to prostate cancer. Benign prostate enlargement is very common, non-cancerous, and causes many of the exact same urinary changes. However, that is not a reason to dismiss new changes, it is precisely why you should get checked.

"Crucially, the absence of symptoms is not reassurance. Proactive conversations with your doctor based on individual risk are essential. For most men, age 50 is when prostate health should move to an active discussion with a GP. But for men with an elevated risk, that conversation should start at 45, 40, or even earlier.

‌



"If you are Black, if your father or brother has had prostate cancer, or if you have multiple relatives who have been affected, do not wait for symptoms or a milestone birthday to speak to your doctor."

Doctor explains relationship between testosterone and prostate health

With Google searches for 'prostate cancer and testosterone levels' rising by 335% over the past year, Dr Foster revealed what men should understand about testosterone levels, testosterone replacement therapy (TRT) and prostate cancer.

‌



Dr Foster said: "As a GP specialising in men's health, one of the most persistent misunderstandings I come across in men's health is that testosterone replacement therapy (TRT) can cause prostate cancer. This concern has shaped clinical practice for decades and has stopped many men seeking the testosterone treatments they need.

"Recent studies, such as the TRAVERSE trial, one of the largest and most rigorous studies of testosterone replacement therapy to date, have disproved this belief. The TRAVERSE trial found that men receiving testosterone replacement therapy (TRT) were at no increased risk of prostate cancer.

‌



"However, while testosterone does not cause prostate cancer, it can accelerate the growth of pre-existing cancer cells if the disease is already present in the body. This is why screening before starting TRT is not optional-it is essential. The PSA test and a clinical assessment prior to treatment are standard practice, and rightly so. But the belief that testosterone itself initiates prostate cancer in otherwise healthy men is not supported by current evidence. At VOY, we always screen for prostate cancer before treatment begins, and continue to check at every monitoring blood test throughout your care."

View 3 Images Exercise is recommended (Image: Maskot via Getty Images)

Article continues below

Lifestyle changes men should consider

Dr Foster said: "There is not much evidence to support that lifestyle changes improve prostate cancer, however, there are consistent patterns worth following. Maintaining a healthy body weight matters: obesity is associated with more aggressive forms of prostate cancer.

"Regular exercise, 45 minutes of meaningful activity three to four times a week, is associated with better outcomes across a range of cancers, and prostate is no exception. Diet plays a role too: diets high in processed meat and saturated fat appear to increase risk, while a Mediterranean-style diet with plenty of vegetables, legumes, and oily fish is broadly associated with reduced risk."

News.title: Pharmacist issues 'ask your GP' Mounjaro warning to parents of teenagers
News.content:
Pharmacist issues 'ask your GP' Mounjaro warning to parents of teenagers

A new study has put the weight-loss injection in the spotlight, but a TikTok pharmacist says there is more parents need to understand

View 2 Images Around 2.6 million adults in Great Britain use GLP-1 weight-loss medications (Image: Nikos Pekiaridis/NurPhoto)

Weight-loss medication continues to create plenty of discussion, but now its potential use among children and young people is under the spotlight. Pharmacist Raj Patel, known as the Straight Talking Pharmacist to his more than 100,000 followers on TikTok, has issued a warning to parents about what the latest research means for their teenagers.

‌



‌



The medical professional turned content creator discussed a clinical trial involving teenagers with obesity, as well as some young people who were overweight and had a related health problem. The study examined tirzepatide, the active ingredient in Mounjaro, alongside support with diet and physical activity.

‌



Published in JAMA in November, the Lilly-funded trial followed 160 young people for 72 weeks. Researchers found average BMI fell by 18.5 per cent among those receiving tirzepatide, compared with a 0.5 per cent increase in the placebo group.

‌



View 2 Images Weight loss jabs are popularly used across the UK (Image: Getty Images)

BMI is a measurement based on a person's weight in relation to their height, and a percentage change in BMI should not be confused with the same percentage change in body weight. The trial also found that 10 of the 108 participants who received tirzepatide stopped treatment because of adverse effects, equivalent to around one in 11.

‌



There is also an important distinction between the trial results and what is currently authorised in the UK. Mounjaro is licensed for treating type 2 diabetes in children and teenagers aged 10 and over, but its product information says its safety and effectiveness for weight management have not been established in people under 18.

Ensure our latest Health headlines always appear at the top of your Google Search by making us a Preferred Source. Click here to activate or add us as Preferred Source in your Google search settings

‌



Mr Patel warned parents against assuming the research means the injection is now an approved weight-loss option for teenagers: "Mounjaro isn't licenced in the UK for weight management under 18 year olds and the trial result is not the same as a new licence."

Article continues below

The NHS advises parents who are concerned about a child's weight to speak to their GP, school nurse or practice nurse, who can offer support with diet and lifestyle changes. The pharmacist also urged families to seek professional advice rather than sharing medication, saying: "And if you're worried about your teenager's weight ask your GP what is available and please don't ever share injections."

The trial provides new evidence about tirzepatide in adolescents, but it does not change the current UK position on its use for weight management in under-18s.

News.title: 'Avoid eating four foods' warning to Wegovy and Mounjaro users over side effects
News.content:
'Avoid eating four foods' warning to Wegovy and Mounjaro users over side effects

Experts urge GLP-1 users to avoid these foods to reduce common side effects, including stomach upset and nausea

View 2 Images GP urges GLP-1 users to avoid these 5 foods to prevent common side effects (Image: Getty)

As millions of Brits turn to popular weight loss medications such as Wegovy and Mounjaro, a leading GP has issued a warning to help users avoid painful digestive side effects ahead of the Christmas period. Dr Ann Nainan cautions that indulging in high-fat, sugary, or ultra-processed foods can exacerbate common GLP-1 side effects.

‌



‌



She warns that common side effects include nausea, acid reflux, and stomach discomfort. She says eating such foods could overwhelm a digestive system already slowed down by the treatment.

‌



Dr Ann Nainan, GP at online weight-loss clinic Medicspot , has shared advice to help Brits taking weight-loss medications understand which foods to avoid for optimal results. "According to a Food Foundation survey, over 8 million Brits have taken or are taking weight loss medications, which highlights how popular drugs such as Wegovy and Mounjaro are," she said.

‌



"While weight loss medications can help people lose weight and live a healthier life, they need to be taken alongside regular exercise and a balanced diet to make them work to their full potential. While all foods can be enjoyed in moderation, opting for meals that are high in fat, sugar and processed foods while taking weight loss medications can hinder results and worsen symptoms such as nausea and vomiting, which are common Wegovy side effects."

She added: "With that in mind, it’s important to understand the foods to limit on weight loss medications, especially over the Christmas period, when people tend to relax their diets." Below are five foods she urges people to limit on weight loss medications.

View 2 Images Ultra-processed foods can exacerbate common GLP-1 side effects

‌



1. Ultra-processed foods

"Food items such as crisps, biscuits and cakes are often seen as convenient, especially for those living busy lives," the health expert said. "However, these snacks are often high in calories and contain next to no protein.

"GLP-1s slow how fast the stomach empties, meaning you’re more likely to experience side effects such as acid reflux and blood sugar swings if consuming these foods regularly and in large volumes."

‌



2. Fried and greasy foods

Dr Ann said: "It’s normal to enjoy foods including fried chicken, pizza and burgers, but it’s important to limit them when taking GLP-1s. Foods with high fat and grease content stay in the stomach for longer, and as GLP-1s cause delayed digestion, you’re at risk of nausea and stomach upset."

Ensure our latest headlines always appear at the top of your Google Search by making us a Preferred Source. Click here to activate or add us as Preferred Source in your Google search settings.

‌



3. Sugary foods

The expert added: "As Christmas approaches, people are more likely to indulge in sweets, chocolate and fizzy drinks, which are known for being high in sugar. The main issue for GLP-1 users who consume large amounts of sugary foods is that they can cause rapid blood sugar fluctuations, which can lead to fatigue and worsening side effects."

‌



4. High-fat foods and meats

The doctor said: "Most people see all meats as a source of protein and are therefore good for you. While true to an extent, fatty cuts of meat such as sausages and bacon could overwhelm the digestive system. The same can be said for other fatty foods, such as butter and cream, which can have the same effect, leading to GLP-1 users experiencing diarrhea and stomach upset. Naturally, this can vary from person to person."

Weight loss jabs could disrupt other medications

‌



What about alcohol?

"While the winter months and the Christmas period are often the most popular times for people to enjoy a glass of their favourite tipple, moderation is key, the GP said. "Alcoholic drinks such as beer, wine and spirits are classed as empty calories, and can be extremely gassy.

"The points mentioned are worsened for GLP-1 users, leading to bloating and stomach discomfort." Excessive drinking can also make dehydration more likely, so remember to stick to the government guidelines on alcohol.

‌



Final tips

For examples of practical tips on what to limit and swap in, see Healthline and Semapen. Most people tolerate smaller, slower meals built around lean proteins (such as chicken, fish, eggs, or tofu), cooked vegetables, whole grains, and regular water intake.

Dr Nainan concludes by sharing the best foods to eat when taking GLP-1s: "For those taking weight loss medications, it’s important to prioritise a balanced diet that includes lean protein like chicken, eggs and turkey, paired with complex carbs such as whole grains, oats and vegetables. It’s also important to keep yourself well hydrated.

Article continues below

"Alongside promoting weight loss, these foods will also keep the stomach and digestive system more settled, reducing the chances of experiencing side effects such as nausea and vomiting. Finally, no matter how healthy your meal may be, it’s essential to keep portions small and regular, eat slowly, and stop when you feel full. Large meals can lead to discomfort and worsening nausea."

News.title: Boss of British Gas owner Centrica 'hugely concerned' over impact of soaring energy bills
News.content:
The boss of British Gas owner Centrica says he is "hugely concerned" about the impact the expected jump in energy bills in January will have on consumers.

Chris O'Shea told the BBC he thought the number of people unable or unwilling to pay their energy bills would rise when prices go up in the new year.

The new energy price cap to take effect from January will be announced on Wednesday and consultancy Cornwall Insight has forecast it will jump by Â£443 a year for a typical household.

The government has said some households will get Â£100 to help with energy bills, but Citizens Advice said it was a "drop in the ocean" while one pressure group called for action on "inflated energy firm profits".

Speaking to the Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg programme, O'Shea said the predictions for a "substantial increase" in bills from January were "materially correct", adding that the first quarter of the year was the time when most energy was consumed.

"That's right at the point where people will be paying for Christmas and the like. So I am hugely concerned," he said.

O'Shea added there was a "massive problem" with people not paying their bills in the UK, with some not able to pay their bills and an "increasing number of people that are choosing not to pay their bills".

He said the collective impact of that was that "every single electricity consumer, is paying about Â£1.50, Â£1.60 a week to cover the cost of people that are not paying their bills, and it's just going to get worse when bills go up".

The amount owed to energy suppliers by households hit Â£5bn in the April to June period, according to energy regulator Ofgem.

News.title: RAF's next fighter jet could be last crewed combat plane, air chief says
News.content:
Britain's next-generation fighter jet could be the last crewed combat aircraft the UK builds, the head of the RAF has said.

Air Chief Marshal Sir Harv Smyth, said Artificial Intelligence (AI) enabled, uncrewed aircraft would "transform military aviation".

His comments refer to the Global Combat Air Programme (GCAP), a partnership between the UK, Italy and Japan to develop a sixth-generation fighter jet, expected to enter service by 2035.

The aircraft, commonly known as Tempest, is expected to provide speed stealth, use advanced sensors and even AI to assist the human pilot when they are overwhelmed, or under extreme stress.

Writing in the Telegraph, external, Sir Harv said the GCAP aircraft was "perhaps the last crewed fighter we will ever build", not because people would become less important, but because advances in technology were changing the nature of air combat.

He said AI and machines would take on "the most dangerous tasks instead of humans", while stressing that technology should enhance human judgement and "not replace accountability". He added: "Uncrewed fighter jets will start flying in UK airspace next year. This is exciting and necessary in equal measure."

Sir Harv also said the RAF of the future would combine Typhoons and F-35s with autonomous systems.

The programme was announced in 2022 by the UK, Italy and Japan, which are jointly developing the aircraft. In July, the three countries signed a Â£4.6bn contract covering the next phase of its design through industry joint venture Edgewing.

According to GCAP, the aircraft will be powered by advanced data processing and artificial intelligence, while also featuring enhanced stealth technology. The UK government says the project already supports 3,500 jobs and 1,000 apprenticeships.

Canada was granted "observer nation" status in July, giving it privileged access to the programme without a decision-making role.

In October, Prime Minister, Andy Burnham, said the UK government would "seek to progress" Germany joining GCAP. He said the partnership could also support cooperation on issues including "countering hybrid attacks" and "countering interference in our democratic processes".

News.title: Russell Brand's wife says she'll honour prison rules after message row
News.content:
The wife of disgraced comedian Russell Brand says she will "honour" the rules of his prison, a week after she read a message from her husband proclaiming his innocence.

Laura Brand, 39, drew criticism from ministers after reading out the message from inside HMP Littlehey last week, prompting the government to seek to have the episode removed from social media platforms.

She said on Sunday that she would continue to defend her family and herself over her portrayal in the media during the couple's weekly podcast, which she now presents alone.

Russell Brand, 51, is currently serving a 10-and-half-year prison sentence after being convicted of rape and three counts of sexual assault.

"Last week's episode drew a considerable amount of attention," Laura Brand said during this week's episode of Sunday Service.

"Now that I understand the parameters set by the brilliant and professional staff at HMP Littlehey, I will absolutely honour that."

In the relayed message last week, Russell Brand had said he was "not guilty of the offences I have been jailed for".

Laura Brand said she had spoken to him at the Cambridgeshire prison and said he was "OK".

Russell Brand was found guilty of raping a woman at his home in 2009, as well as three counts of sexual assault against three other women.

Further allegations have since been reported about him and some have called for consent laws to be revised.

His conviction has renewed conversation about safeguarding in the media industry, and whether some celebrities are still able to use their fame to prey on women and then silence them.

Ministers have pointed out that inmates are prohibited from making statements that are likely to cause their victims distress and have said Brand's message was being investigated.

A woman who alleges she was raped by Brand when she was 16, but who was not among the women whose accusations led to his conviction, said his prison message was "upsetting" and "really shocking".

The government attempted to have the podcast removed from YouTube, but this was refused by its owner Google. Prime Minister Andy Burnham urged social media companies to "show some decency and take these videos down".

On Sunday, Laura Brand also said that Sunday Service would be a place where she would "continue to be proud to be a wife, a mother and a woman defending her family at a time when the media's image of what kind of a woman I am is under so much scrutiny".

She expressed feeling a mixture of "grief", "absence", "desolation" and "loneliness" since her husband's imprisonment.

News.title: BBC apologises after noise disruption during Strictly
News.content:
A recording of sex noises appeared to be playing from the audience during the filming of Strictly Come Dancing in Blackpool on Saturday.

Judge Motsi Mabuse was giving feedback to Delta Goodrem when she paused after the sound started playing.

At the end of the programme, presenter Emma Willis apologised to viewers "if you heard any audio disruptions".

A BBC spokesperson also issued an apology and said it was "investigating how this happened".

BBC journalist Simon Jones has this report.

Read more about the incident during Strictly Come Dancing in Blackpool.

News.title: Miley Cyrus marries Maxx Morando in California ceremony
News.content:
Miley Cyrus has married her partner of four years Maxx Morando during a ceremony in Palm Springs, California.

A string of black and white photos shared by the Flowers singer on Instagram showed the pair kissing while surrounded by white roses.

Her mother, Trisha Cyrus, and sister, Noah Cyrus, could be seen in the background of one image. Her father Billy Ray Cyrus was not in the picture but was at the ceremony with his partner, actress Liz Hurley.

Grammy-winning Cyrus, 33, wore a white silk dress designed by Anthony Vaccarello for Saint Laurent, while 28-year-old drummer Morando said "I do" in a black suit from the same fashion house.

In one of the photographs, which was the first in a series of images shared by the singer in an Instagram post, the newly weds posed next to a golden retriever.

The post was captioned with "M+M" followed by a white heart and the ceremony date, 21 November.

Miley's sister Brandi Cyrus, singer Doechii and fashion designer Donatella Versace were among those to congratulate the couple in the comments.

The ceremony reportedly took place at a resort formerly owned by Fly Me To The Moon singer Frank Sinatra.

Guests stuck to an all-black dress code, according to reports.

News.title: Verstappen wins extraordinary Las Vegas Grand Prix as Ferraris collide
News.content:
Red Bull's Max Verstappen won an extraordinary Las Vegas Grand Prix that featured 34 lead changes in a non-stop battle at the front.

The leading group of 10 cars were tied together for the vast majority of the race as the lead constantly changed hands between Verstappen and the Mercedes drivers George Russell and Kimi Antonelli.

But Verstappen was the one constant, always seeming a step ahead of his rivals as he debated electrical energy deployment strategy with his team.

And in the final laps Mercedes' challenge unravelled as first Russell made a mistake and crashed trying to pass Antonelli, and the Italian lost out to the two McLarens of Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri going into the final lap.

The world champion dropped to fifth going on to the Strip on the last lap but was able to reclaim the place from Alpine's Pierre Gasly at the end of the long straight.

And there was more drama at Ferrari as Charles Leclerc earned a 10-second penalty for tipping Lewis Hamilton into a spin.

Earlier, Hamilton had been given a 10-second penalty of his own for passing Norris off the track in a fight for position that also involved Leclerc.

It was a grand prix more reminiscent of American oval racing than Formula 1, and it depended on unique circumstances revolving around the Las Vegas circuit and energy-starved hybrid engines this year.

But there was no questioning the showbiz value in the city that prides itself as the entertainment capital of the world.

The key stories of an engrossing race were:

News.title: 'Move on!' Former PMs pile in with advice for Andy Burnham, but will he listen?
News.content:
"Move on!" That's Theresa May's frank instruction to Andy Burnham.

She spent years wrangling with the EU to try to forge a decent Brexit deal before being shoved out of her job by her party. Her leadership was broken by Britain's relationship with Brussels. Now she is warning the current resident of No 10 not to risk the same.

In a rare interview, Baroness May - who presided over negotiations with the EU between 2016 and 2019 - told me Burnham ought to respect the public's decision 10 years ago, not "pat them on their head" as if they gave the wrong answer and should have "another go".

And she said she was "aghast" at what he was doing, dangling the possibility of rejoining the EU, warning it would absorb huge amounts of government effort.

"The hours that have to be put in, it's across the whole of government," she said. "It's not just prime ministerial time, [it's] cabinet ministers' time, officials' time, to-ing and fro-ing on those negotiations."

But while some on his own side are very keen to get on with a campaign to rejoin the EU - and the foreign secretary tells me this option is on the table - May is not the only voice urging caution.

Earlier this month David Cameron also said starting a conversation about rejoining would be "long and painful".

And former Prime Minister Sir Tony Blair has told the Sunday Times this weekend that Britain should only rejoin the European Union if it reforms and allows more innovation on technology.

News.title: Why Nicola Coughlan's new drama might leave viewers uncomfortable
News.content:
Filming the series without a script meant the actors were fully immersed in their characters, making them real not just for viewers but for themselves too.

"I'm not playing myself, but there's far less, let's say 'character' here than anything else I've ever done because a lot of this is about just reacting," Coughlan says.

She and Cole would film long takes, some lasting about an hour and often with heated exchanges, which might need to be shot multiple times.

Coughlan describes I Am Helen as "the most challenging thing in terms of material that I've ever worked on", adding for the first time in a role she needed counselling.

"You literally would be physically and mentally quite exhausted," she says.

"There were times that I said to Dominic [Savage] if he wanted to do a third take for example - and I've never said this before on set - but I actually don't think I have that in me because you hit a wall.

"It's a lot to keep going."

Cole agrees that "it was tough".

"When you're given that freedom, things happen and I think you can get some really interesting and also quite shocking stuff," he says.

For him, that came when he damaged a fridge on set with a punch.

But it's that authenticity of emotion which, while difficult for the actors, is what Coughlan thinks makes the series so engaging.

"When people watch the 'I Ams', they feel quite truthful," she says.

"I think that's a big reason as to why, to be honest."

News.title: Theresa May 'aghast' at Burnham's EU plans and says 'Brexit is done'
News.content:
Former Prime Minister Theresa May has warned Andy Burnham he should "move on" from Brexit, telling the BBC she is "aghast" the prime minister could be considering rejoining the EU.

At the Brussels summit this week the PM said he wanted to "brainstorm" options for the future relationship between Britain and the trading bloc.

In an exclusive interview with the BBC's Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg, Baroness May, who spent three years negotiating an EU exit deal, said: "Brexit is done. Just accept Brexit and move on."
