May claimed Burnham "wants to pat people on the head" by suggesting: "Remember that vote? Well, you got it wrong, didn't you. So have another go and come out with the right answer."

May, who was prime minister between 2016 and 2019 urged Burnham to "just get on with" today's challenges rather than re-opening the conversation around being in the European Union.

Before becoming PM she had campaigned to stay in the EU, but when in No 10 she presided over three years of tortuous negotiations.

The deal she concluded was rejected by MPs. She was forced to quit and was replaced by Boris Johnson in 2019.

Telling Burnham to "move on", she said: "What I saw was that the extent of those negotiations, the hours that have to be put in - it's across the whole of government.

"It's not just prime ministerial time, cabinet ministers' time, officials' time, to-ing and fro-ing on those negotiations. Because you have to negotiate hard in order to make sure that you're getting out what you want.

"And that's one of the reasons why I look slightly aghast at what Andy Burnham is talking about, further negotiations of going into the EU. And also we, as a country, we voted for Brexit.

"When I was prime minister I was very clear, we should deliver on that vote. So I'm afraid my message to him really is, you know, people voted for Brexit. Brexit is done. Just accept Brexit and move on."

Warning against another vote, May told the BBC's Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg: "I almost think this is what Andy Burnham is saying to the British people, sort of patting them on the head.

"He wants to pat them on their head and say, you know what, remember that vote? Well, you got it wrong, didn't you? So have another go and come out with the right answer.

"Or what he thinks is the right answer. But as I say, let's just get on with making sure the UK is as strong economically, in security terms, and in terms of opportunities for people as it can be."

Speaking to the BBC back in 2023, she said the UK "would have been better off if MPs had backed her deal to leave the European Union".

Her deal had included the prospect of a vote on holding a second referendum, and a vote on a temporary customs union, as well as promises on workers' rights and environmental protection.

May claimed her plan was thwarted by "hardline" Brexit-supporting MPs and those who wanted to remain in the EU.

News.title: Tories would scrap Burnham's deal with EU, deputy leader says
News.content:
Conservative deputy leader Alex Burghart has said his party would scrap the deal agreed between the UK and the European Union on Friday, if the Tories win the next general election.

The agreement signed by Prime Minister Andy Burnham covers a youth travel scheme, emissions trading and British food exports.

The government has argued scrapping most checks on British food exports will cut costs for businesses and could bring down prices for shoppers.

Burghart told the BBC's Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg programme the deal was "a dog's dinner", which would not lead to lower prices in the shops and would mean the UK "gives up our ability to set our own rules".

Under the agreement, the UK will also have to follow some EU regulations.

Burghart acknowledged the deal would reduce some trade "friction" but he said it would put a "massive additional burden on the 90% of farmers that don't do any trade with the EU".

Pressed over whether the Conservatives were committed to scrapping the deal if the party wins the next general election, Burghart said: "I don't think that there will be positive outcomes, and yes, we would scrap it."

He added: "I also don't think it is a good idea for a country like Britain to hand over control of its rules to another power and have no say over how those rules are created right into the future."

Food retailers have welcomed the deal, saying it will cut costs, reduce bureaucracy and remove barriers to trade.

However, they have not committed to cutting prices as a direct result of the changes.

The British Retail Consortium has said it does not expect prices on supermarket shelves to fall in response to the deal.

It has said upward pressures on prices remain and will not be alleviated by the agreement.

Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband insisted the deal "reduces pressure on trading costs", adding: "They're the things that go into prices."

"It will reduce the costs that the retailers face, all of that Brexit red tape, millions of forms that they were having to fill in, frankly pointlessly, as a result of the bad deal that we had," he told the BBC.

Challenged that the UK was also giving up some powers to set regulations itself, Miliband argued businesses were already "rule takers" from Brussels if they wanted to sell into the European market.

"So they have to abide by the rules of the European Union. But at the same time, because we are not integrated into that market for food and agricultural products, they have to fill in a whole bunch of forms... to confirm that they're observing the right standards, which is frankly crackers," he said.

Under the deal, he said the UK would "be able to shape decisions" for the first time.

News.title: Man dies in M42 crash near Birmingham Airport
News.content:
A man died in a serious crash on the M42 near Birmingham Airport, police said.

The crash, involving a van and a lorry, happened on the northbound carriageway of the motorway between junction 5a and junction six on Saturday, just after 12:30 GMT.

The van driver, a man in his 40s, died at the scene, West Midlands Police said.

The carriageway remained closed for several hours but was fully reopened to traffic earlier on Sunday morning.

Motorists caught in standstill traffic described seeing a "huge fire" after the crash, while West Midlands Police urged motorists to avoid the area.

The driver of the lorry remained at the scene and was helping officers with their investigation as inquiries remained ongoing, a spokesperson added.

News.title: BBC apologises for 'any offence caused' by Strictly noise disruption
News.content:
The BBC has apologised "for any offence caused" after lewd audio was heard during the live broadcast of Strictly Come Dancing.

A recording of sex noises appeared to be playing from the audience in Blackpool's Tower Ballroom as judge Motsi Mabuse gave feedback early in Saturday's episode. She paused before joking: "It's not me."

At the end of the programme, presenter Emma Willis apologised to viewers "if you heard any audio disruptions". A BBC spokesperson also issued an apology and said it was "investigating how this happened".

Lancashire police said it was assessing whether any criminal offences may have taken place, after receiving a formal complaint and a mobile phone being seized.

The moment was streamed on social media by content creator Daniel Jarvis, whose videos include pranks. He appeared to place a phone call before the audio began playing in the ballroom, and suggested he was trying to target judge Craig Revel Horwood for his "bullying".

Jarvis has previously claimed he was responsible for sex noises disrupting Match of the Day in 2023.

Willis told viewers: "Before we see the judges' leaderboard, we'd like to apologise if you heard any audio disruptions earlier in tonight's show and for any offence caused."

News.title: Widow fears losing home built by husband after support payments end
News.content:
Every room in Lauren's family home reminds her of her late husband.

A self-employed builder, Andy carried out much of the work on the property himself, helping create the house where the couple raised their four children.

Now, more than two years after his death from cancer, Lauren fears she may struggle to keep it.

The financial support that helped her cover mortgage payments and household bills has ended, leaving her facing uncertainty as she prepares to remortgage the property.

"I don't want to uproot my children," she said. "They've already been through too much the last two and a half years."

News.title: Village vote 'sent powerful message', say politicians
News.content:
No-one was surprised by the outcome of the poll which saw 257 people vote for the village ''to become an independent self-governing Crown dependency'' and just 16 vote against the idea. One ballot was spoiled.

The result has no legal basis, but there were warnings from local politicians for ministers not to ignore the result.

"It sends a powerful message that it is a completely unsuitable site.

"I hope just for once that the government will actually listen to local people," said Tim Passmore the Conservative Police and Crime Commissioner for Suffolk.

"That is what Andy Burnham said he would do, now it's time for action."

Terry Jermy is the Labour MP for Thetford, which is just two miles away from the base.

He said: "The people of Barnham have done a really good job in raising awareness of the issue and demonstrating the strength of feeling against these plans.

"The message to the government is that this MoD site is not suitable."

While Michael Hadwen, the Reform UK leader of Suffolk County council, said: "This is a clear demonstration of democracy at work.

"Barnham has said loud and clear that that the government cannot impose this base upon them and the government should start to listen because when things like this start to get ignored that's when society starts to collapse."

The estimated turnout of around 70% was lower than campaigners had been hoping for.

When a similar referendum was held in the Oxfordshire village of Piddington 89% of locals took part.

The chair of the residents association in Barnham said some people had decided not to vote after seeing the government ignore the result in Piddington and give planning permission for a nearby military base to be used for asylum seekers.

News.title: Joanna Page says she nearly messed up Gavin and Stacey audition
News.content:
Joanna Page has said she nearly messed up her Gavin And Stacey audition after failing to do a Cardiff accent.

The 49-year-old rose to fame after starring as Stacey in the BBC comedy opposite creators James Corden and Ruth Jones.

Page, from Swansea, told campmates on ITV's I'm A Celebrity... Get Me Out Of Here! that she had initially read some scenes for Jones using her actual accent.

She recounted that she was then asked to do it in a Cardiff accent, as that was where her character was supposed to be from, but Jones told her it sounded "awful" and to "just be you".

Speaking about her preparations for the life-changing audition, she said: "I remember reading the script, Ruth and James had written it and I remember thinking, 'This is me, she is me, I can do this'."

Page said she got the offer for the part in the Bafta-winning sitcom two weeks after being rejected from a West End show.

She said: "I was working in a shoe shop in East Dulwich and I'd just missed out on getting the part in Dirty Dancing The Musical.

"And so if I'd have got that, I never, ever would have done it."

Page also recalled her first impression of Mathew Horne - who played Gavin in the series - during their chemistry read and said "he seemed really cool, and I thought I'm not cool and I'm just a nerd".

The hit series aired for three seasons from 2007 until 2009 followed by Christmas specials including the series finale in 2024.

News.title: Long-lost Chevalier landscape found in charity shop
News.content:
A rediscovered 19th Century oil painting bought for Â£20 in a charity shop could be auctioned for up to Â£20,000.

Cape Schanck, Victoria, by Russian-Swiss artist Nicholas Chevalier, was discovered in a charity shop in Maidenhead, Berkshire.

It was brought to the attention of Adrian Biddell at London's Olympia Auctions, who established the painting was a Chevalier work that had been missing for 160 years.

"To find it now, quite unexpectedly, in a corner of the British high street, is an extraordinary find," he said.

The painting dates from 1862 and depicts the dramatic, rugged coastline at the southernmost tip of Australia's Mornington Peninsula, about 60 miles (96.5km) south of Melbourne.

The auction house said only two of five en plein air - meaning painted directly in front of the landscape it depicts - views of Cape Schanck by Chevalier that year were known to have survived until now.

Both are in the collection of the Art Gallery of New South Wales in Sydney.

It said the charity shop buyer had liked the landscape but had not been familiar with the artist or the painting's value.

Its appearance "resolves a longstanding gap in the documented history of Chevalier's work", it said.

It was leading Chevalier expert Simon Gregg who confirmed its whereabouts had previously been recorded as "unknown" in his catalogue of the artist's work.

"This was definitely painted en plein air," he said. "This was Chevalier's typical modus operandi."

Gregg added: "Most of the oil sketches have not survived, hence my delight that this one has shown up."

Biddell said Chevalier "was a remarkable visual talent, with an extraordinary ability to capture the drama, power and sheer scale of the natural world".

"The discovery of Cape Schanck, Victoria is hugely exciting," he said.

The painting will go under the hammer on 9 December.

News.title: I’m A Celeb: AJ Odudu in tears after Mariella Frostrup calls her ‘aggressive’ during heated clash
News.content:
I’m A Celebrity... Get Me Out Of Here! star AJ Odudu was left in tears as fellow campmate Mariella Frostrup labelled her “aggressive” in yet another clash between the pair.

The argument, which aired on Sunday night’s show, was the third in as many days, following previous fall outs over cooking in camp.

In tonight’s show, campmate Wayne Rooney tried to defuse the tension between both women, only for them to come to blows again, with both ending up in tears.

Watch the full clip above.

News.title: Tarik Skubal agrees to record $450 million, 9-year contract with New York Mets, AP source says
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Tarik Skubal, the two-time Cy Young Award winner who was the top free agent on this offseason's market, has agreed to record $450 million, nine-year contract with the New York Mets, a person familiar with the negotiations told The Associated Press on Sunday.

The person spoke on condition of anonymity because the agreement was subject to a successful physical.

Skubal's deal, averaging $50 million annually, is the largest for a pitcher, topping Yoshinobu Yamamoto's $325 million, 12-year contract with the Los Angeles Dodgers that started in 2024. The previous high for a pitcher's average salary was $37 million for Jacob deGrom in a $185 million, five-year contract with Texas that began in 2023.

It's the fourth largest deal among all baseball players, trailing Juan Soto's $765 million, Shohei Ohtani's $700 million and Vladimir Guerrero Jr.'s $500 million.

Skubal's agreement includes a full no-trade clause and a $45 million signing bonus that is shielded from the management lockout that threatens the 2027 season, the person said.

A two-time All-Star left-hander who turned 30 on Nov. 20, Skubal is 43-17 with a 2.42 ERA in 88 starts over the last four seasons, striking out 655 and walking 95 in 546 innings.

Skubal had a $32 million salary this year after winning a record amount in salary arbitration.

He joins a Mets team that finished last in the NL East at 74-88 despite having baseball's highest payroll on opening day at roughly $352 million. New York's starters had a 4.47 ERA, ranking 23rd in the majors. Skubal will top a rotation featuring youngsters Nolan McLean and Christian Scott, with veterans Sean Manaea and Kodai Senga also under contract.

Skubal was 12-7 with a 2.72 ERA in 26 starts this year for Detroit and the Los Angeles Dodgers, who acquired him on Aug. 2 for three prospects: right-handers River Ryan and Brady Smith, and outfielder Zyhir Hope. Skubal didn't pitch for the Tigers between April 29 and June 13 because of surgery to remove a loose body in his pitching elbow. Dodgers head team physician Dr. Neal ElAttrache used a NanoNeedle scope 2.0 to perform the procedure, designed to speed recovery.

Skubal was 1-1 with a 2.45 ERA in a pair of postseason starts for the Dodgers. He beat Atlanta in a Division Series opener and lost Game 1 of the NL Championship Series against Milwaukee, allowing two runs over five innings in a 2-1 defeat. The Brewers went on to sweep the two-time defending World Series champions.

He averaged 96.8 mph with his four-seam fastball this year, down from 97.6 mph in 2025, when he won his second straight AL Cy Young Award. He threw 38% four-seamers this year, 25.6% changeups, 17.5% sinkers, 13.9% sliders and 5% curveballs.

Skubal is 66-44 with a 3.02 ERA in 160 starts and three relief appearances over seven major league seasons with 1,075 strikeouts over 925 1/3 innings.

News.title: Russian warship sinks at Libya port in suspected Ukrainian drone attack, officials say
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

A Russian ship has been hit off the coast of Libya in a suspected Ukrainian drone attack, officials said on Sunday.

The explosion took place on board Merkury, a Russian navy warship docked at the Benghazi naval base and is suspected to have been caused by drones launched by the Ukrainian military, Libyan officials told the Associated Press.

Satellite images by Vantor showed the ship was a Russian Navy corvette, or small warship. The pictures show that most of the vessel had capsized and sunk on Sunday, with only its bow still visible above water while smoke rises.

No one has officially claimed responsibility for the attack.

A fire is reported to have broken out at the base and the ship is said to be severely damaged. The drones are said to have been launched from a base run by the Ukrainian military in western Libya according to an initial investigation.

Libyan military officials told AP that four drones had been intercepted and destroyed while two hit the warship.

The sources are affiliated with the Libyan National Army, which controls eastern and southern Libya.

open image in gallery A satellite image shows fires near a cargo ship with vehicles onboard after an explosion aboard a Russian ship docked at the Benghazi naval base, which Libya's eastern-based government said was caused by a suspected drone attack, in Benghazi, Libya, November 22, 2026. ( Reuters )

Ten people, both Russians and Libyans, were injured in the attack and are receiving treatment in Benghazi, medical sources told Reuters.

The eastern-based government said in a statement that the Russian ship had stopped at the Libyan port to refuel and resupply on its way back to Russia, under maritime cooperation agreements between the two countries.

In a separate incident, a commercial vessel flying the Maltese flag was also targeted by a drone off the coast of Benghazi on Sunday, two Libyan military sources told the outlet.

open image in gallery Pictures show that most of the vessel had capsized and sunk on Sunday, with only the vessel’s bow still visible above water while smoke rises ( Reuters )

The eastern-based government said that port and naval base facilities, including warehouses, were safe and that normal operations had resumed after the incident.

It condemned the suspected attack as a violation of Libya's sovereignty and a threat to maritime safety and warned that it would take legal and diplomatic measures against anyone found responsible.

The government emphasised that Libya was not involved in the conflict or to any war beyond its borders.

open image in gallery Fire burns after an explosion aboard a Russian ship docked at Benghazi port ( Reuters )

“The Libyan government will not allow Libyan ports, territory or territorial waters to be turned into an arena for settling scores or exporting international conflicts,” it added.

It comes a day after Finland’s prime minister Petteri Orpo warned that the Russia-Ukaine conflict was “spilling over” after a Russian ship was reportedly on fire in Finnish water on Saturday.

“The war is spilling over into our neighbouring areas. Finnish authorities are handling the situation in the Gulf of Finland, where a drone strike has hit a Russian merchant vessel. Ukraine has the right to fight ‌against the aggressor,” Orpo said on X.

open image in gallery In this photo released by the Finnish Border Guard, rescuers' ships try to extinguish a fire in the Russian cargo ship Sparta II in the Gulf of Finland, Sunday, Nov. 22, 2026. ( AP )

Finnish authorities said Russian vessels might eventually tow the wreckage back to Russia after the attack.

The 16-member crew of the Sparta II abandoned the vessel for lifeboats before transferring to a nearby Russian ship to make their way back to the country, Finnish Border Guard Commander Ilja Iljin told public broadcaster Yle late on Saturday.

News.title: Britney Spears apologizes to family for ‘bringing up past issues’ in a since-deleted post
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Britney Spears has shared a surprising message for her estranged family in a since-deleted social media post.

In an Instagram post shared Saturday, the iconic pop singer apologized multiple times to her family members for revisiting “past issues” without speaking to her relatives “face to face” amid their years-long feud.

“I’m so blessed to have such a beautiful family,” Spears, 44, wrote in the caption of her post, which showed an AI-generated image of two cats having tea in London. “I’m so very sorry for bringing up past issues, but I think I did because I realized I needed to protect my heart…it’s the way I love and when I love you, I REALLY love you.”

She continued: “My stubbornness is childish and embarrassing. Thoughts on the past, I’m obviously human and there actually might be something to those things I said [psychology] wise.

“Either way, I’m sorry to my family for bringing up those memories, but I’ve never actually spoke to them face to face on it…it’s frankly bc I just miss them like crazy!!! And I’m very sorry!!!”

open image in gallery Britney Spears was in a court-ordered conservatorship overseen by her father and a lawyer for over a decade ( Getty )

The Independent has reached out to representatives for Spears for comment.

Spears has been estranged from her family in recent years and has been vocal about her complicated relationships with her dad Jamie Spears, 74, mom Lynne Spears, 71, and sister Jamie Lynn Spears, 35.

Earlier this month, the “Toxic” singer shared a post calling out her ex-husband, Kevin Federline, with whom she shares two sons, as well as Jamie Lynn.

“I will find a new family !!!” Spears wrote on Instagram in a post that is still on her account.

The hitmaker went on to say that Jamie Lynn did not let her hold her niece, Ivey, when she visited Louisiana during the Covid pandemic. She also added that Federline “wouldn’t let me use the bathroom when I would pick my children up in their house !!!”

“They made me feel like a slave and have all their secret things they did behind my back and all I ever did was work for my dad !!!” Spears wrote. “I will find a new family !!!”

The Grammy winner was placed in a court-ordered conservatorship overseen by her father and a lawyer in 2008 after undergoing several public crises.

In 2021, Spears challenged the decision in court and told a judge that the arrangement had been “abusive.” The conservatorship was terminated later that year.

News.title: Badenoch hits out at PM’s ‘terrible’ EU deal as Farage warns of rejoin ‘disaster’
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Kemi Badenoch will accuse Andy Burnham of securing a “terrible” deal with the European Union and say he should be “aiming a lot higher” in terms of driving growth, as Nigel Farage warns that closer ties with Brussels would be a “disaster” for British businesses.

The Conservative and Reform UK leaders will both use speeches at the Confederation of British Industry (CBI) annual conference on Monday to attack the Prime Minister’s efforts to reset relations with Brussels.

Mrs Badenoch will argue that Mr Burnham has set his sights too low with his deal aimed at boosting Britain’s economy by 0.4%, while Mr Farage will warn that closer alignment with the EU would hit small businesses with more red tape.

Their interventions follow Friday’s UK-EU summit, at which Mr Burnham struck deals covering food and agriculture exports, emissions trading, and a youth experience scheme.

The Labour leader now intends to discuss options for the future relationship with the bloc over the next 12 months.

Conservative Party leader Kemi Badenoch (Stefan Rousseau/PA) ( PA Wire )

In her speech, Mrs Badenoch will acknowledge the benefits of closer trading ties with Europe, but accuse the Prime Minister of weakening Britain’s negotiating position.

She is expected to say: “Believe me, as a former trade secretary, I understand why some businesses want easier trading relationships with the EU.

“Only around 8% of businesses in the UK trade with the EU, but for those that do closer trading relations would be beneficial.

“Europe is our closest neighbour.

“Despite the challenges countries like Germany and France are facing, they remain huge economies and lucrative markets for our goods and services.”

She will point to the EU’s veterinary agreement with New Zealand, under which the two sides recognise each other’s standards without relinquishing control over their laws.

“Why will the EU give New Zealand something it won’t give us?

“It’s because they knew Andy Burnham would sign Britain up to be a rule taker from the EU instead, because he has no other ideas to grow our economy.”

She will cite Mr Burnham’s remarks that Britain was “not in a position to turn its back on a deal that could add up to 0.4% to GDP.”

“Of course he got a terrible deal, because he made it clear he wouldn’t turn it down.

“It is also thinking way too small.”

The Tory leader will argue that Europe “is not the market of the future” and that Britain should focus on faster-growing economies such as India, Indonesia and the US.

“The question has always been: is it worth locking yourself into one market if it locks you out of another?

“The fact is, Britain needs to be aiming a lot higher than 0.4% growth if we’re going to get out of the economic mess we are in.”

Meanwhile, Mr Farage will accuse large businesses of supporting closer ties with Brussels because of access to cheap labour and regulations that disadvantage smaller competitors.

The Reform UK leader is expected to say: “Rejoining, or even the half-in, half-out alignment some of them want, would plunge millions of businesses into chaos when they now have certainty.

“It will hit the small firms that do not even trade with Europe with more red tape, more compliance costs, more Brussels rules they never asked for.

He will argue that British businesses have benefited from diverging from EU rules in areas including agricultural technology, financial services and artificial intelligence.

“Divergence is our strength. Going backwards into the EU’s orbit would be a disaster for the very British businesses that are trying to compete and innovate. “

News.title: Gerwyn Price ends four-year wait for major title with emphatic Grand Slam win
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Gerwyn Price finally ended his major trophy drought by winning the Grand Slam of Darts and is delighted to silence his critics.

The Welshman had not won a major televised event since 2022 and may have thought it might not happen again after losing three finals this year alone.

But with Luke Littler and Luke Humphries exiting early, Price took his chance with a brilliant 16-11 win over Gian van Veen in Wolverhampton.

Price claimed Grand Slam glory for the fourth time, but this one will surely mean the most to him.

The 41-year-old, who swatted away a wasp and Kevin Doets in the semi-final earlier on Sunday, was embroiled in a tense and nervy encounter which turned in the 15th leg.

Van Veen had six darts to break for an 8-7 lead, but could not finish and Price seized the moment.

He took out double two on his fifth attempt to win the leg and then reeled off the next six to take control.

It was an imperious period of play which left Van Veen with no way back as ‘The Iceman’ coolly saw out the win to get back into the winners’ circle – his eighth major title.

open image in gallery Price won the Grand Slam of Darts for the fourth time (Jacob King/PA) ( PA Wire )

His lack of silverware has been a talking point and he is happy to end the noise.

“I was probably more nervous in this game than ever,” he said after the win. “I’ve lost so many finals. Just to keep the media off my back, it’s not for me.

“I do mind and I don’t mind, but now they can stop talking about it. I’m going to Minehead next week with a major, so they can leave me alone.

“I’ve had some close calls this year where I probably should have won games and tournaments, but when it comes along, it’s nice.”

open image in gallery Gian van Veen was beaten 16-11 (Jacob King/PA) ( PA Wire )

Van Veen has also not won a major in a while, but his chances were limited against a player who he has a poor record against.

“I don’t like Gezzy,” Van Veen, who earlier ended compatriot Michael van Gerwen’s hopes of winning, joked. “Gezzy, I don’t like you.

“I think it was a very close game. He took out a lot of good finishes with me waiting, and I missed a couple of chances.

“So I think the 16-11 was a flattered scoreline. It’s part of the job, and that’s what Gezzy does. He always puts everyone under pressure, and he took his chances, and that’s why he deserves to win. I’m very devastated.”

News.title: Trump wrangles Floyd Mayweather, Kevin O’Leary to join dinner for investors of slumping meme coin
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

President Donald Trump has lined up a roster of celebrity guests for a gala dinner Sunday celebrating his slumping meme coin.

Canadian entrepreneur and Shark Tank cast member Kevin O’Leary and former five-division world boxing champion Floyd Mayweather are among those expected to attend, The Wall Street Journal reported.

Former Cleveland Cavaliers star Tristan Thompson and Israeli mentalist Lior Suchard are also slated to join the event.

The dinner at Trump’s golf club in Virginia is for 185 holders of $TRUMP, the meme coin he launched shortly before his inauguration.

Invitations are awarded through a competition that ranks participants by the size of their holdings and how long they hold them. Securing a seat at the first gala, in May 2025, required at least $55,000 in $TRUMP holdings. This time, one participant qualified with just $518, The Washington Post previously reported.

open image in gallery President Donald Trump has lined up a roster of celebrity guests for a gala dinner Sunday celebrating his slumping meme coin ( AFP via Getty Images )

The sharply reduced threshold comes amid the coin’s plunge to a record low. After surging to about $74 within hours of its launch in January 2025, the token fell to roughly $17 a month later. By Sunday, it was trading at about 89 cents, according to Coinbase.

Hundreds of thousands of buyers have lost a combined $3.8 billion, The New York Times reported in July.

Trump has long brushed aside concerns about his meme coin, which reportedly netted him $635 million in royalties last year. Asked last May whether he was profiting from cryptocurrency, he said, “I haven’t even looked.”

In July, he said: “There’s nothing illegal. There’s nothing wrong with it.”

open image in gallery Canadian entrepreneur and Shark Tank cast member Kevin O’Leary is slated to attend the gala in Virginia Sunday ( Getty Images for Bilt )

open image in gallery Former five-division world boxing champion Floyd Mayweather, who has publicly backed Trump, is among those expected to attend Sunday ( Getty Images )

But his crypto businesses could soon face greater scrutiny. After midterm victories fueled in part by voters’ concerns about corruption, Democrats have vowed to investigate his ventures.

A group of Democratic senators has described the latest gala as an apparent “pay-to-play scheme.”

“This dinner and scoring mechanism appear carefully constructed to increase investment in $TRUMP, allowing the President to abuse the power of his office to personally enrich himself, as he has throughout this term,” they wrote in a letter to the White House.

News.title: Any regrets, Mauricio? Man Utd are deep in relegation battle after Anfield farce
News.content:
Bruno Fernandes says he has shelved talks over a new contract because it is not the “right moment” for discussions over his future as Manchester United captain.

Fernandes, 32, is out of contract next summer although United have a 12-month option to extend his deal to 2028.

The Portugal midfielder is understood to have rejected two contract offers from United since the summer but said all his focus needs to be on trying to help the team out of their current plight.

United head into Sunday’s game against Liverpool at Anfield second from bottom in the Premier League.

“We spoke about the contract at the end of last season,” Fernandes told Sky Sports.

“We came in at the beginning of this season speaking about the contract, but about the context of the team and the club, I just put that to a side because I don’t think it’s the right moment, neither for me, nor for the club, to be talking about negotiations.

“The most important thing now is that the club gets back to winning games.”

Fernandes said claims he wants more money or a longer-term deal on offer are incorrect and that if finances were the issue he would have left Old Trafford before now. The captain has previously rejected lucrative offers from Saudi Arabia.

“The club offered me a new contract, so I think that, from their side, shows that they want me to stay,” he said.

“There’s no negotiations ongoing, but I’ve seen people saying that ‘He’s asked for more money, he’s asked for more years’. If I wanted more money, I wouldn’t be here.

“I had somewhere to go to get much more money than being at Manchester United. I could have been in a place that is much warmer than Manchester.

“Two summers ago, three summers ago, last summer, I always had the chance to leave and I always chose to be here.

“The thing is, I’ve always showed how much I care about the club and how much I want to win at this club. And I always said, in the moment the club thinks it’s time for me to move on, I will move on.

“I’m not going to be the player that I’ve seen many in this time at Manchester United. They’re going to stay here just by staying, just finish my contract and then we will see. In the moment the club says, ‘Bruno, it’s time to part ways’, I’m going to be the first one walking out the door.”

United chief executive Omar Berrada said of Fernandes on Friday that it was “true that we’re having conversations about his new contract” but that the club preferred “to keep that private”.

Having been voted PFA Player of the Year last season, Fernandes’ form has dropped off this term like that of the team.

He was dropped for the 3-0 defeat by Bournemouth in the wake of a 4-1 drubbing by Como when he criticised the tactics and approach of then head coach Michael Carrick.

Mauricio Pochettino, Carrick’s successor, confirmed on Friday that Fernandes would remain as captain.

Fernandes said the United fans had been “far too patient with us” and hopes Pochettino - who wanted to bring the Portuguese to Spurs in 2019 - will bring a fresh energy.

“He’s someone that likes to bring a very good energy to the team, someone very positive, very strong, strict, said it straight away that he won’t allow us to not give him what he demands from the team, from each player,” Fernandes said.

“He wants the club to succeed so much, he wants to win games, and that’s pretty clear and obvious by the way he and his staff speak and want us to improve.

“Obviously [in 2019] I was a very young player that was eager to come to the Premier League. They had [Harry] Kane there, they had Dele Alli, Son, the chance of playing with those players in front was very attractive.”

News.title: Verstappen mocks ‘absolute joke’ Russell after thrilling Las Vegas win
News.content:
Welcome to our live coverage for the 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix, coming to you from very early on a Sunday morning (if you are in the eastern hemisphere) and very late on a Sunday night (if you are in the western hemisphere).

It is a strange race in a strange place, but this is now the fourth edition of the race and it looks to be here to stay for all its strangeness. It does present the teams with problems and problems are there to be solved or negotiated as well as can be in F1. That is the name of the game.

In qualifying yesterday the world champion, Kimi Antonelli, did that expertly, sneaking in at the end to finish fastest. He does, however, take a five-place grid penalty, so will be starting in sixth. Taking first place on the grid will be the in-form Max Verstappen, followed by George Russell, who could do with a strong finish to the season.

Russell seemed miffed about missing out on pole position, particularly with how Mercedes managed the qualifying situation, particularly with how the tow was managed. Antonelli was always going to take a grid penalty, so why give him the tow, was Russell’s reasoning.

In any case, Russell has a good chance to take his third victory this season. At least on paper. Russell’s qualifying has probably been his strongest suit this season, but race days have let him down. Let us not forget that Lando Norris, who won last time out in Brazil, starts third.

There could be a bit of aggro on the first lap, given Russell and Verstappen’s “disagreement” yesterday, but let’s see. It may end up being a clean race.

It all starts in about an hour and we will be here for all the updates and reaction from the 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix.

News.title: Wales ‘frustrated’ after being brought back down to earth by Wallabies
News.content:
Wales have a spring in their step coming into their game tonight as they host Australia at the Principality Stadium. Wales pulled off one of their best wins in recent memory last weekend, ending an over 70-year with for a victory over New Zealand. Despite pulling off that shock victory, Wales sit down in fifth in the northern hemisphere standings coming into this final round of fixtures. In all likelihood, they can only improve one spot. They have made four changes from the historic win over the All Blacks, with the likes of Josh Adams and Aaron Wainwright coming in.

“We were all immensely proud to make history last week,” Wales head coach Steve Tandy said. “There is a new opportunity and challenge for us against Australia and we are looking to back up our performance this weekend. It is our last home game of this competition. The support that fans give to the players and staff has been incredible and we cannot wait to get back out at Principality Stadium.

“We made nearly 350 tackles, the ball in play time was one of the highest in Test rugby in the last three years and we have got competition. The plan was always to freshen up and we are likely to do similar for the week after, because we need to find out about players. We have fresh and hungry players coming in, which will add the energy that we need at the weekend. The training environment is getting more competitive in certain positions we have the ability to put people in and feel confident about performance.”

News.title: Whiff of arrogance as Arsenal unexpectedly implode
News.content:
Speaking to Sky Sports, the Arsenal boss said: “My feeling is that we lost two points today. I think we were exceptional in the first half. At every level. Our intensity, the clarity that we have, how to attack the jumps of Newcastle every time they wanted to go man-to-man, the composure that we have, the way we use our relationship to break their press. And it should have been 2-0, 3-0 or 4-0 up, clear.

“But it wasn’t. And when it wasn’t, then we expected in the second half that we have to again raise the level because the opponent is going to have a reaction. And the opponent did have a reaction and we were very below the level that is required to stretch the gap in a game like this in this stadium. And then we gave them belief.

“And I say we give them belief because we give them a goal, we give them a throw-in that we just give them the ball. We have no structure to control the opposite winger. We concede a goal and it’s game on. And from that it became a very chaotic game. Every set-piece, we know that they are exceptional at it and we concede from a set piece.

“And then you have to react. And then we went back to the team that the exceptional team that we were in the first half again for another 25 minutes and we scored a great goal. We create infinity of openings to create and score the third goal, but we lack some time or to be precise, to make that count.”

News.title: ‘Remarkable’ Ireland deliver perfect riposte to Erasmus mind games
News.content:
Good afternoon and welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of Ireland vs South Africa from the Nations Championship in Dublin, with both teams harbouring hopes of finishing the day at the top of their respective tables.

Ireland and South Africa have both won four of their five games in the group phase of this year’s inaugural Nations Championship, and come into their last match before next weekend’s finals still in contention for the overall title.

Andy Farrell’s men begin the afternoon in third in the Northern Hemisphere table, but level on points with second-placed England, who are currently hosting New Zealand, and just one point behind leaders France, who take on Argentina this evening.

The reigning world champions, meanwhile, are guaranteed to at least remain in second in the Southern Hemisphere table, but are just one point behind the All Blacks at the top of the group, so will be hoping for a favour from Steve Borthwick’s men at Twickenham.

The Springboks will be without head coach Rassie Erasmus for today’s contest in the Irish capital, with the 54-year-old facing a six-match ban because of his criticism of officials following his team’s narrow defeat by France last weekend, including asking whether they were “match-fixing”.

“He’s been hands-on with our team, and we’re in a good space,” assistant coach Mzwandile Stick said of Erasmus on Friday. “Irrespective of what has happened, we love him, we appreciate him, and no one is going to break us. I can tell you that for sure.”

In the same press conference, Erasmus predicted that Sam Prendergast would be cleared to play after being cited for a hip-drop tackle against Fiji. The Ireland fly-half escaped punishment from the independent panel and starts for Farrell’s side this afternoon.

News.title: Alonso heckled as Chelsea are humiliated by Leeds
News.content:
Good afternoon and welcome to coverage from the Premier League as domestic football returns after an international break.

We have five matches to bring you, including Chelsea vs Leeds, Aston Villa vs Sunderland and Tottenham vs Ipswich.

Xabi Alonso said his Chelsea side needs to learn to deal with the absence of Joao Pedro as the Blues struggle for goals in the absence of their injured striker.

The Brazilian has not played since the 2-0 win over Everton on October 17 and will be unavailable again today.

Without a focal point in the number nine position, Chelsea’s goal output has been dramatically reduced and they have dropped to fifth and having suffered two defeats in their last three games.

“(We need) the whole team for that,” said Alonso. “It’s not just the strikers that can score. We can score from set-pieces, from defenders, from midfielders.

“It’s teamwork. For sure Joao is an important player but we need to deal with this time without him. So far we have tried different options and we need to keep trying.

“We need to deal with it. It’s not that I’m going to look for one explanation. I think that there are more explanations for one defeat than missing just one player.”

Tottenham will not have their manager, Roberto De Zerbi, on the touchline after receiving three yellow cards this season.

Gary O’Neil is targeting a “special” result at Tottenham, but promised Ipswich will not make any drastic changes after a four-match winless run.

Ipswich lost 2-1 at home to Bournemouth before the two-week break, which followed draws with Hull and Nottingham Forest along with a narrow defeat at Manchester City, but O’Neil is happy with his new-look group.

“There won’t be any drastic changes. The odd personnel change, (but) I don’t think it’s going to be a big shift for us,” O’Neil told a press conference.

“It’s a very well-balanced squad. There’s going to be no massive uplifts or downgrades when we have to change players within this group.”

Aston Villa will have Johan Manzambi available for the visit of Sunderland.

The midfielder did not feature for Switzerland during the recent international break because of a calf injury but he has trained with the rest of the squad and can feature today.

Villa can also call on right-back Aaron Wan-Bissaka after a muscle injury ruled him out for six matches. His return is timely as Matty Cash is unavailable.

Cash was suspended for Villa’s 4-4 draw with Manchester United before the international break but suffered a concussion while away with Poland.

News.title: England obliterate All Blacks in record win
News.content:
A nearly perfect half for England was ruined just two minutes before half-time when Ben Earl gave up a penalty from the restart, immediately after scoring the home side’s third try. New Zealand kicked to the corner and Ethan de Groot plunged over to give the All Blacks a lifeline they scarcely deserve.

Until that point, this was as dominant a half against top-tier opposition that we have ever seen from Steve Borthwick’s team. Much like they did against Australia, England have strangled the life out of New Zealand and have enjoyed a preposterous 78 per cent territory.

They have also repeatedly cut New Zealand open in midfield. The interplay between Fin Smith, Seb Atkinson and the regal George Furbank has been sumptuous to watch. England have struggled to break New Zealand down in the red zone but still have three tries to show for their efforts. Smith’s cute little poke through was grounded by Henry Slade after five minutes and then scrum half Jack van Poortvliet did his best Superman impression by diving over the top of a ruck for England’s second try.

Earl also went route one, picking off the back of a scrum and through Cam Roigard’s tackle to put England in dreamland. Not every department has functioned perfectly. New Zealand have been on top of the scrum and have stopped the English maul in its tracks, but the All Blacks have been dominated physically. When was the last time we said that about an England team?

The De Groot try has taken the wind out of England’s sails a little but a similar setback took place in the Australia game just before half-time and Borthwick’s team responded with an emphatic second-half performance.

England need to see this out too, otherwise they’ll be kicking themselves all the way through to the World Cup.

Sports.title: Mauricio Pochettino explains tactical reason behind rare Matthijs de Ligt start in Man Utd debut after it backfired
Sports.content:
Next

MAURICIO POCHETTINO unconvincingly defended his decision to start Matthijs de Ligt in Manchester United’s 4-0 thrashing by Liverpool.

De Ligt made his first Premier League start in 357 days at Anfield, where his eighth-minute error led to Leny Yoro’s red card and Dominik Szboszlai scored from the resultant free kick.



Former United head coach Michael Carrick started De Ligt in the 4-1 Champions League drubbing by Como last month but United were without the suspended Yoro and injured Lisandro Martinez.

Carrick preferred to start Yoro, Martinez, Harry Maguire and Ayden Heaven ahead of De Ligt at centre back after the Dutchman returned from a long-term back injury six weeks ago.



De Ligt was sidelined for almost ten months and his back required surgery in May.

Vice-captain Maguire, who started on the bench against Liverpool, had lined up in United’s previous ten Premier League games.



Pochettino said: “I think it’s about trust of the player in the way we arrive.

“Of course, we assess the whole squad and for different reasons and different situations we decide to pick that starting XI.

“But for sure, that question is because we concede and in the moment. So we made one mistake.

“But the mistake [by Jeremy] Jacquet was a penalty on [Bryan] Mbeumo, maybe you congratulate us for the decision.”



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Poch continued: “It’s a tricky question for you but I accept that because we need to be here to explain, I need to explain everything.

“When you don’t win, it’s impossible to be right. Everyone know sees the situation and the game does different things.

“It’s important the way we assess on the inside, I think it was the right decision.”

Pochettino’s post-match press conference also ended with him being asked about De Ligt’s recall: “He was training, he played in Champions League before the international duty.

“I think when we arrive we saw the combination.”

Sports.title: Ex-Man Utd flop Bebe goes viral after wild shot misses goal by miles and SHATTERS LIGHTS in stadium
Sports.content:
Next

MANCHESTER UNITED flop Bebe went viral after a wild shot missed the target and smashed the stadium lights.

The winger went down in Premier League folklore after joining United in rags-to-riches fashion back in 2010 when he was 20 years old.



Spotted at the Homeless World Cup, Man Utd’s legendary manager Sir Alex Ferguson stumped up £7.4million to sign Tiago Manuel Dias Correia, which is his full name.

The Portuguese-born player was recommended to Sir Alex by his then trusty No2 Carlos Queiroz.



And thus the Scottish great activated the then-Vitoria Guimaraes player’s release clause despite having NEVER seen him play.

However, Bebe went down in history as one of the biggest Premier League flops of all time.



The forward only managed a mere seven appearances – in which he scored twice – in all of his four years in Man Utd‘s books.

The Cape Verde international spent a great deal of his United stint going out on loan to the likes of Besiktas, Rio Ave and Pacos de Ferreira before ultimately being sold to Benfica – a move he later dubbed the “best moment of my life”.

Bebe then underwent quite a nomadic career with the likes of Rayo Vallecano, Eibar and Zaragoza before tumbling down to Spain’s lower divisions.

The 36-year-old now plays for third-division outfit Teruel, for whom he started for the first time in his third appearance on Friday’s league clash against Hercules.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

His team lost 1-0, but he still made headlines thanks to one shot just a few minutes before full-time.

Bebe fired a volley towards the visitors’ goal but completely missed the target and instead sent the ball to a bar that was placed behind the stands.

And it seemed like the United flop’s shot was so powerful it actually shattered the lights.



Football fans were left absolutely stunned as they stormed social media in disbelief.

One fan tweeted: “Bebe put out the lights at a bar in Teruel with a single shot.”

Another commented: “Unbelievable!”

A third wrote: “BEBE IS ONE OF A KIND.”

Sports.title: Man Utd have worst defence in EUROPE with even more goals conceded than Prem basement boys Crystal Palace
Sports.content:
Next

MANCHESTER UNITED officially have the leakiest defence in Europe after their humiliating loss to fierce foes Liverpool.

The Red Devils suffered a 4-0 thrashing at Anfield as new boss Mauricio Pochettino made a nightmare start to his reign.



Dominik Szoboszlai, Florian Wirtz, Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz found the net after Leny Yoro’s early red card reduced United to ten men.

And the shock Premier League strugglers’ wretched defensive record plunged to new depths.



United, who also conceded four when they drew with Aston Villa before the international break, have had their backline breached a whopping 34 times in all competitions this season.

It means they have picked the ball out of their own net more than any other side across the continent.



Crystal Palace, who are the only side below United in the Premier League table, suffered a 3-2 loss to Coventry on Saturday.

But the Eagles still have a marginally better defensive record than the Red Devils.

Palace appointed Thomas Frank as their new boss in a bid to tighten things up at the back, having conceded 33 goals.

That is the same record as Bundesliga strugglers Union Berlin, who were beaten 7-0 by a Harry Kane and Michael Olise-inspired Bayern Munich in September.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Sassuolo and Lens have had their respective rearguards breached 32 times.

Pochettino, 54, shattered two unwanted records as United were swept aside by Liverpool.

The Argentine became the first boss to see his side concede twice and receive a red card in the first half of his maiden clash.

And no Premier League chief has ever been forced to deal with one of their stars being sent off earlier.

United had Harry Maguire, Matthijs de Ligt, Lisandro Martinez and Diogo Dalot in their backline following Yoro’s dismissal at Liverpool.



And Old Trafford legend Peter Schmeichel warned Pochettino is in danger of dropping into the Championship if improvements are not made quickly.

The Dane, 63, told Viaplay: “This team looks like a team that could get relegated. So now the target should be to avoid relegation.

“We’ve all played in the Premier League, so we know we’re in November, approaching December. It’s not really now, it’s when we get to March.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

“If they keep doing this for so long, there’s going to be trouble. But I think, at least, I have faith that he can correct those things.

“He’s never going to make a championship-winning team, not with these guys.”

Sports.title: Man Utd fans fear for Gary Neville after club legend slaps himself in the face live on Sky Sports after Liverpool loss
Sports.content:
Next

GARY NEVILLE bizarrely slapped himself in the face live on Sky Sports as he ripped into Manchester United’s defence.

The former United skipper, 51, was on co-commentary duty as the Red Devils were trounced 4-0 by Liverpool in Mauricio Pochettino‘s first game in charge.

Man Utd had been reduced to 10 men in just the eighth minute when Leny Yoro was sent off following a mistake by Matthijs de Ligt.



More errors would follow, with Liverpool creating chances at will as they ripped through their 10-man opponents.



Speaking in the Sky Sports studio after watching his boyhood club get demolished, Neville blasted United defenders’ body language.

He said: “I never see any of them on their toes, alert, looking like they’ve got something fixed in here (points to his head).

“I never see any of them look like that. They look like that…”



At this point Neville stared blankly for several seconds.

He then said “Wake up!” before leaving viewers stunned by slapping himself in the face.

Neville then repeated “Wake up!” and again slapped his own face and bellowed: “You play for Man Utd!”

And fans at home also couldn’t get over the incident.

One wrote on X: “Bruh! Man United players have traumatised Gary Neville. He is literally slapping himself on Sky Sports”.

And a second commented: “He’s lost it”.



A third joked: “My God they’re all cracking the worse it gets”.

Another added: “That’s an all-timer from Neville hahahahah”.

Earlier in the evening, Neville had likened returning from a year out, as De Ligt had against Liverpool, as like “playing after six pints”.

United endured a humiliating defeat at Anfield in new manager Mauricio Pochettino’s first match in charge, keeping them second from bottom in the Premier League’s relegation zone.

Sports.title: Man Utd legend sends RELEGATION warning to Mauricio Pochettino and says safety is new target
Sports.content:

PETER SCHMEICHEL revealed hard truths following Manchester United’s tragic 4-0 defeat at Liverpool.

The Red Devils legend watched on as his former side went down to ten men in the eighth minute after Leny Yoro was sent off before conceding four goals.



Dominik Szoboszlai struck first from the resulting free-kick before Florian Wirtz doubled their lead.

Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz put the icing on the cake for the Reds in the second half.



And, speaking on Viaplay, club legend Schmeichel was left fearing United could actually go down.

The former keeper said: “Realistically, can Man United just finish 10th or 12th? It would be okay.



“I know it’s silly to say, but we are in the relegation zone.”

The catastrophic defeat left United in 19th and marked Mauricio Pochettino‘s first game in the new dugout as one to forget.

There are already 20 points between the struggling side and league leaders Arsenal, but they have 27 games remaining in the Prem season to avoid the drop.

Schmeichel added: “This team looks like a team that could get relegated. So now the target should be to avoid relegation.”



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

“We’ve all played in the Premier League, so we know we’re in November, approaching December. It’s not really now, it’s when we get to March.

“If they keep doing this for so long, I mean, there’s going to be trouble.

“But I think, at least, I have faith that he can correct those things. He’s never going to make a championship-winning team, not with these guys.”

But when the new United boss spoke with Viaplay, he said: “Relegation battle? That is our reality, no…? We are there.

“We need to win games.”



After the game, other ex-United stars gave their two pence on the state of the team.

Roy Keane fumed as he threatened to swear live on the telly, while Gary Neville noted how bad he felt for the fans singing Bob Marley’s Three Little Birds after full-time.

And when the Sky Sports pundits joined up in the studio for the post-match debrief, they nearly ran out of time to analyse the game before they switched channels.



United will travel to Lisbon to face Sporting in the Champions League on Tuesday before hosting Brentford on Saturday.

And fans will be hoping that Pochettino can turn things around pronto with another mid-week game against Newcastle after that.

Sports.title: Price looking to continue trend of Grand Slam victors tasting Worlds glory
Sports.content:
Gerwyn Price won the Grand Slam of Darts with a 16-11 victory over Gian van Veen; the last four winners of the Grand Slam have gone on to win the World Darts Championship at Alexandra Palace; Price is hoping to continue the trend

Gerwyn Price looking to continue trend of Grand Slam victors tasting World Darts Championship glory

Gerwyn Price reflects on winning his first major for four years after beating Gian van Veen in the Grand Slam of Darts final

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

An interesting trend has occurred over the last four years: The winner of the Grand Slam has gone on to win the World Darts Championship.

It started with Michael Smith back in 2022, with Luke Humphries continuing it in 2023.

Of course, Luke Littler's back-to-back triumphs in Wolverhampton in 2024 and 2025 were then followed by him lifting the Sid Waddell Trophy.

Gerwyn Price wants to continue that in 2026.

Price roared to a 16-11 victory over Gian van Veen in the final of the Grand Slam, hitting five massive ton-plus checkouts in a confident display.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Grand Slam of Darts final between Price and Van Veen

The win moves Price up to world No 3 ahead of Humphries and marks his first major title in four years.

Alexandra Palace was immediately on Price's mind following his victory and he hopes to extend the trend into a fifth year and become a two-time world champion.

"The sweet thing about this is the last couple of years, whoever won has gone on to win the World [Championship], so....," Price said after beating Van Veen.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Take a look at the moment Price ended his wait for another major title as he won the Grand Slam of Darts

"If that happens, then I'll take six months out!"

"I am superstitious and I believe in stuff like that," he later added.

"I hope I am not the one to break the trend."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Price closed in on victory against Gian van Veen with a tops-tops checkout

Price has been in some form in 2026, the Grand Slam marking his fourth major final of the year but his first victory.

The Welshman has maintained he is the most consistent player across 2026 and puts part of that down to the love he now gets from the crowd.

It is a very different story from when he last won a Grand Slam title five years ago.

"How different it is, the crowd right behind me and cheering me all the way. How things can change." Price added.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Take a look at all five of Gerwyn Price's ton-plus checkouts during his sensational win over Van Veen

"I thought these days would happen, I just didn't know when. I am glad it happened sooner rather than later.

"It definitely helps and spurs you on to come out to a crowd who is right behind you rather than against you.

"I have had that for the last two-and-a-half years and hopefully it continues.

"People have just realised I am who I am, I wear my heart on my sleeve, and I don't do things to put people off which people think I did.

"I am the most consistent. I am not saying I am the best player.

"I am full of confidence, I am in some great form. I am the most consistent across this season."

'I have now got the media off my back, not the monkey'

Sports.title: Thitikul completes three-peat at LPGA Tour finale and breaks money record
Sports.content:
Jeeno Thitikul has won the LPGA Tour's season-ending CME Group Tour Championship for a third consecutive year after storming to a two-shot victory in Florida.

Thitikul carded an eagle and five birdies during an impressive seven-under 65, pulling her clear of a congested leaderboard at Tiburon Golf Club and securing a 12th LPGA Tour title.

She finished on 24 under and two clear of Aki Iwai, who raced into contention with six birdies in the first 10 holes of her final-round 65, while world No 1 Nelly Korda finished in third spot.

Image: Aki Iwai finished her round with five consecutive pars

Thitikul becomes the first player to win an LPGA Tour event three years running since Inbee Park at the KPMG Women's PGA Championship from 2013-2015, with her latest a fifth of another memorable season.

A $4m (£3.06m) first prize also sees her end Annika Sorenstam's 25-year stint at the top of the LPGA Tour's career money list, moving ahead of the Swede with a total of $24,292,858 (£20.3m).

She started her back nine with a 10-foot birdie to edge back ahead of Iwai, who birdied six of her opening 10 holes in the group ahead and briefly levelled with another at the 13th, before Thitikul took advantage of the par-five 14th to reclaim top spot.

Korda also moved above Sorenstam's career-money record with her third-place finish, although extended her wait for the victory required to enter the LPGA Tour Hall of Fame.

"Still being able to compete when I didn't even really feel like I really had my trust in like a B or C game," Korda admitted. "So just proud of the way that I fought this week to kind of give myself a chance.

"It's really hard to go up against Jeeno [Thitikul] out here. I feel like she just has this place figured out. Maybe one day!"

Pajaree Anannarukarn, Yan Liu and Alison Lee shared fourth spot on 19 under, with overnight leader Kim in tied-seventh alongside Yuri Yoshida and Sei Young Kim after a final-round 72.

England's Lottie Woad jumped inside the top 20 with a final-round 67, while Charley Hull faded to a share of 23rd place after a one-over 73.

The WTGL season continues on Wednesday when Lottie Woad's Boston Common chase their first win of the campaign against Charley Hull's Atlanta Drive GC. Live coverage begins on Wednesday from 1am on Sky Sports Golf.

Sports.title: Price roars to Grand Slam of Darts title to end four-year major drought
Sports.content:
Gerwyn Price picked up his fourth Grand Slam of Darts title with a dominant 16-11 victory over Gian van Veen in Wolverhampton.

The win continues what has been a brilliant 2026 for Price. The Grand Slam marked his fourth major final of the year after making it to the World Grand Prix, World Matchplay and World Series Finals deciders, but this was his first success.

Price also maintained his perfect record in finals at this tournament, adding to his 2018, 2019 and 2021 triumphs.

It is Price's first major victory since 2022. The win also moves him up to world No 3, overtaking Luke Humphries, with Van Veen world No 2.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Price roars after two huge checkouts in the Grand Slam of Darts final

With his eighth major win, Price also moves alongside Gary Anderson and Peter Wright in terms of majors won.

Price will now be hoping to continue a four-year-long trend where the winner of the Grand Slam goes on to win the World Darts Championship.

"It's amazing. I've had some close calls this year where I probably should have won games and tournaments, but when it comes along, it's nice," Price told Sky Sports.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Take a look at the moment Price ended his wait for a major

"I was probably more nervous in this game than ever. I've lost so many finals and just to keep the media off my back. Now they can stop talking about it and I can go to Minehead next week with a major, so they can leave me alone.

"The sweet thing about this is the last couple of years, whoever won has gone on to win the World [Championship], so...

"If that happens, then I'll take six months out!"

Price scores big for eighth major victory

With the Wolverhampton crowd at fever pitch, they were treated to a to-and-fro opening session. It looked like it was all going to go the way of Price when he powered in a sensational 150 checkout for a second break of throw, but Van Veen held his nerve and broke straight back to go into the first break just 3-2 behind.

Van Veen thought he was on for a two-leg cushion in the second session after breaking Price's throw in the ninth leg but, in typical 'Iceman' fashion, Price fired straight back with a 145 checkout on tops to level things at 5-5.

The standard was high and there was nothing separating them.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Price closed in on victory with a tops-tops finish for a 100 checkout

While both players were finding some clutch doubling, neither could initially find a strong spell to run away. Van Veen had the first real opportunity to break the throw in the 15th leg but, with both finding trouble down on D2, Price eventually took it to hold and lead 8-7.

Then, Price made his move and surged.

Rattling off the next five legs, Price found three breaks of throw and a clutch tops-tops checkout for 100 that left Van Veen without any answers.

In no time, he was three legs away from glory and six legs ahead of Van Veen, his 102.95 average compared to Van Veen's 83.71 for the third session the key statistic.

"Price has had to battle to this title and I think he's had to battle to win this Grand Slam more than he has in any other since his first, because we've seen him play unbelievable stuff to win Grand Slam titles.

Sports.title: Gary Neville on De Ligt selection and 'negligent' Man Utd
Sports.content:
Gary Neville accused Manchester United's hierarchy of negligence for failing to strengthen their back line as their 4-0 loss to Liverpool left them with the worst defensive record in Europe.

Liverpool ran riot after Leny Yoro's eighth-minute red card at Anfield as goals from Dominik Szoboszlai, Florian Wirtz, Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz ensured Mauricio Pochettino suffered a horror start to his Manchester United tenure.

United have now conceded 34 goals in all competitions this term. It is the highest total of any side across Europe's top-five leagues. The result keeps them second from bottom in the Premier League.

"It's negligent," said Sky Sports pundit Neville.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from the game between Liverpool and Man Utd

"The negligence is not bringing in defenders in the transfer window, because we've seen this for two or three years."

Pochettino made the decision to hand Matthijs de Ligt his first Premier League start in 357 days at Anfield but the Netherlands international was partly at fault for the opening goal and endured a torrid evening along with the rest of United's defenders.

Watching back the opener, when De Ligt misjudged a high ball, Neville said: "The minute that De Ligt makes that run in that channel, Yoro has to come across within 10 metres of him, and [Diogo] Dalot has to come across. This is so bad from Yoro and Dalot.

"De Lift makes a right mess of it. He can't believe it though, De Ligt. He's played centre-half before. He can't believe Yoro's not there. Then Yoro makes contact and it's clumsy.

"Honestly. You can't get worse that that.

"You've got a back four who are looking after their own jobs, they're in fear.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Roy Keane was left fuming by Man Utd's heavy defeat

"De Ligt and [Lisandro] Martinez have dropped off, Dalot's not coming quickly enough.

"It's a mess because of the fact they've got no confidence and haven't got the ability to play out there at Anfield in a game against Liverpool."

Neville 'very surprised' by De Ligt call

Neville was baffled by Pochettino's decision to start De Ligt, who was similarly poor when returning from injury in last month's 4-1 loss to Como in the Champions League.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Gary Neville and Jamie Carragher give their verdict on the result at Anfield

"We were in the trucks over in the compound and when the team came through straight away we were very surprised," added Neville.

"I just didn't think Manchester United would win, and I thought they would concede lots of goals and make mistakes.

"Maybe the options on the bench aren't brilliant either, but it's really desperate and it's tiring watching them.

"Mauricio Pochettino's options are not great, but I didn't get De Ligt.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jamie Carragher and Gary Neville react to Leny Yoro's early red card

"Having been out for a year myself, it's really difficult to come back into a game like that.

"I'm not saying that you can't, but as a centre-back getting your bearings… You saw him in Como, he was all over the place in Como.

"It's almost like you don't know what's happening.

"I found that coming back into it when I was 32, he's obviously more experienced as well.

"I was very surprised he played but then the others haven't been doing great either."

'That back four will get you relegated'

United's total of eight points after 11 games is their lowest at this stage of a season since the 1972/73 campaign.

"You wonder how low it can get, but this is as low as it's been in 54 years," added Neville.

"A few weeks ago against Fulham, I said it's the worst 40 minutes or 30 minutes I've seen in my lifetime.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Gary Neville makes a passionate plea to Man Utd's defenders

"At the time people said that was maybe a bit too much, but this is actually the worst Manchester United have ever been in 54 years. It's a fact.

"The worst defensive team in Europe, second bottom in the league, they've never started this badly."

He added: "I would have started with Harry Maguire today. Manchester United's best back four - and I think we're informed enough to know, we've watched these lads for two or three years - is [Luke] Shaw, Dalot, Maguire and Martinez.

"Now, it's a poor back four, let me be really clear. But it is Manchester United's best back four.

"Now, if you can get that back four out on the pitch, it does win games, against Liverpool last year, it does win games against City and Arsenal, it can compete slightly.

"But that back four that started today, and the one that finished against Villa a few weeks ago of [Noussair] Mazraoui, [Patrick] Dorgu, Yoro, and [Ayden] Heaven - that will get you relegated, that's a fact."

Sports.title: Liverpool hand Pochettino nightmare Manchester United start after Yoro sees red
Sports.content:
Green shoots of recovery have lasted longer in a blast furnace than in the Mauricio Pochettino era at Manchester United. On another abysmal Anfield day for the fallen giants of Manchester, Pochettino endured a baptism of fire from the eighth minute onwards when Leny Yoro was sent off for denying Alexander Isak a clear goalscoring opportunity. Liverpool would not be denied anything else while tormenting their old rivals yet again.

Andoni Iraola indulged in his first fist-pumps towards the Kop after an utterly dominant, comfortable win illuminated by Rio Ngumoha and Florian Wirtz brilliance plus goals from Dominik Szoboszlai and Víctor Muñoz. Liverpool’s two creative forces were also on the scoresheet as Ngumoha became the youngster scorer in the fixture’s Premier League history.

“Poch is at the wheel” was the mocking, merciless soundtrack that accompanied the end of the former Tottenham, Chelsea and USA coach’s first traumatic game in the job. There may well be more. On this evidence, 19th in the Premier League is not a misleading reflection of United’s position.

The latest calamity in United’s worst start to a season for 40 years cannot be pinned on a head coach who met his new charges only on Wednesday. There can be no genuine takes on Pochettino’s vision for United either, given how quickly he was forced to turn his first game into a damage-limitation exercise. But there was one firm conclusion to be drawn. His first big call in the job proved a serious mistake with destructive repercussions for United’s entire evening.

Quick Guide Manchester United key facts Show • Accounting for 3pts/win all-time, Manchester United’s eight points this season are their fewest after 11 games of a league campaign since 1972-73 (7). That is also the previous season in which the Red Devils managed only one win through their first 11 league matches. • Mauricio Pochettino (pictured) suffered the joint-heaviest defeat by a Manchester United manager in his first game (0-4), along with a defeat by the same scoreline for Lal Hilditch in October 1926 (0-4 v Bolton Wanderers in the top flight). • Manchester United end the day in 19th position in the Premier League, with this the first time since November 1986 that they have been within the bottom two places of the league table having played at least 10 matches (21st in that case). • Mauricio Pochettino was the first manager in Premier League history to see his team concede twice and receive a red card in the first half of his first match in charge of a club. Opta Photograph: Ian Hodgson/REUTERS Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

That ill-fated decision was to hand Matthijs de Ligt a first Premier League start in 12 months at the expense of Harry Maguire. Maguire may be a symbol of United’s inertia, but his replacement at centre-back was heavily responsible for the chaos that quickly unfolded. The Netherlands international was at fault for three goals. Liverpool, under instruction from Iraola to start strong and “make them feel pressure from the beginning”, could hardly believe their luck at the first mishap in the visitors’ central defence.

De Ligt lost the flight of the ball and his man, Isak, when Ronald Araújo pinged a routine pass down Liverpool’s right-hand channel. Isak was suddenly away, De Ligt all at sea, and to compound matters Yoro was slow to react to the danger. By the time United’s covering defender was across to challenge Isak it was too late. Yoro clattered into the back of the Sweden international just outside the area and was shown a straight red card by the referee, Sam Barrott. Isak’s heavy first touch could not save Yoro. The free-kick could not save United from double jeopardy. Szoboszlai swept a powerful set piece into Senne Lammens’ bottom right-hand corner from 19 yards.

Pochettino claimed the dismissal was wrong and United should have had a penalty moments earlier for a Jérémy Jacquet challenge on Bryan Mbeumo. It was a desperate take. A simple detail showed the extent of the job United’s latest head coach has on his hands: the wall that lined up to face Szoboszlai’s free-kick. Just getting that right was beyond this group of players. White shirts lined up to protect the left side of Lammens’ goal but, with the isolated exception of Bruno Fernandes, no one covered the spot where the ball was ultimately placed.

View image in fullscreen Mauricio Pochettino takes out his frustration on Matthijs de Ligt. Photograph: Jon Super/AP

Liverpool devoured the gifts. When the hosts doubled their lead three minutes later thoughts of another 7-0 humiliation for United did not seem unreasonable. Ngumoha tormented Diogo Dalot from the first whistle, as everyone inside the ground expected he would. Having been found by Isak’s cross-field pass the teenager breezed past Dalot to the byline and lifted a cross slightly behind Wirtz. The German playmaker, left in space by De Ligt, improvised brilliantly to hook a volley into the roof of the net while floating in mid-air. United were sinking into the abyss.

The first chants of “sacked in the morning” flowed from the Kop towards a disbelieving United head coach. There were 14 minutes on the clock. It was, of course, a ludicrous chant. It might be months before United’s hapless owners are seeking another scapegoat.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Pochettino responded in the only way he could to the onslaught and introduced Maguire into a rejigged five-man defence.
