Isak got ahead of Yoro and pushed the ball forwards. It was a heavy touch and would have run on to Lammens but Yoro compounded his error by bundling Isak down on the edge of the area. He was sent off by referee Sam Barrott. Only seven minutes and 23secs had elapsed. It was the quickest sending off in United’s Premier League history. It was not a controversy. It was just a show of defensive incompetence.

A free-kick in that kind of position might as well be a penalty when Dominik Szoboszlai is standing over it. He lashed it low and hard past the edge of the United wall. Bruno Fernandes shook a half-interested leg at it. It whistled past him and bulged the corner of the United net.

MATCH FACTS Liverpool (4-2-3-1): Alisson; Araujo (Gomez 85), Jacquet, van Dijk, Kerkez; Szoboszlai, Mac Allister (Nyoni 72); Barcola (Munoz 72), Wirtz, Ngumoha (Frimpong 78); Isak (Koumas 85) Subs not used: Mamardashvili, Tsimikas, McConnell, Chiesa Booked: Barcola Goals: Szoboszlai 10, Wirtz 13, Ngumoha 66, Munoz 82 Manager: Andoni Iraola Man United (4-2-3-1): Lammens; Dalot, Yoro, De Ligt, Martinez; Tielemans (Mount 65), Mainoo (Santos 87); Mbeumo (Maguire 22), Fernandes, Dorgu (Mazraoui 65); Cunha (Zirkzee 46) Subs not used: Heaton, Heaven, Diallo, Lacey Sent off: Yoro Manager: Mauricio Pochettino Referee: Sam Barrott

Three minutes later, Liverpool were further ahead. Ngumoha embarrassed Dalot down the Liverpool left – not for the last time – and pulled a cross back for Wirtz. It was just behind the Germany playmaker but Wirtz has beautiful technique and somehow, he hooked it goalwards with his left foot and it crashed in off the underside of the bar.

United were in chaos. Pochettino looked stunned. He brought on Harry Maguire for Grand Theft Auto aficionado Bryan Mbeumo after 22 minutes. Maybe it was a bitter pill for Mbeumo. Maybe it will have just allowed him to spend more time with his PlayStation. Practice makes perfect, after all.

And so United spent the rest of the half repelling a siege of their goal. Fernandes summoned one shot on target but it dribbled apologetically through to Alisson from the edge of the area. Most of the time, though, it was like the Alamo at the United end. Maguire made one particularly heroic block from Isak.

Liverpool should have gone three-nil up just before the hour. Wirtz played a fine through ball to Barcola, who ran clear of the defence. Barcola had only Lammens to beat but instead of slotting the ball past him, he tried to dribble around him, got his feet mixed up and kicked the ball out of play.

There was frustration at Anfield. They wanted more than this. This was a chance to rub United’s noses in it, to inflict more misery on their hapless rivals. And yet, there was a sense they were letting them off the hook.

That feeling deepened when De Ligt made a dreadful mess of intercepting a lofted pass to Isak, missed his kick and fell over. Isak raced through but then blasted his shot hopelessly high and wide. Then Barcola turned De Ligt and hit another shot too high.

Liverpool could not keep missing all afternoon, though, and they finally got their third when Barcola skipped past Lisandro Martinez on the halfway line as if he wasn’t there and sprinted down the right. He squared the ball across the box to Ngumoha and Ngumoha slammed it unerringly past Lammens. Victor Munoz drilled home the fourth eight minutes from time and United’s humiliation was complete.

Sports.title: Liverpool 4-0 Man United PLAYER RATINGS: Who looked 'like a rabbit in headlights'? Who is 'playing 100 times better' than last season? And which 3/10 star 'is a shadow' of his former self?
Sports.content:
Mauricio Pochettino's Manchester United reign began in humiliating fashion as Liverpool put four past their bitter rivals at Anfield.

Pochettino's game-plan was in tatters inside 15 minutes when Leny Yoro was shown a straight red card and goals from Dominik Szoboszlai and Florian Wirtz took the game away from United.

Even after things settled down, following the introduction of Harry Maguire, United never looked capable of getting back in the game and eventually the worst defence in Europe cost them two more goals.

Rio Ngumoha, the best player on the pitch, converted after a blistering break from Bradley Barcola to make it 3-0.

Victor Munoz, sent on from the bench, added the cherry on top for Liverpool when he buried a fourth late on.

Daily Mail Sport's LEWIS STEELE and NATHAN SALT run the rule over both sets of players at Anfield...

Rio Ngumoha ran Manchester United ragged in his best display in a Liverpool shirt

Mauricio Pochettino learned in a brutal 90 minutes the size of the job he has taken on

Alisson - 7

Made a notable save from Youri Tielemans' early deflected effort but could have had his slippers on with a cuppa for most of the afternoon. Denied Bruno Fernandes late on to keep clean sheet.

Ronald Araujo - 7

A fans' favourite who wears his heart on his sleeve, activating the option to make the Barcelona loanee's stay permanent should be a foregone conclusion.

Jeremy Jacquet - 7

The big French defender looks like he has been playing alongside Virgil van Dijk for years and is a major upgrade on Ibrahima Konate.

Virgil van Dijk - 7

Seemed to enjoy the contest and why wouldn't he? The captain had a quiet afternoon with little to do which, at 35, is not the worst thing ever.

Milos Kerkez - 7

His final cross is still not what we saw at Bournemouth but the Hungary international's off-the-ball runs occupied defenders to allow Ngumoha to flourish.

Dominik Szoboszlai - 8

The best dead-ball specialist in the league, his free-kick left Senne Lammens with no chance. Has not been his best campaign but electric here.

Dominik Szoboszlai set Liverpool on their way when he rifled in the game's opening goal

Alexis Mac Allister - 7

Tenacious midfield display from the Argentine general, who is 100 times better than last season.

Bradley Barcola - 8

Like a Formula One car with pace and power to burn. His assist for Ngumoha was the highlight, even though his final ball was lacking until then.

Florian Wirtz - 9

His best performance in a Liverpool shirt. Has been superb this season but craved a display against one of the big boys. United could not get near him.

Rio Ngumoha - 9 (MOTM)

Unplayable. The most frightening thing for rival fans is that there are still levels for the 18-year-old to step up. When he does, he can be a world-beater.

Liverpool could have had more goals on the day, such was their dominance versus 10 men

Alexander Isak - 7

Could have had a hat-trick on another day but had no luck in front of goal. His overall game was notable, though: crisp passing and shrewd link-up play.

MANAGER: Andoni Iraola - 8

Needed this statement victory. Got his tactics spot on and, if anything, the 4-0 scoreline will frustrate him as it should have been more.

SUBS

Trey Nyoni (for Mac Allister 72) - 6

Victor Munoz (for Barcola 72) - 7

Jeremie Frimpong (for Ngumoha 77)

Joe Gomez (for Araujo 86)

Lewis Koumas (for Isak 86)

MANCHESTER UNITED (4-2-3-1)

Senne Lammens - 4

Took a rollicking - rightly - from Fernandes for his positioning as Szoboszlai's free-kick goes in on his side, but he responded well. Made a good save to deny Mac Allister's low drive down 2-0 and later tipped Szoboszlai's drive from distance over. In the end, as it is every week, he's let down by the hopeless defence in front of him.

Diogo Dalot - 2

Looked like men against boys trying to shut down man of the match Ngumoha, only for the 27-year-old to be made to look like the boy by the electric 18-year-old. Didn't improve when Victor Munoz came on – and scored. Looked like a rabbit in headlights.

Leny Yoro - 3

An Anfield experience that ended after eight minutes thanks to a debatable red card. Clumsy decision making, not least with Isak not in control of the ball, and he was let down by De Ligt and the officials… but the Frenchman's catalogue of mistakes is piling up and it's cause for concern.

Leny Yoro (right) was sent off after eight minutes, but the decision is up for fierce debate

Matthijs de Ligt - 2

Making his first Premier League start in 357 days, De Ligt looked every bit as rusty and compromised as that stat would suggest. Badly sold Yoro short for the Isak run that saw Yoro sent off. Had no idea where Wirtz was for the second goal and mistakes didn't cease in the second half. A display that had you feeling sorry for him.

Lisandro Martinez - 3

Never looked comfortable trying to keep Barcola under wraps and despite being caught out on more than one occasion in the first half, he didn't learn his lesson, dived in, and Barcola burst free down the right to tee up Ngumoha for the third. Did make a crucial block to prevent it becoming 4-0, even if it was to be in vain.

Kobbie Mainoo - 5

Best player in a United shirt on the day, even if it was a painfully low bar. Mauricio Pochettino is having to quickly run the rule over which players he can depend on in the coming weeks and months. Mainoo showed in spells here, namely when he was running through lines, that he should be able to answer the call.

Youri Tielemans - 3

Really poor. The Belgian was caught ball-watching as Wirtz converted brilliantly to make it 2-0. Guilty of giving the ball away in some really dangerous positions. Had a strike from distance that was a rare attempt for United but he looks a shadow of the player that thrived at Aston Villa.

Youri Tielemans (left) looks a shadow of the player that thrived at Aston Villa last season

Bryan Mbeumo - 4

Sacrificed for the greater good as Liverpool looked set to run riot. Puzzling, though, given Mbeumo looked to be one of the only United players capable of beating a man when he burst past Kerkez during the opening 20-minute nightmare. Hooked with 11 touches.

Bruno Fernandes - 5

Spoke in the build-up about contract negotiations being put on hold and that's probably for the best given that is the least of United's problems. Created a handful of chances but when the big chance came, being played through on goal, he lacked the athleticism to trouble Jacquet.

Patrick Dorgu - 4

Started Pochettino's first game in a more advanced role off the left but the tactics went out the window when it all unravelled inside 15 minutes. Got away with murder when he let Barcola run off him. Fortunate the wasteful Liverpool attacker fluffed that chance.

Matheus Cunha - 4

A passenger in a game that was taken away from United as soon as the red card was brandished. A willing runner so to see him taken off for Zirkzee at half-time was somewhat headscratching.

HEAD COACH: Mauricio Pochettino - 5

Only been in position a couple of days and he's not a miracle worker. Certainly not immune to criticism - choosing De Ligt when he is in this kind of form was a choice - but he saw first-hand the size of the job on his hands. He's in a relegation battle.

Pochettino does not have time to fix the numerous issues that are plaguing United's defence

SUBS

Harry Maguire (for Bryan Mbeumo, 22) - 5

Enormous block to deny Isak a third Liverpool goal and did help steady the ship in the first half when United were rocking. By the time the final whistle came he'd been brought down to the level of others.

Joshua Zirkzee (for Matheus Cunha, 46) - 3

Came on at the break in the hope of giving United a focal point to get away from the edge of their own box. Instead he kept giving away possession cheaply.

Mason Mount (for Youri Tielemans, 65) - 4

Made no meaningful contribution on the game. A hugely expensive investment by United that has never come close to paying it back.

Noussair Mazraoui (for Patrick Dorgu, 65) - 4

Andrey Santos (for Kobbie Mainoo, 88)

REFEREE: Sam Barrott - 7

Isak's touch was heavy so the 'denial of goal-scoring opportunity' will be debated but it was the right call. Few other notable incidents.

Sports.title: Hull reignite genuine survival hopes with late Oli McBurnie double to down Brighton, as talk of Seagulls emulating Leicester City-style fairytale is made to look foolish
Sports.content:
When Brighton owner Tony Bloom was asked about his club’s title prospects last week, he suggested they could emulate Leicester City’s 2015-16 fairytale and win the Premier League. It was a bold claim, yet Fabian Hurzeler’s men looked anything but title aspirants after being downed by Oli McBurnie’s dramatic late double for newly-promoted Hull City. Brighton have been the most credible challengers to Arsenal so far this season. That cannot be denied. With Manchester City wobbling alarmingly, and the rest of the traditional big guns largely off the title pace, the Seagulls have at least given Mikel Arteta’s champions something to think about. But this bitterly cold afternoon in East Yorkshire was a reality check for Hurzeler’s men and a harsh lesson in taking the chances that come your way. Brighton didn’t and McBurnie most certainly did, firing home clinically from close range twice in added time shortly after Joao Costinha had been sent off. Oli McBurnie scored a late brace to secure a brilliant three points for Hull against Brighton McBurnie has made a habit of leaving it late – the rejuvenated Scotland striker struck a 95th-minute winner in the Championship play-off final against Middlesbrough at Wembley in May. Hull had gone eight Premier League games without a win before Brighton’s visit and this success lifted them to 11th. Tigers boss Sergej Jakirovic said of McBurnie: 'I’ve never had any doubts over a ‘Braveheart’ like Oli because he’s a natural leader and very important for us.' Asked where the setback left Brighton’s title hopes, Hurzeler said: 'We don’t focus on the table – we focus on performances and how we can make the right improvements into the team. 'That’s the same if we had won or lost, but today showed there are still things we need to do better. That’s what we will do and then see what the outcome will be.' Brighton arrived as favourites and could have cut Arsenal's lead at the top of the table SEAGULLS DENIED BY TZOLAKIS Hull were indebted to a remarkable display from their Greek goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis, who reduced Brighton to an afternoon of frustration and futility. The visitors had 10 attempts at goal during the first half alone, forcing Hull’s summer signing into a string of fine saves and also being denied by the woodwork. At times the Seagulls’ pretty patterns threatened to cut the Tigers apart as the likes of Maxim De Cuyper, Diego Gomez and the effervescent Pascal Gross – on his 300th appearance for the club – knitted them together superbly. Georginio Rutter was involved in a move which saw De Cuyper cross low from the left flank to the onrushing Gomez, whose close-range effort was superbly saved by Tzolakis. That set the tone for an outstanding display by the 24-year-old Greece international, who arrived in the summer from Olympiacos as part of the newly-promoted Tigers’ £150million spending spree which saw 18 players signed. Hull lacked nothing in spirit and fight but Brighton had the quality and constantly threatened to open up their hosts. As half-time approached, Rutter saw a close-range shot repelled by Tzolakis after Yasin Ayari’s effort rebounded off the crossbar. The Tigers were constantly grateful to their goalkeeper, who made another save to keep out an effort from Gomez on the stroke of half-time. Tzolakis continued to prove unbeatable in the second half too, and his opposite number Bart Verbruggen was left grateful to the woodwork after a cross-shot from substitute Sorba Thomas hit the crossbar. Mohamed Belloumi was also a lingering threat for Hull on the right flank and he should have scored after cutting infield before firing wastefully wide. Konstantinos Tzolakis (right) produced a remarkable display to keep Brighton out McBURNIE SEIZES CENTRE STAGE As the game wore on, there was an inescapable feeling that Brighton could be punished for their wastefulness as Hull showed the kind of courage which deserves, and usually gets, its rewards. Regan Slater cleared a shot from Charalampos Kostoulas off the line before Brighton lost Joao Costinha to a second yellow card with a minute remaining. The Tigers sensed blood, pouring forward to lead in the first minute of added time as McBurnie expertly sidefooted them in front from Lucas Gourna-Douath’s neat pass to cap a delightful flowing move. Moments before the final whistle, Hull struck again as McBurnie swept home from close range again from Mo Belloumi’s assist. Cue delirium in the home stands. McBurnie took the acclaim but Tzolakis was Hull’s star man as Jakirovic acknowledged: 'Tzolakis was amazing and we could have been two or three-nil down without his saves. 'We stayed alive because of him and then won the game at the end. Ciao!' Hull had failed to win since beating Manchester United and Coventry in their opening two games in August. Hull reignited their survival hopes with a precious win against an in-form team Crucially, however, they have been competitive in every game this season and are now unbeaten in six home matches. Can they survive? 'Of course, and every win is so important,' declared Jakirovic. 'I wish this feeling I have now would never stop but I know how demanding this league is.' Hurzeler could certainly attest to that.

Sports.title: Scott McTominay and girlfriend Cam Reading announce pregnancy: Ex-Man United star celebrates 'precious gift' months after having heart surgery
Sports.content:
Napoli star Scott McTominay and his girlfriend Cam Reading have announced they're expecting their first child together. The couple shared a joint post on Instagram with one picture of them holding up an ultrasound image, another of Reading reclining in a bikini and a third of the pregnancy test itself. They revealed the news on the same day McTominay broke Napoli's three-game losing streak, scoring the winner in a 1-0 victory over Torino. The couple wrote: 'The most precious gift, a lifetime of love.' McTominay, 29, and Reading have settled into life in Italy after he joined from Man United and revived his career, winning the Scudetto and earning Player of the Year honours. It remains to be seen whether the baby will be born in Italy or back in the UK but the couple were overjoyed at sharing their happy news. It is not exactly clear when McTominay and Reading first crossed paths but they have at least been together since the summer of 2023, when they were pictured on a boat trip in Greece. Cam Reading and Scott McTominay shared the news that they're expecting a baby Reading posted this picture of her bump on her Instagram page and wrote of a 'precious gift' Reading, a director at asset management firm Fortress Capital partners, has seen her personal celebrity skyrocket in that time, zooming up from 10,000 Instagram followers to over 90,000. According to La Repubblica, they have moved into a house by Lago Patria, a coastal lake near the suburb of Giugliano. There, McTominay can be by the seaside quickly after popping out of his door and is only around a 20-minute drive from Napoli's training centre. The couple regularly share photos from their new life together in Italy and McTominay is adored by fans having repeatedly delivered in big moments, none more so than on the final day of the 2024-25 season when an acrobatic strike put Napoli ahead as they clinched the title over Inter Milan. This season has been less straightforward for McTominay. The Scotland international underwent heart surgery after being diagnosed with 'a mild benign arrhythmia', which is an abnormal or irregular heart rhythm deemed non-serious and posing no significant risk to overall health. Before the surgery, the British Heart Foundation explained that the procedure McTominay was having would see heat or cold energy used to create tiny scars in the heart to block faulty signals and restore a typical heartbeat. The procedure took place at the start of September in Manchester, and he was initially supposed to be on the sidelines for two weeks before returning to training. But he was ruled out of Scotland action during the international break and is now back on the grass with Napoli, scoring the winner against Torino on Saturday. McTominay and Reading also posted this snap of the ultrasound and positive test The midfielder scored the winner on Saturday for Napoli against Torino He has now scored 33 goals in 92 matches across all competitions with the Partenopei and remains one of Serie A's leading lights. The Italian press gushed over his contribution on Saturday, with Corriere dello Sport writing: 'He played with fire in his belly. 'Three shots in the opening 16 minutes; seven in total—three on target— and a decisive goal (his fourth against Torino, his favourite Serie A opponent, along with Inter), plus the charisma of a leader.'
