Sports.title: Agit Kabayel Wants Unification After Facing Nelson Hysa
Sports.content:
Agit Kabayel could not get the heavyweights he wanted for his first WBC title defense. Instead, he gets 42-year-old Nelson Hysa on November 28 in Düsseldorf. He is already looking past Saturday. Kabayel wants another belt next, though one possible opponent has to get through a fighter Kabayel already stopped.

“I want only the big fights, but none of the big guys are available. Now I will teach him respect,” said Kabayel in an interview with Queensberry Promotions. The unbeaten champion meets Hysa at Merkur Spiel-Arena, with DAZN streaming the main card from 1 p.m. ET.

Hrgovic Has Mandatory Ahead Of Unification

IBF champion Filip Hrgovic is one option, except Sky Sports reported he is headed toward a mandatory defense against Frank Sanchez in Croatia in early 2027. Hrgovic also wants WBO champion Daniel Dubois. The two faced off after Dubois defended his belt against Fabio Wardley in October.

Sanchez gives Kabayel plenty of reason to watch that IBF fight. Kabayel stopped Sanchez in seven rounds in 2024 on the Oleksandr Usyk vs. Tyson Fury undercard. If Sanchez beats Hrgovic, Kabayel could land a rematch with a second belt on the line. If Hrgovic wins, both Kabayel and Dubois will be chasing him.

Dubois holds the WBO title. He also shares promoter Frank Warren with Kabayel. That gives Warren a clean path to put two belts together while Hrgovic deals with Sanchez, provided both fighters want it. Dubois has also talked about a third fight with Usyk, so Kabayel is not the only name on his list.

What Kabayel Faces In Hysa

Kabayel (27-0, 19 KOs) sat ringside when Hrgovic stopped Moses Itauma for the vacant IBF belt in August. Hysa stopped Thomas Narmo in two rounds on that same undercard, then called out Kabayel and promised a knockout. Now Hysa (25-0, 23 KOs) gets his shot in Germany on Albanian Independence Day.

Hysa carries a streak of 19 straight knockouts into the ring, though he did not turn pro until age 37 and has spent four years beating regional club fighters and aging journeymen like Danny Williams and Patrick Korte. Kabayel stopped Arslanbek Makhmudov, Sanchez, Zhilei Zhang, and Damian Knyba in consecutive fights. He took the interim belt against Zhang before being elevated to full champion in June after Usyk vacated the WBC title.

“Nelson is my focus now. But after this fight, it’s a unification fight,” said Kabayel. Getting past Hysa is the easy part on paper, though a 42-year-old puncher who has never gone past six rounds still has to be put away before Warren can start calling Dubois.

Sports.title: Anthony Joshua Eyes Retirement Ahead Of Tyson Fury Fight
Sports.content:
Anthony Joshua says he expects to retire “pretty soon,” and beating Tyson Fury in Cardiff might give him an easier exit than another loss. At 37, Joshua gets his shot at settling an old score on December 11 at Principality Stadium. Netflix will stream the card.

“When am I going to retire? Pretty soon. I’m getting old now. From an athlete’s point of view, I’m getting old,” said Joshua in an interview with The Sun. He said he had few years left in boxing and brought up investing in longtime sponsor Under Armour once his career ends. He did not set a date.

Through much of his career, Joshua has been at the top of the heavyweight division since winning Olympic gold in 2012.

What A Fury Win Does For Joshua

Joshua stopped Wladimir Klitschko in 2017, outpointed Joseph Parker to pick up the WBO belt in 2018, then avenged his 2019 stoppage loss to Andy Ruiz Jr. six months later by boxing behind his jab for 12 rounds. He proved in that rematch he could stick to a disciplined game plan instead of trading hooks in the pocket.

Fury ended Klitschko’s title run in 2015 and built his reputation on two wins over Deontay Wilder. Both British heavyweights later lost twice to Oleksandr Usyk. Beating Fury settles who owns the head-to-head edge after years of stalled negotiations.

It is tempting to say age is catching up to Joshua, though his problems started back in 2017 when a 40-year-old Wladimir Klitschko put him on the canvas and nearly finished him. Two years later, fringe contender Andy Ruiz Jr. knocked him out in 2019. Then came two losses to Oleksandr Usyk and the fifth-round knockout against Daniel Dubois in 2024.

Joshua’s stamina and punch resistance flaws were there from the beginning, even if Eddie Hearn’s careful matchmaking hid them for years after Joshua’s disputed 2012 Olympic gold medal. Usyk and Dubois simply stripped away the cover. At 37, putting Joshua in with Filip Hrgovic, Agit Kabayel, Moses Itauma, or Frank Sanchez would go badly.

What Joshua Faces In Cardiff

Joshua’s exit would cost British promoters their biggest stadium draw, though that is their problem after December 11. Joshua’s problem is surviving 12 rounds against a 6-foot-9 heavyweight who still knows how to lean on smaller men and spoil their rhythm. He cannot afford to leave his chin up in the pocket the way he did against Dubois. If Joshua wins, he gets to walk away on his own terms. If Fury beats him, retirement stops being a choice he gets to time himself.

Sports.title: Aaron Pryor Overwhelms Gaetan Hart In Six Rounds
Sports.content:
Aaron Pryor never gave Gaétan Hart a chance to settle into their November 22, 1980 title fight at Riverfront Coliseum in Cincinnati. Pryor dropped the Canadian challenger three times and stopped him in the sixth round, keeping his WBA and The Ring junior welterweight belts.

Understandably, referee Roberto Ramírez Sr. stepped in at 2:09 to stop the contest. Hart was pinned in a corner, bleeding, and taking clean shots with nothing coming back.

At 25, Pryor was already a nightmare matchup for anyone at 140 pounds. He came into the fight with an unbeaten record, fresh off flattening Antonio Cervantes in four rounds in the same arena three months earlier.

Hart, a 27-year-old lightweight champion from Buckingham, Quebec, brought legitimate fight-ending power into his first world title shot. It didn’t matter. Pryor forced a pace that kept Hart in a constant state of defense, taking away his leverage before he could ever set his feet to throw heavy shots.

What Followed Hart To Cincinnati

Hart carried dark history into Ohio after two brutal fights in Canada earlier that year. In May, he stopped Ralph Racine in the 12th round of a Canadian lightweight title bout, putting Racine into a coma that ended his career. One month later in Montreal, Hart stopped Cleveland Denny in the 10th round. Denny died 16 days later.

Opponents in Canada made the mistake of letting Hart plant his feet and unload. Pryor never gave him the chance. He backed Hart up in the first round and dropped him 20 seconds into the second. Hart beat the count, then went down again before the bell. He was gassed out before the fight even got started.

Hart Couldn’t Survive Pryor’s Pace

Hart absorbed heavy shots in the third without going down and had a brief spell of offense in the fourth before Pryor took back control and knocked out his mouthpiece. Early in the fifth, a punch buckled Hart’s knees. He steadied himself and landed two crisp lefts that snapped Pryor’s head back, the exact kind of heavy shots that had ruined opponents in Canada. Pryor walked straight through them without getting hurt.

Hart landed first in the sixth, too. Pryor answered with a right hook that sent him down for an eight count, then chased him into the corner until Ramírez waved it off. Pryor was already running away on the cards, leading 50 to 45 on two and 50 to 43 on the third.

Pryor went to 27 and 0 and knocked out his next four challengers before stopping Alexis Argüello twice. He finished 39 and 1 with 35 knockouts and made the Hall of Fame in 1996. Hart never fought for a world title again and later turned up in the documentary The Steak. Nobody at 140 pounds could take Pryor’s punches or survive that pace in 1980.

Sports.title: Liam Paro Sets 24-Hour VADA Deadline For Devin Haney
Sports.content:
IBF welterweight champion Liam Paro has given WBO champion Devin Haney 24 hours to enroll in VADA testing, or he will walk away from their December 20 unification fight in San Francisco. That is a pretty bold ultimatum from a guy entering the biggest payday of his career, especially when Haney is the A-side drawing the crowd at the Chase Center.

No Limit promoter Matt Rose confirmed the deadline on Sunday morning after Paro called Haney out on social media over the delay.

“We’re very disappointed they [Team Haney] have failed to enroll in VADA testing,” Rose told Fox Sports Australia. “One of the first things we agreed to when negotiating this fight was that VADA testing would take place. So now we’re giving them 24 hours …”

Paro already went after Haney on X over the weekend, questioning why the three-division titleholder hadn’t signed the paperwork yet despite preaching about clean boxing for the past two years.

“@realdevinhaney you preach serious boxing and speak out against PEDS, yet we’re still waiting for you to agree to VADA testing to begin. What’s the hold up???” wrote Paro.

Haney fired back quickly, reminding everyone about his testing track record and taking another shot at Ryan Garcia, who tested positive for ostarine after their April 2024 bout.

“This is will be my 14th consecutive fight using VADA testing,” Haney wrote. “Over 65 clean tests. Thanks for tagging the cheater.. the one that got popped for PEDS.”

The Problem With The Paperwork

If Haney has already gone through more than 65 VADA tests without a single issue, what is taking so long to get the forms signed for December 20? You can understand why Paro (25-1, 15 KOs) is suspicious. Haney spent all of 2024 and 2025 demanding 24/7 year-round testing, filing lawsuits against Garcia, and lecturing everyone about drug cheats. Now that he is moving up to 147 pounds to face a tough Australian southpaw, the enrollment is suddenly dragging out less than a month before fight night.

Paro already got under Haney’s skin at their launch press conference when Team Haney showed up nearly half an hour late.

“I don’t want any excuses or lawyers,” Paro said across the stage. “That’s what happened last time, isn’t it?”

Team Haney has until Monday to get the paperwork submitted. If they miss that deadline, Paro can pack his bags in Las Vegas and leave Haney scrambling for a replacement on December 20.

Sports.title: David Morrell Stops Julio Rodriguez in First Round
Sports.content:
David Morrell (13-2, 10 KOs) stopped Julio de Jesus Rodriguez (27-11, 24 KOs) by first-round TKO on Saturday night, November 21, at the Coliseo Carlos “Teo” Cruz in Santo Domingo, Dominican Republic.

The Cuban southpaw hurt Rodriguez with clean power shots and staggered him before the referee stepped in. Their light heavyweight bout was scheduled for 10 rounds on the Shuan Boxing card, though Morrell needed less than one in his first fight in over six months, getting his first win since edging Imam Khataev by split decision in July 2025.

The fight lasted less than a round, yet Morrell immediately fell into the same pattern. Rodriguez walked forward, and Morrell froze behind his shell guard rather than letting his hands go.

Rodriguez simply lacked the quality to make him pay for it. Once Morrell opened up, he clipped Rodriguez with a right hand to the back of the head that sent the 44-year-old backing toward a corner. Sensing Rodriguez was hurt, Morrell unloaded several hard punches until the referee stepped in and waved it off.

Rodriguez brought six straight defeats into Saturday’s fight, five of them inside the distance. The Dominican veteran had 24 knockouts on his record, but his recent form gave little reason to believe he could test Morrell or take him into the later rounds.

Morrell badly needed this victory after getting stopped in the tenth round by late replacement Zak Chelli in Manchester. That loss came on the heels of a unanimous decision defeat to David Benavidez in February 2025, plus a rough night five months later when Imam Khataev dropped him.

At 28, Morrell looks like he hasn’t improved or changed his fighting style at all. Whenever an opponent attacks, he still covers up behind a static shell and waits for them to stop throwing, the exact habit that caused him major trouble against Radivoje Kalajdzic, David Benavidez, and Imam Khataev before Chelli treated him like a heavy bag and stopped him.

Getting past an aging club fighter in Santo Domingo hides the flaw for one night, though against any durable light heavyweight who refuses to stop punching, Morrell will be right back in the same trouble.

Sports.title: Shakur Stevenson Hedges Ahead of Muratalla Purse Bid
Sports.content:
Shakur Stevenson is already building an escape route before the bids are even opened. Asked about his next move, the WBO light welterweight champion waved off talk of an Ashton Sylve bout as nonexistent and left a telling hedge on mandatory challenger Raymond Muratalla.

“To take over the sport of boxing and give the fans every fight they want to see, anybody can get it! If Muratalla has to be the first example, then so be it,” Stevenson told Mike Coppinger on X.

That word “if” does all the talking ahead of the November 30 purse bid, especially since Sylve’s promoter, Amer Abdallah, already went on record saying he hopes to get a deal done.

Stevenson enters the bid as a free agent after splitting with Zuffa Boxing. He has no house promoter with a reason to bid high to keep his belt and future fights in-house. If Matchroom or Top Rank sees this as a pay-per-view, it has to figure out how many buys the fight can generate against the cost of paying both men and putting on an undercard.

At a 75/25 split, a $2 million bid pays Shakur $1.5 million. A $2.5 million bid gets him $1.875 million. Would either figure get him to sign? Muratalla makes that a harder decision. Stevenson could pick off William Zepeda with clean counters as Zepeda came forward.

After enjoying huge purses at Turki Alalshikh’s table on Riyadh Season cards, Stevenson won’t be happy settling for table scraps in a standard U.S. purse bid. He could drop the WBO belt if the winning number comes in low, yet vacating it leaves him chasing deals with Devin Haney, Ryan Garcia, or Richardson Hitchins without a title to bring to the table.

None of those fighters have a reason to overpay a beltless free agent coming off a long layoff. If Stevenson turns down the November 30 bid, he will quickly learn how hard it is to demand Riyadh Season money when you no longer hold a title or a promotional deal.

Sports.title: Chase DeMoor Volunteers To  Step In And Face Deontay Wilder
Sports.content:
Since Jai Opetaia withdrew from his scheduled fight against former WBC world heavyweight champion Deontay Wilder, many well-known heavyweights have asked to fill the December 11th void.

Well-known heavyweights such as Derek Chisora, Jarrell Miller, Frazer Clarke, and Dillian Whyte are all willing to step in on short notice. In addition, a lesser-known heavyweight is also volunteering his services.

Chase DeMoor has thrown his name into the proverbial hat because he wants the opportunity to face Wilder. Some boxing fans are probably reading the name and thinking, who is Chase DeMoor?

A product of Eatonville, Washington, Chase DeMoor led the NCAA Division II in blocked kicks in 2018 as a defensive lineman for Central Washington University. In 2021, he appeared on the Netflix reality TV show Too Hot To Handle.

Soon after, DeMoor participated in an exhibition boxing match against Cory Wharton. In November 2022, DeMoor made his pro debut against Josh Brueckner, and He went viral for his comedic-looking punching technique.

After losing his first two professional fights, Chase DeMoor improved his technique and put together a winning streak. An already popular figure, DeMoor gained more notoriety when he defeated Andrew Tate in a Misfits Boxing bout in 2025.

Now, Chase DeMoor (7-2-1, 7 KOs) wants to reach new heights as he has volunteered to step in to face hard-hitting former WBC heavyweight world champion Deontay “The Bronze Bomber” Wilder (45-4-1, 43 KOs).

In his most recent ring appearance in August 2026, Chase DeMoor stopped Kevin Nagle in the fifth round and won the vacant WBC USA Silver heavyweight title. DeMoor has a solid fanbase, but skeptics also don’t view him as a legitimate boxer.

DeMoor is volunteering his services because he has a passion for boxing and he wants to silence the doubters. The odds of DeMoor getting the Wilder fight are slim, but if he gets it, does DeMoor have a path to victory?

The heavyweights who give Deontay Wilder trouble are 20 to 50 pounds bigger than him; they know how to neutralize his right hand, and they are very skilled. DeMoor has the size, but he doesn’t have the skills or the IQ to neutralize Wilder’s right hand.

Chase DeMoor wants a chance to prove he can be competitive against high-level competition. Hypothetically, if this match were made, DeMoor would bring in casual viewers, and Wilder could get an electrifying tune-up.

Sports.title: Granit Stein Stops Marius Antonietti in Five
Sports.content:
Granit Stein stopped Marius Antonietti 28 seconds into the fifth round to win the vacant IBO International super middleweight title Saturday at the Maritim Hotel in Ingolstadt, Germany. Referee Marco Morales halted the scheduled 10-round main event when Antonietti’s corner threw in the towel after a knockdown. Burim Syleyjmani’s Fides Sports Promotion presented the card, which aired on DAZN.

Stein (22-2-1, 12 KOs), fighting in his hometown, controlled the first three rounds before rocking Romania’s Antonietti (23-6, 19 KOs) with several lead right hands in the fourth. Another right to the chin sent Antonietti to the canvas early in the fifth.

Undercard Results

Heavyweight Luis “El Expreso” José Marín García (18-14-1, 13 KOs) stopped Albon Pervizaj (19-3, 14 KOs) for the second time, winning their scheduled 10-round rematch at 1:04 of the eighth. Pervizaj bloodied García’s nose in the third, and García lost a point for repeated holding in the fifth. Both fighters looked exhausted by the seventh. García dropped Pervizaj in the eighth, and Pervizaj got up but walked away and did not continue.

Kastriot “Super” Sopa (10-1, 5 KOs) knocked down southpaw Victor García (16-8, 13 KOs) three times in the third round, each time with a right hand. The scheduled 10-round bout ended at 1:28 of the third.

Chamseddine “Chamse” Lemjid (15-0, 11 KOs) stopped Michel “El Gallo de Oro” Marcano (43-17-1, 37 KOs) to win the German International title. Lemjid dropped Marcano with a right to the chin in the closing seconds of the fourth round. Marcano got up, but the fight was waved off at 2:59.

WBO European light heavyweight champion Nick Hannig (15-2-1, 8 KOs) outlanded Slavisa Simeunovic (42-97-1, 34 KOs) over the first two rounds of their scheduled six-round bout. Simeunovic retired with a nose injury, and the stoppage was recorded at 0:01 of the third.

Welterweight Rigon Demaku (1-0, 1 KO) dropped Dennis Neuer (2-43, 0 KOs) twice in the opening round to win his professional debut. The scheduled four-rounder ended at 2:27.

Super middleweight Bleron Gashi (1-0, 1 KO) also won his professional debut, dropping Alen Dozo (1-11, 0 KOs) twice in the first round. The scheduled four-round bout was stopped at 2:17.

Cruiserweight Mohammad “Montana” Gholami (1-0, 1 KO) won his professional debut after dropping Goran Panic (2-34, 1 KO) twice in the first round. A shoulder injury ended the scheduled four-round bout between rounds, with the stoppage recorded at 0:01 of the second.

Ghana News.title: GAFM resolves regulatory status with GTEC, clarifies professional certification role
Ghana News.content:
The Global Academy of Finance and Management (GAFM), USA, says it has resolved a regulatory discrepancy with the Ghana Tertiary Education Commission (GTEC) following engagements and the submission of documents on its international recognition and professional accreditations.

In a press release dated November 23, 2026, the organisation said GTEC removed it from its list of unrecognised universities on August 28, 2026, and maintained the exclusion in its subsequent September, October and November directories.

GAFM said the resolution reflects its status as an international professional certification body and standards organisation, rather than a university or an institution that awards academic degrees and diplomas.

It stressed that it had never sought recognition in Ghana as an academic university and did not present its professional certifications as academic qualifications.

According to the organisation, its certifications are designed to demonstrate specialised professional knowledge and competencies. The requirements may include relevant education, examinations, work experience, adherence to ethical standards and continuing professional development.

GAFM said its credentials operate within the professional certification sector, citing designations administered by international bodies such as the Chartered Financial Analyst (CFA) and Project Management Professional (PMP) as examples of professional credentials.

It, however, emphasised that its certifications are not substitutes for academic degrees, government-issued licences or statutory examinations required by law.

GAFM explains international quality certifications

The organisation also highlighted its international quality certifications, including ISO 9001 for Quality Management Systems, ISO 21001 for Educational Organisations and ISO 29993 for Learning Services Outside Formal Education.

It said the certifications provide independent verification of aspects of its quality management systems and learning services.

GAFM clarified, however, that these standards do not amount to university accreditation.

A representative of the organisation welcomed what it described as GTEC's decision, saying the development would help ensure that professional credentials are properly distinguished from academic qualifications.

The representative said GAFM supported the accurate classification of professional certification bodies, adding that the resolution would help protect the integrity of Ghana's academic landscape and regulatory framework.

The organisation said it remained committed to transparency and continued cooperation with GTEC on international quality assurance standards.

GAFM issues professional certifications, chartered designations and continuing education credentials in finance, management and related fields.

Ghana News.title: Barcelona return top of La Liga with Villarreal win
Ghana News.content:
Fermin Lopez has scored eight La Liga goals this season

Barcelona scored three goals in 10 minutes to return to the top of La Liga with a victory over Villarreal at Spotify Nou Camp.

Villarreal scored twice in the opening seven minutes, with Tajon Buchanan and a rifled effort from Tani Oluwaseyi, leaving the home fans stunned.

It is the first time the Blaugrana have conceded twice in the opening seven minutes of a league match since November 1981, against Real Zaragoza.

After 23 minutes, Oluwaseyi fouled Lamine Yamal in the box, and a penalty was awarded after a video assistant referee (VAR) review, but the Spain international dragged it wide.

Gerard Martin headed over from close range just before the break as Barcelona struggled to make the most of their chances.

But Barca came out with more attacking intent in the second half, and Martin made amends, heading home from Pedri's cross to reduce the deficit.

Fermin Lopez slotted home from Lamine Yamal's pass across the box to equalise for Hansi Flick's side on the hour mark.

Eric Garcia's cross was turned into his own net by Villarreal defender Pau Navarro, giving Barca their first lead of the match in the 67th minute.

Navarro's afternoon worsened when he received a second yellow for a foul on Barca captain Raphinha in stoppage time.

Villarreal manager Inigo Perez has now managed six matches against Barca without winning (one draw, five losses).

Barca lead rivals Real Madrid by three points and face Sabah in the Champions League on Wednesday (17:45 GMT).

Ghana News.title: Francis Amissah joins Martell’s Swift Academy in Accra
Ghana News.content:
Ghanaian public relations consultant Francis Amissah, popularly known in entertainment circles as Banks, is set to participate in the Accra edition of Martell’s Swift Academy, an initiative aimed at supporting the development of emerging African creatives.

Amissah, founder and Chief Executive Officer of Elite PR, brings more than a decade of experience in public relations and communications to the programme.

Through Elite PR, he has worked with several artistes and entertainment personalities, including E.L, Wendy Shay, Zlatan, D-Black, the Mitch Brothers, Dulcie Boateng, Mark Asari and RCee.

His work has focused on securing media coverage, strengthening the visibility of talent and connecting creatives with wider audiences.

Amissah says the academy will provide an opportunity to exchange ideas, build industry connections and gain fresh perspectives to support his work in the creative sector.

“I’m glad to be part of this experience. Beyond the opportunity to connect with people in the industry, I look forward to learning, exchanging ideas, and gaining new perspectives that will contribute to my growth and the work I do within the creative space,” he said.

The Accra edition of the Swift Academy, created by Martell and curated by Africa House, is scheduled to run from November 22 to December 19, 2026.

The programme will bring together selected creatives for mentorship sessions, masterclasses and other activities designed to encourage professional development and collaboration within Ghana's creative industry.

Its activities will include a welcome mixer, a group panel discussion, one-on-one mentorship sessions, a workshop day and a music showcase.

The academy's facilitators and resource persons include Ghanaian singer-songwriter Gyakie, rapper M.anifest, award-winning music producer Juls, cultural curator Maxwell Adjavon and talent manager Therese Akua Jones.

Their sessions will draw on experience across music, talent development, cultural programming and the business of entertainment.

For Amissah, participation in the programme offers an opportunity to broaden his professional network and deepen his understanding of the creative industry beyond his established work in public relations.

The academy is expected to bring together emerging and established players in Ghana's creative ecosystem for learning and collaboration.

Ghana News.title: Ashanti NDC Communications Officer Kabore endorses Dr Sammy Ayeh for Deputy National Communications Officer role
Ghana News.content:
Mahmud Kabore (L) & Dr Sammy Ayeh (R).

The newly elected Ashanti Regional Communications Officer of the National Democratic Congress (NDC), Mahmud Kabore, has endorsed Dr Sammy Ayeh for the position of Deputy National Communications Officer, urging party delegates to prioritise competence, experience and continuity in the forthcoming national executive elections.

In a Facebook post on Friday, November 20, 2026, Mr Kabore drew parallels between Dr Ayeh’s candidature and the experience of the party’s former National Communications Officer, Sammy Gyamfi, who, he said, faced similar criticisms over his age and experience before his election in 2018.

He argued that Mr Gyamfi’s eventual success demonstrated why party delegates should look beyond age and other criticisms when assessing candidates for leadership positions.

“Thankfully, the delegates of our great party at the time demonstrated remarkable political wisdom. They refused to be swayed by name-calling, character assassination, smear campaigns and unsubstantiated allegations. Instead, they looked beyond age, recognised ability, rewarded dedication and voted overwhelmingly for competence,” he wrote.

Mr Kabore said the experience should serve as a lesson to Dr Ayeh, whom he urged to remain focused on his campaign and allow his record of service and commitment to the party to speak for him.

“My brother, Dr Sammy Ayeh, I share this history with you because I believe there are important lessons to be learnt from it. Do not be distracted by the noise. Remain focused, articulate your vision, engage the delegates and allow your record of service, competence and commitment to speak for you,” he stated.

Kabore highlights Ayeh's experience and party credentials

In justifying his endorsement, the Ashanti Regional Communications Officer highlighted Dr Ayeh’s political and professional background, particularly his involvement in the NDC’s communication structures and student leadership.

He cited Dr Ayeh’s tenure as President of the Tertiary Education Institutions Network (TEIN) at the University of Cape Coast (UCC), his contribution to the NDC National Communications Team and his role as the party’s Manifesto Spokesperson on Youth Development during the 2024 general elections.

He also referenced Dr Ayeh’s current responsibilities in government communication and his role as host of the party’s weekly media platform, NDC 360.

According to Mr Kabore, these experiences represent more than titles, providing Dr Ayeh with the institutional knowledge, exposure and practical experience required to occupy the deputy communications position.

“These are not merely titles to decorate a political profile. They represent experience, exposure, institutional knowledge and years of demonstrated commitment to the communication machinery of our party,” he said.

He argued that Dr Ayeh’s credentials, coupled with his vision and ability to build on the achievements of Mr Gyamfi’s administration as National Communications Officer, made a compelling case for his candidature.

Mr Kabore, however, stressed that his endorsement was not intended to undermine the contributions or loyalty of other aspirants seeking the position.

He said all candidates deserved respect, adding that the contest should be about identifying the person best positioned to ensure continuity, competence and innovation within the party’s communication machinery.

“As we look towards consolidating our gains and preparing for the political battles ahead, we must elect leaders who understand the demands of the office, appreciate the foundations already laid and possess the capacity to take our communication front to even greater heights,” he added.

He appealed to NDC delegates across the country to choose what he described as competence over sentiment, capacity over rhetoric, and continuity with innovation over unnecessary experimentation.

Endorsement adds to growing support for Dr Ayeh

Mr Kabore’s endorsement adds to a series of public declarations of support for Dr Ayeh’s candidature in recent weeks.

On November 17, a coalition of medical practitioners and former student leaders publicly endorsed the presidential aide, citing his professional background, student leadership experience, political commitment and exposure to public administration.

Earlier, on November 13, Presidential Staffer Beatrice Annan also endorsed his candidature, describing him as a capable individual with the potential to take on greater responsibilities.

“You have demonstrated your ability, competence and potential, and we are all rooting for you,” she wrote in a Facebook post.

Who is Dr Sammy Ayeh?

Dr Sammy Ayeh is a medical doctor and political communicator who currently serves as a Presidential Aide responsible for Communications at the Office of the President.

He holds a Bachelor of Medicine and Bachelor of Surgery degree from the University of Cape Coast and a Master of Business Administration from the University of Gold Coast.

His involvement in NDC politics began during his student days at UCC, where he served as Communications Officer and subsequently President of the university's TEIN branch.

He also became the first medical student at UCC to contest the Students' Representative Council (SRC) presidency.

His political communication work earned him a place on the NDC National Communications Team, where he worked under the leadership of Sammy Gyamfi and benefited from the mentorship of experienced communicators, including Felix Kwakye Ofosu.

During the 2024 general election campaign, he served as the party's Manifesto Spokesperson on Youth Development.

Dr Ayeh has also served on the boards of BOST Energies and Ghana Post.

He formally entered the race on October 21, 2026, when he picked up nomination forms to contest the Deputy National Communications Officer position.

Announcing his bid, he outlined three key priorities: strengthening research-driven political communication, empowering grassroots communicators and improving the party's strategic media engagement.

He said his intention was to build on the existing foundations of the party's communications machinery and make its messaging more responsive to the aspirations of Ghanaians.

Ghana News.title: Argentina midfielder Paredes collapses during TV interview
Ghana News.content:
World Cup-winning midfielder Leandro Paredes collapsed while giving a post-match interview minutes after winning a trophy with Boca Juniors.

The former Paris Saint-Germain midfielder, 32, was suffering from the heat and humidity in Barranquilla, Colombia, where Boca won the Copa Sudamericana by beating Atletico Mineiro of Brazil 2-0.

He was replaced in the second half, then collapsed during a television interview, with pictures showing a journalist trying to break his fall.

After treatment, Argentine Paredes was able to walk to the dressing room and join his team's celebrations.

"Thanks to everyone for the messages, it was just dizziness," he said on Instagram after the match.

Heat was a discussion before the game, with forecasts predicting temperatures could reach 32C and humidity around 80%.

Boca manager Rodolfo Arruabarrena said he noticed the midfielder struggling in the second half.

"He felt dizzy towards the end of the first half," Arruabarrena said.

"He improved a little during the break, but after 10 minutes in the second half you could see he was struggling."

Paredes started his career with Boca before moving to Europe in 2015.

The victory for Boca ended an 18-year international trophy drought for the Argentine side.

By securing their 19th international cup, Boca also became South America's most decorated club since 1960, overtaking domestic rival Independiente, which has 18.

Ghana News.title: PSG’s Doue to have surgery on ruptured ACL
Ghana News.content:
Paris Saint-Germain forward Desire Doue will have surgery later this month after rupturing the anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee.

The 21-year-old was in tears as he was carried off on a stretcher toward the end of the first half in the Ligue 1 champions' 3-2 win over Nice on Saturday night.

Doue, arguably PSG's best player this season, twisted awkwardly and went down with no contact.

The match was stopped for five minutes as Doue, visibly in pain, received treatment before the crowd applauded him off at the Allianz Riviera Stadium.

It is a huge set-back for the France attacker, who missed 13 games in 2025-26 with calf and hamstring injuries.

The European champions have been plagued by injuries so far this season and are already without Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, who sustained an ACL injury against Barcelona in October.

PSG return to action on Wednesday, when they host Roma in the Champions League.

Ghana News.title: Pochettino endures nightmare start as Man United lose to Liverpool
Ghana News.content:
Mauricio Pochettino's reign as Manchester United head coach began in desperate fashion, as his team were thrashed by rivals Liverpool and remained in the Premier League relegation zone.

Almost everything that could go wrong for the visitors did in the first 13 minutes: they conceded two goals and had Leny Yoro sent off, and Liverpool cruised to victory from there.

This was the first time since 1937 that the Red Devils arrived at Anfield in the bottom three, and back then they lost to Liverpool in a season that ended in relegation.

It seems unthinkable for the present-day Manchester United to suffer a similar fate, but this performance and result underlined the size of the task facing Pochettino as he looks to drag them up the table.

Yoro received a straight red card in the eighth minute after he was adjudged to have fouled Alexander Isak just outside the box. Dominik Szoboszlai stepped up to send the free-kick into the bottom left corner.

It got worse for the visitors when Liverpool - looking capable of scoring with every attack - added a second. This time, Rio Ngumoha got a cross in from the left and Florian Wirtz produced a clever volley at an awkward angle.

The only positive for the visitors in the first half was that they conceded no further goals, but they were left with a mountain to climb.

Liverpool fans may have thought a repeat of their 7-0 win over Manchester United three and a half years ago was on the cards, but the hosts seemed to step off their attack in the second half.

The longer it went without a third goal, some Manchester United fans may have hoped for a comeback, but any such thoughts were banished when Ngumoha slotted in from Bradley Barcola's pass.

That goal prompted taunts of "going down" from Liverpool fans, and United fans had more pain to come as the hosts added a fourth late on, with Victor Munoz firing home from Florian Wirtz's neat ball behind the defence.

The performance and result will give Pochettino plenty to ponder over as it leaves Manchester United just one point off the foot of the table. Liverpool, meanwhile, are fourth.

Liverpool analysis: Wirtz stars as Reds take their chances

Liverpool look to be taking encouraging steps under Andoni Iraola, with just two losses in 11 Premier League games so far.

But most of their joy has come away from home, with four wins from their five league road trips.

Home form needed to improve as they went into Sunday's game, having won just once in the Premier League before Manchester United's arrival.

One issue for the Reds has been turning chances into goals, a problem highlighted at the start of November in a home defeat by Arsenal, when they had 17 efforts at goal but none on target.

Undoubtedly, the early red card helped Liverpool here, but they took their chances early to keep this from becoming a frustrating battle against a side looking to nullify the player disadvantage by defending deep.

Wirtz's acrobatic finish was crucial, and the German midfielder rounded off a fine game with the assist for Liverpool's fourth. After a slow start, he looks more like the player the Reds believed they were getting when they signed him last year.

Man Utd analysis: Size of task made clear for Pochettino

Even the most optimistic Manchester United fan knew a change of leader wouldn't instantly fix their problems.

That said, they would have reasonably expected the new-boss bounce to last longer than eight minutes.

Hope filled the away end as they welcomed yet another new era, and former Tottenham and Chelsea boss Pochettino was certainly not afraid to make bold decisions immediately, handing Matthijs de Ligt his first start of the year.

But all the pre-match planning was hugely disrupted when Yoro was sent off for the second time this season.

Pochettino will have to work on discipline, with this being Manchester United's third red card in four games.

It is part of the wider issue of the Red Devils' dreadful defending. The four goals they conceded in this game mean they have let in 34 in all competitions this season, more than any other side from Europe's top five leagues.

For now, they remain in an almost unthinkable position - second bottom of the Premier League and facing the very real possibility of a season-long mission to avoid relegation.

Ghana News.title: Ghana Institute of Architects proposes  structured partnership to protect Ghana’s architectural heritage
Ghana News.content:
The Ghana Institute of Architects (GIA) has proposed the introduction of a legislative instrument to strengthen the protection and preservation of Ghana’s architectural heritage as part of efforts to position architecture as a key driver of tourism and socioeconomic development.

The proposal includes a review of existing policies and the introduction of new legislation to establish a structured partnership between government, architects and other stakeholders in the built environment.

The proposal was made at the GIA’s 2026 Annual General Meeting (AGM), held in Ho, Volta Region, under the theme, “Architecture as a Catalyst for Tourism in Ghana.”

Addressing the opening ceremony, GIA President, Tony Asare called for deliberate efforts to preserve the country’s architectural heritage, particularly historic buildings and structures, while harnessing their potential to attract tourists and stimulate economic growth.

He stressed the need for architects to play a central role in national development, particularly in town planning, urban design and infrastructure development.

Mr Asare proposed that all Metropolitan, Municipal and District Assemblies (MMDAs) engage qualified architects in managing planning and development processes.

He further advocated that major public infrastructure projects, including airports, transport terminals, cultural centres, museums, waterfronts, parks and markets, should be designed under the leadership of qualified architects.

National programme for heritage conservation

The GIA President also called for a national programme to guide the conservation, adaptive reuse and interpretation of Ghana’s built heritage.

He said the programme should establish design standards for tourism corridors, town gateways, rest stops, signage and public amenities.

Mr Asare proposed pilot projects in selected tourism destinations, beginning in the Volta Region, to demonstrate how quality architectural design could enhance the attractiveness and functionality of Ghanaian communities.

He emphasised that a shared national vision was needed to position architecture at the centre of tourism development, job creation, cultural preservation and sustainable development.

“Ghana’s next great tourism asset will not emerge by chance. It must be designed, built, and protected by Ghanaians,” he said.

Malta proposes architectural exchange programme

The Malta High Commissioner to Ghana, His Excellency Ronald Micallef, highlighted how Malta has leveraged its architectural heritage to promote tourism and stimulate economic growth.

He proposed an architectural exchange programme between the Ghana Institute of Architects and a counterpart institution in Malta to facilitate knowledge-sharing and strengthen professional development.

Mr Micallef also encouraged Ghanaian architects to embrace climate-responsive architecture by incorporating features such as natural ventilation, shading and water conservation into building designs.

Government commits resources to tourism infrastructure

The Minister for Roads and Highways, Kwame Governs Agbodza, said the government was investing in road infrastructure to improve access to tourism destinations across the country.

He disclosed that GH¢30 billion had been committed to the Big Push initiative to improve selected roads, with an additional GH¢10 billion allocated to the road sector in 2027.

According to him, the government was working closely with the Ministry of Tourism, Culture and Creative Arts to improve road networks serving tourism destinations.

He noted that the journey to a tourist destination should itself form part of the visitor experience, stressing the importance of incorporating architectural expertise into infrastructure development.

Mr Agbodza also disclosed that the government had allocated US$1 billion to the tourism sector under the New Economy initiative.

He described tourism as the fifth pillar of the initiative and urged architects to collaborate with the Ministry of Tourism to identify innovative ways of unlocking the sector’s potential.

Tourism Minister pledges collaboration with GIA

The Minister for Tourism, Culture and Creative Arts, Dzifa Abla Gomashie, pledged her ministry’s commitment to working with the Ghana Institute of Architects to strengthen the country’s tourism industry.

She expressed concern about encroachment on buffer zones around heritage sites, warning that uncontrolled development and other human activities were threatening historic buildings and their surrounding environments.

“I am looking forward to deepening our partnership with the Ghana Institute of Architects in several important areas,” she said.

Her remarks highlighted the need for stronger collaboration between government and professional institutions to safeguard heritage sites while promoting sustainable tourism development.

Volta Regional Minister highlights architects’ role in nation-building

The Volta Regional Minister, James Gunu, also acknowledged the significant contribution of architects to national development.

He described architects as nation-builders whose expertise was essential to shaping the country’s infrastructure, communities and economic future.

He called for stronger collaboration between the government and the architectural profession to advance Ghana’s development agenda.

The discussions at the AGM reinforced the importance of integrating architectural expertise into national planning and tourism development, while protecting historic structures and promoting sustainable design.

The proposed legislative instrument, if pursued, could provide an important framework for strengthening heritage conservation, improving the quality of public infrastructure and ensuring that Ghana’s architectural identity remains an integral part of its tourism appeal.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: Netanyahu’s Likud, Eisenkot’s Yashar end coalition talks without deal
World.content:
Parties remain split on who will lead the next government and whether far right minister Itamar Ben-Gvir will join.

Talks between the parties of caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot to form a unity government have ended without a deal.

Representatives of Netanyahu’s Likud and Eisenkot’s Yashar parties met in a Herzliya hotel on Sunday, where they remained split on who would lead the next government and whether far-right National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir would be part of it, according to Israel’s Channel 12 broadcaster.

The Yedioth Ahronoth newspaper reported that Likud wanted Ben-Gvir in government, while Yashar insisted on his exclusion.

In a joint statement, the two parties said they had “outlined their positions on a range of substantive issues” and that a “follow-up meeting would be held”, without revealing a date or any further details.

Eisenkot has until December 6 to form a government, with the possibility of a 14-day extension, after the elections in October gave his bloc 48 seats – 13 short of a majority.

Netanyahu has called for a unity government, saying it was the only way that Israel’s security could be guaranteed. Such an arrangement would allow a government to be formed without the inclusion of parties led by Palestinian citizens of Israel, which won a record 19 seats.

Channel 12 reported that former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett, who leads the Together list, proposed a coalition of Together, Yashar, Likud and Avigdor Lieberman’s Yisrael Beiteinu, with Eisenkot serving first and Netanyahu succeeding him.

However, Eisenkot has opposed a rotation, and Netanyahu has reportedly insisted on taking the premiership first, while Lieberman has ruled out joining any government that includes Netanyahu altogether.



If unity talks fail, Yashar plans to seek a confidence vote in the Knesset for a minority government before Eisenkot’s mandate expires. It would rely on outside support from the Arab Joint List, led by Yousef Jabareen, and the United Arab List, led by Mansour Abbas.

World.title: Heartbreak in US capital as Washington Spirit lose women’s football final
World.content:
KC Current win NWSL championship as Spirit lose third consecutive final despite playing in front of rowdy home crowd.

Washington, DC – Trinity Rodman sat on the pitch and held her face in her hands, trying to hold back tears as the final whistle ended her Washington Spirit’s quest for the National Women’s Soccer League (NWSL) with a 2-1 loss to the Kansas City Current.

For Rodman, who could be seen wincing in pain throughout the match after an early shoulder injury, the loss in the final on Saturday night was a familiar feeling. She and the Spirit had reached, but lost, the two previous finals.

This one, however, was different. The Spirit were playing in front of their home fans – a sold-out crowd at Audi Field in Washington, DC, and palpable support across the city.

The third time was not the charm for the Spirit.

The stakes were high on Saturday night with a huge turnout at the stadium and increased interest in women’s football across the country. Former footballer Tobin Heath compared the NWSL to the National Football League (NFL), the most-watched sports league in the US.

And with their cult-like following, the Spirit were hoping to leave local fans with a memory of sporting glory that would last a lifetime.

“The ladies fought hard. I don’t think it was the best performance, but they fought hard. They fought to the end. They were still in it in the 90-something minute, but I wish they would have won,” Spirit fan Angel Ughiovhe told Al Jazeera.

After the KC Current went 2-0 up, Rodman had clawed a goal back in the dying moments of the match, cutting the deficit in half, giving fans a glimmer of hope for a historic comeback that never materialised.



“We were saying internally, third time is a charm,” Kim Bolt, chief marketing and strategy officer at the Washington Spirit, told Al Jazeera on Friday.

“I think especially because our fans mean so much to us, it would just be absolutely incredible if we could get the win in front of our, you know, rowdy Audi crowd.”

That belief was shared across the city. But it just wasn’t meant to be.

Despite the defeat, the final highlighted the passion for women’s football in the US capital and the adoration for the local team.

The soaring arches of the Frederick Douglass Memorial Bridge glowed with the team’s green and pink colours ahead of the final. People across the city walked around with the team’s top that features Washington’s famous cherry blossom. Even the public buses said, “Go Spirit!”

For many Spirit fans, the final was more than a game. Chants of “Free DC” rang out in the stadium at the end of the 51st minute as they have for the past year since President Donald Trump deployed federal troops in the city.

The chant, which is timed to reflect DC’s quest to become the 51st US state, was echoed by spectators outside the stadium at nearby watch parties, highlighting the popularity of the political culture that fans had built around the team.

The capital city is home to nearly 700,000 people who do not have voting members in Congress because DC is not a state.

Carlene Reid said she was disappointed by the outcome of the match on Saturday but she took solace in that people across the country heard the demand for DC statehood.

“This is probably the most inclusive game I’ve ever come to and the most politically sound game,” Reid told Al Jazeera.

“It was absolutely amazing to hear the chant happen as a DC resident. So I’m happy that the message is getting out there that we are fighting for statehood.”

KC Current midfielder Vanessa DiBernardo scored directly from a corner in the 54th minute on Saturday shortly after the stadium erupted with the politically charged chant. Brazilian legend Debinha added a second for the champions from a counterattack in the 97th minute.

Rodman scored from a header minutes later.

The win cements Kansas City’s status as a football hub for the men’s and women’s games. Despite its relatively small population of 520,000 people, the city also has a team in the country’s top men’s football league, Major League Soccer (MLS), and it hosted six FIFA World Cup matches over the summer.



Football has been growing in popularity in the US, especially after Argentinian legend Lionel Messi joined Inter Miami in 2023. Cohosting the World Cup with Canada and Mexico only accelerated that trend. The US also hosted the Club World Cup in 2025.

Bolt said the surging interest in men’s football has not come at the expense of the women’s game.

“We have our own fan base that is passionate, that is hungry for content, that is hungry for our merch, hungry for our ticket sales,” Bolt told Al Jazeera.

“The growth in the men’s game – we’re not seeing that cannibalise or stunt our own growth because I think the fan bases are pretty unique.”

Attendance at Spirit’s home games at Audi Field – a 20,000-seat stadium – backs that theory. The Spirit played in front of sold-out crowds in the quarterfinal and semifinal.

And there wasn’t an empty seat on Saturday night despite the skyrocketing ticket prices, which started at more than $300 on the resale market.

The Spirit partnered with DC Mayor-elect Janeese Lewis George to give away 400 tickets through a raffle.

Audi Field on Saturday featured some of the top players in the game between the two squads, who could play key roles for their national teams at the Women’s World Cup in Brazil next year.

On the Current side, Croix Bethune and Michelle Cooper are likely to feature for the US Women’s National Team (USWNT). Temwa Chawinga, who led Malawi to the Women’s Africa Cup of Nations (WAFCON) final earlier this year, is expected to lead her country at the World Cup.

For the Spirit, Rodman was a young, rising star at the last tournament, but she heads into next year as one of the most renowned players in the sport as the USWNT push to reclaim the title from Spain.

The Spirit’s number 10, Leicy Santos, is also set to shine on the international stage with Colombia, while defender Esme Morgan is likely to be called up for England. Sandy MacIver is expected to start between the sticks for Scotland.

Algeria’s Melissa Bethi could also feature at the tournament after her team secured qualification by reaching the WAFCON semifinals.

“One of the best things about DC is that it is an international city,” Bolt said.

“We love the fact that our team is a reflection of the city, the diversity of the city – that we have so many international players.”

World.title: Fire breaks out at popular tourist hotspot in Zanzibar
World.content:
NewsFeed Fire breaks out at popular tourist hotspot in Zanzibar

A fire tore through six hotels and dozens of shops in Nungwi, a popular tourist hotspot in Zanzibar. Authorities said the blaze began in a hotel bakery oven before spreading to neighbouring thatched buildings. No deaths or injuries were reported, but tourists were evacuated.

World.title: Liverpool 4-0 Manchester United: Five key takeaways for Pochettino
World.content:
United suffer their worst result under a new manager in 100 years as Liverpool cruise past Mauricio Pochettino’s side.

Share Welcome to Manchester! Liverpool give Poch crash course in United’s woes on social media

If Mauricio Pochettino had any doubt about the size of the job in front of him at Manchester United, his players confirmed his worst fears within 13 minutes of his first game in charge – a 4-0 defeat at Liverpool.

As the home side surged into a two-goal lead in the opening exchanges at Anfield, with the away side reduced to 10 men, the sinking sensation for United – who are second bottom of the Premier League – immediately returned.

Any ‘new-manager bounce’, as feared by Reds manager Andoni Iraola, had no time to materialise with a rash challenge from Lenny Yoro on Alexander Isak leading to a straight red in the eighth minute.

The resulting free-kick was powered home by Dominik Szoboszlai, with Florian Wirtz thereafter converting a sharp attack in a flash – ending the match as a contest.

Pochettino slammed the decision to send off Yoro after the game, but there was a familiar feeling about the performance overall.

Al Jazeera Sport takes a look at five key takeaways as the opening salvo of the ninth manager since United’s last league title in 2013 fell apart – resulting in the worst start for a new manager of the club in 100 years.

Was the referee right to send off Manchester United’s Lenny Yoro?

Even though United have greater concerns, the answer was undoubtedly: no. The question for the referee, in sending off Yoro for denying a goalscoring opportunity, had four considerations: distance between the offence and the goal, general direction of the play, likelihood of keeping or gaining control of the ball, and location and number of defenders.



Of those guidelines, the most pertinent were the direction of play, which was at an angle across the box, and the likelihood of keeping control of the ball – Isak arguably had no control of it at all after a heavy first touch that allowed United keeper Senne Lammens to gather.

VAR (video assistant referee) had the chance to ask the referee to reconsider his decision, but decided there was no clear and obvious error. Had the referee reviewed the red card, then he would have surely decided a yellow card would have sufficed.

The play that led to the card being shown, however, was even more questionable than the outcome.

Was Pochettino right to bench Maguire for Man United?

The release of the team sheets, an hour and 15 minutes before kickoff, was the first moment all United fans looked to.

For all the pre-game comments by Pochettino, the Argentinean’s starting 11 was always going to be the first true sense of his evaluation of United’s current woes.

Dropping defender Harry Maguire, a former club captain, was a massive call – all the more so given the inexperience of Yoro and Matthijs de Ligt, who were both selected ahead of the ex-England stalwart.

The ref’s mistake in sending off Yoro was clear, but Yoro and de Ligt were heavily exposed in the play that led to the sending-off.

The latter is easing his way back into first-team action after a year out with a back injury and found himself in no-man’s land as Isak chased a long ball. Yoro sought to cover, but was clumsy and ill-advised in his attempt, allowing Isak to draw what was only a soft challenge and connection.

United were plucky after the change forced by the sending-off, with Maguire replacing the clearly, and understandably, disappointed Bryan Mbeumo.

Maguire’s fine, last-ditch block from Isak’s close-range pivot and shot saved United’s blushes five minutes before the break, and made Pochettino’s first big call look all the worse.

A scuffed attempt at a clearance early in the second half by de Ligt allowed Isak clean through only for the Liverpool forward to slice his effort.

By the time Rio Ngumoha added a 66th-minute third, all the questions about a defence that had previously shipped 30 goals in 15 games this season had been answered. The fourth from Victor Munoz was inevitable, and it could have been a lot worse for United on the day.

Their last defeat at Anfield was a 7-0 victory for the home side – a repeat was certainly possible had Liverpool been more clinical.

Matters were so bad that the former Liverpool defender Jamie Carragher commented on Sky Sports that he “felt sorry” for de Ligt prior to his eventual substitution in the second half.



The consensus was that Pochettino made the wrong call before the start.

What other Man United changes did Pochettino make at Liverpool?

Yoro and de Ligt have been peripheral figures in their time with the Old Trafford club, for varying reasons including injury, but they were not the only big calls made by Pochettino.

Another injury-plagued player, Patrick Dorgu, was also given a start – and in a formation which was not wholly clear. The popular Amad Diallo was forced to make do with a place on the bench alongside Maguire.

Dorgu, whose form has been indifferent at best, can operate as a wide defender or attacker. It appeared as though he was given some licence on the left to get forward, with United reverting to a back four, Lisandro Martinez covering on the flank in defence and Diogo Dalot holding back on the right.

Whether it was a back four or five to begin with – the latter explaining the absence of the more forward-minded Diallo – United were quickly forced to a five with the sending-off and the sacrifice of Mbeumo at the other end of the pitch.

Not only was the decision to pick two less experienced centre-backs at Anfield a monumental – and ultimately costly – call, the move to switch to an unfamiliar feel across the backline was a painful lesson for Pochettino, who himself is more accustomed to a 4-2-3-1 setup.

What next for Manchester United and Mauricio Pochettino?

With 19th-placed United mired in the Premier League drop zone, the UEFA Champions League appears a sideshow, but a trip to Sporting Lisbon awaits on Wednesday.

In some ways, Europe’s elite club competition, which United have returned to after a three-year absence, may well give Pochettino a free hit to explore how he can get the best out of a beleaguered group.
