World.title: Gumi calls for removal of Emirs guilty of immoral conduct
World.content:
Gumi

Islamic cleric, Sheikh Ahmad Gumi, has called for the immediate removal of any Emir found guilty of immoral conduct, saying such action is necessary to protect the integrity and credibility of traditional institutions.

Gumi made the call in a Facebook post on Sunday, stressing that traditional rulers must uphold high standards of conduct befitting the positions they occupy.

He said any Emir found culpable of immoral behaviour should be removed and replaced without delay to preserve the dignity of the traditional institution.

“Any Emir found guilty of immoral conduct should be removed and replaced immediately to safeguard the integrity, dignity and credibility of the traditional institution,” he said.

The cleric’s position underscores the need for accountability among traditional rulers, whose authority and influence in their communities depend significantly on public trust, moral standing and respect for established customs.

Traditional institutions remain important in community leadership, conflict resolution and the preservation of cultural and religious values, making the conduct of their occupants a matter of public concern.

World.title: ‎APC crisis: Tinubu orders Gov Radda, Masari to settle rift
World.content:
President Tinubu

‎–Urges APC leaders to forgive one another, unite ahead of 2027 polls

‎

‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru

‎

‎ABUJA –PRESIDENT Bola Tinubu on Sunday in Lagos underscored the virtue of forgiveness at a prayer session organised in his honour by his extended family, urging APC leaders to forgive one another and seek reconciliation.

‎

‎His message was specifically directed at his Special Adviser on Political Matters, Alhaji Ibrahim Kabiru Masari, and former Defence Minister, Alhaji Abubakar Badaru, both of whom were in the audience at the hall of the Yoruba Tennis Club, where the President spoke.

‎

‎Apparently reacting to reports of a quarrel between Governor Dikko Umar Radda and Masari in Katsina State, President Tinubu urged Masari to go back home to reconcile with his governor.

‎

‎ “Alhaji Kabiru Masari, go back home and reconcile with everybody. That is the President’s order. When you finish that, you move to Jigawa. You move to other places and reconcile them, beg them because we have to reconcile and every anger must dissipate and evaporate,” the President said.

‎

‎He also gave the same order to Badaru, the former governor of Jigawa State.

‎

‎President Tinubu appealed to all APC leaders to set aside personal differences, strengthen internal cohesion, and work collectively to consolidate his administration’s gains ahead of the 2027 elections.

‎

‎The President thanked the organisers of the Islamic prayer session and clerics who prayed for him, his administration, and Nigeria.

‎

‎He thanked God for his victory in the 2023 presidential election, despite formidable obstacles.

‎

‎”People cried. People suffered. People died. People had no five naira in their pockets because their money was in the bank and they couldn’t get it out. There was also no fuel.

‎

‎”We invoked the spirit of Almighty Allah and said, ‘Kun faya kun (‘Be, and it becomes’). It got us there, and we have the presidency. Allah gives power to whom he wants, and he takes it from whoever he wants,” the President said.

‎

‎The prayer session was attended by Muslim and Christian Clerics as well as Governors of Lagos, Kaduna, Kwara, Ogun, and Imo States.

‎

‎Other dignitaries in attendance included National Security Adviser Mallam Nuhu Ribadu, Chief of Staff to the President Femi Gbajabiamila, and Lagos Deputy Governor Kadiri Obafemi Hamzat.

‎

‎Also present were the Minister of Education, Mr Tunji Alausa; Speaker of Lagos State House of Assembly, Mudashiru Obasa; the Grand Chief Imam of Lagos, Sheikh Sulaimon Oluwatoyin Abou-Nolla; the Chairman, Board of Trustees of the Coalition of Northern Groups (CNG), Dr Nasturah Ashir Sharriff; the Tinubu family members and party faithful.

‎

‎The President recalled that he invoked “Emilokan’s spirit (it is my turn) in 2022. It is now your turn (Eyinlokan) to make the re-election possible.”

‎

‎He appealed to Lagosians to come out en masse on Election Day to exercise their right to vote.

‎

‎”The challenge of today is much easier than that of yesterday, but we cannot take it for granted. You must knock on your neighbour’s door, tell them to collect their PVC. If you have PVC, you have the power of January 16th and February 6th, and that’s what I want to ask you to exercise,” the President said.

‎

‎”We must generate enough votes to overwhelm the opponents,” he emphasised.

‎

‎He reaffirmed his commitment to providing purposeful leadership, strengthening national unity and justice, and building a prosperous country for all Nigerians.

‎

‎Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu of Lagos State described the President as an epitome of justice, fairness, equity, and inclusive governance, calling these virtues essential pillars for building a united, peaceful, and prosperous Nigeria.

‎

‎Former Governor of Jigawa, Badaru Abubakar, said Northerners appreciated President Tinubu’s support for the late former President Muhammadu Buhari in his 2015 and 2019 election victories.

‎

‎Badaru urged Northern voters to reciprocate the gesture and help the President consolidate the administration’s achievements so far.

‎

‎The Chairman of the occasion and elder statesman, 94-year-old Alhaji Lateef Femi Okunnu, promised to canvass and vote for the President on January 16, 2027.

‎

‎He said the President has done a lot to be re-elected.

‎

‎The elder statesman also emphasised the need to uphold justice, saying that the Tinubu administration is focusing on the economy and infrastructure, especially the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway and the Sokoto-Badagry Superhighway, as well as strengthening the naira and foreign reserves.

‎

‎In their vote of thanks, representatives of the Tinubu family, Alhaji Rafiu Tinubu and Alhaja Iyalode Bintu Tinubu, thanked God for the family’s blessings and urged Nigerians to support the President in his determination to deliver the dividends of democracy to the people.

‎

‎Rev. Honsu Oluremi, Chairman of Lagos State Government House Chapel, referenced the Bible and urged the people to always pray for leaders’ success.

‎

‎The Coordinator of the Prayer session and the Grand Chief Imam of Lagos, Sheikh Sulaimon Oluwatoyin Abou-Nolla, while reading from the holy Qur’an, asked Allah to grant the President success in his affairs and good health.

World.title: Borno ADC demands whereabouts of detained supporter
World.content:
…Gubio chairman says he ordered his release, denies ADC’s allegations

By Ndahi Marama, Maiduguri

MAIDUGURI — The African Democratic Congress (ADC) Campaign Council in Borno State has demanded the immediate disclosure of the whereabouts of one of its supporters, Alhaji Muktari, whom it alleged was arrested and detained in Gubio Local Government Area.

However, the Executive Chairman of Gubio Local Government Area, Mali Bulama Mali, has dismissed the allegations, insisting that Muktari had been released and had regained his freedom.

The Director of Communications of the ADC Campaign Council in Borno State, Bukar Bukar Petrol, alleged that Muktari was arrested by security operatives following a directive from the local government chairman over his involvement in grassroots mobilisation for the opposition party ahead of the 2027 general elections.

In a statement issued on Sunday, Petrol alleged that Muktari was arrested on November 21, 2026, at about 10pm by individuals described as repentant Boko Haram members allegedly acting on the instructions of the council chairman.

The party expressed concern that Muktari’s whereabouts were unknown to his family and associates, adding that his wife witnessed the incident.

It also alleged that the arrest and detention were carried out outside recognised police procedures, with no confirmation that he was taken to a police station or formally processed by law enforcement authorities.

The ADC further accused Mali of allegedly empowering repentant Boko Haram members to operate as unofficial security operatives and political foot soldiers in the council.

“The circumstances surrounding the arrest are particularly disturbing. Alhaji Mukhtar is reportedly still being held, while his exact whereabouts remain unknown to the party and his associates. His wife witnessed the incident and can provide an account of the circumstances surrounding his arrest,” the statement said.

The party described the alleged development as an abuse of public office and raised concerns about the possible creation of parallel security structures and unlawful deprivation of citizens’ liberty.

Consequently, the ADC demanded the immediate and unconditional release of Muktari, disclosure of his whereabouts and an independent investigation into the alleged involvement of the council chairman.

It also called for an end to the alleged use of repentant Boko Haram members as unofficial security operatives for intimidation, arrests and detention of citizens.

The party maintained that a local government chairman had no constitutional or statutory authority to establish a personal security outfit or delegate police powers to unofficial individuals.

“The ADC will not accept the use of public office as an instrument of political intimidation, coercion or unlawful detention,” Petrol said.

The party warned that it would escalate the matter to national security, human rights and judicial institutions if the authorities failed to address its concerns.

However, reacting to the allegations on Sunday, Mali denied ordering Muktari’s arrest, insisting that the ADC supporter had been released on his intervention.

The chairman alleged that Muktari, whom he described as a non-indigene of Gubio from Guzamala Local Government Area, was arrested by security authorities over an incident that allegedly caused trouble in the council, and not by repentant Boko Haram members as claimed by the ADC.

He said: “Actually, I was the one who ordered for his release and he, Muktari, has regained his freedom, but I cannot guarantee his safety.”

Mali’s response contradicted the ADC’s claim that its supporter remained in detention and that his whereabouts were unknown.

World.title: 2027: Lagos is a big deal to me  -  Tinubu urges Lagosians to get PVC
World.content:
President Bola Tinubu has urged Lagos residents to mobilise voters and ensure they collect their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) ahead of the 2027 elections, declaring that the state remains central to his political ambition.

Tinubu spoke on Sunday at the Yoruba Tennis Club in Onikan, Lagos, during a prayer gathering organised by his family ahead of the general elections.

He urged his supporters to reach out to eligible voters in their neighbourhoods and persuade them to participate in the electoral process, warning against complacency.

“The challenge of today is much easier than that of yesterday. But we cannot take it for granted. You must knock your neighbour’s door. Tell them to go and collect their PVCs,” the President said.

He jokingly told those without voter cards at the gathering that they had come for the food, drawing laughter from attendees.

Tinubu also urged voters to turn out on the scheduled election days, saying their PVCs would give them the opportunity to determine the country’s political direction.

“If you have PVC, you have the power of January 16 and February 6. And that’s what I want to ask you to exercise,” he said.

Describing Lagos as particularly important to his political ambition, the President said the state’s voting strength should translate into greater participation at the polls.

“To me, Lagos is the big deal,” he declared.

Tinubu expressed dissatisfaction with the turnout recorded in previous elections, questioning how a state with millions of registered voters could produce relatively low numbers of votes.

“How can you have seven million registered voters and produce 100,000, 200,000? No. That’s failure. Even if you win and say you win, is it a win? No!” he said.

He further urged residents not to allow disagreements with political leaders to discourage them from voting, saying they could exercise their franchise and still express their grievances afterwards.

Tinubu lost Lagos to Peter Obi of the Labour Party in the 2023 presidential election. Obi secured 575,735 votes against Tinubu’s 573,001, despite Tinubu having governed the state from 1999 to 2007.

World.title: CJN tasks lawyers to embrace scholarship
World.content:
Chief Justice of Nigeria, CJN, Justice Kudirat Kekere-Ekun

…Commends Pinheiro’s 6 law books

By Innocent Anaba

LAGOS—THE Chief Justice of Nigeria, CJN, Justice Kudirat Kekere-Ekun, has commended the contributions of Kemi Pinheiro, SAN, to legal scholarship and professional development, describing six publications presented in his honour as valuable resources that will enrich Nigerian jurisprudence and strengthen the intellectual foundation of the legal profession.



Kekere-Ekun, who spoke, weekend, while chairing the public presentation of the books in Lagos, said the publications reflected an impressive combination of legal scholarship, practical experience and engagement with contemporary developments in the administration of justice.



She noted that the collection, comprising four books authored by Pinheiro and two compilations produced in his honour, addressed significant areas of legal practice, including litigation, arbitration, insolvency, criminal law, technology and contemporary jurisprudence.



According to her, the publications were not merely a collection of books assembled to commemorate an accomplished legal practitioner but works that sought to make legal knowledge more accessible and useful to those responsible for applying, interpreting and developing the law.



The CJN said: “Taken together, the works reflect an engagement with important areas of legal practice and scholarship, as well as an attempt to preserve the experiences and contributions of a distinguished member of our profession.”



Kekere-Ekun described ‘Defining Moments: Chronicles of a Silk’ as particularly significant because it offered a personal account of the experiences, encounters, challenges and defining moments that had shaped Pinheiro’s career spanning close to four decades at the Bar.

She observed that memoirs of this nature were valuable because they preserved aspects of professional life that might never find their way into law reports or formal institutional records.

Such accounts, she said, enabled younger practitioners to appreciate the human experiences behind professional milestones, including the uncertainties, disappointments and perseverance that often accompanied a successful legal career.

The CJN also highlighted the importance of the two publications on arbitration and insolvency, particularly against the background of Nigeria’s increasingly sophisticated business environment

and the need for effective legal responses to commercial transactions.

, financial distress and dispute resolution.

Similarly, she described Insolvency Law in Nigeria: Practice and Procedure as an important contribution to an increasingly relevant area of law under the Companies and Allied Matters Act 2020.

According to her, its examination of corporate rescue, restructuring, administration and other mechanisms for addressing financial distress reflected the growing recognition that preserving viable businesses could, in appropriate circumstances, better serve creditors, employees, investors and the wider economy than immediate liquidation.

On Strategies in Criminal Trials: A Practitioner’s Guide, Kekere-Ekun said the publication would be useful to both experienced practitioners and younger lawyers seeking to strengthen their competence in criminal advocacy.

She noted that criminal litigation required not only sound knowledge of substantive law but also a firm grasp of procedure, evidence and the strategic decisions that arose at different stages of a trial.

She said: “Experience that is not shared may remain a personal achievement. Experience that is documented and transmitted becomes part of the profession’s collective inheritance.”

Earlier, Pinheiro praised the CJN for reforms in the judiciary, particularly the digitisation of the Supreme Court’s operations and the refurbishment of federal courts.

Pinheiro said the four books he authored were products of his practical experiences as an insolvency practitioner, criminal prosecutor and arbitrator, rather than theoretical exercises.

The SAN, who said he would mark 40 years at the Bar in October 2027, explained that the publications represented lessons accumulated over nearly four decades of legal practice and 20 years as a member of the Inner Bar.

World.title: Tinubu’s Reelection: APAC Storms Osun, Begins Massive Grassroots Mobilisation
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

As part of efforts to ensure the re-election of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu with a convincing margin in Osun State, a group, Asiwaju’s Political Action Committee (APAC), has begun an intensive grassroots outreach in the state ahead of the presidential election.

Although the identity of those behind the group is still sketchy as at press time, credible sources close to the group revealed that some private individuals who are friends of the Director-General of the National Sugar Development Council (NSDC), Kamar Bakrin, are behind the project.

Lending credence to the information, Bakrin was sighted in Osun during the week, engaging with some leaders from the Ijesa area of the state, where he hails from.

One of the sources, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said: “You know the man. He is not a politician. But as his friends, we believe that since he is an appointee of Mr. President, he has to mobilise for the President’s re-election. So, this is what we are doing on his behalf.

“And I can confirm to you that what this group is doing has the endorsement of the leader of the APC in the state, our father, the Honourable Minister of Marine and Blue Economy, Adegboyega Oyetola. Ours is to complement his efforts and that of the party, to increase the President’s votes in Osun.”

Investigation reveals that canvassers engaged by the group are already reaching out directly to prospective voters with a view to convincing them to vote for Tinubu, come January 16, 2027

World.title: I Have Not Stepped Down From Presidential Race, Says Atiku
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Chuks Okocha in Abuja

Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has described the claim that he has stepped down from the 2027 presidential race as a brazen, malicious and desperate falsehood.

”I have not made such decision. I am in this race to win”, Atiku stated.

In a statement issued by his Director of Strategic Communication, Phrank Shaibu, Atiku said no group parading itself as his supporters could speak for him or withdraw him from the election.

“Putting my name on a placard does not make someone my supporter. Putting a lie in that person’s mouth does not make it my decision.”

Atiku said those behind the claim appeared to be a political group struggling with defections and resorting to the APC’s old tactic of parading supposed supporters of another candidate.

“Any party promoting the lie that I have stepped down is doing Tinubu’s work. Every false withdrawal story tries to clear his strongest opponent from the field. If I am not on the ballot, Bola Tinubu might as well wait for a coronation. But I am in this race to win, and Nigerians will have their choice.”

He said his Affordable Life campaign was reaching communities across Nigeria and would remain focused on the hardship families face.

“Hunger and poverty are not on social media. They are in our markets, our homes and every community where families struggle to afford food and transport. That is why our campaign is going to every nook and cranny of Nigeria. I do not need anyone to step down for me, and I am stepping down for no one.”

Atiku said any opposition party seeking to force a rival out through falsehood was undermining the fair contest it claimed to support.

“Anyone serious about defeating the APC should take their case to voters. Manufacturing supporters and circulating false declarations will not defeat Tinubu. It only serves him.”

He urged his supporters to remain focused: “Hold your heads high. Keep your PVCs ready. Mobilise from ward to ward. No fabricated headline can withdraw me from an election I intend to win. On 16 January 2027, we will meet and beat Bola Tinubu at the ballot box.”

World.title: Bayelsa Boat Mishap: Tinubu Orders Stiffer Waterway Safety Measures, Thorough Investigation Of Accident
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

.Donates N250m to victims’ families as Shettima visits survivors in Yenagoa

.Says Nigerians travelling by water deserve same protection as road, air passengers

.Casualty figure now 29

Deji Elumoye in Abuja

President Bola Tinubu on Sunday called for stricter enforcement of safety standards on Nigeria’s inland waterways following the tragic boat mishap in Bayelsa State, announcing a N250 million Federal Government donation to support the bereaved families.

He also demanded a thorough investigation into the circumstances surrounding the accident, vowing that the Federal Government would work with relevant authorities and state governments to strengthen vessel inspections, safety compliance and enforcement to prevent further loss of lives.

Vice President Kashim Shettima conveyed the President’s position during a condolence visit to Yenagoa, the Bayelsa State capital, following Friday’s boat accident at the Oweikorogha/Otuan River Junction in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area.

Speaking at Government House, Yenagoa, the Vice President said the tragedy had exposed the urgent need to improve safety on inland waterways, particularly in riverine communities where water transportation remains essential to everyday life.

According to him: “We cannot accept a situation in which citizens must gamble with their lives simply to move between communities. Geography may determine how people travel, but it must never determine how much protection their lives deserve. A Nigerian travelling by boat is entitled to the same concern for safety as one travelling by road or air.”

Shettima said preliminary reports suggesting that the boat developed a mechanical fault must be thoroughly investigated to establish the circumstances of the accident and identify possible failures in safety procedures.

“We have received preliminary reports concerning the circumstances of this accident, including indications of a possible mechanical failure. These reports must be thoroughly investigated by the appropriate authorities. We must establish what happened, identify any failures in safety procedures and take the necessary steps to prevent a recurrence.

“President Tinubu’s administration will continue working with the relevant authorities and state governments to strengthen safety standards, vessel inspections and enforcement on our inland waterways. The lives of our people are too precious for safety to remain an afterthought,” the Vice President stated.

Expressing grief over the tragedy, Shettima described the loss as particularly painful because the victims were travelling to attend a burial ceremony when the accident occurred.

“There is a particular cruelty in the tragedy that has brought us here today. Our brothers and sisters set out on a journey to mourn the dead, only for death to claim some of them along the way,” he lamented.

The Vice President recalled that President Tinubu had, upon receiving news of the disaster, directed relevant federal agencies to commence rescue and recovery operations and ordered that Saturday’s APC presidential campaign rally in Ibadan, Oyo State, be conducted without the usual celebrations in honour of the victims.

He stressed that the victims must not be reduced to casualty figures, noting that each had a family, personal history and responsibilities.

“Each person lost in those waters had a name, a history, relationships and responsibilities. Somewhere, a family is struggling to understand how someone who left home for a funeral will never walk through that door again,” Shettima added.

He commended Governor Douye Diri for visiting the accident scene and coordinating the state’s response, while acknowledging the efforts of the National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA), Bayelsa State Emergency Management Agency (SEMA), Nigerian Red Cross Society, Nigeria Police Force, Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), local divers and community volunteers.

Assuring the bereaved families of the Federal Government’s continued support, the Vice President said, “To the families who have lost their loved ones, I will not pretend that time alone will make this pain disappear. Our responsibility is to stand with you beyond this visit, beyond these condolences and beyond the days when this tragedy dominates the news.”

Before proceeding to the Government House, Shettima visited survivors receiving treatment at the Bayelsa Medical University Teaching Hospital, where he consoled them and assured them of adequate medical care and attention.

The Vice President also met with members of the bereaved families and some survivors at the Government House, conveying President Tinubu’s condolences and the Federal Government’s solidarity with those affected.

Earlier, Governor Diri, while briefing the Vice President and other government officials at the Government House, disclosed that the death toll had risen to 29, while more than 50 passengers survived the accident as of Sunday afternoon.

The Governor attributed the tragedy to an alleged failure by the boat operators to observe established safety protocols, describing the incident as avoidable.

He disclosed that the Bayelsa State Government had constituted a committee to investigate the immediate and remote causes of the accident and recommend measures to prevent similar incidents.

Diri further announced that the state government had taken responsibility for the medical bills and treatment of survivors, assuring the bereaved families that they would not be abandoned.

He thanked the military, paramilitary agencies, emergency responders, local divers and other stakeholders who mobilised to assist the victims and support ongoing rescue and recovery operations.

On arrival in Yenagoa, the Vice President was received by Governor Douye Diri; Minister of State for Petroleum Resources (Oil), Senator Heineken Lokpobiri; Managing Director of the Niger Delta Development Commission (NDDC), Dr. Samuel Ogbuku; Bayelsa State APC Chairman, Dr. Dennis Otiotio; and Managing Director of the Niger Delta River Basin Development Authority, Prince Ebitimi Amgbare.

Others present included members of the National Assembly, members of the Bayelsa State House of Assembly and members of the State Executive Council.

World.title: MPB Raises Cyber Fraud Alarm, Urges Pensioners Not to Disclose Personal Information to Cybercriminals
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Linus Aleke in Abuja

The Military Pensions Board has raised the alarm over increasing cases of cyber fraud targeting pensioners, urging them to remain vigilant and refrain from disclosing personal or financial information to cybercriminals.

The Board advised pensioners to safeguard their sensitive information, exercise caution when responding to unsolicited calls, messages or emails, and report any suspicious activities to the appropriate authorities to prevent fraud and protect their pension entitlements.

According to a statement by the Board’s Public Relations Officer, Squadron Leader Alliyu Mohammed, the Military Pensions Board has received reports that some unscrupulous individuals are circulating messages claiming that a verification exercise is under way and requesting pensioners to provide their personal details and other sensitive information.

Squadron Leader Mohammed said: “The Board wishes to categorically state that these messages are false and should be disregarded. There is currently no ongoing verification exercise being conducted by the Board. Pensioners are strongly advised not to respond to such requests or disclose their personal information to unknown individuals, as such attempts may be intended to defraud or exploit them.

“The Board further urges pensioners to remain vigilant and always verify information through the official communication channels of the Military Pensions Board. Pensioners are also encouraged to contact the Board directly through the appropriate channels for enquiries or clarification.”

The Military Pensions Board, Mohammed said, remains committed to protecting the interests and welfare of military pensioners and will continue to provide accurate and timely information through its recognised channels.

He advised pensioners to disregard unverified messages and rely only on information issued through the Board’s official platforms.

World.title: Rep Dasuki: INEC Under Amupitan Has Worst Voter Data
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Fears compromised register could jeopardise 2027 election

Says shrinking political space, rising violence are dangerous implications of Tinubu’s ‘all is fair in politics’

Deputy Minority Leader of the House of Representatives, Rep. Abdussamad Dasuki, has raised the alarm over what he described as the poor state of the Independent National Electoral Commission’s (INEC) voter data under its chairman, Prof. Joash Amupitan, warning that a compromised voters’ register could jeopardise the electoral process and put the credibility of the 2027 general elections in peril.

Dasuki also noted that the shrinking political space and rising violence against opposition parties, could jeopardise the credibility of the 2027 general elections.

The lawmaker warned that a compromised voters’ register could undermine the electoral process and erode public confidence in the outcome of the next general elections.

Rep Dasuki spoke while addressing supporters of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate Atiku Abubakar in Lagos at the weekend.

“INEC has not provided the assurance to Nigerians that the final register that would be used for next year’s election would be credible. This should worry all Nigerians,” he said.

He warned that the credibility of the 2027 elections could be seriously undermined if the commission failed to address concerns surrounding the integrity of its voter database before the final register is certified.

His concerns come against the backdrop of recent revelations by INEC that some of its registration officials abused their official access to create fraudulent voter records, including profiles containing fake photographs and manipulated biometric details.

Concern over the integrity of the database, however, intensified after INEC announced that it had removed 1,609,553 records from the voters’ register following a technical assessment.

The development has raised fresh questions about the effectiveness of the commission’s voter registration safeguards, the reliability of its database and whether adequate measures are being taken to prevent fraudulent records from finding their way into the final register.

INEC has, however, maintained that it remains committed to completing the necessary verification, adjudication and data-cleanup processes ahead of the scheduled certification of the final register of voters on December 15, 2026.

Dasuki disclosed that Amupitan would appear before the House committee this week, where he would be questioned on the growing concerns among Nigerians over the credibility of INEC’s voter data.

According to him, the INEC chairman would be expected to provide explanations on the circumstances surrounding the discovery of fraudulent voter records, the removal of over 1.6 million entries and the safeguards being put in place to ensure that the final register is reliable.

Beyond the concerns over voter data, Dasuki also warned that the shrinking political space and increasing violence against opposition parties and their supporters were dangerous implications of President Bola Tinubu’s “All is fair in politics” remark ahead of the 2027 elections.

He called on the President to retract the statement and publicly condemn actions threatening democratic participation, warning that the growing atmosphere of political intolerance could undermine the country’s democratic institutions and electoral process.

The lawmaker expressed concern over what he described as increasing attempts to restrict opposition parties’ access to public facilities, impose prohibitive fees on campaign billboards, instigate internal crises within opposition parties and intimidate political candidates and their supporters.

He said the political environment was becoming increasingly tense as the country approached the 2027 elections, adding that the President’s remark risked emboldening political actors who might interpret it as a justification for actions inconsistent with democratic principles.

“Although the President may have intended his remarks as an expression of determination to defend his political position, such language, coming from the nation’s highest political office, risks sending the wrong signal to political actors, particularly those who may interpret it as an endorsement of a politics without restraint,” he said.

Dasuki maintained that political competition must be guided by constitutional provisions, respect for human rights and the rule of law.

“In a democracy, not everything is fair in politics. Political competition must operate within the boundaries of the Constitution, the rule of law, respect for human rights and the fundamental principles of democratic engagement,” he stated.

Citing developments across the country, the lawmaker pointed to the controversy surrounding the African Democratic Congress’ presidential campaign flag-off in Sokoto State, where the opposition party accused the state government of denying it access to public facilities traditionally used for political activities.

He also referenced the attack on Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) supporters during a town hall meeting at the Classique Event Centre in Oregun, Lagos State, where suspected political thugs invaded the venue in an attempt to disrupt the gathering.

The lawmaker further cited the reported attack on the Benin City residence of former Edo State Governor, Chief John Odigie-Oyegun, during a political meeting attended by prominent opposition figures, including Peter Obi and Olumide Akpata.

On the financial restrictions facing opposition campaigns, Dasuki expressed concern over reports of exorbitant billboard permit fees in some states, arguing that such charges could create barriers to equal political participation.

He said the combination of restrictions on political activities, attacks on supporters and administrative measures that make campaigning difficult could weaken opposition parties and undermine the electorate’s ability to freely make political choices.

The lawmaker also expressed concern over the use of conflicting judicial pronouncements and prolonged legal disputes in ways that could leave opposition parties distracted and weakened, stressing that the independence of the judiciary must be protected from political interference.

World.title: FG Intensifies Efforts to Cut Off Terrorism Financing
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

*Moves against illicit financial flows networks

Linus Aleke in Abuja

The Federal Government has stated that lasting peace requires dismantling the criminal economies that finance insurgency, including kidnapping for ransom, illegal mining, cattle rustling and illicit arms trafficking.

Speaking at the third edition of the Schuman Security and Defence Forum, held at the European Parliament in Brussels, the Minister of Defence, General Christopher Gwabin Musa (Rtd), stressed that the Nigerian Financial Intelligence Unit (NFIU), the National Counter Terrorism Centre (NCTC) and security agencies are actively tracing illicit financial flows, prosecuting criminal facilitators and securing national borders to disrupt terrorist supply chains.

The Minister also reiterated the Government’s commitment to a comprehensive, multi-dimensional strategy to prevent and counter terrorism, while calling for stronger intelligence, technological and operational partnerships with the European Union (EU) and regional allies.

General Musa further reaffirmed Nigeria’s commitment to collective regional security through the Multinational Joint Task Force (MNJTF) in the Lake Chad Basin, ECOWAS, the African Union and international initiatives such as the West Africa Police Information System (WAPIS).

Outlining Nigeria’s counter-terrorism strategy under the leadership of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, the Minister noted that terrorism is a complex security challenge that exploits economic vulnerabilities, porous borders, local grievances and transnational organised crime.

According to a statement by the Special Assistant on Media to the Minister of Defence, Leah Katung-Babatunde, Nigeria, guided by its National Counter Terrorism Strategy (NACTEST), has transitioned from a predominantly kinetic approach to a coordinated framework that integrates military operations, intelligence, law enforcement, community engagement and socio-economic interventions.

Addressing the evolving tactics of violent extremist groups, the Minister highlighted Nigeria’s proactive measures to counter the illicit use of drones, digital communications and satellite technologies.

“Through intelligence-led operations, advanced surveillance, unmanned aerial platforms and military artificial intelligence, the Armed Forces of Nigeria continue to degrade terrorist capabilities.

“Notably, in May 2026, troops of Operation Hadin Kai successfully intercepted more than 400 Starlink communication devices linked to terrorist networks in the North-East,” the statement said.

Beyond operational interceptions, General Musa said the Ministry is actively promoting indigenous defence innovation through research and private-sector partnerships, while seeking closer collaboration with the EU in counter-drone technologies, digital forensics and satellite intelligence.

The Minister stated that the Armed Forces of Nigeria remain strictly bound by national laws and international humanitarian law, prioritising civilian protection, due process in the prosecution of suspects, and structured rehabilitation and reintegration pathways for eligible former combatants through initiatives such as Operation SAFE CORRIDOR.

The Schuman Security and Defence Forum provides a platform for high-level dialogue on international peace, security and defence issues. It brings together defence ministers from partner countries and EU Member States, representatives of international organisations and leading think tanks.

World.title: Infrastructure, Education Top Lists of Yayi’s Devt Agenda for Ogun State
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

James Sowole in Abeokuta

The All Progressives Congress (APC) governorship candidate in Ogun State, Senator Solomon Olamilekan Adeola, popularly known as Yayi, has identified infrastructure development and education as major priorities of his nine-point development agenda, outlining plans to improve road connectivity, expand access to electricity, and modernise learning facilities across the state.

The candidate revealed his plan yesterday, at the official unveiling of his manifesto, titled “Governance That Works for Everyone: My Economic and Social Development Covenant with the People of Ogun State”.

At the event held on at the June 12 Cultural Centre, Kuto, Abeokuta, and which attracted political bigwigs from accross the 20 local government areas of the state, Adeola assured the people of Ogun State of massive development and transformation of the state.

Adeola noted that the manifesto set out to address infrastructure deficits and strengthen human capital as part of efforts to drive economic growth and improve residents’ quality of life.

Under the infrastructure pillar, he proposed the construction and rehabilitation of rural access and agro-link roads, modern intercity transport terminals in Abeokuta, Sagamu, Ijebu-Ode and Ota, as well as the operationalisation of the Gateway Agro-Cargo Airport, advancement of the Kajola Dry Port and preliminary development of the proposed Ogun Waterside Deep Sea Port.

He further proposed the rehabilitation and equipping of public schools, improved access to clean water, sanitation and solar power in learning facilities, alongside measures to reduce school completion gaps and make education more inclusive for children in vulnerable, rural and border communities.

According to him, his education agenda would also include modernising school curricula, recruiting and training teachers, equipping secondary schools with ICT laboratories and introducing coding, robotics and digital learning programmes.

The APC candidate noted that the development plan is designed to connect communities to economic opportunities while preparing young people for the demands of a changing economy.

He explained that the proposed investments would be pursued alongside other pillars of his manifesto to ensure that infrastructure and human capital development contribute to shared prosperity across Ogun State.

“The story of Ogun State is written every day by ordinary citizens who rise early to work, farm, teach, and build. We offer leadership shaped by your hopes, grounded in truth, and dedicated to measurable action,” he said.

World.title: Reps FCT Committee Hails Betara at 60, Celebrates Legislative Leadership
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Michael Olugbode in Abuja

Members of the House of Representatives Committee on the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) have lauded their chairman, Rt. Hon. Muktar Betara Aliyu, for his leadership, legislative contributions and commitment to public service as he clocks 60.

The lawmakers described Betara as a distinguished legislator whose capacity to build consensus, drive legislative engagements and demonstrate purposeful leadership had earned him respect among colleagues and strengthened the work of the committee.

In a congratulatory statement signed by members of the committee on Sunday, they said the milestone offered an opportunity to celebrate a life defined by courage, legislative ingenuity, resilience and dedication to the service of the nation and his constituents.

They said Betara, as chairman of the committee, had demonstrated exemplary leadership, uncommon dedication and an impressive capacity to inspire confidence and deliver results.

“Your commitment to the work of the Committee and the development of the Federal Capital Territory reflects your deep understanding of public service and the responsibility entrusted to you,” the lawmakers said.

They also applauded his contributions to nation-building and his enduring commitment to the people of Biu, Bayo, Kwaya-Kusar and Shani Federal Constituency of Borno State, noting that his record of service had continued to distinguish him.

The lawmakers further celebrated Betara’s recognition as The Sun Newspaper’s House of Representatives Member of the Year, 2026, describing the award as a deserved acknowledgement of his legislative accomplishments, leadership and positive impact in public service.

According to them, the honour further underscores his dedication to legislative responsibilities and the contributions he has made to national development.

“At 60, you stand as an inspiring example of purposeful leadership, resilience and service with distinction. We are proud to be associated with your leadership and privileged to serve alongside you,” they said.

The committee members prayed that Almighty Allah would grant the celebrant sound health, greater wisdom, renewed strength and abundant grace as he begins a new decade.

They expressed hope that the years ahead would bring him greater accomplishments, fulfilment and more opportunities to serve the nation and humanity, wishing him a rewarding and impactful 60th birthday.

World.title: Rassie sets his sights on France with bold social media move
World.content:
Rassie has followed the France rugby team on X. Images via X

He may not be able to set foot in the stadium on match day, or give his opponents a stare-down during a training session, but Rassie Erasmus is still laser-focused on the Springboks’ next opponents – France.

South Africa will play their final test at Twickenham next weekend in the inaugural Nations Championship tournament.

RASSIE FOLLOWS FRANCE ON X

Hours after SA’s 20-17 defeat to Ireland, and subsequent advancement to the Nations Championship finals, Springbok coach clicked “follow” on the official X account for the French rugby team.



The countries will clash again – two weeks after playing in Paris – as the Northern and Southern Hemisphere contenders.

The match will take place at the Allianz Stadium in Twickenham, England, on Sunday, 29 November.

As Rassie has been sanctioned by World Rugby over comments questioning the efficiency of match officials, he will be watching from the sidelines, and not the coaches’ box.



Rassie is prohibited from entering the stadium on match day, communicating with players or coaching staff, issuing instructions, influencing tactical decisions or performing match-day media duties.

However, he can continue to perform his general head coaching duties in the build-up to match day, provided he does not breach the conditions of his suspension.

He is likely to be formulating his master plan, which could possibly rely on monitoring France’s social media activity for new information.



HOW TO WATCH SPRINGBOKS FINAL TEST MATCH

South Africa’s face-off against France in the Nations Championships will be broadcast on Sunday, 29 November at 18:40 SA time.

The match will be broadcast on DStv’s SuperSport Rugby channels on the premium package, open to all DStv subscribers under its OpenTime promotion, which runs from 25 November to 25 December.

This means that irrespective of package, subscribers will have access to every live channel at no extra cost.

World.title: Former Pirates superstar says Mofokeng is always five steps ahead
World.content:
The former Orlando Pirates and Bafana Bafana ace has been particularly impressed by the way Relebohile Mofokeng reads matches and anticipates situations before they develop.

The 22-year-old has enjoyed a productive start to the 2026/27 campaign. He has delivered 10 goals and four assists in 20 appearances for club and country.

RELEBOHILE MOFOKENG FLYING IN EUROPE

His move to Belgian side Royale Union Saint-Gilloise has also provided another opportunity to test himself outside South Africa after establishing his reputation at Orlando Pirates.



Modise believes the midfielder’s understanding of the game is what separates him from many other players.

Speaking on the CARWASH podcast, the former Bafana international suggested that Mofokeng still has another level to reach.

“He is a different player. If South Africans think they have seen the best of Rele, they haven’t,” Modise said.



“I honestly believe that. You can see that he is five steps ahead in everything that he does. You can see his movements. It’s amazing to see.”

The assessment goes beyond his technical ability. Modise is particularly impressed by the youngster’s movement and his ability to influence matches without necessarily being involved in every attacking action.

Mofokeng initially attracted attention as an attacking midfielder, but his development has shown that he can contribute in different areas of the pitch.



Modise believes there is no need to place unnecessary restrictions on his game. “So we are not saying we need to protect Rele anymore; we need to let Rele fly! Rele is football,” he added.

BRIGHTON MHLONGO HIGHLIGHTS ANOTHER IMPORTANT FACTOR

Former Pirates goalkeeper Brighton Mhlongo has also praised the youngster, although his attention was directed towards the mentality that has helped him reach this level.

For Mhlongo, the support Mofokeng received from his family during his development deserves recognition.



He believes the player’s willingness to learn and remain grounded could become just as important as his footballing qualities.

“Credit must go to his parents for supporting him and being there for him as a child, not as a superstar. What we are seeing is someone who is enjoying his football and someone who is willing to learn,” he said.

World.title: Kaizer Chiefs prepare to promote two new youngsters
World.content:
Kaizer Chiefs duo Neo Bohloko and Steven Mendes have emerged as candidates for promotion, with the club’s technical team monitoring their progress under reserve coach Vela Khumalo.

The possibility of integrating the pair into the first team comes during a season in which Chiefs’ reserve side has established itself at the top of the DDC standings.

BOHLOKO LEADS KAIZER CHIEFS’ GOALSCORING CHARGE

Bohloko has scored 11 goals in nine appearances, including a penalty in Chiefs’ 2-1 victory over Milford FC.



His scoring record has made him one of the leading attacking performers in the competition.

The 18-year-old Mendes has also contributed to the team’s attacking output. The attacking midfielder previously won the Golden Boot at the COSAFA Under-20 Championship with Amajita.

He has continued his involvement in the final third at club level, providing assists and scoring goals for Khumalo’s side.



According to a report by KickOff, Chiefs are considering gradually introducing both players to senior training, with possible first-team opportunities towards the end of the season.

A source told the publication:

“The boys have shown that they are simply outgrowing the reserve level. The technical team is very impressed with their maturity and consistency.



“The plan being discussed is to gradually integrate them into first-team training and potentially give them their senior debuts maybe at the end of the season.”

AMAKHOSI RESERVE SIDE SETS THE PACE

Under Khumalo, Chiefs had won their opening nine DDC matches, collecting 27 points to occupy first position in the standings.

That run included the 2-1 victory over Milford, in which Bohloko converted from the penalty spot.



Mendes’ international achievements have also added to his profile. His Golden Boot at the COSAFA U20 Championship came while representing South Africa’s junior national team.

World.title: Former player warns of a dangerous future for Kaizer Chiefs winger
World.content:
The 21-year-old Kaizer Chiefs attacker has found himself in an uncomfortable situation at Naturena. He failed to return to training following the recent international break.

His absence also meant missing Amakhosi’s preparations in Polokwane ahead of their Carling Knockout semi-final against Mamelodi Sundowns.

KAIZER CHIEFS STAR FAIZ ABRAHAMS GOES AWOL

Abrahams joined Amakhosi on a season-long loan from Stellenbosch FC in August, having previously played for Cape Town Spurs.



His situation has attracted attention, particularly following reports that he is considering walking away from professional football altogether.

Khanye believes the youngster needs to understand the significance of the opportunity he has been given.

The former Chiefs attacker knows what it means to represent one of the country’s biggest football institutions. He also knows how quickly things can change when a player’s conduct becomes an issue.



“For a boy of his age to be given a chance to play for an institution as massive as Kaizer Chiefs and decide to misuse it like he is doing currently, he must be from a very wealthy family,” says Khanye, in conversation with KickOff.

“Do you know how many players across South Africa would give everything just to train at Naturena for one day? When you get to Chiefs, you have arrived at the biggest stage in local football, yet he is treating it like it is nothing.”

Khanye’s concern is not only about the current situation but also how other clubs might view Abrahams when he eventually looks for another opportunity.



A reputation can be difficult to rebuild in professional football, especially when a young player is still trying to establish himself.

THE WARNING FROM JUNIOR KHANYE’S OWN EXPERIENCE

Khanye’s comments carry an additional dimension because his own career at Chiefs was affected by off-field controversies.

He believes Abrahams could be making a decision that becomes difficult to reverse once the immediate emotions surrounding his situation have passed.



“What the boy is doing right now is going to haunt him for the rest of his life,” Khanye added.

“Knowing South African teams, they will always judge him on this even if he is done serving his sentence. To everyone, he will always appear as a Bad Boy from now on.

“Chiefs are very professional. Where is Dumisani Zuma? We were also favourites of Bra K [Kaizer Motaung] and Bobby Motaung, but nevertheless we were released because of our bad behavior, even though we were from the club’s development.



Khanye concluded to say Abrahams doesn’t know what he is doing. He may end up in the bush.

DO YOU AGREE WITH THE FORMER KAIZER CHIEFS WINGER?

World.title: Former Pirates and Sundowns star says footballers need more than money
World.content:
Formerly a defender/midfielder for Orlando Pirates and Mamelodi Sundowns, Mhlongo feels the proposed pension fund for footballers is overdue but not enough. He is calling for a more serious issue.

For Mhlongo, the pressures experienced by players during their careers deserve equal attention, with Faiz Abrahams being the latest case.

BENSON MHLONGO CALLS FOR PYSCHOLOGISTS

Footballers are often expected to perform at the highest level while dealing with personal responsibilities that extend well beyond their professional commitments.



Some become the main providers for their families before they have developed the experience needed to manage the demands that come with financial responsibility.

Mhlongo believes clubs and football authorities should recognise that reality rather than treating players purely as sporting assets.

“That’s not even a question, we must have (psychologists), we’re dealing with human beings here. Human beings from different backgrounds, some of them are carrying huge responsibilities that are overwhelming and we’re not talking about people who are from the university,” Mhlongo told Kick Off.



His argument is that a player’s age does not necessarily reflect their ability to deal with the pressures of professional football.

Many young players enter the game having spent most of their childhood concentrating on training, matches and developing their abilities.

Suddenly, a professional contract can change their circumstances and those of the people around them.



The responsibility of supporting an entire family can become overwhelming, particularly when a young footballer is still learning how to navigate life outside the game.

Mhlongo believes this is where psychologists can make a meaningful difference.

Rather than waiting until a player experiences serious difficulties, clubs should have professionals who can help them understand and manage their challenges.



The former Cape Town Spurs assistant coach also highlighted the difference between entering a profession later in life and becoming financially responsible while still young.

“Where you start your career at the age of 28 or 30 and you are knowledgeable. We’re talking about young boys, who, the only thing they have been focusing on is playing football and when they become bread-winners at a young age there is a lot they encounter in family dynamics,” Mhlongo continued.

“So we need such people to help how to navigate around our challenges,” the Bafana Bafana legend added.

World.title: Sundowns coach says a different Chiefs player was the real Man of the Match
World.content:
Miguel Cardoso believes Mamelodi Sundowns had enough opportunities to change the outcome against Kaizer Chiefs, but their failure to take them proved costly in the Carling Knockout semi-final.

The Portuguese coach was particularly unhappy with the way his team handled possession in dangerous areas, arguing that unnecessary mistakes allowed Amakhosi to exploit spaces during transitions.

CARLING KNOCKOUT: MAMELODI SUNDOWNS 1-2 KAIZER CHIEFS

Kaizer Chiefs eventually secured a 2-1 extra-time victory at Loftus Versfeld, with Elias Mokwana playing a decisive role after coming off the bench.



But while Mfundo Vilakazi received the Man of the Match award, Cardoso had another player in mind.

The Sundowns coach singled out Brandon Petersen, whose performance between the posts helped Chiefs survive several difficult moments during the encounter.

“Just score our moments, I hope the fans at home understand that today the man of the match is Petersen, a goalkeeper today that showed himself in a level that we have…he is a wonderful goalkeeper but today he was extraordinary,” Cardoso told SuperSport.



The Carling Knockout award is determined through fan voting, meaning Cardoso’s preferred choice did not necessarily reflect the outcome of the supporters’ selection.

Petersen’s contribution was particularly important because Chiefs had to withstand pressure from a Sundowns side that struggled to turn its possession into goals.

Cardoso, however, felt the result was more about his team’s mistakes than anything else.



WHY MIGUEL CARDOSO BELIEVES SUNDOWNS LOST

The former Sporting CP coach pointed to the midfield as an area where Sundowns repeatedly gave away possession.

He believes those errors allowed Chiefs to attack quickly, something that played into Da Cruz’s tactical approach.

“That’s the story of this match, I told before details will define it, we didn’t score our moments, they profited two mistakes from us, we made a few of those mistakes wrong passes in the middle, allowing transitions and that’s what their game, it’s the game they play.



“The intention is to use the mistakes to profit from spaces, you need to be accurate, you cannot make those mistakes it’s so clear, the boys tried, but the story of the game is definition, definition, definition.”

Sundowns will now have to put the cup disappointment behind them as they return to Betway Premiership action. Cardoso’s immediate task is to get his players ready for their next league assignment against Kruger United.

With another trophy opportunity gone, the pressure will be on the Brazilians to respond positively in the league.

World.title: Tatjana Smith claps back at ‘running away’ criticism
World.content:
Tatjana Schoenmaker has reflected on representing South Africa as a professional swimmer. Images via IG

Tatjana Smith has responded to critics who’ve accused her of “running away” after she announced her decision to switch sporting nationalities from South Africa to the Netherlands.

Earlier this month, the Olympic swimmer revealed that she would be representing the European country, to which she has dual citizenship.

This follows her sharing her grievances with Swimming South Africa (SSA).



TATJANA SMITH RESPONDS TO CRITICISM OF SPORTING NATIONALITY

In a social media post, Tatjana Smith reflected on representing South Africa as a professional swimmer. She also responded to her critics who questioned her new allegiance to the Netherlands, of which she holds dual citizenship.

Posting a montage of her career highlights, Tatjana shared: “11 years being part of Team SA.

One flag. Countless sacrifices. Four Olympic medals. World Championship medals. Commonwealth medals. African Championship medals.



“Years of dedication, commitment and pride in wearing the green and gold”

She continued: “Giving up when things get difficult doesn’t produce a journey like this. And running away when things get tough? I think 11 years tells a different story”.

Tatjana – whose gold and silver Olympic medals will remain SA accolades – added: “Forever grateful for the privilege of representing South Africa”.



‘I CAN ALREADY FEEL THE DIFFERENCE’

In an interview with SwimSwam earlier this month, Tatjana Smith set the record straight on why she chose to switch sporting nationalities.

The 29-year-old explained that she held dual citizenship because her father was a Dutch citizen.

“The reality is that it was always an option”, she said.



Because she hadn’t competed for her country since announcing her retirement at the 2024 Paris Olympics, she was now eligible to represent the Netherlands.

Despite her “love and pride”, Tatjana Smith detailed the financial, practical, and emotional “burdens” she faced in the South.

Since switching nationalities, the Olympic gold medallist stated that she was impressed by how the Dutch prioritised their athletes’ well-being.



She said: “Off the bat, I can already feel the difference and changes. I don’t have to self-fund my way to get to World Championships”

In a clip announcing her decision to switch nationalities, the 29-year-old revealed that she had based her decision on financial stability, support, and sustainability.

World.title: ‘I can do taxes but too old for companies’: Pensioner hits back at age barrier
World.content:
An older man wearing eyeglasses is reading documents next to a laptop at home. Image: Pexels

A South African pensioner has called on employers to give older people a chance at work, saying age should not cancel out years of experience.

Ria Cordier shared the plea on The South African’s Facebook page, where grant recipients discussed returning to work to supplement their SASSA payments.

“They must hire pensioners; we will work, unlike the youngsters who think the world owes them everything. We have skills; I can do taxes, but I’m too old for companies,” Cordier wrote.



‘We will work’

Cordier’s comment speaks to a frustration shared by many older South Africans who still want to earn an income but say the door is closed to them.

According to Cordier, the issue is not ability or willingness. The skills are there, including tax work, but companies see age first.

The comment also aims at younger job seekers, suggesting that older workers bring a stronger work ethic to the table. It is a view likely to spark debate in a country where youth unemployment remains a major challenge.



Still job hunting after retirement

Cordier is not alone in looking for work later in life.

Esaiah Scavity Padi shared a brief update on his own situation in the same thread.

“Still looking for a job as pensioner now,” Padi wrote.



The short comment shows how retirement no longer means the end of the job search for many South Africans. With the grant under pressure from rising prices, some pensioners say part-time or contract work is the only way to keep up with monthly expenses.

For older job seekers, the search often means competing against younger candidates for limited positions, while facing assumptions about their health, energy or ability to adapt to new technology.

Can pensioners work and keep their grant?

Pensioners who find work should be aware that the Older Persons Grant is means tested. The test determines the amount of the grant a person can receive based on their financial situation, and for married applicants, both spouses’ income and assets are taken into account.



This means income from a job could affect the grant amount. Pensioners considering work should check with SASSA before taking on employment so they understand how their earnings could affect their payments.

The Older Persons Grant increased by R80 to R2 400 from April 2026, an amount many grant recipients say does not stretch far enough

Win R2 000 in the South African SASSA grant survey

If you receive a SASSA grant and want to share your story, we want to hear from you.



Take part in our survey and stand a chance to win R2 000. Your responses help us tell the stories that matter.

World.title: Overberg fire contained - Municipality
World.content:
CAPE TOWN - A fire that had engulfed parts of the Overberg has been contained.

According to the Overberg District Municipality, there is no immediate threat to the surrounding communities.

Firefighters managed to bring the De Hoop-Potberg blaze under control overnight. The fire threatened residential areas in Malgas and Reverine.

Despite the fires being brought under control, the devastation is significant.

Over 25,000 hectares and 22 homes were destroyed.

Firefighting teams are still working to prevent the blaze from spreading towards Infanta and Sandhoogte.

Residents are being urged to remain vigilant.

World.title: Surveyed teenagers confident they can refuse alcohol
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - About 75% of teenagers say they are confident refusing alcohol.

This is according to Aware.org's alcohol awareness program targeted at high school students.

They are working on ways to curb alcohol-related harm through education and prevention programs

With the academic year winding down, a lot of teenagers will be looking for different ways to keep themselves entertained.

In the organisation's latest study, over 100,000 students were questioned in 2025 broadly.

In their targeted groups 10,000 were reviewed and 75% of those said that they were confident to not engage in underage drinking.

World.title: Ferrari chief furious after Leclerc, Hamilton clash again
World.content:
Ferrari boss Fred Vasseur lambasted Charles Leclerc for a "lack of respect" after the Monegasque driver's latest clash with team-mate Lewis Hamilton torpedoed the Italian team's Las Vegas Grand Prix.

Vasseur was left furious after Leclerc collided with Hamilton on lap 38 in Las Vegas -- just weeks after the drivers had been told that the team must come first after clashing at the Mexico Grand Prix.

Leclerc was subsequently hit with a 10-second penalty after an FIA Stewards inquiry and finished in 10th, while Hamilton finished seventh.

"Honestly, my position is that once again it's more than unacceptable," Vasseur said of the latest incident.

"I had exactly the same word after Mexico -- but it's a lack of respect. It's a lack of respect for the team, for the sponsor, but mainly for the people at home.

"Charles clearly made a mistake, and it has cost the team dearly."

The signs of lingering tension between Hamilton and Leclerc had been brewing during the early stages of Saturday's race.

A frustrated Hamilton at one point used an expletive as he told the team over the radio to get Leclerc to "back off" while he chased the leaders.

Vasseur said he had given Leclerc a warning shortly before he collided with Hamilton.

"I think I was quite harsh, we passed the message to Charles five corners before, and for me it's a professional mistake," Vasseur said.

"I know that he apologized. I know that he was sorry. But once again we destroyed the race today that we could have done much better... we can't lose points like this.

"More than points, it's the motivation of everybody -- the reward of the job done, the reward of the effort, and this it's a huge frustration for me."

Asked if he felt both drivers bore some of the responsibility for the latest controversy, Vasseur replied: "No, I think the decision of the FIA was quite clear."

Hamilton meanwhile would not answer when asked if he felt Ferrari should issue clear team rules to its drivers.

"That is for Ferrari to decide," the seven-time world champion told Sky Sports.

"I've done all I can and I've said everything and more. It has been difficult.

"All I can do is show up and give it everything I can, and hopefully in the background they eventually figure it out."

World.title: Prayer service held in honour of Phumzile Mlambo-Ngcuka
World.content:
She became a deputy minister of trade and industry from 1996 until 1999. Thereafter she became minister of Minerals and Energy from 1999 until 2005.

Mlambo-Ngcuka served as deputy president under former president Thabo Mbeki from 2005 until 2007. At the time of her death, she served as Chancellor at the University of Johannesburg since 2022.

She is survived by her husband, former head of the National Prosecuting Authority, Adv Bulelani Ngcuka and her five children.

She has been granted a state funeral and will be buried on Saturday at eXesi in the Eastern Cape.

World.title: Family searching for Mathibestad granny who went missing on Durban trip
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The family of an elderly woman are in desperate search after she went missing in Durban on Monday.

Selinah Boiyane Peete (84) from Mathibestad near Hammanskraal was part of a group of elderly women who regularly play soccer together.

The group, that had been visiting Durban, went to the beach before checking into the Albany Hotel.

Peete is said to have disappeared between getting off the bus and reaching the hotel.

A missing person's case has been opened with the Durban Central Police. However, there has been no breakthrough as yet.

Her grandson and a councillor from Moretele Local Municipality have since travelled to Durban, to join the search party.

World.title: Summer rains temporary relief as SA farmers brace themselves for drought
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - South Africa has over the past few weeks been experiencing rainy weather that is bringing much needed relief to the country's farmers.

According to Agbiz Chief economist, Wandile Sihlobo, despite this, there is still a risk of a drought.

Improved soil moisture and grazing conditions do not necessarily mean the drought threat has passed.

Sihlobo says while some areas might have experience flooding, which might many farmers think the country is out of the woods. The data shows that South Africa will experience a delayed drought.

World.title: DA, ActionSA failing to find each other
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Democratic Alliance leader Geordin Hill-Lewis has accused ActionSA leader Herman Mashaba of trying to justify his U-turn on working with the ANC.

The DA has made what it has called its full and final offer to ActionSA. The offer includes offering Tshwane in exchange for Johannesburg and Ekurhuleni.

This will mean that Nasiphi Moya remains mayor of the Tshwane if elected by council.

Mashaba, however, has rejected the proposal, saying it does not deserve a response.

Hill-Lewis insists that compromises are necessary, describing the offer as reasonable.

"He has to find a way to justify his betrayal to the voters wishes," Hill-Lewis says about Mashaba.

World.title: Fossil fuels still missing from latest COP31 draft deal
World.content:
The COP31 presidency proposed an eleventh-hour deal Sunday that again fails to mention fossil fuels -- an omission that deepened a tense standoff at the UN climate talks.

The latest offering by summit co-hosts Turkey and Australia published deep into overtime leaves unresolved tensions over planet-heating fossil fuels but retains a much-sought goal to electrify the global economy.

The proposal needs consensus approval from nearly 200 nations at a closing session Sunday but they have struggled to bridge differences during two weeks of grinding negotiations.

The European Union and other nations have pushed for strong language on transitioning away from fossil fuels, a call that has faced resistance from oil-rich Saudi Arabia.

An EU official told AFP the latest proposal was a "backwards" step, warning there was a "very real possibility" that COP31 ends with no deal.

"I am more pessimistic today than I was yesterday," the official said on condition of anonymity.

"The situation is difficult, and the outcome is uncertain. The oil-producing countries are putting up a fierce fight," a German official said.

A Saudi official declined to comment when approached by AFP.

Fossil fuels are a flashpoint at the climate talks and the summit comes against a difficult backdrop of soaring energy prices and geopolitical tensions stemming from the war in Iran.

A draft deal unveiled earlier this week called for a faster phase out of fossil fuels but a second, pared-down version released Thursday stripped away all mentions of coal, oil and gas.

Threats of a walkout prompted Turkey and Australia to convene a hurried meeting between the European Union and Saudi Arabia in a bid to broker a compromise.

The latest text introduces a reference to a previous global deal in 2023 to shift the world away from fossil fuels -- but stops short of naming them explicitly.

And it retains a contentious push to expand carbon capture and storage, a technology championed by the fossil fuel industry but criticised as costly and ineffective in cutting emissions.

"We are very disappointed with how the text looks," the environment minister of Antigua and Barbuda, Michael Joseph, told AFP after leaving the COP31 presidency's offices.

"I can't honestly say that I'm okay with it passing" in its current state, Joseph said, adding that the draft was "quite silent" on fossil fuels.

- Goal to electrify -

The draft also calls for global efforts to boost the share of electricity in total final energy consumption to 35 percent by 2035 and the expansion of "clean energy".

The summit had been under pressure to show progress in tackling soaring greenhouse gas emissions in a year of climate-linked disasters from Europe to Nepal and Indonesia.

Facing blowback over fossil fuels, Turkey and Australia pointed to "electrification" as a way to cut heat-trapping emissions and bolster energy security.

This works by replacing technologies that burn fossil fuels directly -- like diesel cars and gas heating -- with electric alternatives.

But some nations had demanded an explicitly "clean" target to ensure the electrification push was powered by renewable energy and not fossil fuels.

Around one-third of global electricity is produced using coal and another fifth using fossil gas.

Attempts by Saudi Arabia, India and Kenya meanwhile to delay the next set of reports by the UN's Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) have been another major source of friction at the talks.

The draft text "highlights the importance" of these reports for an upcoming stocktake of global carbon-cutting efforts in 2028.

Dozens of countries across Europe, Africa and the Pacific want these assessments by the global scientific authority on climate change published in time for that crucial stocktake.

Countries have also disagreed at COP31 over how to respond to the looming breach of the 1.5C warming target set under the Paris climate accord.

The latest draft expressed "deep concern" that global warming would cross 1.5C above pre-industrial levels in the next few years.

The talks also jammed over long-running complaints that rich nations are shirking their obligations to help developing nations confront climate change.

The removal of a $120 billion target for climate adaptation angered developing nations.

By Laurent Thomet, Nick Perry And Fulya Ozerkan

World.title: Ruto seeks way out of isolation as regional leaders lose trust in him
World.content:
President William Ruto arrives in Congo Brazzaville for a high level meeting on November 21, 2026. [PCS]

President William Ruto arrived in the northern Congolese town of Oyo on Saturday evening aboard a military aircraft from Kisumu, stepping into a four-way summit convened by Congolese President Denis Sassou Nguesso with the explicit hope of arresting a diplomatic free fall that has left Kenya increasingly isolated in its own neighborhood.

On Sunday, Ruto came face to face with Democratic Republic of Congo President Félix Tshisekedi for the first time since relations between Nairobi and Kinshasa soured nearly three years ago.

World.title: Shun leaders inciting you to cause chaos, PS Omollo tells youth
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Internal Security Principal Secretary Raymond Omollo. [File,Standard]

Internal Security Principal Secretary Raymond Omollo has warned young people against political violence, saying the destruction of public property costs lives and diverts resources meant for development.

The warning comes amid concerns over political violence in Embu following the September 12 incident at Nembure Stadium, where a meeting attended by Deputy President Kithure Kindiki was disrupted, leaving one person dead, six vehicles torched and three others vandalised.

Speaking during a Mass at St Thomas More Kairuri Parish in Embu County, Omollo challenged young people to question leaders who ask them to disrupt meetings, block roads or destroy property.

“Before you leave home to disrupt a meeting, ask that leader whether they would allow their own child to do what they are asking you to do,” he said.

“Ask them what they are doing to help you access education, training and employment.”

Omollo said young people should also question what political leaders were doing to improve their access to education, technical training and employment.

He said the Government was working to expand opportunities for young people through education, technical training and employment.

The PS welcomed efforts in the technical and vocational education and training (TVET) sector to equip young people in Embu with skills to pursue their ambitions.

At the same time, Omollo commended county leadership for working with the national government to combat illicit alcohol and drug abuse.

Omollo said proposed legislative changes targeting the sector had passed the first reading in Parliament and urged residents to participate in the next stages of the legislative process.

On security, the PS acknowledged calls for more police vehicles, saying the Government was investing in personnel, vehicles and equipment.

However, he challenged residents to help protect public investments, citing reports that 10 police vehicles had been burned in Embu.

“We use our taxes to buy police vehicles, build markets and construct roads. We cannot pay for development and then allow a few individuals to destroy what belongs to all of us,” he said.

Omollo warned that anyone suspected of destroying property would be taken to court in accordance with the law, where the judiciary would determine their cases.

He maintained that political differences should not be used to justify vandalism, endanger lives or disrupt public services.

“The Constitution protects the right to express ourselves peacefully and unarmed. Political differences cannot be an excuse to vandalise property, endanger lives or disrupt the services our communities depend on,” he said.

Those present included Public Service, Human Capital Development and Special Programmes Cabinet Secretary Geoffrey Ruku, Embu Governor Cecily Mbarire, Senator Alexander Munyi and Deputy Governor Kinyua Mugo, among others.

World.title: Narok Senator under fire after threatening to shoot auctioneers in Sh1.2m dispute
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize
