World.title: La campaña eleva el drama en la recta final: “¡A por ellos!”. “¡No pasarán!”
World.content:
La plaza de toros de Valencia, completamente llena, espera el momento cumbre del mitin: la salida de su líder, Alberto Núñez Feijóo, más crecido que nunca tras el debate del jueves. Pero antes de verlo en persona, los militantes lo miran en dibujos animados. En la pantalla gigante aparece un vídeo de anime: Sánchez es un malvado monstruo enorme, de capa negra y ojos rojos, que lanza rayos del mismo color y domina con ellos a miles de ciudadanos también con ojos enrojecidos. Entonces llega Feijóo como un superhéroe que lanza rayos azules y vence a Sánchez para salvar al pueblo. El público aplaude enfervorecido. Poco después sale el líder del PP, el real, y avisa: “no os fieis de nada. Son capaces de todo, y heridos son todavía más peligrosos”. Y ahí la plaza de toros entera, de forma espontánea y por primera vez en un mitin del PP, canta “¡A por ellos, oé! ¡A por ellos, oé!”, mientras Feijóo sonríe.

La siguiente escena, solo media hora después pero muy lejos de Valencia, es en Santa Cruz de Tenerife. Otro mitin, esta vez de Pedro Sánchez. Arranca con música. En el escenario cantan “gallo negro, gallo rojo”, una mítica canción antifranquista. “Se encontraron en la arena, los dos gallos, frente a frente. El gallo negro era grande, pero el rojo era valiente”, se escucha. Muchos la cantan. Y también espontáneamente, con Sánchez en primera fila, la gente empieza a gritar: “¡No pasarán!¡No pasarán!“, el lema de la resistencia antifascista en la Guerra Civil.

La campaña encara su semana final en un tono de creciente dramatismo y con el sondeo de 40dB situando en práctico empate técnico al PP y el PSOE para el primer partido, aunque el bloque de derecha conserva una cómoda mayoría absoluta de 187 diputados que, sin embargo, ha ido bajando ligeramente desde los 191 que le auguraba esta misma encuestadora hace dos semanas. El tracking diario, que solo se puede publicar hasta el lunes, demuestra que, pese al consenso amplio de que Sánchez tuvo peor desempeño que Feijóo, el debate no ha frenado el lento pero constante crecimiento del PSOE, e incluso está reduciendo ligeramente sus fugas hacia la derecha.

01:22 Feijóo: "No os fieis, heridos son más peligrosos" El candidato a la presidencia del Gobierno por el PP, Alberto Núñez Feijóo, en el centro, junto a Miguel Tellado (izq), su director de campaña. Foto: Mònica Torres

Pero el problema para la izquierda es que el Frente Amplio está cada vez más débil, con muchísima transferencia hacia el PSOE —18,9%— y eso permite al bloque de la derecha llegar cómodamente a la mayoría que no logró en 2023. “La izquierda tiene aún más margen para movilizar, los indecisos están sobre todo en la izquierda, hay más movilización en la derecha”, resume Belén Barreiro, responsable de este sondeo.

El PSOE busca esa movilización, también en el votante más templado, y Sánchez recibió en este contexto un espaldarazo de la plana mayor del Gobierno de Felipe González, con varios ex ministros clave pidiendo el voto para él y José Bono, otro histórico, criticando al ex presidente por anunciar el voto en blanco: “no hagas el tonto, Felipe, que el PSOE te debe mucho a ti pero tú mucho más al PSOE”.

Con este empate técnico por arriba según 40dB, los dos grandes líderes ya no están para medias tintas y lanzan sendos órdagos a sus compañeros de bloque para acumular voto útil. Sánchez anuncia que este martes se prorrogará el impuesto a la banca, una señal nítidamente de izquierdas, una reclamación histórica del espacio del Frente Amplio. “No son dos derechas, es una única involución, y hay una única papeleta que puede frenarlas, la del PSOE”, clama el presidente en una apelación muy clara a concentrar el voto.

01:48 Ada Colau y Yolanda Dïaz comparten mitin y critican las "mentiras de Feijóo" De izquierda a derecha: Emilio Delgado, Ada Colau, la vicepresidenta Yolanda Díaz, Ernesto Urtasun y Gerardo Pisarello, este sábado en Barcelona. Foto: GIANLUCA BATTISTA

Es tan evidente este intento que Yolanda Díaz, que ha vuelto a la campaña para revitalizar al Frente Amplio, critica abiertamente a Sánchez desde un mitin en Barcelona: “El PSOE se equivoca. Esto no va de ser el primero y sacar el mejor resultado. Quedar primero no sirve para gobernar, sino para entregarle las llaves de la Moncloa a Feijóo y Abascal. No va de ser el más listo de la clase, va de que el bloque sume”.

Esta batalla en el bloque de la izquierda es muy relevante, porque el único gran hito que tiene para darle la vuelta a las encuestas es el debate a cuatro del jueves. Ahí, en 2023, con Feijóo ausente, Sánchez y Díaz hicieron un ticket, mostraron mucha sintonía, y se vendieron como una coalición bien avenida. Y funcionó. Ahora, ya sin Díaz, la candidata, Ada Colau, que no tiene esa química con Sánchez, está obligada a distanciarse para luchar contra el voto útil. Mientras, habrá que ver cómo funcionan Feijóo y Santiago Abascal, porque nunca han estado juntos en un debate. Y ahí también hay una guerra encarnizada por el voto útil.

Tanto, que mientras Sánchez se centra en la izquierda, vuelve a su perfil habitual y deja atrás el fallido intento por reconvertirse en moderado por una noche, Feijóo promete en Valencia una ley antiocupación, uno de los asuntos estrella de Vox, el día anterior en Canarias habla de usar a las fuerzas armadas contra la inmigración, y aprovecha el debate para ofrecerse como el verdadero líder del antisanchismo: “El jueves no entré solo en ese plató. Pensé en cuánta gente querría estar en mi lugar y mirarle a la cara y decirle lo que siente”, lanza con el público cada vez más caliente contra Sánchez.

Abascal también se indigna con Feijóo por buscar el voto útil. “Que cada uno vote a quien quiera”, clama en Sevilla. “Solo el crecimiento de Vox es lo que está asegurando la alternativa el día 29. Le pido al PP que deje esa estrategia”, se reivindica. Y remata: “me gustaría que el señor Feijóo, que el otro día zarandeó a Pedro Sánchez en el debate, conteste con quién va a pactar el 29 de noviembre”. Abascal lanza así la idea de que Feijóo podría intentar una abstención de un PSOE ya sin Sánchez para no depender de Vox, algo muy improbable, pero así intenta evitar que el PP le arrebate votos.

En el PSOE intentan superar el debate cuanto antes, como en 2023. Entonces también salió mal y, sin embargo, después las elecciones fueron mucho mejor de lo esperado. La frustración con la estrategia y, sobre todo, la ejecución de Sánchez está muy extendida en el Gobierno y el PSOE. “No hay que darle muchas vueltas. El presidente no es bueno en los debates televisivos, sí en los parlamentarios. Nunca le ha salido bien un debate en televisión, especialmente los cara a cara”, resume un miembro del Gobierno.

Y sin embargo, el debate del jueves es decisivo, la última oportunidad. Para el cara a cara, Sánchez rechazó ensayar con sparring, algo muy habitual y que había hecho otras veces. Feijóo usó a sus colaboradores para que le lanzaran preguntas difíciles constantemente en los días previos. Sánchez no hizo ese ejercicio, se encerró con las fichas y escribió él mismo buena parte de las respuestas. Esta vez lo preparó mucho más en soledad que otras.

Aunque aún no parece haber decisión tomada, es muy probable que Sánchez, que es un pragmático que cambia sin problemas cuando algo no funciona, dé un giro radical a su estrategia. Además esta vez tendrá ahí a Abascal, que es uno de los ejes de su campaña contra la ultraderecha mundial.

Mientras, en el PP no se creen los sondeos que no detectan movimiento después del debate y están convencidos de que el encuentro sirvió para frenar mucha sangría hacia Vox, porque la gente más antisanchista vio cómo se enfrentó al presidente y eso hace que pierda mucha fuerza Abascal. Por eso el debate del jueves también es importante en esa batalla.

Un dirigente del PP analiza las consecuencias del debate y lo que queda. “Es muy importante lo que hizo Alberto el jueves. La derecha pudo ver cómo se enfrenta al que consideran gran enemigo de España. Y el debate a cuatro es distinto pero no es muy peligroso. Nadie moderado va a ver a Colau como referente para el Gobierno de España, a Díaz sí se la podía ver más amable, Colau tiene una imagen muy dura”, resume.

A Sánchez le queda, además del debate, un Consejo de Ministros con anuncios importantes este martes, como este impuesto a la banca, pero habrá más, según fuentes del Gobierno, y varias entrevistas y mítines grandes para buscar la remontada. El problema es que la izquierda necesita que pase algo que gire la situación. Y en 2023 eso no vino de un movimiento genial de los progresistas, sino de una cadena de errores tanto del PP como de Vox. Y esta vez ambos han aprendido la lección, o al menos eso dicen en sus cúpulas, y van a minimizar los riesgos.

El presidente de VOX, Santiago Abascal, el sábado durante un mitin en Sevilla. PACO PUENTES

Abascal llegó a decir el martes de esa última semana que Cataluña sufriría algo “peor que el 155 de chiste de Rajoy″ si él gobernaba con el PP, y los expertos detectaron justo después un gran aumento del voto del PSC en esta comunidad. Feijóo tuvo el último lunes de campaña un grave error con las pensiones en la entrevista con Silvia Intxaurrondo en TVE, no fue al debate a cuatro el jueves y en los últimos días se metió en varios líos dialécticos por su relación con Marcial Dorado, de quien llegó a decir que no sabía de sus antecedentes delictivos porque “entonces no había internet ni google”.

Esta vez Feijóo no ha confirmado aún entrevista con Intxaurrondo, aunque es probable que sí acuda. Le quedan esta semana 12 entrevistas y media docena de mítines, además del debate. Pero en su entorno señalan que Feijóo aprendió muy claramente de 2023 y esta vez todo está mucho más controlado. No habrá errores esta semana, insisten, y con eso debería bastar para consolidar el domingo esa mayoría absoluta con Vox que le dan los sondeos. Pero él mismo sabe que todo se puede jugar en esos días, y por eso avisó en el mitin: “No basta con la victoria emocional del jueves, esto ha sido un entrenamiento, ahora nos queda el partido. Todo lo importante es lo que ocurra a partir del lunes, y lo trascendente es lo que pasa el jueves, viernes, sábado y domingo”. Ahora todo lo que suceda cuenta doble o triple.

World.title: El maestro Alcaraz, hasta donde él quiera: ni el isquio ni Zverev pudieron con él
World.content:
El murciano doblega al número uno, muy superado hasta el amago del final, y acaba con 28 años de negativas para el tenis español en la cita de los mejores: 6-2 y 7-6(7)

Ahí se las apaña el prestidigitador, ese joven de pulsaciones cero que cuanto más fea se pone la cosa, cuando Alexander Zverev apunta al reenganche —6-3 para él en el tie-break de la segunda manga—y cuando a la mayoría le entra el canguelo, lo hace así de bien, como los ángeles, como si nada: dos dejadas, un par de caricias, y todo en su sitio. Él, ya Maestro. 23 años tiene y por fin se acabó la maldición, ese impedimento arrastrado por el tenis español masculino desde el 98, Álex Corretja, sucesor de quien abrió vía, Manolo Orantes en el 76. No pudo lograrlo Rafael Nadal ni tampoco Moyà, Ferrero ni Ferrer, pero lo canta bien alto ahora él, murcianico y campeonissimo: 6-2 y 7-6(7), en 2h 02m.

Estampa el revés rabioso y cae a plomo sobre la pista, más éxito y más y más historia. ¿Límites? Ni más ni menos, los que él mismo se imponga. Hasta donde quiera y más allá. Bailoteando ya con Andre Agassi, Roger Federer y Novak Djokovic: posee los cuatro grandes y también esta condecoración que lleva el sello de la adversidad, de ese isquio travieso que ha duplicado el reto y que a su vez lo magnifica. Efectivamente, también se puede hacer así: “Si te retirases mañana, ya estaría bien. Ya puedes relajarte, Carlos…”, bromea el otro finalista, rendido a la obviedad. Así es, continúa viajando a la velocidad de la luz.

Más información Alexander Zverev, el rey cuestionado

A ras de pista, la movilidad de Zverev impresiona. Él, una mole que roza los dos metros y desplaza alrededor de 100 kilos en cada maniobra, se desenvuelve en términos de movilidad como uno más. Lo mece Alcaraz de un lado a otro, percutor el español, y no desiste en la carrera el alemán, que devuelve dos pelotazos muy meritorios y recibe el aplauso del padre de Alcaraz. Podría haber sido un pívot o darle al vóleibol, pero eligió la raqueta y mal no se le da. Los críticos van recogiendo cable. Ahora bien, lo del arte es para otros y en esas hay un murciano que nació con duende en el brazo y una pista en la cabeza.

Alcaraz, al servicio. Guglielmo Mangiapane (REUTERS)

Cuadra ese tenis tan genuino, elegantemente barroco y a la vez cargado de modernidad, con la voz imponente de Andrea Bocelli, que antes amenizaba el preámbulo entonando Il Canto de degli Italiani: todo el mundo en pie, Jannik Sinner viéndolo desde el sofá, el español con cara de póquer —concentradísimo, al igual que todos estos días— y una derecha primorosa que va despidiendo fuego a discreción. Diez minutos dura el primer juego y Zverev ya está apagando llamas. No se salvará poco después, cuando tres pelotas mal tocadas despliegan una alfombra roja por la que desfila felizmente Alcaraz, en su absoluta salsa.

Con mucho ‘flow’

Temeroso, el de Hamburgo (29 años) apenas sale de la cueva y concede demasiados metros; si no, él mismo se los brinda. Da igual. No suele ser él (23) de los que pregunte. Adueñado de la zona nuclear, le pega que da gusto y al rival se le va poniendo mala cara, pensando quizá en que ha caído ya en el remolino: ¡El tormento! La mente, tan poderosa y a la vez tan puñetera. Ya le ha caído una advertencia y recibirá otra.

Bota y bota Zverev la pelota como si no hubiera un mañana, a ver si así Alcaraz se contagia de la parsimonia, de ese proceder pastoso y necesario para él. Pero nada, no hay manera. Vías absolutamente divergentes. Quiere uno que todo sea lento y el otro apuesta otra vez por la celeridad, un pim-pam-pum arrasador. El dj pincha los acordes iniciales de las Ocho Millas de Eminem y el de El Palmar, americanizado, con todo ese flow que maneja, menea la cabeza acompañando el rap. En cualquier caso, poco importa la música, el escenario y todo lo que gire a su alrededor: es en sí una fiesta.

Zverev, cabizbajo en otro instante del partido. Guglielmo Mangiapane (REUTERS)

Sin medias tintas, salvador. En una era todavía por configurarse, sus arabescos son una bendición que atrapa, tan seductor como eficiente ese repertorio que en poco más que un santiamén, menos de tres meses, ha dejado claro el orden natural de las cosas. Todo el merecimiento para el alemán, pero en el fondo, es perfectamente consciente de lo que hay. Aun así, debe creérselo. Contragolpea, del 4-1 al break y 4-2, aunque no es más que un espejismo. Mira al infinito, se cabrea con Aurélie Tourte (venga ya…) y lanza la raqueta con cuidado hacia el fondo, que la final está rompiéndose (set), pero no vaya a ser que la líe de más.

Siesta y arrebato

Entonces se van los dos al vestuario, y si uno vuelve tan lozano, fresquísimo, el otro lo hace desencajado. Un tenista se derrumba. Mentalmente, Zverev va quebrándose. “¡Sas-cha, Sas-cha, Sas-cha!”. Esfuerzo en vano. La evolución de este año con la derecha, punto débil, va yéndose por el sumidero y si para él es imposible ganar con un solo costado, el revés, a Alcaraz le basta con una pierna para seguir haciendo de las suyas con poesía, pero firme, que lo de hoy va de ganar. En su caso, no ha lugar disociar lo uno de lo otro. Puro disfrute para el ojo.

Sigue tocándola más o menos como quiere, y, en paralelo, el adversario no encuentra la manera de reengancharse. Desde el punto de vista anímico, suspenso. Muy flojito esta vez. El español, en cambio, parece poseído, todo y más le entra, cabeza bien alta y puño arriba cuando sus colegas, en uno de los córneres, le lanzan los cumplidos. Desde el box, Samuel López le sugiere “¡que venga, que venga él!”, mientras que el tallo camina todo el rato mirando al suelo y deambulante, quizá compadeciéndose, asumiendo que no puede. ¿No?

Alcaraz, sobre la pista tras lograr la victoria. Guglielmo Mangiapane (REUTERS)

3-1 abajo ya, no había perdido el servicio en todo el torneo y lo ha entregado cuatro veces. Sencillamente, tenis. Se podrá discutir de todo, de los materiales a los formatos o a las superficies, de épocas, velocidades o de físicos. En el fondo, la naturaleza de este deporte es profundamente incomprensible. El irse y el volver. ¿Zverev con vida? Exacto. Increíble pero cierto. De estar a un suspiro del 5-2, a solo dos puntos de que el alemán se haga con el set. ¿Y qué ha ocurrido? Alcaraz pierde temporalmente el norte, la precisión, como si necesitase ser exigido para reactivarse y frotar otra vez la lámpara. Nada nuevo, de la niñez hasta hoy.

Tras la siestecilla, el arrebato demoledor. ¡Esto es mío!

Y así, al tira y afloja del desempate, con maestría, termina cerrándose esta historia para recordar, el relato de una semana en la que la rodilla y el muslo dispararon todas las alarmas, pero resuelta finalmente bajo una ley simple, la selvática: la del más fuerte. Desde esa peana del fondo descerraja e inteligentemente, con esa capacidad extraordinaria que él tiene para simplificar lo complejo y revertir los malos momentos, Alcaraz se corona al compás de un “¡Viva Murcia!” y refrenda lo sospechado: ser el número uno no significa ser necesariamente el mejor.

World.title: Marc Márquez es eterno: levanta su octavo título de MotoGP tras culminar una remontada increíble en el GP de Portugal
World.content:
El piloto de Ducati iguala la marca de Agostini en la categoría reina y logra su décimo cetro mundialista tras rematar la faena con una octava plaza en Portimao y pasar de los 102 puntos de distancia en junio a ser campeón

A finales de mayo, las matemáticas decían que el alirón era altamente improbable, pero con Marc Márquez queda de sobras demostrado que nada es imposible. No importó la brecha de más de 100 puntos abierta por los rivales ni su brazo derecho hecho trizas, operado por novena vez en siete años unas semanas antes. El supercampeón de Cervera, a sus 33 años, ahora el tercer campeón más veterano de la historia de MotoGP, puso más cabeza que nunca en la persecución del nuevo título, el octavo en la categoría reina y el décimo en toda la escalera mundialista. Con los riesgos asumidos en la gira asiática, y pese al resbalón del sábado, le bastó una octava posición en el GP de Portugal este domingo para consumar su remontada inverosímil en el campeonato del mundo.

El alirón sitúa al 93 a la altura de los ocho títulos del mito Giacomo Agostini, el no va más y el hombre de todos los récords en el motociclismo de velocidad. Le permite, además, superar los siete —nueve en el cómputo global— de su viejo enemigo, el gran icono de la especialidad Valentino Rossi.

Con el sol brillando tras el chaparrón en la víspera, Márquez arrancó convencido la carrera en el Autódromo Internacional do Algarve, pero luego se fue deshinchando, víctima del tembleque, la tensión y, en cierta medida, la calculadora. Tras meterle la moto al poleman Marco Bezzecchi en la primera frenada y liderar la primera vuelta, el piloto catalán bajó una marcha y empezó a verse superado por varios pilotos en apenas un giro, de la primera a la séptima plaza. Raúl Fernández le vapuleó en un abrir y cerrar de ojos, luego un Martín que remontó encendido desde la séptima plaza para terminar segundo en una carrera ganada por su compañero Bezzecchi, en otro triplete amargo para Aprilia.

Pero Márquez resistió lo justo y necesario. Rodó gran parte de la carrera en novena plaza, la única que le garantizaba rematar la faena sin depender del resto de rivales, leyendo la pizarra donde le mantenían informado sobre las posiciones de sus contrincantes. Y cumplió. Al cruzar la meta, soltó toda la tensión acumulada y se desgañitó ante su público.

Marc Márquez celebra con su equipo su victoria. Diogo Cardoso (Getty Images)

Primero les agradeció desde un palco frente a la grada, plagada con sus fieles. “Señoras y señores, el año pasado dije que me quedé en paz conmigo mismo. ¡Este año va por vosotros!”, quiso dedicarles, enfundado ya en una camiseta conmemorativa con el número 1 en la espalda. Por detrás, después de subir unas escaleras mientras la sombra de una cabra se proyectaba en una pantalla a sus espaldas –juego visual con el acrónimo inglés para ‘GOAT’, greatest of all time, el mejor de todos los tiempos–, apareció por una puerta el mismo Giacomo Agostini, a sus 84 años, para cederle el testigo en forma de casco dorado, sentido abrazo entre ambos en una imagen preciosa.

Para asombrar una vez más, Márquez tuvo que superar un reto inédito en la historia del Mundial de motociclismo y darle la espalda a la probabilidad estadística. Tras iniciar el curso renqueante de su última lesión en el brazo derecho —que le obligó a pasar por quirófano para intentar solventar la papeleta y saltarse dos grandes premios en el proceso—, llegó a verse 102 puntos abajo después de siete citas disputadas. Nadie había remontado jamás semejante desventaja en la disciplina.

Él lo ha hecho posible adaptándose a las limitaciones de un brazo que los doctores consideran al 50% de sus facultades. No solo ahora, sino ya de por vida, producto de las nueve operaciones que acumula la extremidad de 2020 en adelante. En definitiva, Márquez ha puesto más cabeza que físico, más talento que moto después de la que la RS-GP de Aprilia se mostrara mucho más redonda que la Desmosedici GP de Ducati esta campaña. “Marc creyó y siempre ha creído, y eso ha motivado a todo el equipo para mejorar y darlo todo para conseguir este título”, valora Gigi Dall’Igna, máximo responsable del departamento de carreras de la fábrica de Bolonia.

A partir del GP de Hungría a comienzos de junio, su primer doblete y victoria dominical del curso, Márquez ha arrasado a la competencia con siete victorias de domingo en 13 paradas del calendario —otras ocho contando los sábados—. Su cómputo tras 42 carreras disputadas hasta ahora es de 17 triunfos y 22 podios, más que sus cinco perseguidores más inmediatos en la tabla juntos. Sus principales rivales, Jorge Martín y Marco Bezzecchi, Aprilia en conjunto, pusieron bastante de su parte con fallos estúpidos, caídas evitables y rabietas inauditas. “En Sachsenring [a mediados de julio] empecé a pensar que estaba metido de nuevo en la lucha por el título. Mis rivales me dieron la oportunidad de volver a entrar en la batalla, y lo cierto es que este título solo lo podían perder ellos”, reconocía el flamante campeón tras encarrilar su coronación a principios de mes en el GP de Malasia, su último triunfo por ahora.

“El mérito de Marc es enorme, porque nunca ha tirado la toalla. Y esto acrecienta su leyenda, no solo por ser uno de los más rápidos y ganadores de la historia, sino por ser un referente de todas las virtudes que construyen a un gran campeón del mundo: personalidad, esfuerzo, lucha, insistencia. Esos problemas en el hombro le convirtieron en un piloto irreconocible a comienzos de año. Una vez resueltas o camufladas esas molestias, ha ido ganando de nuevo la confianza hasta parecerse algo más al Marc de toda la vida”, valora el expiloto Carlos Checa. “Es indudable que en Aprilia han hecho una pésima gestión deportiva, porque tiene la mejor moto hoy en día. Los errores han condenado a Bezzecchi, y Martín sí ha estado a un gran nivel, pero la caída y lesión hace cuatro semanas en Australia ha sido su condena”, remata el que fuera corredor de MotoGP más de una década y campeón de Superbike en 2011.

Para las mentes brillantes y cuadriculadas del paddock, un festín de la ciencia y la ingeniería, solo la fe en Márquez es capaz de superar, hoy en día, la fe en la técnica. Ningún otro piloto lo consigue. “La remontada de Marc solo la podía lograr él. Lo más fácil era tirar la toalla, y él no lo ha hecho. El cambio de mentalidad y la gestión de las carreras, de marcarse en qué circuitos podía atacar y en cuáles debía defender, es algo solo al alcance de Márquez”, señala Ramon Forcada, tricampeón de MotoGP como jefe de mecánicos de Jorge Lorenzo.“La mejor moto no existe, pero la moto más equilibrada viendo los resultados es la Aprilia, porque ha ido bien en cualquier circuito con cualquiera de sus pilotos. Si hubiesen mantenido sus resultados de principios de año, Marc no hubiera podido hacer nada”, desgrana.

Marc Márquez, se prepara para salir a pista en el box de Ducati en Portugal, este viernes, en un fin de semana clave para su carrera en el GP de Portugal. JOSE SENA GOULAO (EFE)

Dall’Igna, dentro del garaje de Ducati, no sale de su asombro: “Desde que volvió de la lesión, literalmente no ha puesto un pie mal, y esa es la verdadera marca de un campeón”. Márquez se retiró entre lágrimas y adelantó una operación ya prevista con sus médicos de confianza tras sufrir una dura caída durante la ‘sprint’ del GP de Francia, a comienzos de mayo. Tras la intervención que le liberó un nervio pinzado en el hombro, se saltó el GP de Catalunya donde casi fallece en un espeluznante accidente su hermano Alex y luego regresó a finales de mes en el GP de Italia. “Después de Mugello parecía imposible, pero esa derrota nos dio toda la fuerza que necesitábamos. Con su mentalidad y con nuestro equipo, todo es posible. Aquí nunca dejamos de creer”, concluye Davide Tardozzi, jefe del equipo oficial de Ducati.

La remontada inverosímil de Márquez, 102 puntos abajo en junio, 43 de ventaja a falta de una última carrera, supera la que logró su compañero de equipo Pecco Bagnaia en 2022, cuando le comió 91 puntos al francés de Yamaha Fabio Quartararo —eso sí, solo se repartían 25 puntos cada fin de semana, por los 37 de ahora tras la introducción de las ‘sprint’ en 2023—. Martín, un rival digno sin estar tampoco a su 100% físico casi todo el año, ha plantado batalla hasta quedarse sin aliento. En Portimao, uno de los trazados más físicos del calendario, ya no pudo obrar más milagros con su muñeca rota en Phillip Island. Fue segundo este domingo y bajo la bandera de cuadros terminó su esfuerzo titánico a lo largo de las tres últimas citas, lo único que ha mantenido viva la llama del campeonato.

“No han sido suficientes cuatro Aprilias para vencer a Marc Márquez”, asegura Massimo Rivola, máximo responsable de la casa de Noale. Coinciden sus pilotos de puertas afuera, aunque entre bambalinas hay críticas también a la gestión deportiva de la marca del grupo Piaggio, incapaz de manejar el enorme cojín y controlar el ímpetu de sus estrellas.

Tras la remontada de todas las remontadas, lo que siempre fue una opinión válida es ahora estadística: Marc Márquez es el número uno, al menos así lo señala la cuenta de títulos en la cumbre del motociclismo de velocidad. Ocho alirones en MotoGP y diez en la escalera mundialista, ya solo superado allí por Agostini (15) y Ángel Nieto (13), pilotos de otra época. Con 98 victorias totales en su palmarés, en el horizonte aparecen ya otros dos récords definitivos: los 89 triunfos de Rossi en MotoGP (él tiene 68) o los 122 de Agostini en todas las categorías. Un supercampeón que es eterno y se eterniza.

World.title: IDFA 2026 winners: Chinese family portrait takes top prize
World.content:
The Year of the Ghost, a Dutch-Chinese documentary about a filmmaker’s mother and sister after his father’s death, has won the top prize at the International Documentary Film Festival Amsterdam (IDFA).

Louis Hothothot’s film won three awards at Thursday’s ceremony at the Eye Filmmuseum. It took best film in the International Competition, which carries a €15,000 prize, as well as best editing and the €5,000 award for best Dutch film.

The festival’s 39th edition runs until Sunday, with 253 films from 80 countries. One of the five documentaries in our preview, You Can See Everything, came second in the audience vote.

These are the films that took the main prizes:



The Year of the Ghost

Hothothot was born in China in 1986 as a second child under the one-child policy and moved to Amsterdam in his twenties. His first film, Four Journeys, opened at IDFA in 2021. In this second film, Covid restrictions stop him from getting back to China in time to say goodbye to his father. He then follows his mother, who wants to stay in her husband’s home town to care for his spirit, and his sister, who is trying to get by as a single woman in a big city. The jury praised the film’s “bold honesty, a rare attention to detail, cinematic curiosity and love”.

Memories of Lightning

Riccardo Giacconi’s French-Italian film won best film in the Envision Competition for experimental work, also worth €15,000. Radio journalist Sibilla Scinti Roger (30) travels to an almost deserted village in Le Marche, central Italy, to make an audio documentary about a murder there in 1982 – and finds out the 14-year-old victim was her aunt. Scinti Roger also won the award for outstanding artistic contribution.

Hazara Town

Afghan-born director Khadim Dai won the award for best first feature and the international critics’ prize (Fipresci), as well as a special mention in the International Competition. The film follows his Hazara family, who fled Afghanistan 20 years ago and now face growing persecution in Pakistan. They have to decide whether to stay together or leave one by one, knowing they may never see each other again.

The Clearing

Dutch director Sabine Groenewegen won the award for best use of archive footage, sponsored by the media archive Beeld & Geluid. Her film is a feminist history of Dutch colonial rubber plantations in the Dutch East Indies, where local women were subjected to violence and sexual enslavement. On the festival’s opening night, Groenewegen also received the €50,000 Cultuurfonds documentary grant, which an anonymous donor gives every year to a Dutch documentary maker.

Women and War

The €5,000 audience award, announced on Friday, went to Elwira Niewiera’s German-Polish-Ukrainian documentary. Four women attend therapy sessions in a chalet in the Ukrainian mountains, each trying to recover from very different traumatic experiences of the war. Festivalgoers gave it an average score of 4.856 out of 5, just ahead of You Can See Everything on 4.842.

Other winners included Joël Akafou’s Lonan Tché for best directing and Tala Hadid’s Bardi, set among horse riders in central Morocco, for best cinematography. Raluca Lupaşcu’s A Modern Roma Fairytale got a special mention for best Dutch film, and Ant Hampton’s Dutch-Belgian All the Downtime won the DocLab award for digital storytelling.

The full list of winners is on the IDFA website.

World.title: Inburgering with DN: understanding education system acronyms
World.content:
International parents in the Netherlands often find the Dutch school system baffling: HBO, SBO, DUO, WO… the jargon is endless. So to help you pass this particular parenting test, our Inburgering course this month looks at educational acronyms and the like.

Lesson 65: educational jargon

Primary school in the Netherlands is relatively straightforward – although parents often face a bewildering number of school philosophies when deciding which school to entrust their offspring to. It is in groep 8, the final year of primary school, that the trouble really starts.

Doorstroomtoets

Previously known as the Citotoets and the Eindtoets Basisonderwijs, the doorstroomtoets is taken by children in their final year at primary school. The tests focus on language and arithmetic, and the results are used to help determine which type of secondary education children should go on to. In principle, the teacher’s recommendation takes precedence.

The Dutch love of tests and early streaming has been widely criticised, and more secondary schools now offer mixed-ability classes in the first and second years.

Secondary education itself is divided into three main streams. Schools may offer just one – typically in cities – or a combination.

VWO

VWO (voorbereidend wetenschappelijk onderwijs, or preparatory academic education) is the highest level of Dutch secondary education and is followed by some 20% of pupils. A VWO education takes six years, with pupils choosing a specialism (profiel) in the sciences or humanities after three. There are two variants: atheneum and gymnasium. Gymnasium pupils take Latin and Greek in addition to the dozen or so other VWO subjects.

HAVO

HAVO (hoger algemeen voortgezet onderwijs) literally means ‘higher general continued education’. It takes five years to get a HAVO diploma, which prepares school leavers for a hogeschool (see HBO below) rather than a university. Around 30% of pupils are in a HAVO stream. After three years, HAVO pupils also choose a specialism in the sciences or humanities.

VMBO

VMBO stands for voorbereidend middelbaar beroepsonderwijs (preparatory intermediate vocational education). Some 50% of pupils attend this type of secondary education, which is subdivided into four streams. It takes four years to complete a VMBO course.

The most academic VMBO stream is still widely known as MAVO (middelbaar algemeen voortgezet onderwijs, or intermediate general continued education), after the type of school it replaced in 1999.

Middle-class parents push hard to avoid a VMBO recommendation, hence the popularity of tutors and crammers – and exam stress – for 12-year-olds.

SBO, SO and VSO

Special needs pupils have their own category of jargon, depending on their age, the nature of their disability and how much care they need. The main types are speciaal basisonderwijs (SBO, special primary education), speciaal onderwijs (SO, special education) and voortgezet speciaal onderwijs (VSO, special secondary education).

Lighthouse Special Education in The Hague is the only international school for special needs pupils.

After secondary school, most young people move on to further education. Education is compulsory until 16, and until 18 for anyone who does not yet have at least a HAVO, VWO or MBO level 2 diploma.

MBO

MBO, or middelbaar beroepsonderwijs (vocational education and training), is the highest level of education reached by around 40% of the working population. There are four levels of MBO diploma, and students can either attend college full time or combine work and study.

HBO

There are two types of degree course in the Netherlands: the academic courses offered by universities and the more vocational courses (HBO, or hoger beroepsonderwijs) offered by hogescholen. Their umbrella body, the Vereniging Hogescholen, calls them ‘universities of applied sciences’ in English. The Netherlands has 36 hogescholen ranging from art academies to hotel schools and technical colleges.

WO

The Netherlands has 14 official universities offering wetenschappelijk onderwijs (research-oriented education), including the Open University. Delft, Eindhoven and Twente are universities of technology, while Wageningen focuses on agriculture and food. A bachelor’s degree takes three years, a master’s one or two.

DUO

If you have any connection to post-school education, you cannot avoid dealing with the education ministry’s Dienst Uitvoering Onderwijs (DUO), which runs student finance and related services. DUO holds the diploma records that colleges and universities use to check whether you can enrol, organises the lotteries for popular courses and works out how much student finance you are entitled to.

After you graduate, DUO will follow you for years to make sure you pay back your student loan. DUO should not be confused with DUWO, which specialises in student housing.

World.title: Prosecutors hacked and wiretapped Tata Steel, court hears
World.content:
The public prosecution service (OM) hacked into Tata Steel’s internal communication network, wiretapped phones, and made video recordings as part of its investigation into alleged criminal pollution, it was revealed on Friday in Amsterdam’s district court.

During the first hearing of the case, the OM revealed it had conducted a “covert intrusion into Tata Steel’s corporate network”, broadcaster NOS reported. Documents were also taken, witnesses questioned and deposition measurements examined.

The case, which has been years in the making, accuses the steelmaker of intentionally ignoring harmful pollution stemming from its coke and gas plants in IJmuiden.

Police and prosecutors are allowed to use hacking techniques in criminal cases under highly specific circumstances. This has been allowed since 2019, NOS reported, and only in a handful of cases, including child pornography and criminal communication investigations.

A defence lawyer for Tata Steel said that there was “unfounded distrust” against the company, that its employees go to work to do the right thing, and that “wire tapping and hacking” had been used as part of an “unbalanced” criminal file.

The investigation is ongoing and could lead to the prosecution of individual executives of the company. The process is not expected to be completed until the first quarter of next year, the OM said, at which point it will also become clear if the current CEO Hans van den Berg could be charged.

The public health institute RIVM records an above-average rate of lung cancer for residents living around the plant, and soot regularly collects in the surrounding neighbourhoods, including school playgrounds.

Many people have suffered serious health problems, which they attribute to the plant.

In 2021, lawyer Bénédicte Ficq filed a complaint on behalf of 1,200 residents and the following year prosecutors began investigating. In July, the OM summoned Tata Steel to court on criminal charges.

Shortly thereafter, the government said it could pull out of a planned €2 billion subsidy package for the company if the criminal case raises “serious concerns” for the Dutch state.

World.title: Bruna and Readshop avoid bankruptcy, for now
World.content:
Audax, the parent company of the popular Bruna and Readshop shops, was granted two months of protection against creditors by a Breda court Thursday.

The move follows a provisional cooling-off period granted to the company earlier this month and a hearing earlier this week attended by more than 10 creditors and auditors, many of whom signaled they were willing to grant Audax more time to get its financial affairs in order.

Audax, which was acquired by Lector Capital in January 2026, has been experiencing financial difficulties for years. It says at the time of the acquisition, Lector agreed to invest €8.6 million in Audax, money they say never came through.

Audax is said to owe its suppliers more than €9 million. Some have demanded payment before delivering new products, which could impact the upcoming Christmas shopping season.

World.title: Exiled Colombian climate activist wins children’s peace prize
World.content:
Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

A 17-year-old Colombian climate activist, Francisco Javier Vera Manzanares, has won the 2026 International Children’s Peace Prize given out by the Amsterdam-based KidsRights Foundation for “putting children’s rights at the heart of climate justice”.

The young activist is currently living in exile in Spain after receiving death threats over his activism in Colombia.

“Although our 17-year-old winner Francisco is an example of peaceful activism for climate rights defenders around the world, he has been forced to flee due to violent death threats against him,” KidsRights chairman Marc Dullaert told broadcaster NOS.

“It is shocking that peaceful child activists are threatened and that governments are unable to protect these children and their right to be heard.”

But in the imposing Peace Palace in The Hague Thursday afternoon, it was all celebration as Francisco received the prize from 72-year-old Kailash Satyarthi, an Indian child rights activist and 2014 Nobel Peace Prize winner.

“All children around the world have the right to live on a healthy, clean, dignified, and peaceful planet,” Francisco said.

Child activist

Francisco got involved in climate action in 2019 after seeing devastating wildfires engulf the Amazon rainforest. At just nine-years-old, he and six friends founded Guardians for Life, which today has more than 1,400 young members from across Colombia and Latin America.

He became the first child ever in Colombia to speak before Congress that same year.

According to KidsRights, Francisco “believes children are citizens of today, not just tomorrow, and should have a meaningful voice in the decisions that shape their lives and futures.”

He’s served as a Child Advisor to the UN Committee on the Rights of the Child, helping to craft implementation guidelines on children’s rights and climate change.

Francisco’s work has led to the planting of more than 5,000 trees across Latin America and Europe and the training of some 10,000 young people in climate leadership, human rights and citizen participation.

More young winners

Francisco was chosen from 280 nominations across 57 countries. Former winners include Swedish activist Greta Thunberg, who won the prestigious award in 2019.

Two finalists were also recognised at Thursday’s ceremony, Chilean justice activist Issaiah Guzman Arancibia (15) and 17-year-old Sufaira, a Rohingya refugee from Myanmar currently living in Bangladesh who works to prevent child marriages.

Some 700,000 Rohingya fled to Bangladesh refugee camps after a 2017 government crackdown that judges in the same Peace Palace ruled hours before the award ceremony was a genocide committed by Myanmar against its Rohingya population – the first time a country has been held responsible for committing genocide.

World.title: Students walk out against conscription and defence spending
World.content:
High school and university students nationwide will walk out of their classrooms at 1pm on Friday in a National Peace Protest against conscription and increasing defence spending, part of an international action day also taking place in 24 other countries including Germany, England and France.

“In our opinion, money is being taken away from care, education and housing to go to defence,” National Student Union (LSVb) chairwoman Evy Kras told RTL news. “At the same time, they want us to enlist. Young people feel betrayed and say: so far and no further. We want to be invested in us.”

She says these political spending choices are at the expense of young people, and that campaigns by the defence ministry paint an unrealistic picture of war. “They pretend it’s all very adventurous and flashy, but fighting in a war is not flashy.”

The LSVb, together with research and activist group Stop Wapenhandel, published a report earlier this week saying that defence spends €260 million annually on recruitment campaigns at schools and online. Meanwhile, they say, students have trouble making ends meet.

In at least 16 Dutch cities and dozens of schools, students will leave their classrooms at 1pm, fighting for an “affordable future”. In Amsterdam, students will gather at the Stopera, while in Utrecht, they’ll head to the Domplein and in Groningen to the Broerplein.

The Dutch group Stop the War Fever, which is organising the walkout, says on its website that the government refuses to work towards peace yet “pumps billions into weapons and war.”

Conscription

The group is asking to do away with conscription, move defence out of education and invest in the future of young people instead of weapons of war.

Currently, both men and women in the Netherlands aged between 17 and 45 must register for conscription, but since 1997, there has been no obligation to serve.

But the government is preparing legislation for a selective military conscription system that could be employed if it’s deemed necessary for security reasons.

Junior minister Derk Boswijk said in March that he couldn’t rule out the deployment of young people in the coming years.

“Many young people see it coming, now that the war is near at hand on the European continent,” student Camiel Breet told RTL News. “We want to fight against the cabinet’s plans.”

“This is the first post-Cold War generation that is both the generation of misfortune and grows up with the threat of war,” Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam professor of social change and conflict Jacquelien van Stekelenburg told RTL News. “A basic sense of peace is no longer self-evident for them.”

World.title: Tata Steel goes on trial accused of deliberate air pollution
World.content:
The criminal case against Tata Steel over alleged deliberate air pollution around its IJmuiden plant began at Amsterdam district court on Friday.

The public prosecution service (OM) accuses Tata Steel IJmuiden of intentionally and unlawfully releasing harmful substances into the air. The complainants say they suffer serious health problems and worry about local children, with soot accumulating in local playgrounds, broadcaster NOS reported. The public health institute RIVM has recorded above-average lung cancer rates in the area.

The case began in 2021, when lawyer Bénédicte Ficq filed a complaint on behalf of people living near the plant. Prosecutors opened an investigation the following year and announced in July that they would take the company to court. They are still considering whether individual managers can be held personally liable.

The case focuses on the plant’s coke-making ovens, where coal is heated at very high temperatures without oxygen to produce coke, a material used to make steel. If the coal is not heated for long enough, it remains partly unfinished (called raw coke) and can release harmful gases into the air and spread soot into the environment.

Tata says it is technically unavoidable that a batch is sometimes not heated for long enough. Prosecutors suspect the company accepts these incidents and deliberately does not report them. In July, Tata called the allegations “essentially unjust”.

Ficq told NOS it was “a tremendously important day” and said the emissions incidents were “foreseeable and avoidable”. She wants executives, including chairman Hans van den Berg, to be prosecuted as well.

€2bn subsidy at steak

The criminal case also affects a €2 billion state support package for Tata’s switch to greener steel. The cabinet said in July that it could pull out of the deal if the investigation raised “serious concerns”. According to NOS, talks have now been extended to March, and the trial is unlikely to be over by then.

We cannot do what we do without your support. A consortium led by FedEx has completed its €7.8 billion (34.5 billion zloty) takeover of Polish delivery giant InPost. The deal will see InPost remain headquartered in Poland, with founder and CEO Rafał Brzoska staying at the helm. Friday’s announcement brings to a close a process that was first announced in February and received European Commission approval in August. InPost’s shares have now been delisted from the stock exchange. The takeover follows years of rapid growth for InPost, which pioneered the use of parcel delivery lockers in Poland before spreading rapidly in major western European markets, including France, Spain and the UK. A consortium of Advent, FedEx, A&R Investments and PPF has completed its takeover of Poland's InPost, which is now private. InPost has delisted from Euronext Amsterdam. Founder Rafał Brzoska stays on as CEO, and the company remains headquartered in Poland. pic.twitter.com/HWigKVPC3w — IPO Newsroom (@IPONewsroom_) November 20, 2026 Under the deal, FedEx and Advent, an American private equity firm, each hold 37% of InPost. A&R Investments, Brzoska’s own investment vehicle, has 16% and PPF, a Czech investment fund founded by the late billionaire Petr Kellner, 10%. PPF, A&R and Advent were previously already stakeholders. The consortium acquired InPost at a price of €15.60 per share, valuing the company at approximately €7.8 billion. In a statement published on Friday, Advent confirmed that InPost would retain its name, branding, Polish headquarters and operational independence following the takeover. Brzoska, who founded his business in 1999, will continue as CEO alongside the existing management team. “InPost’s home market of Poland will remain the blueprint for new innovations, which will then be scaled across InPost’s wider European network,” said Advent. They added that the new consortium would now “accelerate investment” in InPost’s operations, helping the firm “extend its reach further”. FedEx and InPost would also “explore opportunities” to cooperate with one another. “InPost has built a leading position in Europe’s out-of-home delivery segment,” said FedEx’s CEO and president, Raj Subramaniam. “Connecting our global network…with InPost’s last-mile capabilities gives both businesses a potential springboard for profitable growth.” Brzoska, who is one of Poland’s wealthiest individuals, said that the new partnership would “deliver the long-term capital, global reach and deep technology expertise we require to build on what we have already achieved together as a leading European e-commerce enabler”. President Macron has thanked Polish delivery giant InPost for its latest investment in France The firm, which already operates over 9,000 parcel lockers in France through its subsidiary Mondial Relay, will now spend a further €500m to expand its presence https://t.co/caOGNQemfm — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) June 2, 2026 InPost is the largest operator of parcel lockers in Europe, with around 70,000 across the continent. That includes roughly 30,000 in Poland and 16,000 in the UK, including in branches of the British Post Office, with over 23,000 more in the seven Eurozone countries where InPost operates. In the second quarter of 2026, InPost had revenue of 4.18 billion zloty (€970 million), up 18.2% year on year, while its number of parcels handled rose 16% to 380.9 million. The strongest revenue growth came in the eurozone, where sales increased 37.9%, followed by Poland, with 12.7% growth. Revenue in the UK and Ireland rose 9.8%. Poland recently managed to prevent a planned Russian “false-flag operation” at the border that, if it had not been stopped, could have “ended tragically”, says a retired general who acts as an advisor to the defence minister. His statement follows a report earlier this week by a leading newspaper, based on statements by unnamed senior officials, that Poland had foiled an attempt by Russia to carry out a major “provocation” on the border with the Russian exclave of Kaliningrad. Polish government figures, including Prime Minister Donald Tusk, have confirmed that a Russian operation at the border was prevented, though they have not provided further details. Generał Mieczysław Bieniek o próbie rosyjskiej prowokacji przy granicy z Polską !!! Polskie władze potwierdzają udaremnioną próbę rosyjskiej prowokacji przy granicy z obwodem królewieckim. – Udało się udaremnić, być może tragiczny w skutkach, incydent – przyznał w "Faktach po… pic.twitter.com/raQMfJ4uUp — Andrzej Mitura #Mocnytakżeosobno (@AndrzejekMitura) November 19, 2026 “The public isn’t informed about everything,” retired general Mieczysław Bieniek, who acts as an advisor to defence minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz, told broadcaster TVN on Thursday. Bieniek then revealed that, “based on information we received from both our allies and our own intelligence services, we managed to thwart an incident with potentially tragic consequences, because the planned false-flag operation could have ended tragically”. “For example, if a group of people crossed the border and later dressed in uniforms, whether Ukrainian or Polish, but were Russian citizens disguised as others, and carried out an attack on their target, the side whose uniforms were worn would naturally be blamed,” continued the general. “Fortunately, nothing of the sort happened,” he added. “Certainly this preventative action [by Poland] forced the other side to desist from these acts.” Bieniek’s comments followed a report published on Wednesday by the Rzeczpospolita daily, which said it had learned of a planned Russian sabotage operation on the border between Poland and the Kaliningrad exclave. The newspaper, citing unnamed high-ranking figures from the uniformed services, said that the planned incident could have involved Russia mounting an attack on one of its own facilities but blaming it on Ukraine. Such actions are known as false-flag operations. “It was supposed to be reminiscent of the Gleiwitz incident,” said one unnamed source, referring to a false-flag attack in 1939 staged by Nazi Germany, in which German operatives dressed in Polish uniforms. It was one of a number of such staged incidents used to justify the invasion of Poland. 🔴 Operacja polskich służb oraz wojska na przełomie października i listopada zapobiegła rosyjskiej prowokacji na granicy z obwodem królewieckim – wynika z ustaleń @marek_kozubal https://t.co/EFWsdlZUHY — Rzeczpospolita (@rzeczpospolita) November 18, 2026 According to Rzeczpospolita, concerns over this planned Russian operation were what prompted Poland to bolster security in regions along the Kaliningrad border in late October. On 3 November, Prime Minister Donald Tusk declared that Poland had “managed to prevent a provocation” on the border after “individuals with flashlights” were spotted. However, he did not provide further details at the time. When Rzeczpospolita this week asked Tomasz Siemoniak, the minister in charge of the security services, if Russia had been planning a terrorist attack, he replied: “You’d have to ask the Russians. And they usually don’t admit to planning such actions. Even if we have such information, we don’t share it.” “If we took certain steps, it was because we recognised there was a real threat,” added Siemoniak. “Appropriate actions were taken by the border guard, the police and the military. I can’t go into details.” Polish Prime Minister @donaldtusk claims that "individuals with flashlights" were observed at the Russian border last night. "We very quickly mobilised the appropriate forces and resources there, and managed to prevent a provocation," he added https://t.co/kD5OmpNagf — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) November 3, 2026 On Wednesday afternoon, Kosiniak-Kamysz himself was asked about reports of a planned border provocation. “It didn’t happen, because we responded appropriately,” said the defence minister. “Russia is rapidly climbing the escalation ladder, moving from airspace violations, attempted train bombings, sabotage of arms factories, as well as cyberspace activity, [and] it can also provoke at the border,” he continued, referring to some of the actions Russia has already taken against Poland. However, Kosiniak-Kamysz did not comment on or provide any specific details of what kind of incident Poland may have prevented on the Kaliningrad border. Later on Wednesday, Tusk himself reiterated to journalists that “we received signals that some unacceptable events could occur near the Polish-Russian border” and that “it seems that the mobilisation of the border guard and police in this place blocked any plans or ideas to carry out any provocation”. However, he added that further details are “kept confidential for obvious reasons”. Two Russian missiles and what is likely to have been a jet-powered drone struck Poland last night during large-scale attacks on Ukraine, the defence minister has confirmed https://t.co/QM2t2hOwlg — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) November 20, 2026 Poland’s government has for months been warning that Russia is planning escalatory provocations against eastern NATO states, which could involve border and airspace violations. In June, foreign minister Radosław Sikorski even announced that he was “expecting an attack on Russian territory under a false flag, to which Putin will ‘respond'”. Sikorski pointed to the Gleiwitz incident as an example of such an operation. On Friday morning, two Russian missiles and what is believed to be a drone entered Polish airspace and hit the ground in three locations. Tusk condemned the incident as a further “Russian escalation” and said that it was likely to have been “an intentional provocation”. World.title: Two Ukrainians charged with vandalising Polish monuments on behalf of Russia
World.content: Why are you now seeing adverts on our website for the first time? Click here to learn more. Keep our news free from paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. Two Ukrainians have been charged in Poland with working on behalf of Russia to paint slogans praising the Ukrainian Insurgent Army (UPA), a nationalist formation responsible for massacring Poles during World War Two, on three monuments in the Polish city of Poznań. Polish prosecutors say that the operation was intended to fuel hostility between Poles and Ukrainians. The incidents in Poznań were part of a seemingly coordinated wave of similar graffiti on monuments in three other Polish cities. Ukraińcy malowali na pomnikach hasła „Sława UPA”. Działali na zlecenie wywiaduhttps://t.co/knLgZzo8ct — Rzeczpospolita (@rzeczpospolita) November 19, 2026 In early November, the words “Slava UPA” (“Glory to the UPA”) were painted in red on three monuments in Poznań commemorating World War Two soldiers. While the UPA is remembered by many in Ukraine for fighting for independence from Moscow-imposed Soviet rule, in Poland it is primarily associated with leading the Volhynia massacres, in which around 100,000 Polish civilians, mostly women and children, were slaughtered as part of an ethnic cleansing operation. The history of those massacres, and the continued veneration of the UPA by some in Ukraine, has regularly stirred tension between Poland and Ukraine, who are otherwise close allies. On Thursday, the National Prosecutor’s Office confirmed to the Polish Press Agency (PAP) that two Ukrainians, who can be named only as Nikita S. and Dmytro Y. under Polish privacy law, had been detained and charged in relation to the vandalism. According to prosecutors, Nikita S., “acting on behalf of Russian intelligence and in order to obtain financial benefit of $500”, persuaded Dmytro Y. to “commit an act of sabotage by painting the slogans” with the aim of “publicly inciting hatred based on national differences between the Polish and Ukrainian peoples”. The suspects were identified by police and the Internal Security Agency (ABW), who had analysed surveillance footage of the perpetrator, reports the Gazeta Wyborcza daily. Both were detained in Poznań, according to PAP. In the wake of the Poznań vandalism, Poland-based Belarusian news outlet MOST reported that, a few days before the graffiti appeared, an advert offering $500 for someone to paint pro-UPA slogans on monuments in the city had appeared on messaging service Telegram. When an undercover journalist from the outlet contacted the person offering the job, they were told that similar work was available in other Polish cities. Around the same time, almost identical graffiti praising the UPA appeared on further monuments in the cities of Gdańsk, Gdynia and Warsaw, including one dedicated to the heroes of the Warsaw Ghetto Uprising. Around a dozen monuments in Poland, including one dedicated to the Warsaw Ghetto Uprising, have been defaced with graffiti glorifying the WWII Ukrainian Insurgent Army (UPA). Ukraine’s embassy in Warsaw has condemned the vandalism and blamed it on Russia https://t.co/iaZb2CyiPx — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) November 15, 2026 Last week, local police in Gdańsk confirmed that they had detained a 17-year-old Ukrainian suspected of carrying out the graffiti there and in Gdynia. He has been charged with promoting fascist ideology, incitement to violence and hatred based on nationality, and desecration of monuments. The Ukrainian embassy in Poland has condemned the acts of vandalism, calling them a “disgraceful provocation” and “a manifestation of the hybrid war that Russia is attempting to wage by any means in European states”. Poland has been a primary target for Russia’s so-called hybrid actions in Europe, which have included acts of sabotage, espionage, disinformation and efforts to stir hostility towards Ukrainians. Such operations are rarely carried out by Russian operatives themselves. Instead, Russia often recruits people already on the ground, often members of Poland’s large Ukrainian and Belarusian migrant communities, as well as Poles themselves in some cases. In July this year, a Ukrainian teenager was indicted by Polish prosecutors on charges of painting dozens of pro-UPA slogans in public places, including on a monument to victims of the Volhynia massacres. Two Russian missiles and what is likely to have been a jet-powered drone struck Poland today amid large-scale attacks on Ukraine, the defence minister has confirmed. On Friday morning, an image published by Polish media outlet Wirtualna Polska showed a crater in the ground with a fire burning in the middle of it. The website reported that it had been caused by an object landing in a field in the village of Nowy Lipowiec in southeastern Poland, around 60 kilometres from the Ukrainian border. 🔴Tu spadł niezidentyfikowany obiekt. Mamy zdjęcie Niezidentyfikowany obiekt spadł w piątek rano na pole w miejscowości Nowy Lipowiec w powiecie biłgorajskim. Stało się to kilkaset metrów od zabudowań. Nikomu nic się nie stało. Mamy zdjęcie z tego miejsca… — Wirtualna Polska (@wirtualnapolska) November 20, 2026 At a press conference later on Friday morning, Kosiniak-Kamysz said that the object in Nowy Lipowiec was a Russian Kh-101 cruise missile (the same type as one that entered Polish airspace and exploded in eastern Poland in July this year). The defence minister also revealed that another missile had fallen in the town of Rudnik nad Sanem and what is likely to be a jet-powered drone had struck in the village of Mołodycz. Both of those locations are also in southeastern Poland, not far from the Ukrainian border. He added that there were no reports of injuries or any damage to critical infrastructure as a result of the incidents in Poland, which he noted had taken place during “one of the largest Russian attacks on Ukraine since the beginning of the full-scale war”. Kosiniak-Kamysz also suggested that the fact that these incidents had taken place now was “no coincidence”, given that military exercises of the Coalition of the Willing – a group of countries supporting Ukraine – are taking place in Poland not far from where the missiles and drone struck. Addressing the media on Friday afternoon, Prime Minister Donald Tusk declared that Friday represented “another instalment in the Russian escalation”. He said that there was no doubt that the objects which had hit Poland were Russian. “I’m cautious in my wording, but it does seem that we’re dealing with an intentional provocation,” added the prime minister. NATO’s secretary general, Mark Rutte, announced that he had spoken with Tusk about “the grave violations of Polish airspace” and declared that the alliance “stands in solidarity with Poland and will continue to strengthen our ability to deter and defend”. Spoke with @donaldtusk about the grave violations of Polish airspace overnight. NATO jets were scrambled in response. We stand in solidarity with Poland and will continue to strengthen our ability to deter and defend. This incident is clearly dangerous – a consequence of… — Mark Rutte (@SecGenNATO) November 20, 2026 During the early hours of Friday, operational command of Poland’s armed forces reported that they had “activated the necessary forces in response to Russia’s strikes on targets in Ukraine”. Such communiques have become common in recent months, as Poland has had to scramble its forces in response to Russia’s increasing strikes on targets in western Ukraine, including a passenger train travelling between Kyiv and Warsaw that was hit by a jet-powered drone in September this year. In recent months, the Polish government has warned of intelligence suggesting the likelihood of “provocations” by Russia, including airspace and border violations. In September this year, a Russian helicopter briefly crossed the border from the Russian exclave of Kaliningrad. Earlier this month, Poland claimed to have foiled a ground operation around the border with Kaliningrad. Polish Prime Minister @donaldtusk claims that "individuals with flashlights" were observed at the Russian border last night. "We very quickly mobilised the appropriate forces and resources there, and managed to prevent a provocation," he added https://t.co/kD5OmpNagf — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) November 3, 2026 In September 2025, around 20 Russian drones crossed Poland’s eastern borders in an unprecedented violation that prompted Poland to trigger NATO’s Article 4. Back in November 2022, during the early stages of Russia’s war in Ukraine, two people died in Poland after a missile crossed the Ukrainian border and struck the ground. It later transpired to have been a Ukrainian air-defence missile fired in response to Russian attacks. Poland’s consumer protection authority, UOKiK, has fined Allegro, one of Europe’s largest e-commerce platforms, 55 million zloty (€12.3 million) for misleading consumers over a campaign that promised to plant trees in exchange for collecting parcels through its delivery service. The case is one of a series of investigations into so-called “greenwashing” launched by the authority against companies operating in Poland. UOKiK found that two of the Polish e-commerce group’s practices relating to the tree-planting initiative had infringed consumers’ interests. The first involved promotional claims suggesting that collecting 10 parcels through Allegro’s delivery service would result in a tree being planted. In practice, however, Allegro calculated the number of trees to be planted using forecasts prepared the previous year, rather than linking plantings to individual consumers’ parcel collections. This meant that decisions on the number of trees had already been made before customers collected their parcels. 🌳 Greenwashing ma swoją cenę! Blisko 55 mln zł kary dla Allegro – ekologiczne obietnice miały zachęcać do odbioru paczek, ale rzeczywistość nie była tak zielona. Milionów deklarowanych drzew nigdy nie posadzono. ❌ Ekościema nie może się opłacać 🔎https://t.co/yPQznKz0H1 pic.twitter.com/UDcWXWq3LI — UOKiK (@UOKiKgovPL) November 18, 2026 The second breach concerned the conditions attached to the campaign, which Allegro failed to communicate clearly to consumers. According to UOKiK, Allegro’s promotional messages could have led customers to believe that collecting 10 parcels through their delivery was sufficient to trigger tree planting. In fact, customers had to do it within a single calendar year and, from January 2024, submit a dedication for the tree within a specified period. Without a dedication, collecting the required number of parcels did not result in a tree being planted or assigned to the customer. UOKiK also found that the option to submit a dedication was unavailable for extended periods. Between March and November 2024, the feature was disabled for a total of 264 days, the watchdog said. The prolonged interruptions could have led customers to forget about the requirement or abandon their attempts to submit a dedication, meaning they would not receive the promised tree. UOKiK imposed a fine of 29.9 million zloty for the first practice and 24.9 million zloty for the second. Its decision can still be appealed in court by Allegro, which has not yet commented on the decision. “Green claims must be truthful, specific and verifiable; otherwise, they may mislead consumers and constitute an example of greenwashing,” said UOKiK president Tomasz Chróstny. “If a consumer hears, ‘collect 10 parcels, and we will plant a tree,’ they have the right to interpret that literally,” Chróstny said, adding that “several million [trees] – more than half of the total number claimed by Allegro – were never planted at all”. When announcing its decision, UOKiK noted that, according to a 2025 consumer survey conducted by the European Union, 43% of Poles said that the environmental impact of a product or service influenced their choices. The Allegro case forms part of a broader crackdown on suspected greenwashing by companies operating in Poland. Alongside Allegro, UOKiK has brought charges against delivery companies DHL, DPD and InPost, mobility firm Bolt, retailers Tchibo and Zara, and cosmetics firm L’Oréal Polska. World.content: Why are you now seeing adverts on our website for the first time? Click here to learn more. Keep our news free from paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Poland has signed memorandums with four of its neighbouring countries – Hungary, the Czech Republic, Slovakia and Lithuania – pledging to strengthen regional cooperation on natural gas supplies and the security of infrastructure. The initiative comes amid Poland’s efforts to use its liquefied natural gas (LNG) capacity and transmission links to establish itself as a regional energy hub, helping its neighbours, especially landlocked countries to the south, diversify supplies and reduce their reliance on Russia. The two memorandums of understanding were signed in Warsaw during a ministerial meeting at the Partnership for Transatlantic Energy Cooperation (P-TEC), co-organised by the US Department of Energy, Poland’s energy ministry and the Global Energy Centre run by the Atlantic Council. Rozpoczęliśmy 7. edycję Partnership for Transatlantic Energy Cooperation (P-TEC) – jednego z kluczowych forów współpracy energetycznej Stanów Zjednoczonych oraz krajów Europy Środkowo-Wschodniej. ⚡️ W Warszawie spotkali się przedstawiciele rządu Stanów Zjednoczonych, państw… pic.twitter.com/7t8kLluubF — GAZ-SYSTEM (@GAZ_SYSTEM) November 18, 2026 One of them, signed by Poland, Slovakia, Hungary and the Czech Republic – who collectively form the Visegrad Group – establishes a framework for closer collaboration between their gas transmission system operators and more effective use of existing infrastructure. In late 2022, for example, a new gas interconnector opened between Poland and Slovakia. However, since then, the pipeline has seen very little use, as Bratislava has continued to rely on Russian gas supplies. Hungary has also remained reliant on Russian gas. By contrast, Poland quickly phased out its imports of Russian energy after the full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. It now receives most of its gas via a pipeline that runs from Norway through Denmark and through LNG that arrives by sea, sourced mainly from the US and Qatar. From autumn 2027, the EU will ban its member states from importing Russian gas. In September, Hungary’s energy minister said that his country will be ready to meet that deadline. Slovakia, however, is challenging the import ban at the European Court of Justice. As part of the new memorandum signed this week, the four Visegrad countries will assess the impact of phasing out Russian supplies on regional energy security. The second memorandum, signed between Poland’s Gaz-System and Lithuania’s Amber Grid and KN Energies – which operate gas and LNG infrastructure in the two countries – focuses on strengthening the resilience and security of energy infrastructure around the Baltic Sea. It provides for closer coordination between the companies, including information-sharing on threats and incidents, joint risk assessments, exchanges of expertise on infrastructure protection and crisis response, and joint training sessions and exercises. “The LNG terminals in Poland and Lithuania serve as critical supply hubs for…Central and Eastern Europe, significantly enhancing energy security and bolstering regional resilience,” said Sławomir Hinc, CEO of Gaz-System. But that “security depends on the resilience of every link in the chain”, added his counterpart at Amber Grid, Nemunas Biknius. “This regional agreement will enable us to strengthen that chain in a structured and coordinated way.” Poland has declared its ambition to become a hub for supplying gas to the CEE region, including Ukraine, in particular by expanding imports of LNG from the United States. In addition to its existing LNG terminal in Świnoujście, which opened a decade ago, it is planning to build two further floating storage and regasification units that will be located in the Bay of Gdańsk. The first of those, under construction in South Korea, is due to open in 2028. Last year, a record amount of natural gas was traded in Poland, surpassing the levels seen before Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine and the energy crisis that followed. Among those arrested were some who had used AI to produce content depicting the abuse of minors. Around 170 searches took place, with prosecutors seizing a total of 1,096 electronic devices. Initial analysis indicates that almost 2.8 million files containing child sex abuse material were contained on them, said the National Prosecutor’s Office, which oversaw the operation. The doctor, an anaesthesiologist, was found to be in possession of around 75,000 files containing child sexual abuse material. Prosecutors have already charged 94 of the suspects with producing, possessing and/or disseminating materials related to the sexual exploitation of minors. Those crimes carry a jail term of up to 15 years. Thirty-one of the suspects have been placed in pretrial detention. “Among those detained were people who used AI technology to produce materials depicting the sexual abuse of minors,” wrote the National Prosecutor’s Office. One suspect is also accused of taking photographs and videos of himself and children naked at a public swimming pool. In May this year, prosecutors announced the results of a similar operation against child pornography, which, by coincidence, also resulted in 123 people being detained. Among those detained at that time was a teacher accused of recording and photographing children, as well as another suspect accusing of grooming minors through a messaging app before encouraging them to perform sexual acts.
