World.title: 24 civilians killed in fresh South Sudan violence
World.content:
JUBA, South Sudan: A weekend attack by opposition forces in volatile South Sudan killed 24 civilians, including seven children, local authorities said Sunday.

The world’s youngest country, which gained independence in 2011, has been torn apart by violence between rival political factions, often linked to ethnicity or cattle rustling.

An area called Bol Bol Boma in the country’s northwest was targeted in an attack between Saturday night and Sunday morning, Machuei Bith, acting commissioner of Tonj East County in Warrap State, told AFP.

He said the attackers came from the neighboring Unity State and were part of the SPLA-IO forces loyal to former vice president Riek Machar, who has been under house arrest since March 2025.

Twenty-four civilians, including herders, were killed, Bith told AFP on Sunday evening, raising the previous toll of 15 dead.

The victims included seven children and six women.

Four armed attackers “wearing SPLA-IO uniforms” were also killed, he had said earlier.

A local police officer confirmed this on condition of anonymity.

The toll could rise, and a team is to be sent to the scene, he told AFP.

Last week, two groups from two districts of Warrap State clashed in a market in the town of Makuach, leaving 17 dead and 23 injured, according to local authorities.

Last month, at least 72 people were killed in intercommunal violence on the border between Warrap State and Unity State.

The region has been trapped for years in a cycle of revenge killings, cattle raids, and fighting for control of territory, exacerbated by the proliferation of firearms.

The East African country endured a bloody civil war between 2013 and 2018 between troops loyal to President Salva Kiir and those loyal to Machar, which claimed more than 400,000 lives.

Clashes have intensified in recent months between forces loyal to the two men in the country, where the humanitarian situation is catastrophic in many areas.

World.title: Liverpool thrash 10-man Man Utd in Pochettino’s first match
World.content:
LIVERPOOL: Mauricio Pochettino endured a nightmare start as Manchester United manager with a 4-0 defeat at Liverpool that left the Red Devils still rooted in the Premier League relegation zone.

United never recovered from Leny Yoro’s controversial red card after just eight minutes as Dominik Szoboszlai and Florian Wirtz quickly made Liverpool’s man advantage count.

Teenager Rio Ngumoha rounded off a stunning individual with Liverpool’s third before Victor Munoz completed the rout.

Defeat leaves United second bottom of the table and gave Pochettino an early indication of the huge job he has ahead to restore the 20-time English champions to their former glories.

“We feel pain for that defeat, but we need to keep the head up and translate that anger to an energy to start to work from tomorrow for the next game,” said Pochettino, who was furious at the decision to dismiss Yoro.

“I need to defend my club and say what I feel. I feel like that was an action that everyone who plays football can see was clearly not a red card..”

Liverpool climb into the top four and within seven points of leaders Arsenal to rekindle faint hopes of challenging for the title.

“We could have scored more,” said Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola.

“In other games you will remember those chances, but today we’ve controlled the game and everything was happening around the (United) box.”

Pochettino answered United’s call after Michael Carrick was sacked last week after winning just one of the Red Devils’ first 10 league games in charge.

The Argentine has been linked with a move to Old Trafford for a decade, but failed to make a strong first impression on the United fans.

Europe’s worst defense

Pochettino’s bold team selection backfired with the center-back pairing of Matthijs de Ligt and Yoro at fault for the game’s decisive moment.

De Ligt, on his first Premier League start for nearly a year, let a long ball down the middle and go and allowed Alexander Isak to bear down on goal.

The Swedish striker took a heavy touch before he was clipped by Yoro, but referee Sam Barrott still deemed the French defender had denied a clear goalscoring opportunity and produced a red card.

Szoboszlai rubbed salt into United wounds by drilling home the resulting free-kick from the edge of the box.

Moments later Ngumoha skipped past Diogo Dalot and crossed for Wirtz to hook a shot in off the underside of the bar.

Having relegated Harry Maguire to the bench, Pochettino was forced to turn to the veteran center-back just 22 minutes in to try and stem the bleeding.

United lost 7-0 at Anfield three years ago and a switch to a back five helped avoid similar damage, albeit with the help of some wayward Liverpool finishing.

Maguire made a brilliant block to deny Isak a third goal just before half-time.

Bradley Barcola and Isak were guilty of wasting huge chances early in the second half.

But Barcola’s blistering speed created Liverpool’s third just after the hour mark.

The French international destroyed Lisandro Martinez for pace before picking out Ngumoha to slot home.

Wirtz rounded off one of his best Liverpool displays since a £100 million ($131 million) move from Bayer Leverkusen last year with the assist for Munoz to crash home the fourth goal eight minutes from time.

Liverpool fans rejoiced in their rivals’ pain with chants of “you are going down.”

United have not been relegated since 1974 but find themselves in a battle for survival despite still enjoying one of the biggest revenues in world football.

The 34 goals they have conceded in all competitions is the worst defensive record of any team in Europe’s top five leagues this season.

World.title: Poland says Russia allegedly twice tried to kill a Ukrainian American rapper
World.content:
WARSAW, Poland: Denmark has expelled a Russian official after it said it had thwarted an alleged plot to kill a Ukrainian American citizen on Danish soil. The case took a new twist Sunday when Polish authorities revealed that the same man was allegedly targeted by Moscow’s intelligence services last summer in Poland.

Denmark is expected to ask the European Union this week for more decisive action stemming from the case, perhaps restricting Russian citizens from entering and traveling freely within the EU. Poland said it would support such measures.

European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said Russia’s threats were becoming more real, reaching EU soil as the bloc continues supporting Ukraine as Moscow’s full-scale invasion nears the five-year mark.

The case involves Albert Vasiliev, a rapper who performs under the name Kyivstoner and holds Ukrainian and US citizenship, according to Danish media.

The assassination attempt in Denmark was planned for Sept. 25 during a concert north of Copenhagen, according to the Danish Security and Intelligence Service, known by its acronym PET. It said the plot was “planned and initiated by Russian intelligence services.”

The plot was thwarted by authorities, the Danish prime minister’s office said Friday. PET said two men were charged with attempted murder and assisting a foreign intelligence service in operating in Denmark. They were linked to Loyal to Familia, it said, a banned gang known for “extensive, serious and violent criminal activity.”

Russia dismissed the allegations through its embassy in Copenhagen, saying the accusations were unsubstantiated.

Denmark responded by expelling Russia’s defense attaché.

“In our assessment, the individual concerned was a particular target of the Russian intelligence services,” said Rasmus Kieffer-Kristensen, director general of PET. “The case demonstrates that Russian intelligence services are both willing and capable of initiating an assassination attempt on Danish soil — at a public event and using individuals from Danish criminal gangs. This is a concrete indication of the heightened threat posed by Russia.”

Poland reveals a plot against the rapper in August

As Denmark announced the plot against the rapper on Friday, the Polish Foreign Ministry posted on X that it was noting the news with “outrage and concern.”

“This is another assassination attempt against this person — the first took place on Polish territory in August 2026 but was thwarted thanks to the efforts of the Polish services and the would-be perpetrator, a Russian citizen, was detained,” the ministry said.

The suspect, who was allegedly recruited by Russia’s secret services, was detained by Polish authorities on Aug. 7.

Maciej Wewiór, a Foreign Ministry spokesman, confirmed to The Associated Press the previous attempt to kill Vasiliev in Poland.

On Aug. 13, Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk disclosed the plot to kill a Ukrainian American citizen in Warsaw was thwarted, noting it was the first time that “someone on the order of Russia” sought to attack a US citizen on the territory of another NATO country.

Tusk did not, however, disclose Vasiliev’s name, saying only that the target “was uncomfortable” for Russian President Vladimir Putin’s government.

The rapper left Ukraine after the full-scale invasion

Vasiliev was born in Kyiv in 1991, according to Polish media. He posted online comedy sketches and was a former member of the Ukrainian band Hryby. He also was popular in Russia before the full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

But he left Ukraine after the war broke out and lived for two years in the US before moving to Slovakia. He has expressed his support for Ukraine against Russia.

He performed across Europe this year before his concerts were canceled for security reasons.

Russia’s domestic security service, the FSB, accused Vasiliev of being involved in supplying drones for an alleged Ukrainian attack on a defense enterprise in the Moscow region. It said he was “acting under the patronage” of Ukraine’s internal security service, the SBU.

Danish broadcaster DR reported that Vasiliev denied the FSB accusations.

He did not comment on social media about the plot against him in Poland, but DR reported that he announced on Instagram that “the intelligence service banned us from holding the concert,” referring to the cancelation of his event in Denmark.

Western officials have accused Russia and its proxies of staging dozens of attacks and other incidents across Europe since the invasion of Ukraine.

“Russia’s hybrid threats are becoming less and less hybrid, and more and more real,” said von der Leyen, the EC president, who condemned the alleged plot against Vasiliev in Denmark.

The Polish Foreign Ministry said in a statement that “the events in Denmark are another example of Russia’s criminal activity on the territory of an EU member state, aimed at intimidating and destabilizing our societies.”

Russia has denied accusations by Western officials that it was conducting a sabotage campaign in Europe.

World.title: Alcaraz downs Zverev to win ATP Finals for first time
World.content:
TURIN, Italy: Carlos Alcaraz won the ATP Finals with a 6-2, 7-6 (9/7) victory over world number one Alexander Zverev in the title match in Turin on Sunday.

After becoming the youngest man to complete a career Grand Slam at the start of the season with victory in the Australian Open, the 23-year-old has bookended an up-and-down year with a first title at the season-ending showpiece tournament.

Alongside Roger Federer, Andre Agassi and Novak Djokovic, Alcaraz now forms part of an exclusive list of men to have won all four majors and the ATP Finals.

With his illustrious compatriot Rafael Nadal never managing to win the season-ending tournament, Alcaraz became the first Spanish champion since Alex Corretja in 1998.

“It’s been an amazing week. I couldn’t finish the week in a better way, so I’m really proud,” Alcaraz said after capturing his sixth title of the year.

“I’ve been through really difficult moments with myself, with my team, and we could go through everything. I’m playing great tennis, so for me, lifting this trophy is something that I’ve been chasing for a really long time. It means the world to me,” he added of the hamstring issue he suffered earlier in the tournament.

A wrist injury had caused Alcaraz to miss a good chunk of the middle of the season and following that victory in Melbourne he failed to add to his seven major titles.

But since returning in August, he has enjoyed a blistering end to the year, winning his last 14 matches to capture trophies at the Vienna Open, the Paris Masters for the first time and now the elusive ATP Finals.

He lost in the season-ender’s final to Jannik Sinner last year, but with the injured Italian having curtailed his season, Alcaraz found himself again in the Turin title match against a world number one.

Zverev, a two-time ATP Finals champion, broke his Grand Slam duck this season by claiming the French and US Opens, catapulting him above Alcaraz and Sinner to the top of the rankings.

Topsy-turvy

The top two seeds in Italy, Alcaraz and Zverev were a cut above the rest all throughout the tournament, both topping their respective pools with three wins from three.

The first set of Alcaraz’s semifinal win over Ben Shelton was the only frame either player had dropped all week.

Indeed Zverev had marched into the final without dropping a service game, but he was mightily tested straight out of the traps by Alcaraz as the world number three forced three break points in the very first game before the German dug in to hold.

Alcaraz was not so wasteful two games later, however, as he broke Zverev to love when the 29-year-old overcooked a mid-court forehand.

Zverev forced break-back points in the next game but, after failing to convert, he was left to rue his luck even further as the Spaniard broke to 30 to grow his lead to 4-1.

Zverev wiped out one break but Alcaraz was nonetheless firmly in the ascendancy and pounced for a third time on the Hamburg native’s serve in an entertaining seventh game which saw Zverev dejectedly chuck his racquet to the floor after netting a smash from an Alcaraz tweener lob.

A netted backhand by Zverev — his 19th unforced error of the match — on Alcaraz’s first set point then brought an end to a surprisingly sloppy opening frame.

Both players exchanged breaks in the second set as it went the distance.

The Murcian took a 3-0 lead in the tie-break before Zverev won the next six points to bring up three set points.

But the Spaniard struck back to wipe them out before getting a mini-break to bring up championship point on his own serve.

The first went begging when he whipped a forehand into the tramlines but he brought up a second with a drop-shot and sealed the title with a backhand.

World.title: Netanyahu, Eisenkot parties end talks without deal on forming Israel govt
World.content:
HERZLIYA: The parties of caretaker Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his rival Gadi Eisenkot concluded a new round of talks on Sunday without reaching an agreement on a possible coalition government, which would require concessions from both sides.

Delegations from Eisenkot’s Yashar party and Netanyahu’s Likud met for four hours at a hotel in Herzliya, near Tel Aviv, following a first round of discussions last Sunday.

“The latest round of coalition talks... has concluded. The two sides outlined their positions on a range of substantive issues and discussed them in detail,” the two parties said in a joint statement.

“A follow-up meeting will be held,” they added, without specifying a date or revealing any other details.

A former army chief of staff, Eisenkot has until Dec. 6 to form a government, with the possibility of a 14-day extension, after October elections failed to give either camp an absolute majority.

His 48-member bloc, which needs 61 lawmakers to reach a majority, remains divided over whether to build a coalition through an alliance with ultra-Orthodox parties, a rapprochement with Arab parties, or a national unity government with Likud.

Netanyahu is pushing for a national unity government, which could see a rotation of the premiership between the two men, a mechanism already tried in Israel.

Such an arrangement could allow Netanyahu to keep his political protection against the corruption charges he faces, as well as continue to oppose the creation of an independent commission of inquiry into the security failures that preceded the Hamas attack of Oct. 7, 2023.

But that prospect runs up against Eisenkot’s refusal to serve in a cabinet led by Netanyahu, against whom he centered his campaign.

His ally Naftali Bennett, a former prime minister, also reiterated on Saturday his refusal to join a coalition with “Netanyahu or his bloc, under any circumstances.”

- National ‘unity’? -

On Saturday, Yashar presented the resumption of talks as “a genuine commitment to forming the broadest possible government,” saying that Eisenkot had asked his representatives to explore all options.

But Likud immediately laid down several conditions for its participation in a unity government, a formula backed by Netanyahu.

Among other things, it demands an end to “all personal attacks and incitement to hatred” targeting Netanyahu and his government.

It also called for bringing together “all the parties that support the existence of the State of Israel as the nation-state of the Jewish people,” without the participation of Arab parties.

Netanyahu and his allies regularly target Arab parties, which secured a record 19 seats in the legislature and are opposed to Netanyahu remaining in power.

Likud is also demanding agreement on several major policy positions, notably rejecting the creation of a Palestinian state, maintaining Israeli control over territories in Syria, Lebanon and the Gaza Strip.

It is also pushing for a compromise on conscription of ultra-Orthodox Jews, a particularly sensitive issue in Israel.

On Friday, Eisenkot warned that he would not allow the talks to drag on, saying he was ready to submit to parliament an “emergency national government.”

Although he did not spell out how, his statements suggest a two-stage plan: the swift formation of a minority government based on the core opposition parties, and then broadening it.

A minority Eisenkot government could receive support from the 19 Arab party lawmakers but Eisenkot’s right-wing ally Avigdor Liberman rejects working with them and instead advocates an alliance with ultra-Orthodox Jewish parties.

World.title: Saudi, Bulgarian ministers discuss strengthening cooperation
World.content:
Saudi Minister of Communications and Information Technology Abdullah Al-Swaha met Bulgarian Minister of Innovation and Digital Transformation Ivan Vasilev in Riyadh on Sunday.

The two ministers discussed opportunities to strengthen cooperation in artificial intelligence, technology innovation and digital skills development, as well as to support the growth of the digital economy, the Saudi Press Agency reported.

The meeting also covered developing innovative technology solutions, exchanging expertise in building digital capabilities, supporting technology entrepreneurship and expanding partnerships between companies in the two countries.

World.title: Is environmental destruction part of Israel’s displacement playbook?
World.content:
DUBAI: Families returning to southern Lebanon after being displaced by fighting between Hezbollah and the Israeli military have found olive trees uprooted and fields scorched. For communities that have worked the land for generations, the damage threatens both their livelihoods and a way of life.

Palestinians in the occupied West Bank and Gaza face similar losses. Damage attributed to Israeli forces includes the destruction of olive groves and the loss of access to water and farmland. As the resources they depend on become harder to reach or disappear altogether, families find it harder to stay on their land.

Together, these cases raise a broader question about the environmental toll of Israel’s military operations and how it shapes who can stay, who is forced to leave and who can return.

For Abbas Ali, who returned to his hometown of Nabatiyeh in southern Lebanon after the latest Israel-Hezbollah ceasefire, the devastation was deeply personal. His childhood home was badly damaged, its windows shattered, stonework smashed and water tank destroyed.

“When we finally managed to return home, the sight of our village was enough to bring tears to our eyes,” he told Arab News.

“Within our culture, we don’t look at a landscape as just a physical place. They represent generations of memories, history and a way of life that we are trying to protect.”

Hawraa Ibrahim also returned to find piles of rubble where greenery once stood. Although the olive trees in her village had survived, those in neighboring communities were less fortunate.”

“In areas where Israeli forces entered, they uprooted the trees with bulldozers, tearing them from the land. Some trees were even taken away, leaving behind nothing but destruction,” she told Arab News.

Humanitarian organizations have long raised concerns about the environmental impact of Israeli military operations in southern Lebanon, particularly the use of white phosphorus munitions and the destruction of agricultural land.

Ghiwa Nakat, executive director of Greenpeace Middle East and North Africa, said the operations were “damaging the environmental foundations of life.”

She told Arab News: “They’re ruining the air people breathe, the water they depend on, the soil and ecosystems that sustains those communities.”

The Israeli military maintains that its campaign in Lebanon is directed at Hezbollah, which began firing across the border following the Hamas-led attack on southern Israel on Oct. 7, 2023, triggering multiple bouts of conflict.

It says vegetation clearance and the creation of buffer areas are necessary to prevent armed groups from using natural cover to launch attacks.

Israel also says it takes precautions to minimize environmental damage and does not deliberately target vegetation to displace civilians.

However, researchers and rights organizations have questioned the scale and methods of the destruction.

Human Rights Watch and Amnesty International have documented Israeli use of white phosphorus in or near residential areas, raising concerns about civilian safety and environmental damage.

White phosphorus ignites upon contact with oxygen, producing intense heat and smoke. It can cause severe chemical burns and ignite vegetation, potentially spreading fires across forests and farmland.

Israel maintains that its operations in south Lebanon are intended to weaken Hezbollah and prevent cross-border attacks. (AFP file)

The Israeli military says the munitions are used for purposes such as creating smoke screens or marking targets, rather than deliberately starting fires, and that its procedures generally restrict their use in densely populated areas.

Ahmad Baydoun, a doctoral researcher at TU Delft studying the spatial and environmental impacts of warfare, has documented 282 white phosphorus strikes in southern Lebanon and one in northern Israel between October 2023 and May 2026.

His research identified 120 strikes in residential areas, 40 in agricultural areas and 93 in forests or open terrain. He argued that almost half violated international law.

“It’s not illegal to use white phosphorus, but it becomes illegal once you use it over civilians,” he said.

The legality of its use depends on the circumstances, including the presence of civilians and compliance with international humanitarian law governing distinction, proportionality and precautions in attack.

Baydoun also found that just 15 of the 282 strikes in Lebanon fell outside a proposed Israeli buffer zone, extending up to 10 kilometers into the south.

He argued that the pattern suggested the strikes had effectively traced the boundaries of the security zone before it was formally announced.

“They really wanted to remove literally any single tree that’s still standing on the border, for clearance, for visibility purposes, not to allow anyone to hide under any tree,” he said.

Lebanese officials and environmental researchers argue that the extent of fires, bulldozing and herbicide spraying points to a deliberate effort to strip vegetation and establish a depopulated buffer zone.

Israel disputes allegations of deliberate environmental destruction, maintaining that its operations are intended to weaken Hezbollah and prevent cross-border attacks.

Similar patterns of destruction by Israeli forces have been documented in occupied West Bank and Gaza and south Lebanon. (AFP file)

Whatever the intent, the consequences for communities dependent on agriculture have been severe.

Olive cultivation and oil production have sustained generations of families in southern Lebanon, providing income and a connection to their ancestral homes. Damage to farmland has also undermined confidence in local produce.

“In areas where white phosphorus was dropped, some people have become afraid to buy olive oil produced there,” said Ibrahim. “They worry that the soil may have been polluted or contaminated and that the olive oil might no longer be safe to consume.”

The destruction also threatens Lebanon’s cultural heritage.

“There are the pine trees … the cedar tree, which is represented on our national flag. These trees are deeply connected to our heritage and identity,” said Ali. “I believe white phosphorus was used deliberately to damage the land and destroy everything growing on it.”

Damage to essential infrastructure has compounded the crisis. A UN report published in August estimated that more than 700,000 people in southern Lebanon faced reduced access to safe drinking water because of damage to water and electricity networks.

Earlier this year, Lebanon’s agriculture and environment ministries reported that Israeli light aircraft had sprayed glyphosate, a herbicide, over parts of the south. Laboratory tests reportedly detected concentrations in some samples 20 to 30 times higher than those associated with normal use.

“This caused very serious damage and burning of vegetation,” said Nakat. “It also damages soil fertility and it has potential risk on the water and the food chain.”

Together, the destruction of farmland, vegetation and infrastructure threatens to make recovery increasingly difficult, even if hostilities subside.

Researchers and rights organizations have questioned the scale and methods of Israeli destruction in south Lebanon. (AFP file)

In the occupied West Bank, agricultural destruction has taken a different form, with Palestinian farmers facing attacks by Israeli settlers, restrictions on access to their land and the uprooting of olive trees.

According to the UN, 272 olive harvest-related settler attacks were documented between Sept. 1 and Oct. 19, 2026.

The Israeli military says some tree removals are necessary to eliminate cover that could be used by attackers targeting roads and nearby communities.

Palestinian residents and rights organizations dispute whether such measures justify the destruction of privately owned olive groves.

Hussein Hureini, a Palestinian journalist in the West Bank, said this year’s harvest had been particularly dangerous.

“When Palestinian farmers go, the settlers come and throw stones, shoot them,” he said. “The Israeli army, also, they come and cover the settlers, to protect the settlers and kick the farmers out and no one can collect olives.”

Hureini said settlers had cut down trees in Masafer Yatta and villages north and east of Ramallah. Reuters separately reported that Israeli military bulldozers had plowed through rows of olive trees in a village near Ramallah.

“The olive trees, we call it petrol here in Palestine. Green petrol,” he said, emphasizing their economic importance.

He described one farmer who previously produced around 400 bottles of olive oil but has been unable to access his land since the escalation of violence following Oct. 7, 2023.

Hureini believes the attacks and restrictions are intended to drive Palestinians from their villages.

Nakat expressed similar concerns about the broader consequences of environmental destruction.

Questions have arisen about whether damage in Gaza is a consequence of warfare or part of a broader pattern of dispossession. (AFP file)

“I truly believe this is part of a system plan to uproot the people and displace the people from their region.”

Even if the fighting ends, she warned, the loss of the resources and environmental conditions needed for recovery could prevent displaced communities from rebuilding their lives.

For those who have returned to southern Lebanon, the uncertainty remains.

Although Ibrahim is back in Nabatiyeh, many of her relatives are still displaced.

“Even though those areas are not occupied, that doesn’t mean they’re safe,” she said. “You never truly feel safe, even in your own home.”

She also worries about the long-term health consequences of wartime contamination, particularly for her children, although the extent of any future health effects remains uncertain.

“We’ve seen the consequences of war before, and I fear history will repeat itself,” she said.

Ali fears the devastation witnessed in Gaza could eventually be repeated in southern Lebanon. Yet despite the destruction of his home and surrounding landscape, he remains determined to stay.

“The war may have changed our lives but it hasn’t taken away our love for our land or our determination to return to it.”

World.title: A flavorful stop at Aykr in Sikkah Boulevard
World.content:
RIYADH: Tucked into Sikkah Boulevard, Aykr offers a relaxed dining experience that pairs a modern setting with a menu built around bold flavors and familiar ingredients with a twist.

The meal got off to a strong start with the tempura eggplant, which was crisp on the outside while remaining tender inside. Served with a miso ranch sauce, the dish had a satisfying combination of textures and flavors, with the creamy sauce adding another layer to the crispy eggplant.

The blooming onion was another enjoyable appetizer, arriving crunchy and well-seasoned, making it an easy choice for sharing.

The standout of the appetizers for me, however, was the chipotle corn. Combining fried and grilled corn, the dish is finished with a drizzle of chipotle sauce and sour cream and served with a lime wedge on the side.

The contrast between the smoky grilled notes, crispy fried corn, and creamy toppings made it particularly enjoyable. The lime is also worth using, especially for those who prefer a little extra tanginess, as its acidity cuts through the richness and brings the flavors together.

For the main course, I tried the shrimp tostada, which comes as a serving of two, making it a convenient option to share. While the tostadas are on the smaller side, they pack plenty of flavor. The shrimp is paired with mango and avocado salsa and a spicy peanut sauce, creating an interesting balance between sweet, creamy, and spicy elements.

The rigatoni was another solid choice, offering a comforting pasta option alongside the more adventurous dishes on the menu.

To accompany the meal, I went for the passionfruit mocktail. Refreshing and pleasantly fruity, it was a good match for the variety of flavors throughout the meal and made for an enjoyable drink to sip between dishes.

Beyond the food, Aykr’s setting adds to the experience. The atmosphere is calm, with soft lighting and a sleek, modern interior that gives the restaurant a polished yet comfortable feel. Its large glass windows allow plenty of natural light into the space, making it particularly inviting during the day.

Its location within Sikkah Boulevard is another advantage. After finishing a meal, diners can easily step outside and continue exploring the surrounding area, whether browsing the nearby shops or simply taking a walk.

Overall, Aykr is a good option for a relaxed meal in a stylish setting, particularly for those who enjoy sharing several dishes and exploring a mix of familiar flavors with a modern twist.

For more information, check out Aykr on Instagram @aykr.sa.

World.title: Iraq offers $33 per barrel discount for December oil sales
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi oil is once again being offered at significant discounts for shipments that will be loaded in December 2026, as challenges related to crude oil exports from the country’s southern ports persist.

Iraq’s State Oil Marketing Organization (SOMO) has decided to offer Basra crude shipments with discounts reaching as much as $33 per barrel.

These offers cover both Basra Medium and Basra Heavy crude grades for loading in December, with buyers left to determine the specific quantities they wish to purchase.

These new discounts follow similar offers for October shipments—which reached as high as $37 per barrel—as Baghdad seeks to maintain its oil export flows amid rising shipping and insurance costs, as well as risks associated with navigation through the Strait of Hormuz.

SOMO views the discounts on Iraqi oil as an opportunity to market shipments of Basra crude for this coming December, particularly with the ongoing crisis related to the restricted passage of tankers through the strategic waterway.

The offers include Basra Medium crude at a discount of $29.20 per barrel and Basra Heavy crude at a discount of $33 per barrel.

The discounts have narrowed by $5.30 per barrel for Basra Medium crude and by $4 per barrel for Basra Heavy crude compared to oil shipments in October.

World.title: Four killed in power plant explosion in southern Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – At least four people were killed and 35 others injured on Saturday following a massive gas pipeline explosion and fire at the al-Hartha thermal power station in southern Iraq.

The explosion took place around 6:00 a.m. local time at the Hartha power station, located north of the Basra province.

The Iraqi Ministry of Electricity mentioned that an explosion in a gas pipeline servicing the power plant was the cause of the fire.

According to reports, investigations are ongoing to determine the cause of the pipeline explosion.

Flames spread rapidly from the power plant to nearby trailers and informal homes.

Locals with burns and smoke inhalation make up the majority of the 35 injured, with officials warning that that the death toll may increase.

While Electricity Minister Ali Saadi Waheeb called for an emergency meeting to address facility repairs and power supply interruptions, Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi instructed the Health Ministry and the authorities in Basra to mobilize all available medical resources for the victims.

The power plant, which has a capacity of 800 megawatts and was producing about 400 megawatts before the incident, had to shut down entirely.

World.title: Iraq pushes to raise oil output to 10 million barrels per day
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi ordered on Sunday accelerated oilfield operations and extended working hours to advance Iraq’s push to reach 10 million barrels per day by 2032.

Al-Zaidi’s remarks took place during his meeting with Meg O’Neill, CEO of British Petroleum (BP), where he emphasized the importance of expanding the recovery of associated gas and ending gas flaring, according to the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

The development would bolster Iraq’s energy supplies and meet domestic consumption needs, according to al-Zaidi.

The meeting addressed the development of oil fields and the extension of exploration areas, particularly the Kirkuk field, the Eridu field in Dhi Qar, and the Rumaila field in Basra.

The discussion is part of the Iraqi government’s goal to increase production rates and produce 10 million barrels per day by 2032.

O’Neill affirmed BP’s readiness to expand its operations in Iraq, leveraging its advanced technical and technological expertise to increase production and develop oil fields in line with established plans.

Iraq produces 4.88 million barrels of crude oil per day, according to OPEC data for October 2026, which is based on official Iraqi figures.

BP is involved in projects to develop Iraq’s oil sector; in March 2025, the company signed a deal with the North Oil Company (NOC) and the North Gas Company (NGC) to develop and rehabilitate the Kirkuk fields.

Additionally, BP provides technical support for the development of the Rumaila field in Basra.

BP’s deal in Kirkuk is not limited to developing oil production; it also encompasses the development of gas resources and the establishment of projects to expand infrastructure and processing facilities.

Iraq continues to flare approximately 24 billion cubic meters of gas annually—according to World Bank estimates for 2025—despite its need for gas to provide fuel for power plants and reduce reliance on imports.

World.title: KDP and PUK resume dialogue in Erbil amid disputes over parliament and Sulaymaniyah status
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Efforts to reset relations between the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) and the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) have brought fundamental questions over the political trajectory of the Kurdistan Region back to the forefront following a high-level meeting between the two rival parties in Erbil on Saturday, November 21, 2026.

While the talks reopened cautious optimism about breaking the region’s prolonged political deadlock, subsequent statements from Sulaymaniyah revealed persistent disputes over the legitimacy of the Kurdistan Parliament’s recent session, power-sharing mechanisms, and mounting calls for the administrative separation of Sulaymaniyah from Erbil.

The core institutional dispute centers on the legality of the Kurdistan Parliament’s latest session, which the KDP defends as constitutionally sound while the PUK refuses to recognize.

Speaking at a press conference in Sulaymaniyah, KDP 21st Branch official Sattar Awlani asserted that reactivating parliament is a national duty backed by clear attendance figures and legal foundations. Echoing KDP President Masoud Barzani’s call for inclusive dialogue, Awlani stressed that the party’s doors remain open to the PUK and all political forces to form a broad-based regional administration.

On the PUK side, Politburo member Imad Ahmad struck an optimistic yet guarded tone, telling reporters that the Erbil meeting “went well, God willing,” while declining to disclose substantive details of the negotiations.

KDP Central Committee member Sanaw Fereydoun similarly welcomed the resumption of dialogue as a hopeful step, emphasizing that any durable settlement must respect voter mandates and election results, while suggesting that rigid pre-negotiation stances could soften as talks progress.

Complicating the parliamentary impasse are renewed calls advocating the administrative separation of Sulaymaniyah Governorate from Erbil. Awlani flatly rejected such proposals, warning that separating Sulaymaniyah lacks any constitutional or legal basis and is destined to fail, urging all sides to resolve grievances through institutional partnership rather than unilateral moves.

Despite their internal divisions, leaders from both the KDP and PUK closed ranks regarding federal moves by Baghdad to tighten control over oil revenues and combat smuggling—an issue heightened by Prime Minister Ali Faleh Al-Zaidi’s recent enforcement campaign in northern Babylon.

Both parties emphasized the Kurdistan Region’s distinct constitutional status. Awlani noted that the region is a legally protected constitutional entity whose authorities must be respected in any federal measures, while Imad Ahmad affirmed that disputes between Baghdad and Erbil must be settled strictly within the framework of the Iraqi Constitution, balancing mutual obligations and rights.

Taking a sharper stance, Sanaw Fereydoun dismissed reports suggesting federal anti-smuggling campaigns could extend into the Kurdistan Region’s border crossings as baseless rumors propagated by hostile actors.

Linking Kurdistan’s internal deadlock to Iraq’s wider political turbulence, political analyst Arslan Mohammed told Shafaq News that the country is navigating a quasi-transitional phase marked by friction between Baghdad and armed factions, oil disputes, economic strain, and rifts within both the Shia and Sunni political houses.

Mohammed warned that persistent KDP-PUK discord compounds public anxiety over political and economic stability, criticizing both parties for keeping citizens in the dark through vague official statements. He urged Kurdish political forces to publicly clarify their intentions, explain sudden unilateral decisions, and clearly delineate between governing partners and opposition actors in order to rebuild public trust in regional institutions.

World.title: Iraqi bodybuilder dies three days after winning Asian championship
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Three days after taking home a gold medal at the Asian Championships in Pattaya, Thailand, Iraqi international bodybuilding champion Sajad Jawad passed away at the age of 30.

Fans, other athletes, and authorities have expressed their sorrow at his unexpected death, which has shocked Iraq’s sports community.

After having previously finished in 11th place in the same event, Jawad reached an important milestone at the Asian Bodybuilding Championships in Thailand by winning first place and securing the continental championship in the 90-kilogram category.

On Thursday, the Iraqi National Federation of Bodybuilding and Fitness announced Jawad’s death through the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA).

Federation President Faiz Abdul-Hassan and board members offered Jawad’s family condolences for his death.

Officials have not revealed the cause of his death. No medical report has been issued to confirm any reasons, despite reports of an unexpected health setback or physical weariness during competition preparation.

Jawad has over 260,000 Instagram followers and represented Iraq in several national and continental contests. His final social media post praising his gold-medal victory received hundreds of condolences after the announcement.

World.title: Al Zaidi to visit Cairo for talks on energy and defense
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Faleh Al-Zaidi is scheduled to travel to the Egyptian capital, Cairo, on Monday, November 23, 2026, at the head of a high-level government delegation for official talks focused on political coordination, security, economic investment, oil and energy integration, and defense procurement, according to a government source.

During the visit, Al-Zaidi will meet with senior Egyptian officials—including President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi—to advance bilateral ties and expand Egyptian corporate participation in Iraqi infrastructure and reconstruction projects.

The summit builds directly on preparatory talks held in Baghdad on October 18, 2026, when Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty conveyed an official invitation from President el-Sisi and discussed activating the tripartite cooperation mechanism linking Iraq, Egypt, and Jordan, with particular emphasis on regional electrical grid interconnection and oil transport projects.

The Cairo trip marks the latest leg in an intensive regional diplomatic push launched by Al-Zaidi over the past five weeks to strengthen Iraq’s Arab neighborhood ties and energy transit corridors.

His recent regional itinerary began on October 14 with a visit to Saudi Arabia for talks with Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, followed by a stop in Jordan on October 26 to meet King Abdullah II.

Two days later, on October 28, Al-Zaidi traveled to Damascus to meet Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa, where discussions centered on border security, trade, and the potential rehabilitation of the Iraqi crude oil pipeline running across Syrian territory to the Mediterranean port of Baniyas.

On November 4, he made a landmark visit to Bahrain—the first by an Iraqi prime minister to Manama since 2003—to bolster bilateral economic relations and regional coordination.

Al-Zaidi’s resumption of foreign travel comes immediately after the de-escalation of last week’s security crisis in Jurf al-Sakhar (Jurf al-Nasr) in northern Babylon Governorate. On November 17, the Prime Minister had postponed a scheduled official visit to Beirut in order to remain in Baghdad in his capacity as Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces and oversee federal deployments during the standoff with Kata’ib Hezbollah.

World.title: Behind the Jurf al-Sakhar truce: Kata’ib Hezbollah remains in place as Qaani brokers year-long timeline
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Two days after federal security forces entered Jurf al-Sakhar (Jurf al-Nasr) in what Baghdad hailed as its first assertion of state authority over the closed northern Babylon subdistrict in 12 years, local sources and insiders close to Iraqi armed factions have disclosed details contradicting the official narrative, according to a report by Al-Mada newspaper.

While Prime Minister Ali Faleh Al-Zaidi addressed troops from the newly established joint control headquarters on Friday, November 20, declaring that “there are no weapons outside state authority,” sources on the ground indicate that the federal deployment has not displaced Kata’ib Hezbollah.

Instead, incoming Federal Police units were positioned near the town of Musayyib—where most displaced Jurf al-Sakhar residents have lived since 2014—well outside Kata’ib Hezbollah’s core security perimeter, while additional Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF/Hashd al-Shaabi) formations entering the area are described by locals as sympathetic to the faction.

A senior Shia political leader close to the factions told Al-Mada that the recent movements amount to reinforcing Kata’ib Hezbollah’s existing PMF brigades (the 45th, 46th, and 47th Brigades), rotating Federal Police detachments, and deploying Energy Police along pipeline corridors rather than dismantling the group’s military infrastructure.

Even if Kata’ib Hezbollah formally commits to vacating the district, the source estimated that dismantling bases and relocating heavy weaponry would require at least a full year—a timeline extending well beyond Baghdad’s June 30, 2027 deadline for bringing all weapons under state control.

Coordination Framework insiders linked this extended reprieve—and Kata’ib Hezbollah’s abrupt de-escalation after threatening to carry the confrontation into Baghdad’s Green Zone—directly to an eleventh-hour intervention by Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Quds Force Commander Esmail Qaani.

Prior to Friday’s deadline, Qaani met in Baghdad with Kata’ib Hezbollah Secretary-General Abu Hussein Al-Hamidawi, Badr Organization leader Hadi Al-Amiri, and PMF Chairman Falih Al-Fayyadh, prompting Al-Hamidawi to instruct fighters to stand down from high alert and resolve disputes with the government through private channels.

Despite brokering the ceasefire, Iranian officials reportedly expressed sharp dissatisfaction with Kata’ib Hezbollah’s brinkmanship, urging the faction to follow the path of other armed groups that have pivoted toward political integration and state posts.

According to coalition sources, Tehran has spent recent months cultivating more disciplined, tightly controlled armed formations with stronger direct ties to Iran rather than domestic Iraqi politics—a shift coinciding with the sudden emergence of a previously unknown group calling itself “Asa’ib al-Jihad.”

Appearing in a video statement under the banner of the “Islamic Resistance Front in Iraq,” Asa’ib al-Jihad displayed an explosive-laden drone and threatened Shia political parties and factions it accused of abandoning armed resistance in exchange for government positions and financial gain.

Political observers suspect the group represents a hardline splinter faction broken away from Asa’ib Ahl al-Haq following the latter’s decision to comply with weapons-handover initiatives.

As Baghdad sought to project calm in northern Babylon, Al-Zaidi’s government was hit by a major energy security incident in southern Iraq on Saturday, November 21, when an explosion along the gas pipeline feeding the Al-Hartha thermal power station in Basra sparked a deadly blaze that killed and injured dozens and damaged nearby homes. While the government launched an urgent technical probe, political and security circles raised suspicions of a potential drone strike echoing prior attacks on energy infrastructure.

Analyzing the broader political stalemate, academic and political researcher Ghalib Al-Daami argued that the Jurf al-Sakhar compromise underscores the structural constraints placed on Al-Zaidi by the very ruling coalition that brought him to power.

Within Iraq’s consensus system, Al-Daami noted, strengthening sovereign state institutions directly erodes the entrenched economic and security interests of ruling factions—leading influential Coordination Framework actors to impose clear boundaries on how far the Prime Minister can push state consolidation without destabilizing the coalition.

World.title: US dollar dips slightly across Baghdad, Erbil, and Basra markets
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate of the U.S. dollar against the Iraqi dinar edged slightly lower across major domestic parallel markets on Sunday morning, November 22, 2026, with purchasing bids settling below the 170,000-dinar threshold in both Baghdad and Erbil while retail selling rates hovered narrowly above that mark across primary trading hubs.

According to morning market figures, physical banknote rates traded across Baghdad, Erbil, and Basra as follows:

In Baghdad, currency exchange counters posted retail selling rates at 170,050 IQD against buying offers of 169,500 IQD per $100.

In Erbil, currency desks quoted retail selling rates at 170,300 IQD alongside matching purchasing bids of 169,500 IQD per $100.

In Basra, foreign exchange offices recorded slightly firmer quotes, with retail selling rates at 170,500 IQD and buying offers holding at 170,000 IQD per $100.

Parallel cash rates continue to trade at a wide spread of roughly 18,050 to 18,500 dinars above the Central Bank of Iraq’s (CBI) official rate of 152,000 IQD per $100 (1,520 IQD per dollar).

World.title: Food regulator FSSAI sanctions prosecution of Bisleri, 4 other firms
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (

) has sanctioned prosecution against five food businesses, including Bisleri International Pvt Ltd, over food products found unsafe or substandard, while suspending the licences of two other establishments over serious food safety and hygiene violations.

FSSAI has sanctioned prosecution against Bisleri over a sample of packaged drinking water that was found non-compliant with prescribed bromate limits and declared unsafe under Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. The Referral Food Laboratory too declared it unsafe after detecting polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons. Bisleri International was contacted for its response but had not responded till the time this report was filed.

Vasant Masala Pvt Ltd was prosecuted after its chilli powder was found to contain difenoconazole, a pesticide residue, above the allowed limit. Tit-Bit Foods (India) Pvt Ltd faced prosecution over its pre-packed chilli powder containing excess pesticide residues and turmeric powder containing tin above the permitted limit.

Mimansa Industries Private Limited faced prosecution over walnut kernels found substandard and unsafe. Asha Confectionery faced prosecution over chocolate-filled cookies found misbranded, substandard and unsafe due to discrepancies in declared sugar values.

World.title: India, Nepal set to ink pacts on energy, infra, tech on Balen Shah's 1st visit
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Foreign minister S Jaishankar called on Nepal PM Balendra Shah, who arrived in India on Sunday for what is his first bilateral visit abroad. PM Modi will host Shah for their first in-person meeting on Monday that will be followed by an exchange of "forward-looking" agreements spanning key areas of cooperation: infrastructure, technology, connectivity, development partnership, energy, hydropower, railways, climate change and disaster resilience.

"India cherishes the special friendship with Nepal. Look forward to his engagements with PM @narendramodi tomorrow," said Jaishankar in a post on X after the meeting. Official sources said that the leaders will virtually inaugurate several completed initiatives, apart from joining foundation stone-laying ceremonies for some new projects. Shah is also expected to reiterate Nepal's request for two-way low-altitude air entry corridors through Indian airspace near western border entry points.



Securing direct air routes is essential for Nepal to attract international airlines and make its new Bhairahawa airport commercially viable. âThis visit comes at an opportune moment when there is considerable synergy between the national priorities of both countries in terms of economic growth, social development, expansion of infrastructure, adoption of technology and addressing issues like natural disasters and climate change,â said a source, adding that the leaders will look to provide political direction that will shape the roadmap for bilateral cooperation for many years to come.





The two sides have finalised a joint vision for bilateral relations that is expected to be released after the meeting. Nepal is also seeking an economic package worth $2 billion from India. While Shah may raise the boundary issue, itâs unlikely to be a sticking point in the meeting.

India sees its ties with Nepal as unique and comprehensive, characterised by mutual trust, open borders, shared traditions and close people-to-people ties.

Govt sources highlighted how India is Nepalâs largest trade, transit and investment partner. Nepal enjoys duty-free access to the Indian market and India is also Nepalâs biggest export destination and receives about 80% of Nepalâs goods exports, they said.

The visit is expected to build upon the goodwill generated in Nepal by Indiaâs assistance to the country after the devastating floods earlier this year. India provided about 140 tonnes of emergency supplies and extended technical assistance in tunnel rescue and forensic activities following the flash flood.

India and Nepal are exploring the development of new pipelines and terminals to further enhance energy connectivity. Both sides are also discussing new possibilities, such as the RaxaulKathmandu railway link, which could open new avenues for cross-border passenger and freight connectivity

World.title: NHAI puts 50,000 km of highways under dashcam watch, to automate penalties for contractors
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Highway concessionaires, maintenance contractors and NHAI officials will no longer be able to dodge or delay action on defects, such as potholes, faded road markings, rutting and faulty lights, which remain major recurring problems on NH stretches.

NHAI has rolled out a system for weekly monitoring of 40 types of defects through dashcams installed in patrolling vehicles covering nearly 50,000 km of NH network.

NHAI officials said that not only will data and details be collected with exact location and visual evidence, but these will also be shared with respective contractors responsible for specific stretches.

âThe dashcams can detect potholes as small as two inches pothole.



Currently, failing to rectify defect within a set timeline attracts penalties, which are calculated as per contract conditions. In the next couple of months, the penalty calculation will become automatic. We have been sensitising contractors and officers for the past two months,â said a senior NHAI official.

Dashcams detecting highway defects

This covers all NH stretches under NHAI that are under operation and maintenance. This is significant considering that the highways authority has faced public ire over poor maintenance of several road stretches.





Data accessed by TOI showed that 92,088 defects were detected through dashcam recordings since the exercise was rolled out two months back. Nearly 23% of these related to faded road markings and around 15% to potholes. While nearly 72% of the defects were rectified, around 17% remain overdue for rectification.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

As per the set timelines, contractors get two days to fill potholes, one day to fix defunct lights and safety issues at work zones, and seven days to close unauthorised openings, to name a few.

âSince the details of defects are backed by evidence and every contractor and field officer can see them on our central server, there is no question of any dispute. Highway contractors also understand that timely maintenance reduces their burden. The defects are closed only when details of rectification with pictorial evidence are uploaded and verified,â said another NHAI official.

TOI has learnt that at a later stage, the public would also be able see the details and give their feedback.

World.title: Indian Navy allows marriage for Agniveers opting for 2-year service extension
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Easing rules to make naval jobs more attractive, the

has allowed Agniveers who opt for a two-year extension after the initial four-year service to get married. The policy relaxation comes just as the first batch of Naval Agniveers â recruited in late 2022 â completes its initial four-year stint this month.

The Union Cabinet recently approved a two-year extended service period for Agniveers, officially called âSecond Tour of Dutyâ.

âThose Agniveers who have completed their four-year initial service period and have opted for the two-year extension will be allowed to marry, though only after completion of their mandatory initial training on joining. The training will be professional and trade specific,â a defence source told TOI.



After completing their training, Agniveers can take the entitled leave for marriage purposes, the source said.

The marriage provision is currently not available for Naval Agniveers (ages 17.5 to 21) during the initial four-year service period under the Agnipath scheme. âNavy has made the decision on marriage provision and orders have been issued,â the source said. After the Navy, Indian Army and Indian Air Force could follow suit by allowing Agniveers to marry as per their own specifications.

On Nov 4, Chief of Defence Staff General N S Raja Subramani announced the âSecond Tour of Dutyâ provision under the Agnipath scheme, increasing Agniveersâ service duty period from four years to six with increased remuneration. Govt has also decided to create a pathway for âall Agniveers to be enrolled as regular soldiers (permanent job)â if they are willing to continue and meet selection criteria. To make the extension lucrative, extended-tenure Agniveers will receive Rs 43,500 per month in the first year of extension and Rs 47,500 per month in the second year (plus applicable allowances), while govtâs Seva Nidhi contribution will rise to 70% during those two years.

World.title: Ladakh chief secretary cites cites 70% panchayat poll turnout, sticks to December 4 hill council voting
World.content:
SRINAGAR: Ladakh chief secretary Ashish Kundra on Sunday welcomed the high voter turnout in panchayat and municipal elections held the previous day, saying it reflected that people want democracy as he appealed for greater participation in hill council (LAHDC) polls scheduled for Dec 4.

The turnout was 70.03% in Saturdayâs panchayat elections and 52.4% in municipal polls. âWe must not forget that the last panchayat and municipal elections were held in 2018. This is the first time elections are being held since Ladakh became a Union Territory (in 2019),â Kundra said.

Kundra announced that talks between Ladakhi representatives and the Union home ministry (MHA) on autonomy would resume after the LAHDC elections.



Leh Apex Body (LAH) member and climate activist Sonam Wangchuk is at the forefront of protests by Ladakhi groups against holding the LAHDC polls in the harsh winter when they claim many people are away.

Kundra asked Wangchuk not to make âprovocative statementsâ during election season. Asked about LABâs demand to delay LAHDC polls, Kundra said: âOnly 10 to 12 days are left. Around 70% of the people voted in the panchayat election.

World.title: Kaiga nuclear unit-1 attains criticality again, gets a second life
World.content:
A unit attaining criticality means it has reached a self-sustaining, controlled nuclear fission chain reaction inside its reactor core

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: In a big milestone for the countryâs nuclear sector, Kaiga Generating Station Unit-1 (KGS-1) in Karnataka successfully attained criticality early Sunday for the second time, giving a new lease of life to the nuclear power unit that had been taken offline for life-extension work after 25 years of operation. The disclosure was made on Sunday by Nuclear Power Corporation of India Limited (NPCIL), the PSU that designs, builds, commissions and operates nuclear power plants across India.A unit attaining criticality means it has reached a self-sustaining, controlled nuclear fission chain reaction inside its reactor core.KGS-1 had reached first criticality on Sept 26, 2000, and had supplied 37,670 million units before it was shut down for refurbishment activities in April last year. The same unit had set a world record for 962 days of continuous operation on Dec 31, 2018, operating at a 99.3% plant load factor, surpassing the previous global record of 940 days held by Heysham II (Unit 8/Reactor 2) in the UK.âThe accomplishing this in just 600 days following its shutdown for major refurbishment activities of EMCCR (en-masse coolant channel replacement) and EMFR (en-masse feeder replacement) on April 1, 2025, KGS-1 has set a new fleet-wide benchmark as the first NPCIL reactor to reach criticality in such a short span,â NPCIL said on X on Sunday.It said, âThis remarkable success stands as a reflection of extraordinary dedication, technical excellence, and unified teamwork. âKaiga generating station has four operational nuclear units totalling 880 MW and two additional units (5 and 6) under construction, adding 1,400 MW and bringing the total planned capacity to 2,280 MW across six units.Kaiga Units-5 & 6 are state-of-the-art, indigenous 700 MW pressurized heavy-water reactors (PHWRs), which incorporate advanced safety features and are among the safest in the world. Three such PHWRs â KAPS-3&4 and RAPP-7 â are successfully operating in the states of Gujarat and Rajasthan respectively. The components and equipment for the project are supplied by domestic industry partners and works are being executed by Indian contractors, aligning with the Atmanirbhar initiatives of the Modi govt.Just days before, in another development, Atomic Energy Regulatory Board (AERB) granted permission for the first approach to criticality of Rajasthan atomic power project unit-8 (RAPP-8) at Rawatbhata, following satisfactory completion of safety reviews.

World.title: SCO Civilisational Dialogue at Purana Qila concludes with  'Indraprastha Communique' affirming to respect every civilisation as an 'equal voice'
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The first Shanghai Cooperation Organisation Civilisational Dialogue Forum hosted by India at the historic Purana Qila concluded on Sunday with the âIndraprastha Communiqueâ -- an outcome document with affirmations ranging from protecting heritage from threats and exploring joint nominations for UNESCO heritage tag to constructively using Artificial Intelligence and creating a digital repository of manuscripts and records of cultural histories.

The communique affirmed respect for every civilisation as an âequal voiceâ, and acknowledged its identity and contribution to humanity. Reading out the communique at the closing session of the meet on Sunday evening, culture secretary Vivek Aggarwal said that India has proposed that the SCO Civilisational Dialogue be held once every two years at a place to be decided by the SCO member states.

The three-day meet inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday saw the participation of 116 delegates from 22 countries, including Pakistanâs federal minister Musadik Malik.



PM Modi had proposed the SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum at the 25th SCO Summit in Tianjin, China, in 2025 and the idea was welcomed and endorsed subsequently enabling India to host the first Forum in Delhi from Nov 20 to 22.

The venue, Purana Qila, took centre stage at the event as India showcased the siteâs multi-layered history and its identity as the ancient city of Indraprastha mentioned in the epic âMahabharataâ.





The name of the communique reaffirmed that message, which was reiterated by India through the layers of excavations and exhibits displayed at Purana Qila during the meet, presenting thousands of years of history.

The communique called for celebrating âdiversity as a strengthâ and recognised culture as a âvital bridge for friendship, good neighbourliness among nationsâ.

The outcome document also highlighted the need to evolve an SCO mechanism for collaborative projects and exhibitions and a platform for collaboration between cultural institutions of SCO countries.

To protect heritage from various kinds of threats, it called for exploring the creation of a platform for resilience against climatic tragedies.

It further called for honouring spiritual and philosophical traditions, and places of learning and pilgrimage, and encouraging respectful dialogue with due regard for diversity of beliefs and practices.

Asked if any formal bilateral talks were held between India and Pakistan on the sidelines of the event, Aggarwal answered in the negative, but said that just as with other member countries, the Indian side had interactions with Pakistanâs representative during the course of the event.

On Sunday evening, Musadik visited the Mahabharata Pavillion displaying the rare 18th century Mahabharata scroll. He called it âvery impressiveâ, appreciated its artistic and religious value, and lauded the commitment of the artist for the delicate and intricate work on the scroll.

He reiterated the affirmation made in the Indraprastha Communique of working with SCO members to create a digital repository of manuscripts from the region and said that Pakistan would be keen to explore showcasing knowledge about many artefacts, including those excavated from Mohenjo-Daro, once a framework is developed for the same.

He expressed optimism that cross-border visits and regional relationships would improve ahead of Pakistanâs hosting the next SCO Council of Heads of State summit in Islamabad in August 2027.

The first SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum in India was organised jointly by the ministry of culture, and the ministry of external affairs with the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (IGNCA) serving as the knowledge partner.

On Saturday, the thematic session "Civilisational and Cultural Expressions" saw ministers and representatives of participating countries present their perspectives on their cultural traditions, historical experiences and areas of common interest. The exchanges brought into focus the importance of safeguarding tangible and intangible heritage, strengthening institutional linkages, encouraging interaction among scholars and artists, and advancing joint research and documentation.

A dedicated session organised by the Archaeological Survey of India, titled "A Shared Cultural Canvas - Artistic and Architectural Exchanges Among SCO Nations", examined the many historical encounters that have shaped the region's artistic and architectural landscape. According to details shared by culture ministry and IGNCA discussions traversed prehistoric and Bronze Age linkages, Buddhist art and architecture, Silk Route exchanges, Indo-Persian influences and maritime connections, while also considering collaborative approaches to heritage conservation and digital documentation.

On Sunday deliberations centred on two themes: "Language, Literature, Script and Manuscript Traditions" and "Monastic Trails - Religious and Philosophical Traditions". The first session explored approaches to preserving languages, scripts, manuscripts and literary heritage, as well as the transmission of knowledge across generations and geographical boundaries. The second examined the journeys of faith and philosophy and the historical relationships linking religious institutions, centres of learning and communities across the SCO region.

World.title: Wanted man held after 14 months for mob attack on Delhi police team in Chhatarpur
World.content:
A 20-year-old man wanted in connection with a mob attack on police personnel in south Delhi’s Chhatarpur, in which four policemen were injured, has been arrested from Rajasthan after evading arrest for over 14 months, police said on Sunday (November 22, 2026)

The accused, identified as Arbaj Khan alias Baiju, a resident of Chandan Holla village in Chhatarpur, was apprehended by the Special Staff of South district from Village Gadpur in Bhiwadi on November 20, following a tip-off received two days earlier, police said.

According to the police, the incident took place on September 15, 2025, when a police team performing official duties in Chandan Holla village was attacked by a mob armed with bricks, sticks and stones. Four police personnel sustained injuries in the attack, while the mob also obstructed the team from carrying out its duties.

An FIR was registered at Fatehpur Beri police station on September 16, 2025, under sections 221, 132, 121(1), 110, 351(2) and 3(5) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).

Police said a team of the Special Staff developed the intelligence input about Khan’s whereabouts and conducted an operation in Bhiwadi to apprehend him. He was subsequently brought to Delhi and arrested on November 20 in connection with the case.

The police said the accused had no previous criminal involvement. Further investigation remains under way.

World.title: Netanyahu, Eisenkot parties end talks without deal on forming Israel government
World.content:
The parties of caretaker Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his rival Gadi Eisenkot concluded a new round of talks on Sunday (November 22, 2026) without reaching an agreement on a possible coalition government, which would require concessions from both sides.

Also read | Israeli President picks Gadi Eisenkot, Netanyahu rival, to try to form government

Delegations from Eisenkot's Yashar party and Netanyahu's Likud met for four hours at a hotel in Herzliya, near Tel Aviv, following a first round of discussions last Sunday (November 22).

"The latest round of coalition talks... has concluded. The two sides outlined their positions on a range of substantive issues and discussed them in detail," the two parties said in a joint statement.

"A follow-up meeting will be held," they added, without specifying a date or revealing any other details.

A former army chief of staff, Eisenkot has until December 6 to form a government, with the possibility of a 14?day extension, after October elections failed to give either camp an absolute majority.

His 48-member bloc, which needs 61 lawmakers to reach a majority, remains divided over whether to build a coalition through an alliance with ultra?Orthodox parties, a rapprochement with Arab parties, or a national unity government with Likud.

Netanyahu is pushing for a national unity government, which could see a rotation of the premiership between the two men, a mechanism already tried in Israel.

Such an arrangement could allow Netanyahu to keep his political protection against the corruption charges he faces, as well as continue to oppose the creation of an independent commission of inquiry into the security failures that preceded the Hamas attack of October 7, 2023.

But that prospect runs up against Eisenkot's refusal to serve in a cabinet led by Netanyahu, against whom he centred his campaign.

His ally Naftali Bennett, a former prime minister, also reiterated on Saturday his refusal to join a coalition with "Netanyahu or his bloc, under any circumstances".

National ‘unity’

On Saturday (November 22), Yashar presented the resumption of talks as "a genuine commitment to forming the broadest possible government", saying that Eisenkot had asked his representatives to explore all options.

But Likud immediately laid down several conditions for its participation in a unity government, a formula backed by Mr. Netanyahu.

Among other things, it demands an end to "all personal attacks and incitement to hatred" targeting Mr. Netanyahu and his government.

It also called for bringing together "all the parties that support the existence of the State of Israel as the nation-state of the Jewish people", without the participation of Arab parties.

Mr. Netanyahu and his allies regularly target Arab parties, which secured a record 19 seats in the legislature and are opposed to Mr. Netanyahu remaining in power.

Likud is also demanding agreement on several major policy positions, notably rejecting the creation of a Palestinian state, maintaining Israeli control over territories in Syria, Lebanon and the Gaza Strip.

It is also pushing for a compromise on conscription of ultra-Orthodox Jews, a particularly sensitive issue in Israel.

On Friday (November 20), Mr. Eisenkot warned that he would not allow the talks to drag on, saying he was ready to submit to parliament an "emergency national government".

Although he did not spell out how, his statements suggest a two-stage plan: the swift formation of a minority government based on the core opposition parties, and then broadening it.

A minority Eisenkot government could receive support from the 19 Arab party lawmakers but Mr. Eisenkot's right-wing ally Avigdor Liberman rejects working with them and instead advocates an alliance with ultra-Orthodox Jewish parties.

World.title: 18th U.P. Legislative Assembly sits less than 90 days, experts point to unhealthy concentration of power in the Executive
World.content:
With hardly two months left for Uttar Pradesh assembly polls and the 18th Uttar Pradesh Legislative Assembly (May 2022- March 2027) nearing completion, question marks have been raised over the fewer days/meetings of the Legislative Assembly in the last five years.

Editorial | Stoop to conquer: On the Opposition’s seat-sharing ahead of U.P. polls

As the 18th Uttar Pradesh Legislative Assembly functioned for only 84 days, an average of 17 days a year, Opposition parties and constitutional experts in the State said fewer functioning days directly limit legislative oversight, and MLAs lose opportunities to raise constituency-centric issues.

They added that in a State having a population of over 25 crores (250 million people), at least 50 days of Assembly sessions per year, similar to the Lok Sabha, are necessary.

As per the data accessed by The Hindu and reverified through the data available with PRS Legislative Research as well as the U.P. Legislative Assembly Official Website, the State Assembly functioned for 16 days in 2022, 20 days in 2023, 16 days in 2024, 18 days in 2025 and 14 days in 2026 till now. The Assembly functioned for only over 500 hours in the last roughly five years in 15 sessions. In comparison, the 17th Lok Sabha, which functioned between June 2019 and May 2024, functioned for 274 days, across 15 sessions, averaging 55 sitting/days per year.

“The nearing conclusion of the tenure of the 18th Uttar Pradesh Legislative Assembly presents an unsettling indictment of legislative governance in India’s most populous State. A House entrusted with representing more than 25 crore citizens reportedly sat for only 84 days over its five-year tenure, averaging just 17 sitting days a year. Such infrequent sittings are not a matter of administrative convenience; they strike at the heart of the constitutional scheme of accountable government. For a State grappling with enormous developmental challenges, law-and-order concerns and a population larger than that of most countries, such limited legislative engagement is indefensible. If the Lok Sabha can meet for around sixty days annually, Uttar Pradesh should institutionalize at least fifty sitting days every year as a constitutional minimum. Democracy is not sustained merely by periodic elections; it survives through continuous legislative vigilance. A Legislature that seldom meets risks converting representative government into a constitutional ritual and reducing executive accountability to an illusion. Such a trend ought to alarm every citizen who values constitutionalism, democratic oversight and the rule of law,” said Syed Mohammad Haider Rizvi, an expert on Constitutional Law and Legislative Processes and practicing advocate based in Lucknow.

Sudhir Panwar, a senior Samajwadi Party (SP) leader said, “the Constitution distributed power and responsibility between legislature and executive for efficient working of democratic system. The legislature is responsible for oversight on functioning of executive and budget scrutiny. There is a fine balance between executive and legislative; fewer sitting disturb that balance in favor of the executive. The other dimension is relationship between fewer sitting and concentration of power in political system and those at helm of affairs as Chief Minister. In state assembly for continuous working, the committee system like Parliament needs to be introduced,”.

Highlighting the Constitutional provisions, Mr. Rizvi added that when the Assembly sits for barely a handful of days each year, legislative oversight becomes diluted, financial scrutiny under Articles 202 to 207 becomes truncated, and the representatives of the people are deprived of sufficient opportunities to raise constituency-centric concerns, and the inevitable consequence is an unhealthy concentration of power in the Executive, contrary to the spirit of constitutional checks and balances.

“The Constitution of India envisages a Legislature that is not a passive spectator but an active constitutional check upon executive authority. Articles 163 and 164 make the Council of Ministers collectively responsible to the Legislative Assembly, a responsibility that can be meaningfully enforced only when the House meets frequently enough to question, debate, scrutinize, and hold the Government to account. Likewise, Article 174 requires the Legislature to meet at regular intervals and clearly contemplates a living, functioning institution rather than one that assembles merely to satisfy the minimum constitutional formality. In constitutional theory and democratic practice alike, the Legislature is the foremost forum through which the sovereign will of the people finds expression,” he said.

World.title: Three arrested for stabbing two youths in northeast Delhi; screwdriver used in attack recovered
World.content:
