World.title: Tony Carter to replace Sir Rob McLeod as Sanford chair
World.content:
Seafood company Sanford has announced a change of leadership at the top of its board.

Outgoing chairman Sir Rob McLeod will retire as a director and chair on 16 December, to be replaced by experienced businessman and company director Tony Carter.

The transition will occur at Sanford's annual shareholder meeting, subject to Carter being elected as a director by shareholders.

McLeod joined Sanford's board in 2016 and has chaired the company since 2019. He said the timing was right to step down.

"After close to eleven years as director, and with a strong Board and leadership team in place, this is a natural point to hand over."

McLeod leaves as Sanford comes off a record annual result, reporting a $74.5 million profit for the year ended September.

Tony Carter brings a heavyweight business CV as the current chairman of Datacom, having previously chaired Air New Zealand and Fisher & Paykel Healthcare and served on the boards of Fletcher Building, ANZ Bank New Zealand and Vector.

Before that he was the chief executive and managing director of Foodstuffs for a decade.

"Sanford is a great New Zealand company with a proud history and a talented team, and I am excited to be working alongside my fellow directors, management and our shareholders in the period ahead. On behalf of the Board, I thank Sir Rob for his service."

World.title: A vaccine for acne? Scientists are working on it
World.content: These studies are designed to assess the safety of the vaccines, the immune responses they produce and whether they improve acne. Importantly, the participants already have acne, so the trials are investigating the vaccines as treatments rather than as a way of preventing acne in the first place.

World.title: Joeys come back to Earth with frustrating World Cup result
World.content:
The Joeys have been left facing a slightly nervy final group match before guaranteeing their spot in the knockout stages at the Under-17 World Cup following a frustrating goalless draw against Denmark.

Australia's bright soccer teenagers, who had begun so sparkly with Akol Akon inspiring them to a 2-0 victory over Argentina in Doha, were brought down to Earth somewhat as they dominated possession and chances against the Danes only to draw a blank.

The Joeys could not quite find the killer blow against the Danes. (Getty Images: Lewis Storey )

With Argentina bouncing back to beat Mozambique 2-1 later on Sunday, local time, the outcome of group C is not cut and dried going into the final round of pool games on Wednesday.

Australia still leads the way on four points, with Argentina and Mozambique both on three and Denmark on one.

Just a draw against Mozambique would guarantee a top-two place in the group and give Carl Veart's players a place in the last 32, while even defeat to the African side might not be calamitous because the 48-team format awards places to the eight best third-place finishers.

Young Aussies stun Argentina Sydney FC prodigy Akol Akon inspires the Joeys to a shock 2–0 victory over Argentina to launch their U17 World Cup campaign in style in Qatar.

But Australia will still want to deliver a better display than the one it produced against Denmark, which was hammered 4-0 by Mozambique in its opening outing.

Brisbane's 17-year-old box-to-box midfielder Emmett Shaw was named the player-of-the match but he will rue missing the best chance of the match when he should have sunk a free header in the 74th minute while unmarked.

While Australia enjoyed 66 per cent of possession, it took it 55 minutes to get a shot on target, with Shaw's long-range free-kick proving far too hopeful, although Akon did come closer with a curling free kick in the 69th minute.

Impressive young Brighton keeper Charlie Wilson-Papps did not have a great deal to do but, when really called on in the 83rd minute, he got down sharply to make a key stop to thwart a low shot, Denmark's best chance of the match.

AAP

World.title: In F1's 'most chaotic race ever', Piastri finally able to find his mojo
World.content:
With a beaming grin from ear to ear, covered in champagne and looking like a man who had a weight lifted off his shoulders, Oscar Piastri summed up his stunning Las Vegas Grand Prix in six words: "It was a lot of fun."

2026 has not been Piastri's year, and of the top drivers in F1, he has had the most disappointing season.

But on the Las Vegas Strip, in a grand prix that teammate Lando Norris called the "most chaotic race ever", Piastri found his mojo, and has allowed himself the chance to finish 2026 with a bang.

Piastri third, snaps at McLaren team, in Vegas GP with 352 overtakes Oscar Piastri produces his finest performance of the 2026 season, claiming a sensational podium in Las Vegas after starting 17th on the grid.

Following on from the bitter disappointment of losing out in last year's thrilling world championship fight to Norris, Piastri's 2026 season started horribly, and never really got any better.

The soaring highs of leading the championship in 2025 felt like a distant memory when he failed to start the opening two races this season.

But a second-place finish in Japan and third in Miami — rounds three and four of the season — gave a false hope that Piastri could be in contention again in 2026.

It wasn't to be.

Piastri would not be on the podium in the next 16 grands prix, the longest streak of his F1 career.

Meanwhile, Norris claimed three brilliant race wins and is fighting to finish third in the championship, while Piastri languishes in seventh.

The Las Vegas Grand Prix, on paper, should have been like the rest of Piastri's 2026 — a struggle.

He qualified seventh, took a penalty for adding a new internal combustion engine to his power unit, and started a lowly 17th on the grid.

What followed was tremendous racecraft, as Piastri sliced his way through the field.

Oscar Piastri's third place finish in Las Vegas was his first podium since Miami, 17 rounds ago. (Getty Images: LAT Images/Alastair Staley)

In a race where the field was pretty much bunched up for all 50 laps, and with a ridiculous 352 overtakes across the grand prix, Piastri made sure he was going forward more than he was going backwards.

He didn't have it all his own way. He was behind his teammate when the safety car was called and dropped from ninth to 13th while he had to wait for Norris to pit first.

That still didn't matter.

Piastri just went back to work, picking off his rivals one by one, until the most unlikely of podiums was in sight.

He had a bit of luck to get there. George Russell hitting the wall, and Kimi Antonelli losing battery power late in the race cleared the path for Piastri's podium finish — but the Victorian had made his own luck.

And luck is something he has had little of in 2026.

Asked post-race if he had turned a corner, and could eye off bigger and better things in 2027, Piastri, as usual, remained grounded.

"It's hard to say. I think the pace in general was pretty strong, so I was happy," her said.

"But that was such a particular race — the next two weeks are not going to look like that."

He's right. The next two races in Qatar and Abu Dhabi will not look like the frantic, action-packed, drama-filled grand prix in Las Vegas.

But history suggests there could be at least one similarity — Piastri on the podium.

Piastri's first win in F1 was the Qatar sprint race in 2024, and he went on to finish third in the grand prix.

Last year he again won the sprint race, and should have won the grand prix had it not been for a disastrous pit strategy by McLaren, which practically handed the race win to Max Verstappen. Piastri still finished second that day.

Now he goes into a track that, statistically, he is exceptional at, and has confidence following one of the best drives from anyone this season.

Piastri also has success at Abu Dhabi, with a best finish of second, which he achieved last year. He started on the front row there as well in 2024, but was taken out by Verstappen on the first lap.

He is heading to tracks he enjoys, and where he has enjoyed great results.

His Las Vegas podium does not mean he has turned the corner, and Piastri is the first to acknowledge that.

But the terrific performance could not have come at a better time, and could be the first step in his rise back to the top.

World.title: How Prespakis and Rowbottom are leading new era of AFLW stars
World.content:
Since the AFLW was made an 18-team competition, much speculation heading into the league's night of nights has been whether star Roo Jasmine Garner will earn the recognition she deserves.

Where in the past it has been players who have been around from the competition's inception who were the top vote-getters in the AFLW Best and Fairest Award — eight of the 10 winners to date were listed in the first two seasons — this year it is the top two draftees from the 2021 draft who are shaping up as the best chance at winning on Monday evening.

Garner is still a genuine chance at the medal, as is Sydney dynamo Chloe Molloy, but it is Charlie Rowbottom and Georgie Prespakis who are deemed the genuine frontrunners.

Ahead of that draft night in 2021, Rowbottom made waves by nominating the Queensland draft pool — obviously, before there was a truly national draft — and as a result, was taken with the first pick by Gold Coast. That left the other top pick contender, Prespakis, to fall to Geelong at number two.

Both have been vital cogs of their respective midfields across their seven seasons, and although some raw numbers do look very similar, the way they play their footy could not be more different.

What looks similar

As pure ball winners, both Prespakis and Rowbottom have been right at the top of the league throughout the home-and-away season.

They have each attended the most average centre stoppages for their respective sides, and therefore their average contested possession and clearance numbers also sit first and second across the league.

Georgie Prespakis (AFLW rank) Charlie Rowbottom (AFLW rank) Avg. Disposals 30.6 (sixth) 32.6 (second) Avg. Handballs 17.3 (second) 16.8 (third) Avg. Contested Possessions 17.6 (first) 17.3 (second) Avg. Clearances 8.1 (first) 7.9 (second) Avg. Hard Ball Gets 5.2 (first) 4.9 (second)

Each strong at the source, they are key starting points for their respective teams' attack. They have both played every game this season — for teams that reached finals for the first time since 2023, no less — and regularly starred along the way.

What is different

After that first phase of play, however, each player prioritises differently. Rowbottom tends to remain a tough, defensive option, bringing her physicality, while Prespakis is that sleek runner taking the ball forward.

Charlie Rowbottom has been a leader in the Gold Coast midfield this season. (Getty Images: AFL Photos/Michael Willson)

The Gold Coast star is staunch in tight, choosing to release her running teammates like Niamh McLaughin, Ava Usher, and Lucy Single.

Her capacity to be the big body drawing attention that ultimately creates space for those on the outside was critical to the Suns' game plan this year, which averaged nearly four more goals per game in 2026 than it did in 2025.

So, for Rowbottom, the numbers that stand out in addition to those above are her average tackles (6.2) and marks (3.6), while she also pressed forward to kick a career-best five goals.

She is not a player who repeatedly gets involved in a transitional passage of play; rather, she is often the starting point and has developed the capacity to become the end point more reliably.

She finished with five or more tackles in seven of her games, and 10 or more clearances in four of those.

Prespakis is more of that player who remains involved in running handball chains to set up those inside her team's attacking 50. She was the number one score involvement player across the AFLW in the season, sits first for average loose ball gets (7.6) and sixth for average metres gained (428.2).

No-one playing in the AFLW has more score involvements than Georgie Prespakis this season. (Getty Images: AFL Photos/Adam Trafford)

Her clearance game is more about her agility to evade danger and run the ball out, with her handball numbers more indicative of those back-and-forths as she and teammates dash up the field.

This resulted in six home and away games with eight or more score involvements, and seven recording 400 or more metres gained.

This style of play was emblematic of how the Cats played their footy this year. Fast, predictable to one another, and with every intention to take the game forward.

Georgie Prespakis Charlie Rowbottom Avg. Tackles 5.1 6.2 Avg. Marks 2.5 3.6 Avg. Intercepts 5.2 3.9 Avg. Metres Gained 428.2 328.3

For an effective midfield to operate, each style of midfielder is necessary: the big-bodied contested beast, and the dashing metres-gained player. It is fair to say that — maybe except Garner herself — each of Prespakis and Rowbottom has been the best of their respective style of midfielder this year.

Should one of the pair claim the medal on Monday night, it would be a key signifier of this fresh era of the AFLW, leaning on those players who have enjoyed greater junior pathway opportunities, and greater support in their talent development at the elite level.

World.title: CA says Cummins backing not a sign it is taking sides in sandpaper spat
World.content:
Todd Greenberg insists Cricket Australia has not taken Pat Cummins's side in the ball-tampering saga, adamant that keeping the quick as Test captain should not deter others from contributing to the upcoming truth forum.

Cummins is expected to train again at the SCG early this week, as he and the fellow pacemen press on with their preparations for the first Test against New Zealand starting on December 9.

The 33-year-old confirmed on Saturday he would contribute to CA's independent forum, and make his own submissions over the events of the 2018 South Africa tour.

The context you need to understand Bancroft's version of Sandpapergate If you feel like you missed a beat with the Australian cricket's sandpaper scandal and why its back in the news, this breakdown of Cameron Bancroft's article will bring you up to speed.

It is expected the quick will deny any prior knowledge of the use of sandpaper on the ball on that tour until Cameron Bancroft was caught in Cape Town, a position the bowlers have maintained since that day.

Officials will lay out the parameters for the forum in the coming days, but have already made clear there will be no further sanctions, regardless of the findings.

There had initially been a fear that only those with an axe to grind may contribute, following claims by Usman Khawaja and Bancroft that the entire team knew of the ball-tampering plot.

David Warner and Chadd Sayers have also backed the claims raised in Khawaja's book, which kicked off the renewed furore a month ago.

But Cricket Australia CEO Greenberg has now had to deny that the CA board publicly standing by Cummins to remain captain on Saturday had swung it back in the other direction, and dissuaded those with opposing views.

Cricket Australia boss Todd Greenberg says the organisation is not picking sides amid the reignited Sandpapergate furore. (ABC News: Ebony ten Broeke )

"I don't see it that way, because I support their version of events and their ability to share what they think happened at that period of time," Greenberg told the BBC.

"That's their version. Equally, that's Pat's version as well.

"I am not putting someone's version of events over somebody else's. That's the one thing we're not doing.

"Pat has been the captain for five years, we haven't made any changes.

"If we were to, that would believe someone's events over the others."

Then-Australian coach Darren Lehmann has repeatedly denied prior knowledge of the plot to use sandpaper in Cape Town. (Jason McCawley - CA/Cricket Australia via Getty Images)

Beyond Cummins, then-coach Darren Lehmann has also indicated he will contribute, after denying Bancroft's assertions that he was aware of the plot on Saturday night.

Greenberg also maintained that the board's unanimous support of Cummins did not mean they thought Khawaja or Bancroft were lying.

Asked what would happen if the majority of the 2018 touring party — including staff and players — claimed everyone knew, Greenberg suggested nothing would change.

"Then so be it," Greenberg said.

"We're going in with an open mind and without providing sanctions."

Steve Smith received a heroes welcome at the SCG when he lined up for New South Wales in the Sheffield Shield on Sunday. (Getty Images: Mark Metcalfe)

Former CA board member Michael Kasprowicz reiterated on Monday that the 2018 bans handed down to Steve Smith, Warner and Bancroft were not solely related to tampering.

Kasprowicz was a director in 2018 when CA's investigation found the trio were the only three to know of the plot.

"I am not sure it is actually about sandpaper, because the umpires didn't even change the ball," Kasprowicz told AAP.

"I know from a board point of view at the time, it wasn't about damaging the ball. It was about damaging the brand.

"That's why steps had to be made in those circumstances."

Usman Khawaja (left) will link up with Darren Lehmann (right) during an exhibition T20 clash in Cairns on Sunday night. (Getty Images: Matt Roberts)

Kasprowicz is due to link up with both Khawaja and Lehmann in the celebrity cricket Gold Clash in Cairns on Sunday night.

Asked if he believed the sanctions may have been different had Khawaja or Bancroft given their most recent accounts then, Kasprowicz was uncertain.

"I don't know, eight years ago is eight years ago," the 38-Test seamer said.

"Your receipts and tax records only last for seven and you have to chuck them.

"That's why I am thinking what is going on right now is even more extraordinary."

Cricket on Sunday attempted to move on from the Sandpapergate saga, with Steve Smith returning from his neck injury to the Sheffield Shield alongside Nathan Lyon.

Smith spent most of the day fielding at slip for NSW, taking a catch to remove Test hopeful Jack Clayton on 10 in the middle session at the SCG.

He also bowled two overs of leg spin in the final session, to strong applause from a crowd of just under 2,000 at the SCG.

AAP

World.title: Horne-Francis planning to recruit Nasiah during AFL Origin camp
World.content:
Jason Horne-Francis is open to throwing his weight around in South Australia's AFL Origin camp to recruit St Kilda superstar and friend Nasiah Wanganeen-Milera.

South Australia and Western Australia today named their first five representatives for next year's Origin match, to be played at Perth Stadium on February 27.

Wanganeen-Milera and Port Adelaide's Horne-Francis were picked by SA coach Craig McRae, along with Saints co-captain Callum Wilkie, Adelaide skipper Jordan Dawson and Collingwood boom recruit Lachie Neale.

Players committed to 2027 AFL Origin SOUTH AUSTRALIA: Jason Horne-Francis, Callum Wilkie, Lachie Neale, Jordan Dawson, Nasiah Wanganeen-Milera WESTERN AUSTRALIA: Patrick Cripps, Charlie Cameron, Kysaiah Pickett, Luke Jackson, Tom Barrass

Wanganeen-Milera rejected massive interest from his native South Australia in 2025 to re-sign on a two-season, $4 million deal with the Saints.

Locking away the silky 23-year-old playmaker on an extension is top of St Kilda's agenda.

This year's Origin revival match between WA and Victoria allowed Western Bulldogs captain Marcus Bontempelli to build a connection with Zak Butters, who crossed from Port Adelaide in the off-season.

While already mates with Wanganeen-Milera, Horne-Francis is mindful of the recruitment opportunity Origin camp presents.

"That worked, didn't it," he told reporters, referring to the Butters-Bontempelli connection developed through Victoria's Origin team.

Marcus Bontempelli (background) successfully recruited Victorian teammate Zak Butters (foreground) to the Western Bulldogs. (Daniel Carson/AFL Photos via Getty Images)

"So maybe I've got to try to do the same thing. Not that we need any more bonding time — we see each other bloody all the time anyway.

"We ran out together in the [Indigenous] All-Stars as well, so it will be good to run out with him again and see what he's got for us."

The 23-year-old admitted he might have to battle with Crows rivals to wrap an arm around Wanganeen-Milera, who finished fourth in St Kilda's best-and-fairest this season.

"There might be a bit of push and shove there," the Port ball-winner said.

St KIlda star Nasiah Wanganeen-Milera is once again in high demand as he comes out of contract. (Getty Images: Morgan Hancock)

Horne-Francis and other Adelaide-based SA representatives may have to go through Wilkie to get some alone time with Wanganeen-Milera.

"I won't let him talk to Dawson or anyone from Port," Wilkie joked.

"He'll stay right under my wing.

"Nas is amazing at putting that [contract speculation] to bed and focusing on us and what he brings to the club on field and off field."

Wilkie said he and Wanganeen-Milera had been speaking about the possibility of donning the SA jumper all year.

Collingwood coach Craig McRae will lead Wanganeen-Milera and South Australia in the Origin clash. (Getty Images: Quinn Rooney)

"That's what's so special about it," he said.

"You think when you're getting drafted you're never going to be able to pull the colours on again."

WA coach Dean Cox's first selections are Hawthorn defender Tom Barrass, Brisbane forward Charlie Cameron, Carlton skipper Patrick Cripps, Fremantle ruck Luke Jackson and Melbourne livewire Kysaiah Pickett.

Cripps, who captained WA against Victoria this year, is also due to come off contract at the end of next season.

Carlton captain Patrick Cripps has no plans to finish his AFL career in WA. (Getty images/AFL Photos: Matt King)

But the dual Brownlow Medal winner hosed down the possibility of finishing his illustrious career in his home state after the Blues made the finals under now-permanent coach Josh Fraser, despite starting last season 1-8.

"I've been here that long, you sort of become ingrained in the club," Cripps said.

"I sort of feel like a Carlton supporter these days … this is my 14th season.

"I've always loved playing footy at Carlton and been driven to try and build the club from the ground up, and I'm really excited about where we are right now."

AAP

World.title: India breaks New Zealand Test record with monster innings in Wellington
World.content:
India has broken the record for the highest Test score in a match played in New Zealand as it put itself in a commanding position to win the first Test in Wellington.

New Zealand reached 2-119 at the close of play on day four as it fought to save the first Test after India declared on a mammoth 9-720 with an imposing first-innings lead of 352.

India's assault was led by Rishabh Pant (128), whose six sixes took his career tally to 108 in just 53 Tests, now second behind all-time best Ben Stokes (138). Pant surpassed former NZ captain Brendon McCullum (107) during the innings.

New Zealand's hopes of a result rest on batting for much of the remainder of the match and forcing a draw, despite losing Tom Latham for a duck and first-innings centurion Henry Nicholls for 31.

Opener Devon Conway, who scored his 22nd Test half-century on his way to an unbeaten 59, and Rachin Ravindra (27 not out) will resume on day five with the Black Caps still 233 runs from forcing India to bat again.

India's pace spearhead Jasprit Bumrah (1-33) again made an early breakthrough, sending Latham back on the second ball of the innings, the New Zealand skipper edging behind to take a pair.

Nicholls, whose 175 was the backbone of New Zealand's first-innings 368, got an edge and a bit of thigh pad on a Prasidh Krishna delivery, and Dhruv Jurel showed stunning reflexes to take the catch at short leg.

Jurel had earlier become the sixth batter to score a half-century in India's innings before being caught in the deep for 78, triggering the declaration an hour before tea.

India had resumed on 4-486 on another sunny morning at the Basin Reserve with the clear intent of pushing their 118-run lead out to the sort of tally that would take the possibility of a New Zealand victory out of the equation.

There are few better batters for such a task than Pant, and the swashbuckling wicketkeeper showed the full range of his shots as he approached his ninth Test hundred.

Pant was finally caught on the boundary for 128 off the bowling of Ravindra to bring up lunch, but the punishment for New Zealand continued into the second session.

Jacob Duffy finished with 1-201 off 33 overs. (Getty Images: Hagen Hopkins)

India's final score was well clear of its previous best innings tally in New Zealand of 520 all out in Hamilton in 2009 — a match they won by 10 wickets.

All-rounder Glenn Phillips (3-154) picked a couple of wickets as the Indian batters went for their shots ahead of the declaration to make his figures a bit more respectable.

Seamer Jacob Duffy, though, finished with unenviable figures of 1-201 from his 33 overs, only 28 runs shy of New Zealand's most expensive ever bowling display, which spinner Stephen Boock tallied against Pakistan in 1989.

Reuters

World.title: Wallabies still have a pulse despite nervous moments in win over Wales
World.content:
In Les Kiss's words, the Wallabies "earned their corn" with their gritty 29-26 Nations Championship win over Wales in Cardiff.

After ending a four-match losing streak, the Wallabies coach struck a relieved but proud figure when he and captain Harry Wilson fronted the post-match media conference.

It couldn't be described as a polished display on the field, nor was there a moment during the match where it seemed the Wallabies were dominating their opposition.

Each time they opened up an encouraging lead on the scoreboard, it never felt as though Wales was too far away from clawing its way back into the contest.

Wallabies defeat Wales The Wallabies hold on to defeat Wales 29-26 following a thrilling finish to their Nations Championship Test in Cardiff.

But winning breeds confidence, which had been in short supply for the Wallabies following losses to New Zealand (twice), England and Scotland.

"They had to work hard for it and I think tonight was a true Test match [and] they earned their corn and got what they deserved," Kiss said.

An improved defensive effort was among the positives in the Wallabies' performance.

While three of the four tries they conceded came from driving mauls off line-outs, they denied Wales more than once with their scramble defence deep inside the 22.

"When we do it [defence] well, it's a real point of difference for us," Wilson said.

"I thought our D-zone [inside 22] defence tonight was unbelievable."

The Wallabies' aerial game in attack also showed glimpses of its potential, with Max Jorgensen's second-half try an example of the pressure they can apply to opposition teams.

The line-out was strong (they enjoyed a clean sheet on their throw), highlighted by Josh Canham's clutch steal when Wales was camped inside the Wallabies' 22 during the first half.

Wallabies lock Josh Canham (right) enjoyed an excellent all-round performance. (Getty Images: Michael Steele)

But the Wallabies let themselves down with poor discipline, especially inside their territory.

They conceded nine penalties in the opening 40 minutes, seven of which were on their side of the halfway line.

By full-time, the Wallabies had given 11 penalties away inside their half, with Wilson shown a yellow card in the 77th minute for one of those indiscretions.

If the Wallabies do the same against Ireland at Twickenham next weekend, they won't be shown any leniency.

Kiss admits the Wallabies' penalty count gave him "the shits".

"Discipline was a little bit disappointing, I must say … it kept them [Wales] in the game with field position and a few things like that," he said.

"So we're going to have to look at that as well."

Ikitau to the fore

Among individual performances, Carter Gordon looked assured at fly half.

The Wallabies were still pedestrian at times with ball in hand, however Gordon did enough to indicate he's the most suitable candidate to wear the number 10 jersey.

Wallabies fly half Carter Gordon looked solid against Wales. (Reuters: Andrew Couldridge)

Len Ikitau was deservedly named player of the match, again proving he's a world-class operator.

But the question remains whether he's better suited to inside or outside centre.

When the Wallabies pulled off their upset 42-38 win over the world champion Springboks in Perth in September, his performance at outside was superb until he left the field injured.

On that occasion, he was partnered in the centres by Hunter Paisami, who is unavailable for the Wallabies' Nations Championship campaign in Great Britain.

Ikitau played inside centre against Wales, with Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii admirably slotting in at 13.

Len Ikitau was outstanding in the Wallabies' win. (Getty Images/CameraSport: Ian Cook)

A permanent Ikitau-Paisami midfield combination may be the Wallabies' best option at next year's Rugby World Cup, although Suaalii's stocks at outside centre rose in Cardiff, even though he appears more comfortable on the wing.

For now, the Wallabies will turn their focus to the Ireland Test, which pits the two third-ranked teams from the respective Nations Championship groups against each other.

Their spirits will be buoyed by halting their losing streak, but Kiss knows the pressure of Test rugby never lets up.

"Test match footy doesn't hand you things easy," Kiss said.

World.title: Bellamy to end Storm coaching stint after 2027 NRL season
World.content:
Melbourne can officially begin planning for life after Craig Bellamy, after the veteran coach confirmed the longest tenure in NRL premiership history would end in 2027.

After years of speculation about his future, Bellamy will officially finish with the Storm next year at the end of his 25th season in charge of the club.

The 67-year-old's call to walk away comes after he was diagnosed with a neurodegenerative disorder this year.

Craig Bellamy's coaching CV NRL - Brisbane Broncos (2002): Two matches, one win, one loss

NRL - Melbourne Storm (2003-current): 630 matches, 433 wins, 195 losses, two draws

NRL premierships: 2012, 2017, 2020 (all with Storm)

State of Origin - New South Wales (2008-10): Nine matches, two wins, seven losses

But he still hopes to play some role around the club after 2027, with the five-time premiership-winning coach the most powerful figure in the Storm's history.

"I love this club and everything it represents, the people, our history and our fans," Bellamy said.

"I still have huge passion for the job, and I'm excited about what we can achieve together in 2027.

"While 2027 will be my final season as senior coach, I'm determined to make the most of the opportunity and give everything I can to our club and our players.

"I've always said I'll continue coaching while I believe I can make a positive contribution, and I feel I can still do that.

"I also feel the time is right to make 2027 my final year."

Cameron Munster is one of several big-name Storm stars who are off-contract at the end of the 2027 season. (Getty Images: Pete Dovgan/Speed Media/Icon Sportswire)

Bellamy's decision to officially call stumps comes after chief executive Justin Rodksi admitted on Friday the uncertain future had complicated contract talks with the club's biggest names.

Harry Grant, Cameron Munster and Stefano Utoikamanu are all off-contract at the end of 2027, with the Storm facing an uphill fight to retain all three.

Melbourne hasn't been able to provide clarity on who will coach the club in 2028, unable to officially move on appointing a successor until Bellamy had decided his future.

Billy Slater remains the biggest name linked with Melbourne after he walked away from the Queensland State of Origin job in August.

Billy Slater is the highest-profile name tipped to be Bellamy's successor for the Storm. (Getty Images: Darrian Traynor)

Slater does sit on Melbourne's part-time staff, but has so far suggested he does not want to coach in the NRL.

Bellamy also declared in August that Melbourne's next coach should come from within, with Marc Brentnall, Ryan Hinchliffe and Bellamy's son Aaron his full-time assistants.

Brad Arthur, Michael Maguire, Anthony Seibold and Jason Ryles are among coaches to have come out of Bellamy's system in Melbourne.

Arthur is currently coaching Leeds in the Super League, but has signalled a desire to return to the NRL, while Maguire is under pressure at the Broncos.

Ryles is on the verge of signing an extension at Parramatta, while Seibold is a free agent after being sacked by Manly last season.

"Craig is one of the greatest coaches in the history of rugby league, and we're proud of everything he has achieved in the game," Storm chairman Matthew Tripp said.

"We're also delighted he'll have one final season in charge in 2027.

"While we would obviously love to have Craig coaching our team forever, we understand how significant this decision is and are incredibly grateful that we will have another season with him leading our club."

AAP

Tech.title: Delta flights in and out of Atlanta delayed due to system outage
Tech.content:
The system that went offline calculates the total weight of an airplane, including its airframe, fuel, passengers and their baggage. The system also allows pilots to determine the plane’s center of gravity and whether the weight is evenly distributed — data points that help ensure safe passage.

“Delta teams are using manual workarounds this morning to safely get flights departed while work continues to restore automation,” the airline said in a statement on Sunday.

Tech.title: Binding of Isaac developer removes AI music from Repentance Plus
Tech.content:
is the Verge’s weekend editor. He’s covered the tech industry for over 18 years and knows a thing or two about synths.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

The Binding of Isaac: Repentance Plus has spent the last few days getting review-bombed on Steam after it was discovered that a particular segment of the game used AI music. Reddit user ShweetsStuff discovered the songs used during a Grand Theft Auto-themed section. They found several audio files with Suno metadata that pointed back to the tracks on Suno’s site.

Creator Edmund McMillen took to X to apologize and claimed he “had no idea” the in-game GTA parody used generative AI music. Adding to the drama, Valve requires developers to disclose how and when they use generative AI in the development process, and Nicalis, Inc., the studio behind Repentance Plus, doesn’t appear to have mentioned the AI music anywhere.

Within hours of the discovery, Nicalis shared on X that Repentance Plus had been updated and the generated music files had been removed. While reviews on Steam have yet to rebound, and the game is still rated as “overwhelmingly negative,” users on X seem to be giving McMillen the benefit of the doubt, likely because he’s been quite outspoken on AI in game development, calling it “uninspired and bland” in a TikTok from 2024.

Tech.title: Sheherazaad’s Khudgarzi is gorgeous, ‘genre-chaotic’ South Asian folk
Tech.content:
is the Verge’s weekend editor. He’s covered the tech industry for over 18 years and knows a thing or two about synths.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

Sheherazaad started making ripples in the music world a few years ago with her EP Qasr, which was produced by Grammy Award winner Arooj Aftab. Now she’s back with Khudgarzi, her reverb-drenched folk-noir debut LP that’s primarily sung in Urdu.

The instrumentation on Khudgarzi draws on traditional South Asian music, including Carnatic and Hindustani styles, but also dabbles in Arabic folk traditions, as well as modern Western electronic music. Trip-hop flourishes and Spaghetti Western guitar brush up against tanbur and ghatam. Sheherazaad’s stunning voice sits atop dripping percussion and seasick drones singing about the plight of “The Selfish Woman.”

For Sheherazaad, the character of the selfish woman isn’t the villain, it’s a charge leveled at women who didn’t conform to societal norms, “eccentric women whose desire for agency was often met with an awful end.” Even if you can’t understand most of the lyrics, the atmosphere tells the story clearly enough. From the barely simmering anger of “Registaan” to the bleak repetition of “Qatil” and the fantastical yearning of “Zeher,” Khudgarzi is clearly the work of a woman exploring what it means to be a woman, the lasting legacy of colonialism, and the perpetual threats of a patriarchal society.

Khudgarzi is alternately a funeral dirge and a celebration of femininity. Sheherazaad owes a lot of the album’s ability to navigate these various themes and moods to her impressive production work, top-notch mixing by J. Valleau, and the cast of over 30 “genre-chaotic” virtuosic musicians including Ria Modak, Sarathy Korwar, Jay Chakravorty, Shunya, and Qasim Naqvi. The instrumentation never distracts, though. It’s not showy, and all emulsifies around Sheherazaad’s vocals in a shawl that feels equal parts comforting and oppressive.

Khudgarzi is available now on Bandcamp and most major streaming platforms, including YouTube Music, Spotify, Apple Music, Deezer, and Qobuz.

Tech.title: Protesters storm Meta offices in India
Tech.content:
is the Verge’s weekend editor. He’s covered the tech industry for over 18 years and knows a thing or two about synths.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

Members of the opposition Congress party protested outside Meta’s offices in Delhi on Friday and appear to have entered the building in a video shared by CNN. Members of the party’s youth wing are demanding the company restore accounts of party leaders and warned of more protests to come. The Congress party has criticized Meta for censoring speech that Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his BJP party disagree with, and has placed banners accusing Mark Zuckerberg of favoring BJP around the city.

While two accounts in question were restored Friday, Manu Jain, who oversees social media for the party’s youth wing, told Reuters that “thousands of accounts of journalists, creators and influencers critical of the government remain restricted.”

In February, India issued tighter rules around the removal of “unlawful” content, changing the timeline from 36 hours to just three. Modi and the Indian government have long been criticized for their restrictive policies around free speech and accused of stifling opposition viewpoints and attempting to bully the press.

Meta did not immediately return a request for comment.

Tech.title: ‘The show is starting soon. Please turn on your headphones.’
Tech.content:
is a senior reviewer covering TVs and audio. He has over 20 years experience in AV, and has previously been on staff at Digital Trends and Reviewed.

Up a few concrete steps and through the front door of a 200-year-old row house in New York City, I follow a crowd of people into the 178-seat SoHo Playhouse. As we filter to our seats, ushers hand each person a black drawstring bag with a pair of wired headphones connected to a small Auracast receiver. Then, soon after the play begins, we’re instructed to put them on.

The headphones are an integral storytelling tool of Love Me — a one-man show from the minds of stand-up comedian and former Saturday Night Live writer Drew Michael and director Prashanth Venkataramanujam. It’s a show about love and the bid for connection, told in five chapters about different relationships in Michael’s life, bound by the threads of his hearing loss and self-discovery.

Related The tech world is sleeping on the most exciting Bluetooth feature in years

Love Me’s experimental sound design is possible thanks to Auracast, a technology based on Bluetooth that can broadcast a high-quality audio stream to any number of nearby devices. As the show follows Michael from childhood through adulthood, sound designer Daniel Kluger uses the headphones in combination with the theater speakers to create experiences that wouldn’t be possible with a traditional setup. Tinnitus ringing and hearing test tones play in the music between sections as subtle clues as the show builds to Michael’s epiphany about his hearing loss. Kluger also explores the world through varying levels of sonic clarity. Sound playing through the theater’s speakers is sometimes intentionally muffled, which is then further dulled by the headphones, giving the audience a sense of what Michael is hearing in those moments.

But one sound that stays clear and pristine is Michael’s inner monologue, heard in the headphones throughout the show. The inner monologue consists of both prerecorded tracks and the live feed from Michael’s microphone on stage as he talks back and forth with himself. “Any time you’re in my head — anything in the headphones is coming through clearly,” Michael tells me after the show. “[We’re] trying to also highlight that the appeal of the inner world is such that it’s the highest fidelity space for this person. It’s more comfortable.”

The different sound sources and treatments of the sound can lead to intentionally confusing scenes for the audience. During one, where Michael is doing a stand-up set at a comedy club, three sounds compete for attention: The theater speakers play the crowd’s reactions (including a heckler whose voice is sometimes muffled and sometimes clear); his prerecorded inner monologue reacting to the crowd plays in the headphones; and on stage, Michael is performing the set, with his mic muffled so our focus is on his inner monologue. It’s one of the definitive moments where the audience feels the constant concentration necessary to parse what’s happening when sounds aren’t clear and become overwhelming.

Before the show begins, there are instructions on the screen to make sure the provided headphones are connected and working properly. Photo: John Higgins / The Verge Soon after the show starts, the audience is instructed to put on their headphones and wear them for most of the show. Photo: Curtis Brown

But the biggest impact comes during a climactic scene the sound design has been building toward, a realization that also incorporates the visuals of a series of Michael’s audiograms over the years. “I had this massive breakthrough about the whole history of what I’ve been doing — the cognitive labor, the invisible to myself labor that was affecting every single minute of my life,” Michael says. “That was a huge moment.”

That’s when the audience is instructed to remove the headphones we’ve been wearing for nearly the entire show. As Michael comes to the recognition of his relationship with his hearing loss and the clarity of mind that gives him, what we’ve become used to for the entire show’s experience — the headphones — are now gone, as is that literal weight from our heads. It’s an emotional moment, one that I’ve thought about multiple times since seeing the show.

It also leads into the final act, where Michael begins to understand his own Deaf identity. “The deafness is not the culprit, it’s the denial of it.” he tells me. “My hearing currently has never been worse, but I’ve never been more self-affirmed or self-actualized or felt happier in myself. It’s a misconception, I think, about deafness as a tragedy, deafness as a deficit, deafness as a burden, deafness as something that plagues a person.”

The ability of Auracast to broadcast an audio stream that any number of headphones can connect to is what made Love Me a possibility. Any Auracast headphones can connect to the audience broadcast — I brought along the Nothing Pro 1 to test the ability and connected to the audience broadcast channel in seconds — but I used the provided Auri receiver and Austrian Audio headset for the performance. The show’s sound was designed with those in mind, and I didn’t want the differing isolation of the Nothing headphones to affect the intent of the experience.

Audience members can use the provided headphones or connect their hearing aids or cochlear implants to the Auracast stream. Photo: John Higgins / The Verge iPads are also available for those who want to have captions during the show. Photo: Curtis Brown

Love Me is presented in partnership with Deaf West Theatre, which supports Deaf-centered storytelling in theatrical productions. In addition to the audience Auracast feed, there’s one for users of hearing aids and cochlear implants that’s designed for compliance with those devices, and iPads with captions are also available. During the performance, Michael connects to his own broadcast channel with Auracast-enabled Phonak Eon Sphere hearing aids. “We talked about using in-ear monitors, but if I use an in-ear monitor, then I don’t have amplification from my environment, so then I lose contact with the audience,” Michael says. “These function as two things: They’re hearing aids and also in-ear monitors.”

Love Me relies on the Auracast technology to tell its story, but it isn’t a story about hearing technology. The technology is there to tell the story of connection and discovery of identity. “I think right now … there are two things that are at odds — the hearing aid and audiological tech side of deafness and then the cultural identity side of deafness,” Michael says. Technological improvements, like cochlear implants and hearing aids, are cited as one of the reasons schools for the deaf have been on the decline, which leads to kids being mainstreamed (put into regular public schools) and losing out on Deaf history and culture. “I’m not against the tech,” Michael says, “I just think tech and Deaf identity should be a marriage rather than a divide.”

And that collaboration is why Love Me works as well as it does. The Auracast technology is there both for accessibility — in the same way it’s already used in other performances, lectures, or announcement systems — and to uplift the show’s story of love, acceptance, and acknowledgement of one’s own Deaf identity. It’s an inventive use of the technology that carries with it a powerful message.

Tech.title: ‘You Can See Everything’ has made more than $100M worldwide
Tech.content:
In Brief

“You Can See Everything,” Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim’s documentary about Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes, reached an impressive box office milestone this weekend, becoming one of the few documentaries to make more than $100 million worldwide.

Variety reports that almost all of the film’s $102.4 million box office has come from U.S. audiences, from whom it has grossed $93.4 million so far.

“You Can See Everything” will be opening in many more countries over the next few months — starting with Mexico, Brazil and Argentina on Nov. 25 and 26 — so its box office total could end up significantly higher.
